title: Pangilinan links timing of ₱41-M Carpio withdrawals to Duterte’s DepEd exit, drug charges
summary: **MANILA, Philippines —** Senator-Judge Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan questioned the timing of P41 million in cash withdrawals made by lawyer Manases “Mans” Carpio on Aug. 6, 2024, six days after drug-related charges were filed against him and
content:
**MANILA, Philippines —** Senator-Judge Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan questioned the timing of P41 million in cash withdrawals made by lawyer Manases “Mans” Carpio on Aug. 6, 2024, six days after drug-related charges were filed against him and weeks after his wife, Vice President Sara Duterte, resigned as education secretary.

During the 38th day of Duterte’s impeachment trial, Pangilinan said that Duterte resigned as Department of Education secretary on July 19, 2024, while charges against Carpio in connection with the alleged magnetic lifter incident were filed on July 30.

*   [Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/unexplained-wealth-of-vp-could-hit-p15b/2443897)

According to financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera’s report, Carpio withdrew the P41 million within approximately one hour and 13 minutes.

“I became curious about what happened on August 6, or where they were at the time,” Pangilinan said. Cabrera confirmed that the accounts involved belonged to Carpio.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Earlier, Cabrera told Senator-Judge Risa Hontiveros that the transactions appeared unusual because withdrawals resumed immediately after a lunch break.

“It seemed as though there was some urgency because the transactions continued immediately after lunch. It also takes considerable time to count P41 million in cash,” Cabrera said.

He added that large cash transactions and gaps in documentation could raise red flags in a forensic investigation, but did not establish that the withdrawals themselves constituted wrongdoing.

*   ![Image 1: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

Pangilinan also questioned the ownership of Cale88, whose 2025 records indicated that Carpio had transferred his shares to Pikimong Pikimong Philippines Corp.

Cabrera said the forensic team continued to consider Carpio the owner because it found no documentation establishing that the shares had been transferred.

The team examined corporate records filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), he said, describing Pikimong Pikimong as a shell company.

Cabrera said the company had only two shareholders and reported equity of P56,000 in 2024. Its reported assets in 2025 amounted to P86,000.

*   ![Image 2: Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256345.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/news/sandiganbayan-suspends-jinggoy-anew-over-floor-control-mess/2443890)

He said the records showed no transactions or disclosures establishing that Pikimong Pikimong had purchased Carpio’s shares in Cale88.

“Because there is no record of the transfer, the official records prevail,” he said.

Pangilinan questioned how a company with such limited reported capital could acquire an interest in Cale88, which recorded substantial financial inflows.

Cabrera clarified that the prosecution’s report identified approximately P222 million in relevant remittances, while about P319 million referred to amounts flagged in Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) records.

*   ![Image 3: Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254608.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/legarda-may-rejoin-senate-majority-pangilinan/2443223)

He said the team could not establish the funds’ ultimate destination.

Pangilinan also questioned the repeated conversion of cash into managers’ checks, including checks issued in Carpio’s name. Cabrera said he had not previously encountered such a pattern in his professional work.

He explained that converting cash into a manager’s check does not eliminate the obligation to declare the amount in a Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN).

“If the cash is no longer declared, the receivable should be declared instead,” Cabrera said.

He identified P96 million in managers’ checks, comprising P41 million and P55 million in transactions, which he said should have been reflected as receivables in the relevant SALNs.

Pangilinan also examined Cabrera’s findings on GenCorp, which reportedly grew from approximately P28 million in revenue in 2021 to more than P520 million in 2025, despite reporting paid-in capital of only P1.25 million.

Cabrera said the company’s financial statements did not clearly explain the source of the funds supporting its growth and acquisitions.

He explained that funds entering a business would ordinarily be expected to finance operations, equipment, inventory, employee salaries or debt payments.

When money moves into and out of a company without apparently adding economic value, the pattern can raise concerns, he said.

title: Zelenskyy says Russia violates energy ceasefire despite Trump’s claim
summary: **KYIV, Ukraine —** Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday that while Ukraine is willing to halt attacks on Russia's energy infrastructure, Moscow has continued to strike his country's energy sites despite U.S. President Donald
content:
**KYIV, Ukraine —** Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday that while Ukraine is willing to halt attacks on Russia's energy infrastructure, Moscow has continued to strike his country's energy sites despite U.S. President Donald Trump's announcement that the warring countries had agreed to cease such attacks.

Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum in Poland, Zelenskyy said Ukraine had been “horribly surprised” that Moscow struck a power plant in the northeastern city of Kharkiv, as well as a gas production facility and a civilian gas station hours after Trump announced the purported “energy ceasefire” in the 4 1/2-year-old war.

Later on Monday, during an interview on Fox News Channel’s “America’s Newsroom,” Zelenksyy said his government had refrained from striking Russian energy sites since Trump’s announcement Sunday, and was ready to honor an energy ceasefire as “a good first step” toward closing the war.

*   [Selma Blair taken into custody in New York after an alleged assault on a Delta flight](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/world/selma-blair-taken-into-custody-in-new-york-after-an-alleged-assault-on-a-delta-flight/2444092)

But, he said, "I’m not sure that (Russian President Vladimir) Putin is ready."

“Even after yesterday’s messages from (Trump) ... Putin attacked our gas infrastructure,” Zelenskyy said. “When we speak about energy ceasefire, it means only one thing: that they don’t attack our energy infrastructure and we don’t respond on their energy infrastructure.”

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Trump’s brief social media post Sunday offered few details but said the energy ceasefire took effect immediately, adding: “Do not break it!” On Monday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov wouldn’t say whether Russia had agreed to such a ceasefire, saying only: “Contacts are ongoing."

**Energy strikes have caused pain for both Ukraine and Russia**

Trump previously announced a similar agreement on ceasing energy strikes that did not come to fruition. In a social media post on Sept. 14, he said both countries had agreed “not to hit” each other’s energy infrastructure, but offered no details on that proposal either.

*   ![Image 1: Pangilinan links timing of ₱41-M Carpio withdrawals to Duterte’s DepEd exit, drug charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256649.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan links timing of ₱41-M Carpio withdrawals to Duterte’s DepEd exit, drug charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/pangilinan-links-timing-of-41-m-carpio-withdrawals-to-dutertes-deped-exit-drug-charges/2444082)

Russia has used attacks on energy facilities in order to deny Ukrainian civilians power, heat and running water during the war, hoping to wear down public support for Ukraine's response to Moscow’s full-scale invasion. Ukrainian officials describe the strategy as “weaponizing winter," and fear Russia could ramp up such attacks as cold weather approaches.

Ukraine, meanwhile, has launched strikes against Russian energy sites like oil refineries, sometimes deep within Russian territory. That's prompted Trump to blame Zelenskyy for record US diesel prices — rather than the US-led war in Iran — and to strike a deal with Putin on Friday to import diesel from Russia in an attempt to bring fuel prices down ahead of US midterm elections.

Speaking on Fox News on Monday, Zelenskyy pushed back on Trump's claims that Ukrainian strikes in Russia were driving up fuel prices, saying: “Everybody understands that the prices on diesel (don't) depend on our attacks on diesel in Russia. Everybody understands that it depends on the blocking (of the) Strait of Hormuz.”

**EU foreign policy chief skeptical of energy ceasefire**

*   ![Image 2: Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256531.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/unexplained-wealth-of-vp-could-hit-p15b/2443897)

The European Union’s top diplomat on Monday welcomed the prospect of a pause in energy strikes on Ukraine, but said she sees no sign that Russia is willing to respect it.

“We haven’t yet seen that ... Russia will stick to it,” EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said at a meeting of the bloc's foreign ministers in Luxembourg. “Personally, I would also welcome that the ceasefire would include people not being killed, not only energy.”

Trump's deal with Putin to purchase diesel from Russia dismayed officials in the US, Ukraine and around Europe. A bipartisan group of six US senators, including four Republicans, called Sunday on the Trump administration to “immediately reverse course” on the deal, saying the U.S. should “not provide Putin with a financial lifeline” while Russia is killing Ukrainian civilians.

Kallas also pushed back on Trump's comments Saturday that it was time for Ukraine to get a new president and that Zelenskyy has not done enough to end the war. She said that now is not the time to hold elections in Ukraine, at least not without a ceasefire.

*   ![Image 3: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

On Monday, Zelenskyy said holding elections in Ukraine was impossible during war time, especially with new Russian tactics involving attacks day and night. He added, however, that he would be ready to work toward doing so if Ukraine secured a full ceasefire lasting at least 60 days.

In response, Kremlin spokesman Peskov said in a statement that in case of a Ukrainian election, Putin would be ready to halt strikes on Ukraine “specifically on election day,” and that Kyiv only wanted a 60-day ceasefire “to gather their strength, heal their wounds, and continue the war.”

**Russian attacks kill 5 and injure others, including children**

Meanwhile, Zelenskyy called for greater pressure on Russia to end the war after a Russian drone struck a high-rise apartment building in Kyiv on Monday evening, killing two people and injuring nine.

“This is further proof that Russia must face greater pressure. They are the ones continuing the brutal strikes. They are the ones prolonging the war,” he said in a post on X.

He called the attack a “response” to the U.S. proposal for an energy ceasefire.

“We count on the United States to recognize these signals from Russia and act with strength. Strength is needed to force Russia to end this war,” Zelenskyy said.

Monday's attack came a day after a Russian drone struck the village of Pisochyn in the Kharkiv district, killing three people and injuring nine others, including children, according to the Kharkiv Regional Prosecutor’s Office.

Ukrainian air defense forces shot down or suppressed 89 of 121 Russian drones overnight Monday, Ukraine’s Air Force said in a Telegram post. The attacks included one Kh-59 guided air-to-surface missile and 76 jet-powered Shahed-type drones, the statement said. Strikes were recorded at 15 locations in Ukraine, while debris from downed drones fell at four locations.

Meanwhile, the Russian Defense Ministry said Monday its air defenses overnight intercepted 151 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions as well as the illegally annexed Crimea and the waters of the Black Sea.

In a separate statement, the ministry said its forces carried out drone strikes overnight on Ukraine’s port infrastructure and a bulk carrier heading to Ukraine's port city of Odesa with military cargo on board.

title: Wage hike proposals met with mixed reactions
summary: **ILOILO CITY —**Calls for a wage increase comparable to those granted in other regions and for the deferment of an adjustment amid rising business costs emerged during a public hearing on minimum wage rates for private-sector workers in We
content:
**ILOILO CITY —**Calls for a wage increase comparable to those granted in other regions and for the deferment of an adjustment amid rising business costs emerged during a public hearing on minimum wage rates for private-sector workers in Western Visayas.

The Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board-Western Visayas (RTWPB-6) conducted its third public hearing on the proposed wage adjustment on Oct. 9, with stakeholders from Iloilo City and the provinces of Iloilo, Antique and Guimaras.

Jessraf Palmares, president of the Iloilo Federation for Information Technology, Inc., supported a wage increase but urged the board to consider rates in neighboring regions rather than compete with wage boards granting substantially higher adjustments.

*   [More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

“If possible, Iloilo should have the same minimum wage as Cebu,” he said.

He claimed that two BPO companies had planned to establish operations in Iloilo but eventually withdrew and redirected their plans to Cebu because of Iloilo’s higher minimum wage.

 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

A teacher from St. Anthony’s College in Antique also supported a wage increase but said a P200 daily adjustment would be too much for educational institutions to absorb.

She suggested an increase comparable to those granted in other regions, saying an additional P60 a day would provide some relief to workers without imposing an excessive burden on employers.

“Sixty pesos is more or less acceptable. It is not substantial but it could help,” she said.

*   ![Image 1: Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256531.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/unexplained-wealth-of-vp-could-hit-p15b/2443897)

The teacher warned that a P200 increase could adversely affect private schools, particularly as they consider possible tuition adjustments.

In Central Visayas, private-sector workers are scheduled to receive a P42 daily minimum wage increase starting Oct. 14, 2026.

The minimum wage in expanded Metro Cebu and other Class A areas will rise from P540 to P582, while rates in covered Class B cities and municipalities will increase from P500 to P542.

In the National Capital Region, a P60 daily wage increase took effect on Sept. 26, raising the minimum wage to P755 for non-agricultural workers and P718 for agricultural workers and employees of certain small establishments. In Western Visayas, the current daily minimum wage rates are P550 for workers in non-agricultural, industrial and commercial establishments employing more than 10 workers; P525 for those in establishments employing 10 or fewer workers; and P520 for agricultural workers.

*   ![Image 2: Aston Martin DBX GT puts luxury first](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255560.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Aston Martin DBX GT puts luxury first](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/fast-times/aston-martin-dbx-gt-puts-luxury-first/2443744)

The Western Visayas rates were established under a wage order that took effect on Nov. 19, 2025.

**Businesses seek deferment**

Happy Mapua Abenir, president of the Iloilo Hotels, Restaurants, and Resorts Association, Inc., called for the deferment of the proposed wage increase until next year, citing economic uncertainties and mounting operating costs.

“The business sector is now experiencing an extraordinary event in 2026. It is very worrisome because we cannot seem to predict what will happen until the end of the year,” she argued.

*   ![Image 3: Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256345.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/news/sandiganbayan-suspends-jinggoy-anew-over-floor-control-mess/2443890)

She described the current business environment as worse than the Covid-19 pandemic, saying businesses were struggling not only with rising prices but also with numerous expenses that had become increasingly difficult to sustain.

While acknowledging local governments’ efforts to help alleviate poverty, Abenir said providing loans is only a “band-aid” solution and would not address the underlying problems faced by businesses.

Instead, she called for relief from high taxes, rental costs, electricity bills and fuel expenses.

A resort owner in Guimaras likewise sought a deferment, explaining that the tourism business was seasonal and that establishments still had to retain employees during off-peak periods despite having little or no income.

“I hope the increase can be deferred for now because this is the off-season for resorts. We are just waiting for people to take their vacations at our resort,” she said.

Tiffany Ong of the Federation of Free Workers, who represented health workers during the hearing, called for government intervention through subsidies and temporary relief from mandatory deductions.

She proposed a moratorium on deductions for government-mandated contributions, including those for the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth), Social Security System (SSS), and Pag-IBIG Fund.

“I hope these deductions can be temporarily suspended. We can hardly feel our salaries because of the mandatory deductions,” Ong said.

MSMEs need support

Palmares, who also operates a small business, said soaring electricity and rental costs had forced them to reduce their workforce and assign more responsibilities to their remaining employees.

He urged the government to provide subsidies and tax relief to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), including measures to ease their tax burden.

“What is the plan of the government to subsidize the MSMEs? I hope there will be a tax bracket under which value-added tax can be removed. MSME taxes should be reduced so we can still earn a profit,” Palmares said.

Elmer Forro, one of the lead convenors of the United Labor-Western Visayas Workers’ Alliance (ULWVA), which filed a petition seeking a P250 daily wage increase, said workers and small businesses had yet to benefit sufficiently from the region’s economic growth.

Western Visayas recorded a 6.4 percent growth rate in its Gross Regional Domestic Product in 2025, ranking as the fastest-growing regional economy among the Philippines’ 18 regions and outperforming the national average of 4.4 percent.

“But workers and MSMEs cannot feel this growth. Its benefits have not reached workers, and MSMEs but have also gone to big businesses investing here,” Forro said.

He acknowledged the difficulty of balancing workers’ demands for higher wages with the capacity of MSMEs to absorb additional labor costs.

“The big question in the debate between workers and MSMEs is the issue of wages. Higher wages are a burden for MSMEs, but workers also cannot survive if the minimum wage does not increase,” he said.

Forro questioned the government’s role in addressing the situation, saying one-time financial assistance was insufficient to address the underlying problems.

“We do not just need one-time, substantial financial assistance. The government needs to help MSMEs increase their capacity to provide fair wages to their workers,” he said.

He added that the government should provide greater assistance to MSMEs to help balance the interests of employers and workers.

“To our MSMEs and labor groups, it is high time for us to unite. We have a common problem. We are both victims. We should seek from the government what we deserve,” Forro said.

**Wage decision eyed before year-end**

Lawyer Sixto Rodriguez Jr., RTWPB-6 chairman and concurrently director of the Department of Labor and Employment in Region 6, said the board could decide before the end of the year whether to issue a new wage order.

“We will have to act within a reasonable time because you know the last wage order was Nov. 19. It might be after that; it should not be before that. Yes (before the year ends),” he said.

Rodriguez added that wage determination involved balancing workers’ right to fair compensation with employers’ interests in sustaining their businesses, taking into account prevailing economic conditions.

The RTWPB-6 received four petitions seeking a wage increase.

On April 30, ULWVA filed a petition seeking a P250 daily wage increase, which would raise the regional minimum wage from P550 to P800, along with a cost-of-living allowance.

The group cited global oil supply disruptions and their effects on the regional economy.

On June 5, the Iloilo Doctors Hospital Employees Union, also a member of ULWVA, filed a similar petition.

Following an evaluation, the board found that the petition substantially complied with legal requirements and issued a resolution recognizing its sufficiency.

The BPO Industry Employees Network filed another petition on June 26 seeking the same adjustment, citing concerns specific to BPO workers.

The fourth petition was filed on July 24 by the Iloilo Pepsi-Cola Workers Independent Union, which also sought a P250 daily wage increase.

“Our decision is always based on facts and based on evidence presented, as well as what constitutes a just and reasonable amount,” Rodriguez said.

title: Trump’s ‘energy ceasefire’ creates confusion
summary: **WASHINGTON**—US President Donald Trump sowed confusion on Sunday, announcing an “energy ceasefire” between Ukraine and Russia that sparked astonishment in Kyiv, silence from Moscow and support from Ukraine’s Western allies. The ceasefire
content:
**WASHINGTON**—US President Donald Trump sowed confusion on Sunday, announcing an “energy ceasefire” between Ukraine and Russia that sparked astonishment in Kyiv, silence from Moscow and support from Ukraine’s Western allies.

The ceasefire appeared shaky at best as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia struck multiple Ukrainian power plants on Sunday, including one in the capital and another in Kharkiv, leading to power outages and outrage.

Trump’s announcement came two days after he declared a temporary easing of US sanctions on Russian diesel, prompting outrage by European allies and Kyiv, who said it would only embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin.

*   [NATO to warn Russia against any attack](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/world/americas-emea/nato-to-warn-russia-against-any-attack/2443624)

“Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine,” Trump said early Sunday on Truth Social. “Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!”

Zelenskyy appeared to express surprise at the announcement, saying he was seeking further details, but added that “Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well.”

 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Russia has yet to confirm its agreement.

Zelenskyy later said that multiple Ukrainian power stations had been hit and that “Ukrainian skies have been infested with Russian ‘shaheds’ all day,” referring to a type of drone originally designed by Iran that is now used extensively by Russia.

## **‘Up to our people’**

The ceasefire appeared to garner support on Sunday from Ukraine’s key western allies, including the UK, France, Canada and the European Commission.

Several leaders called on Russia to uphold the deal.

That support was in contrast to broad criticism of the US-Russia diesel deal earlier in the week, which has led to mounting tensions between Trump and Zelenskyy.

Zelenskyy said the diesel deal was a “weak decision,” while several of Ukraine’s European allies expressed outrage and pledged to increase pressure on Moscow.

Seven US senators -- including four Republicans -- released a statement Sunday blasting the diesel deal with Russia, saying it was illegal.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney added to the chorus on Sunday after a call with Zelensky, saying the diesel deal “is in direct opposition to the efforts of Ukraine, Canada and our allies to create peace and stability in Europe.”

## **Support for Zelenskyy**

Germany’s foreign minister said Sunday that Berlin continued to “fully support” Zelenskyy.

“Europe needs stability and that means that we are very clearly continuing to stay by the side of Ukraine and its government,” Johann Wadephul said in Berlin.

*   ![Image 1: Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256531.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/unexplained-wealth-of-vp-could-hit-p15b/2443897)

EU chief Ursula von der Leyen also backed the Ukrainian leader “as he leads the fight for his people’s freedom.”

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham also said his country “strongly supports President Trump’s call today for a sustained energy ceasefire to start now.”

In Kyiv, several residents expressed concern about Trump’s call for Zelenskyy to be replaced.

“I believe our president is the best, and Americans should think about their own president,” said 40-year-old Olesia Goncharuk.

“We Ukrainians decide our own fate and our own freedom, and we are free people,” she told AFP.

title: Prepare for El Niño, Marcos urges Filipinos
summary: PRESIDENT Ferdinand Marcos Jr. urged Filipinos to prepare for a super El Niño, including collecting rainwater and planting their own vegetables at home, to minimize the impact from the weather pattern. In a press briefing, Marcos stressed h
content:
PRESIDENT Ferdinand Marcos Jr. urged Filipinos to prepare for a super El Niño, including collecting rainwater and planting their own vegetables at home, to minimize the impact from the weather pattern.

In a press briefing, Marcos stressed how impactful El Niño was likely to be, citing government forecasts that indicate severe dry conditions lasting through the first quarter of next year.

He stressed that along with government programs, everyday households play a critical role in mitigating the severe impacts of the expected dry conditions.

*   [China's carmakers rely on overseas markets as monthly domestic sales decline continues](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/business/foreign-business/chinas-carmakers-rely-on-overseas-markets-as-monthly-domestic-sales-decline-continues/2443941)

“Part of that public service — and those public service messages — will be to gather or buy buckets now so that when it rains, you can collect all the water,” Marcos said.

He added that the government would be providing guidance and water-treatment tools to ensure home-collected rainwater is safe for domestic use.

“We will teach you... We’ll give you the filter, we’ll teach you how to do everything so you won’t get sick, and the water is treated properly.”

He also stressed that practicing strict household water conservation — such as reusing dishwashing water to tend to home vegetable plots — would help cushion families against rising food prices and supply constraints.

Marcos also highlighted the importance of keeping the momentum of the “green revolution,” or the movement to increase food production.

*   ![Image 1: Paper is not proof](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256393.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Paper is not proof](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/opinion/columns/paper-is-not-proof/2443919)

“Get everybody to plant their own vegetables. That’s why if — that will help again. It won’t solve the entire problem, but it will help,” he said, encouraging a national revival of backyard farming and planting, similar to the time of the pandemic.

Beyond household-level measures, Marcos assured the public that Task Force El Niño, led by the Department of Science and Technology, had activated coordinated contingency plans.

The plans include ensuring medical facilities maintain standby generators, fuel reserves and water stores during potential heat waves and power outages.

The national government is also securing grain supplies through strategic imports while preparing cash-for-work and livelihood assistance.

*   ![Image 2: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

Cloud-seeding operations will be done to boost reservoir levels before the onset of the peak summer months.

“It’s not just a regular El Niño. It’s going to be a Super El Niño... starting late October, beginning November, and continuing until March next year,” Marcos said.

“We should all prepare. We’re taking this very, very seriously.”

As this developed, the Department of Energy (DOE) on Monday also warned of rotating brownouts, particularly in the Visayas, where supply is already under pressure due to insufficient baseload capacity nationwide, with a super El Niño expected to put the power grid under severe strain.

*   ![Image 3: Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256531.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/unexplained-wealth-of-vp-could-hit-p15b/2443897)

Energy Undersecretary Mario Marasigan said the department was closely watching.

He said the agency is doing various simulations with increased demand due to El Niño and noted that Visayas could again be hit with plenty of red alerts because of various plants’ possibility of going offline unscheduled due to the heat.

“Based on our simulations, and assuming we are under normal condition or there are no unannounced power interruptions, we are seeing a little amount of red alerts for Luzon, but will not necessarily translate to manual load dropping, or rotating brownouts,” Marasigan said in an online media briefing.

Marasigan continued that the DOE was closely monitoring the Visayas and working on the completion of immediate and interim energy generation solutions by the first quarter of 2027.

“If there are ancillary services that are available from these intermediate and immediate facilities, then we will be able to greatly reduce the potential of having red and yellow alerts in the island group,” he said.

Mindanao, meanwhile, will likely see limited yellow alerts, while Luzon could see a few red alerts but not rotational brownouts.

“I would say that we are still preparing for El Niño and that related programs are in place and already activated via the Task Force on Energy Resiliency,” Energy Secretary Sharon Garin said.

Malacañang, the DOE said, has been calling for meetings under a whole-of-government approach that will include an extensive education and information campaign on how the country is supposed to handle the situation for the coming months.

**PARIS** —France’s high school students on Monday begin a new stage of their campaign for improved conditions, hoping to maintain the momentum with a fresh wave of demonstrations.

The new protests, scheduled for Tuesday, could be a turning point in the movement, launched in mid-September, which the government hopes is already winding down.

On Friday, the government noted a dramatic drop in the number of blockades and meetings outside the country’s lycées, where students -- most between 15 and 18 -- complete their high school education.

More than 96 percent were opening Friday, said the education ministry.

The authorities are all the more keen to see the student protests end given that online activists have called for demonstrations next Saturday to protest the cost of living.

For President Emmanuel Macron’s administration, that brings back troubling memories of the grassroots Yellow Vest movement.

Their protests, launched in 2018 over a planned fuel tax rise, saw massive demonstrations and clashes between police and protesters that shook the presidency during Macron’s first term in office.

## **Concessions**

The government is still counting the cost of the high school protests.

A government source told journalists last week that the cost for damage caused by the demonstrations was “at least 30 million euros”.

On Friday, the justice ministry said more than 6,800 people had been detained since the demonstrations started, 86 percent of them minors.

After clashes between some protesters and riot police left some students severely injured, sparking criticism of police tactics, the government suspended the use of stun grenades that cost one student his hand.

Police are investigating 18 alleged cases of misconduct within their ranks.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Sunday promised to make changes to the planned budget 2027 to respond to some demands set out in an online platform the government set up to gather students’ views.

## **‘Crumbs’**

The student organizations behind the protests are yet to be convinced.

The Union of High School students described the initial announcements last week as “crumbs”.

France’s 10,000 medical students, however, are beginning to express concern at the effect any continued school blockades could have on exams starting Monday that help determine their eventual specialty.

They do not want to see the students’ action disrupt such a crucial stage of their education.

Nearly 256,000 took part in last Tuesday’s day of action.

title: Prosecutors to review NBI-flagged properties
summary: HOUSE prosecutors will review the National Bureau of Investigation’s (NBI) findings on properties linked to Vice President Sara Duterte and her family to determine whether the assets were included in the prosecution’s computation of P817.87
content:
HOUSE prosecutors will review the National Bureau of Investigation’s (NBI) findings on properties linked to Vice President Sara Duterte and her family to determine whether the assets were included in the prosecution’s computation of P817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth.

Senator-Judge Erwin Tulfo sought the review on Monday after the NBI presented its initial assessment of properties linked to Duterte and Davao City Rep. Paolo Duterte, citing discrepancies between declared acquisition costs in their statements of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALNs) and the bureau’s preliminary estimates.

“Would you later look into this to counter-check whether the NBI’s investigation is correct?” Tulfo asked House prosecutor Chel Diokno during the 38th day of Duterte’s impeachment trial.

*   [Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/legarda-may-rejoin-senate-majority-pangilinan/2443223)

“Sure, we will do that, your honor,” Diokno replied.

Tulfo showed financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera materials from the NBI’s press briefing earlier that day and asked whether the properties had been included in his assessment of Duterte’s finances.

Cabrera said he could not confirm this without examining the relevant documents, including transfer certificates of title (TCTs), property addresses and land areas.

Tulfo specifically asked about an agricultural property in Barangay Santo Niño, Balac, on the Island Garden City of Samal (Igacos), reportedly declared at an acquisition cost of P200,000.

Asked whether two properties presented by the NBI were included in the approximately P817 million in alleged unexplained wealth attributed to Duterte, Cabrera said he was unsure.

“I am not sure whether those are included,” he said, adding that the properties might already have been covered by Duterte’s declarations.

Cabrera also said that one property appeared valuable because it had two swimming pools, but stressed that its appearance alone was insufficient to determine whether it had been included in his computation.

Diokno told the impeachment court that the prosecution had copies of Duterte’s SALNs detailing her declared real properties but had not yet reviewed the NBI presentation.

Tulfo asked the prosecution to obtain the relevant documents and compare them with Cabrera’s findings.

*   ![Image 2: Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1255072.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/legal-advice/who-should-pay-capital-gains-tax/2443313)

**‘Numbers don’t lie’**

Separately, Diokno defended the prosecution’s reliance on financial records, saying the unexplained wealth allegations ultimately concern transparency and accountability in public office.

Responding to Senator-Judge Lito Lapid, who asked what the public should take away from the witnesses and documents presented during the trial, Diokno said an honest public official should have nothing to hide.

“It is easy to pretend to be an ordinary person who eats at a neighborhood eatery, but under Article II on unexplained wealth, that’s where the truth comes out. The numbers do not lie,” Diokno said.

*   ![Image 3: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

Lapid raised the question following testimony on the P817.87 million in allegedly undeclared assets and unexplained wealth attributed to Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio.

Diokno said the central issue under Article II, which accuses Duterte of unexplained wealth, was straightforward.

“When we look at the heart of Article II, I think it comes down to this: an honest public official has nothing to hide,” he said.

He said the case hinged not on witness testimony alone but on financial records from banks, the Anti-Money Laundering Council, the Bureau of Internal Revenue and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

“What matters here is not the witnesses themselves, but the documents and the numbers,” Diokno said.

“These bank documents, for example, did not pass through the hands of the prosecution. The banks sent them directly to this court. So we can say that these are independent facts that anyone can verify,” he added.

Diokno said the proceedings were not simply about Duterte as a person but also about public trust, leadership and accountability.

“This case is really not about Vice President Sara Duterte as a person. To me, it is about the trust the people have placed in her,” Diokno said.

“It is not about her as a person, but about leadership — whether she has governed properly and, more importantly, whether a high-ranking public official has the integrity and fitness to continue serving in office,” he added.

Lapid’s questions followed testimony from Cabrera, who presented a computation of P817,874,867 in allegedly undeclared wealth involving Duterte and Carpio from 2022 to 2025.

The total covered allegedly undeclared cash, personal and real properties, income attributed to the couple, and amounts computed from several corporate entities.

The highest annual figure was recorded in 2024 at P264,217,123, followed by P195,692,505 in 2025, P190,628,012 in 2022 and P167,337,227 in 2023.

Cabrera identified P207,696,933 in allegedly undeclared cash over the four-year period: P60,214,776 in 2022, P80,701,151 in 2023, P23,169,077 in 2024 and P43,611,929 in 2025.

He also identified P143,497,177 in other allegedly undeclared personal and real properties, net of deductions. The annual figures were P76,147,730 in 2022, P3,934,560 in 2023, P52,016,994 in 2024 and P11,397,893 in 2025.

The analysis also calculated P111,852,349 in allegedly undeclared income attributed to the couple, broken down into P50,474,511 in 2022, P12,198,235 in 2023, P28,030,203 in 2024 and P21,149,400 in 2025.

For Cale88 Foods Corp. and Metro City Chow, Cabrera computed P142,198,690 in allegedly undeclared income. The annual figures were P3,790,995 in 2022, P14,788,989 in 2023, P86,944,369 in 2024 and P36,674,337 in 2025.

For GenCorp Industries Inc., the computed amount reached P212,629,718 from 2023 to 2025: P55,714,292 in 2023, P74,056,480 in 2024 and P82,858,946 in 2025. No amount was recorded for 2022 under this category.

Cabrera, a lawyer and certified public accountant with more than three decades of experience in accounting, taxation, law and financial forensics, has defended the computation before the impeachment court.

CATHERINE VALENTE

title: 3 Filipinos in ICU after Riyadh airport attack
summary: THREE of four Filipinos injured in an attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia remained in intensive care on Monday, with at least one in critical condition, the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) said Monday. DM
content:
THREE of four Filipinos injured in an attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia remained in intensive care on Monday, with at least one in critical condition, the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) said Monday.

DMW Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac said the fourth injured Filipino had been discharged from the hospital but would continue to receive assistance.

“He had some problems in his lumbar area, so this will be continually monitored,” Cacdac said during a briefing on Oct. 12. “He had some trauma burns, but again, he is healthy enough to be released from hospital.” Two of the injured Filipinos worked at the airport, while the other two were passengers. They were two men and two women.

*   [DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

Cacdac said the government had reached out to the families of the injured Filipinos following the incident.

“We have also reached out per directive of the president to reach out to their families to help the families,” he said.

 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Meanwhile, Philippine officials were assisting Filipinos affected by flight cancellations and the temporary closure of Riyadh airport.

Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) Administrator Patricia Yvonne Caunan reported that 30 people, including overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) and dependents, were stranded in Riyadh.

Of the 30, 20 were staying in hotels sponsored by the DMW and OWWA, while seven had been picked up by relatives. Two seafarers in transit were staying at an airline-sponsored hotel, and one person had been picked up by an employer.

*   ![Image 1: Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1255072.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/legal-advice/who-should-pay-capital-gains-tax/2443313)

Another 94 OFWs whose flights to Riyadh were diverted to Jeddah were receiving assistance from the Philippine labor office there while awaiting the resumption of flights.

“Currently, they are billeted and they’re being assisted in Jeddah awaiting for the resumption of flights,” Cacdac said.

The government was providing temporary accommodation, food, transportation assistance and help with flight rebooking.

In Manila, 37 OFWs sought assistance following flight cancellations, including temporary accommodation and transportation to their homes in Metro Manila and the provinces. Three remained in hotels as of the briefing.

*   ![Image 2: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

One other Filipino was reported stranded at Dammam International Airport in eastern Saudi Arabia after a flight cancellation. Officials said assistance was being provided.

Despite the attacks, the DMW said there is no deployment ban in place for Saudi Arabia as it monitors security developments and flight disruptions in the kingdom.

“At this stage, no deployment ban to Saudi,” Cacdac said on Monday.

Cacdac said the department was coordinating with the Department of Foreign Affairs and the Department of National Defense to assess the political and security situation.

*   ![Image 3: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

He noted that economic activity in Saudi Arabia continued despite the recent attacks and said that the government would remain in contact with its counterparts as developments unfolded.

**Tested**

Saudi Arabia’s energy minister acknowledged on Monday that the kingdom’s infrastructure and resilience had been tested, as he vowed a firm response following a wave of deadly attacks by Yemen’s Houthis.

The Houthi attacks over the weekend marked a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Saudi Arabia has long supported the internationally recognized government.

On Sunday, a strike hit Riyadh’s international airport, killing one person, just hours after another Houthi-claimed on the site killed 13 people and left hundreds of others wounded, forcing authorities to suspend operations there.

The attacks on Saudi Arabia, a regional powerhouse and the world’s top oil exporter which has poured billions of dollars into its military, were the deadliest to hit the kingdom in a decade.

“For Saudi Arabia, these circumstances have tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people, and our resilience. They have also tested decisions made long before present crises, because resilience is built before crises begin,” Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said.

“Energy security can’t be taken for granted,” he told a high-profile conference in Riyadh. “The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious.”

The airport was not the only one in the country to be targeted: the civil aviation authority also reported another on Dammam airport in the east.

The Saudi-led coalition said Monday it had also “intercepted and destroyed” a Houthi ballistic missile heading for the southern city of Khamis Mushait, home to a major military base.

title: Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B
summary: VICE President Sara Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, could have up to P1.5 billion in unexplained wealth from 2022 to 2025, nearly double the prosecution’s conservative estimate of P817.87 million, financial forensic analyst
content:
VICE President Sara Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, could have up to P1.5 billion in unexplained wealth from 2022 to 2025, nearly double the prosecution’s conservative estimate of P817.87 million, financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera told the Senate impeachment court on Monday.

Testifying on Day 38 of Duterte’s impeachment trial, Cabrera confirmed the maximum estimate after Senate President and Presiding Officer Francis Escudero sought clarification on the potential total, excluding double-counting of assets.

“I’ll be more specific, sir. P1.5 billion would be the maximum estimate of the undeclared wealth of the respondents from 2022 to 2025, without any double booking?” Escudero asked.

*   [Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/legal-advice/who-should-pay-capital-gains-tax/2443313)

“Yes,” Cabrera replied.

“The amounts vary each year, and when you add them all up, that would be the ceiling,” Escudero said, explaining that the amounts varied by year and would reach that ceiling when added together.

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

“That’s correct,” Cabrera said.

Escudero then asked Cabrera how high the estimate could go if the prosecution’s financial analysis did not rely on conservative assumptions.

Cabrera explained that his team had deliberately used conservative figures in computing the couple’s alleged unexplained wealth.

*   ![Image 1: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

Escudero also pointed out that deducting assets attributed to MetroChow, Cale88 and GenCorp from the P817-million total in undeclared assets would still leave P463.046 million in alleged unexplained wealth.

The deductions included P142.198 million attributed to Cale88 and P212 million in GenCorp assets, based on the figures cited during the proceedings.

The higher estimate could reach P1.5 billion if confidential funds, discrepancies reflected in Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) reports and less conservative figures for GenCorp were factored into the computation, Cabrera said.

The estimates cover the period from 2022 to 2025 and are based on the documents and assumptions discussed during the proceedings.

*   ![Image 2: Eala suffers worst loss of 2026 season, falls to world No. 217 Shi](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256500.png?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Eala suffers worst loss of 2026 season, falls to world No. 217 Shi](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/sports/eala-suffers-worst-loss-of-2026-season-falls-to-world-no-217-shi/2443990)

**Unexplained inflows**

A banana chip exporter linked to Vice President Duterte’s husband reported persistent losses despite substantial cash inflows, Cabrera testified.

Another company also linked to the vice president had P1 billion in alleged undeclared inflows, he said.

Cabrera flagged financial discrepancies involving the two companies, Cale88 Foods Corp. and GenCorp Industries Inc., as senators scrutinized their transactions, potential tax liabilities and ownership structures.

*   ![Image 3: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

Cabrera also defended his estimate of P817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth involving Duterte and her husband from 2022 to 2025, while acknowledging that P211 million of the total depended on an assumption about Duterte’s ownership stake in GenCorp.

During his interjection, Senator-Judge and Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian questioned Cabrera about P1 billion in alleged undeclared inflows recorded by GenCorp from 2022 to 2025.

Cabrera said the funds were not reflected in the company’s balance sheet, income statement or income tax returns, based on his analysis.

Asked whether the money could have come from loans, advances or pass-through transactions rather than sales, Cabrera said this was unlikely because such transactions should also have been recorded as payables.

Using a 25-percent tax rate, he estimated GenCorp’s potential tax liability at P250 million.

He agreed that the circumstances could warrant examining whether the corporate veil could be pierced, potentially extending liability to shareholders if the legal requirements were met.

Cabrera acknowledged that he had not prepared specific court rulings involving the piercing of the corporate veil in cases of unpaid taxes but promised to submit a relevant case reference to the Senate.

**Discrepancies noted**

He also questioned discrepancies between GenCorp’s general information sheet (GIS) and Duterte’s statement of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN). Duterte’s name was reportedly absent from the company’s GIS, although GenCorp appeared in her SALN.

Cabrera said he gave greater weight to the SALN because it is signed under oath. He also questioned whether GenCorp’s corporate disclosures adequately identified its ultimate beneficial owner under Securities and Exchange Commission rules.

He said his team used a 20-percent ownership stake for Duterte as a conservative assumption, based partly on her SALN declaration and previous business relationships.

He acknowledged that the actual percentage could be lower or higher and required verification.

Cabrera previously testified that GenCorp’s revenue rose from about P28 million in 2021 to more than P520 million in 2025, despite reported paid-in capital of only P1.25 million.

He said the company’s financial statements did not clearly explain the sources of funds supporting its growth and acquisitions.

Cale88 Foods Corp., a banana chip exporter linked to Carpio, also came under scrutiny over its financial statements and substantial cash movements.

Questioned by Senator-Judge Raffy Tulfo, Cabrera said a comparison with five or six similarly sized export companies revealed differences in assets, inventories and profitability.

He pointed to the absence of recorded accounts payable, accounts receivable and raw-material or work-in-process inventories despite Cale88’s purported manufacturing and export operations.

“There are really many things that are not in the proper place in that financial statement,” Cabrera said.

He added that the company continued to report losses despite substantial amounts moving through its accounts.

Cabrera likened the transactions to a revolving door, with money flowing in and quickly going out without an apparent contribution to the company’s operations. He cautioned that this pattern warranted scrutiny but did not, by itself, establish wrongdoing.

Cale88 was also flagged for about P35 million in alleged undeclared inflows. Cabrera estimated a potential tax liability of P5 million to P6 million based on the documents his team reviewed.

The AMLC had reported about P1.25 billion in covered and suspicious transactions involving Cale88 from 2022 to 2025, including P319.33 million in remittances originating from China and Hong Kong, according to testimony presented during the proceedings.

Gatchalian separately questioned the discrepancy between an AMLC report indicating about P700 million in total inflows and Cabrera’s calculation of about P247 million in bank inflows.

Cabrera said the difference could partly reflect duplicate tagging when funds entered foreign-currency accounts and were subsequently converted into pesos or transferred elsewhere. He said his team attempted to eliminate duplicate transactions and adopted a conservative approach.

Senator-Judge Bam Aquino pressed Cabrera to distinguish findings based on documentary records from estimates dependent on assumptions about corporate ownership and the attribution of undeclared income.

The discussion centered on Table 39 of Cabrera’s report, which covered undeclared cash balances, personal properties and investments, unexplained outflows, and income attributed to companies.

Cabrera acknowledged that the 20-percent ownership interest attributed to Duterte in GenCorp was an assumption rather than a figure established by the corporate records he examined.

Aquino stressed that the actual ownership percentage could differ and that the final estimate should be determined by the evidence.

After excluding about P211 million associated with the GenCorp ownership assumption, Cabrera said the remaining estimate was about P606 million based on the records examined.

Aquino cautioned against introducing other allegations to offset reductions in the total, emphasizing that each component of the calculation should stand on its own evidentiary basis.

Cabrera said his analysis also considered whether undeclared corporate income could be attributed to beneficial owners under the legal doctrine of piercing the corporate veil. He acknowledged that the senator-judges would have to assess whether the doctrine applied.

During cross-examination, defense counsel Kristine Ferrer questioned Cabrera’s methodology, his access to corporate records and the absence of direct input from Duterte and Carpio.

Cabrera acknowledged that he had not received documents directly from the couple for his forensic accounting review.

He said his team examined materials submitted in connection with Duterte’s responses to the House of Representatives and the Senate but found no documents from the couple that could be used in the analysis.

“Had there been, I would have used [them],” Cabrera said.

Ferrer also questioned findings concerning alleged advances to Cale88, including P8.7 million attributed to Carpio in 2022, noting that Cabrera had not examined the company’s books of accounts.

Cabrera confirmed that his analysis attributed a 20-percent capital interest in Cale88 to Duterte based on documents examined by the prosecution.

He also acknowledged that time constraints prevented his team from reviewing all the bank documents provided and said the AMLC report was not used to determine Duterte’s net assets.

Meanwhile, Senator-Judge Francis Pangilinan questioned P41 million in cash withdrawals made by Carpio on Aug. 6, 2024, six days after drug-related charges were filed against him in connection with the alleged magnetic lifter incident.

Pangilinan said Duterte had resigned as Education secretary on July 19, 2024, while the charges against Carpio were filed on July 30.

According to Cabrera’s report, Carpio withdrew the money within about one hour and 13 minutes.

“I became curious about what happened on Aug. 6, or where they were at the time,” Pangilinan said.

Cabrera confirmed that the accounts belonged to Carpio and described the sequence of transactions as unusual, noting that withdrawals resumed immediately after a lunch break.

He cautioned, however, that the timing and amount of the withdrawals did not establish that the transactions were unlawful.

Pangilinan also questioned the reported transfer of Carpio’s shares in Cale88 to Pikimong Pikimong Philippines Corp. in 2025.

Cabrera said his team continued to attribute the shares to Carpio because it found no documentation establishing that the transfer had taken place.

He described Pikimong Pikimong as a shell company, citing records showing two shareholders, equity of P56,000 in 2024 and reported ass

content:
台北 —

在中国外交部星期一(10月12日)针对台湾邦交国的两名部长级官员祭出制裁后，台湾外交部谴责中国对其友邦官员的制裁，称其内容“荒谬至极，公然干涉他国主权及外交政策”，以及其“心态可议，手段卑劣”。分析人士指出，中国针对这些国家政治精英的“精准打击”，意图引发“寒蝉效应”。

中国外交部当地时间星期一上午发表声明，指责巴拉圭通信和技术部长比利亚特(Gustavo Villate)、伯利兹外交暨外贸部长弗朗西斯·丰塞卡(Francis Fonseca)为“反华政客”，顽固支持与台湾所谓的“邦交”关系，并对两人实施制裁措施，内容包括冻结两人在中国境内的财产、禁止境内组织及个人与其交易合作，以及不予签发签证、不准入境等。制裁同一天正式实施。

目前与台湾维持正式邦交的国家仅有12个，巴拉圭是南美洲唯一的一个。伯利兹位于中美洲。这些国家承认在台湾的中华民国为中国代表。自从2016年倾向台湾独立的民进党执政后，北京加大施压，台北先后失去10个邦交国。

中国外交部发言人毛宁在稍晚的例行记者会上表示，巴拉圭和伯利兹个别政客“甘当台湾当局倚外谋‘独’的棋子”，窜访台湾，并接待“台独”分裂分子窜访，严重干涉中国内政。

毛宁进一步向台湾邦交国喊话道：“不要反覆被‘台独’分裂势力操纵利用，同‘台独’势力绑在一起没有任何前途，只会错失发展机遇，孤立于国际社会。”

台湾外交部谴责中国外交部对其友邦官员的制裁。

台湾外交部星期一发表声明说，中方说法内容荒谬至极，公然干涉他国主权及外交政策，违反国际法原则，赤裸展现中国妄图以政治恫吓与跨国镇压手段，迫使他国屈从其政治企图，并破坏台湾与贝里斯及巴拉圭长久以来笃实紧密邦谊，心态可议、手段卑劣。

中国过往曾制裁支持台湾的外国政要，多数来自欧美政界，这次则是首次将矛头指向台湾邦交国的政要。

**比利亚特提过“人民自决”；丰塞卡曾称“台湾是国家”**

位于台北的政治大学外交系教授黄奎博分析，这两位被北京制裁的友邦官员，可能是在国际场合发言的时候明显踩到中共在台湾议题立场的红线。

黄奎博以书面方式向美国之音表示，比利亚特在祝贺中华民国国庆日的X贴文中，提到了“人民自决”(The self-determination of peoples)；丰塞卡则是在联合国大会上发言说“台湾是一个国家”(Taiwan is a nation)。他补充指出，很多中华民国的友邦在公开发言的时候，在比较有政治敏感度的部分，都会用中华民国或中华民国台湾。

丰塞卡曾两度访台，9月刚刚接待台湾外交部长林佳龙，两人签署外交人员训练与交流合作协定及联合公报。比利亚特5月访台签署AI算力中心合作备忘录，随后又接待台湾外交部政务次长陈明祺，讨论AI算力中心进度。

路透社报道指出，鉴于台湾邦交国的部长级官员通常不会造访中国，这些制裁在很大程度上只是象征性。

**中国欲挖角巴拉圭 伯利兹和台湾邦谊稳定**

巴拉圭不仅是台湾在南美洲唯一的邦交国，也是仅剩邦交国中面积最大者，两国建交69年，在两岸的外交争夺战上具有指标意义。

巴拉圭官方多次表示，愿意与中国发展经贸往来，但前提是“不涉及对台外交”。据中国官方统计，2025年中国同巴拉圭贸易总额为32.01亿美元，同比分别增长23.5%。

《纽约时报》今年4月报道称中国被指控贿赂巴拉圭高层政界人士，并以奢华的北京之旅来拉拢议员，另借由对巴拉圭农产品进口设下障碍，促使巴拉圭畜牧呼吁政府改变立场。

位于加勒比海地区的伯利兹曾于1987与中国建交，两年后即外交转向承认，在台湾外交圈评估中属于邦谊稳定的邦交国。

台湾上一个失去的邦交国是太平洋岛国瑙鲁。当时是2024年1月15日，民进党籍的赖清德当选总统的2天后。

虽然台湾在过去2年多的时间稳住了邦交国的阵脚，但是中国在外交上针对台湾的打压并没有松手迹象。

**北京打压台湾工具多 锁定第三国友台政界精英**

位于台北的政治大学国关中心研究员严震生指出，过去一段时间中国使出许多旨在打压台湾国际空间的新手段，比如赖清德原定访问友邦史瓦帝尼，临行前却因为总统专机无预警遭非洲三国取消飞航与降落许可，导致出访被迫暂缓。

严震生告诉美国之音：“就是它(中国)的工具箱里头东西很多，在外交上面在国际空间方面，所以这一些的动作，不晓得它什么时候会提出来，那不晓得在哪个地方，基本上就是不同的工具在进行外交打压。”

台湾国防安全研究院助理研究员杨一逵接受美国之音采访时表示，中国祭出的制裁手法不外乎是冻结在华资产、禁止入境中国，并不特别新颖。虽然目前不清楚两名被制裁的友邦官员或亲属是否和中国有往来，不过以反向来思考，会被制裁便代表他们确实是友台的盟友伙伴。

杨一逵认为，北京祭出制裁这一招，不太可能会牵动伯利兹和巴拉圭外交转向，反而只会把制裁对象推得更远，这一点北京恐怕也是心知肚明。

他强调，真正的危机在于可能引起的寒蝉效应，也就是说中国真正锁定的对象是台湾其他的邦交国官员，或是虽然和台湾无正式邦交但是仍保有密切实质关系的发展中国家，迫使他们与台湾保持距离，或是顺从北京的涉台立场。

杨一逵说：“它(中国)是针对这些国家的政治精英，针对你个人式的这种精准打击式的这种制裁方式，那其实它(中国)就是想要去影响，或者是去引起其他国家政治精英界的这种寒蝉效应。”

中国因与台湾的关系而制裁巴拉圭通讯部长和伯利兹外交部长。

_Chinese foreign ministry cites national sovereignty and Taiwan separatist activities as reasons behind the measures._

China has sanctioned Paraguay’s communications minister and Belize’s foreign minister over ties to Taiwan.

The Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs made the announcement on Monday, citing the safeguarding of China’s national sovereignty and opposition to Taiwan separatist activities as the reasons behind the measures, which went into effect the same day.

The measures against Paraguay’s Communications Minister Gustavo Villate and Belize’s Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca include the freezing of their assets in China and the denial of entry visas to Hong Kong and Macau.

The sanctions also prohibit Chinese organisations and individuals from engaging in transactions, cooperation or other activities with the ministers.

The Foreign Ministry said that “certain anti-China politicians” who are “driven by self-interest” have pushed their nations to maintain diplomatic relations with Taiwan.

Beijing said the ministers had “taken a series of egregious actions and statements”, which are “damaging China’s core interests”.

Paraguay and Belize are two of 12 countries that maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan.

China views Taiwan as its territory, a view the island’s government strongly rejects.

The measures come two days after Taiwan’s National Day celebration.

In a National Day speech outside the Presidential Office on Saturday, Taiwan President William Lai Ching-te said the island “cherishes peace” and will “not give up our freedom”.

China’s Taiwan Affairs Office condemned Lai’s speech, saying it “disregards facts, ⁠distorts the truth, misleads the public, and reveals ulterior motives”.

In January, Chinese President Xi Jinping [pledged to achieve](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1/1/chinas-xi-says-reunification-with-taiwan-unstoppable) the “reunification” of China and Taiwan, calling the goal “unstoppable”.

Paraguay’s Communications Minister Villate marked Taiwan’s National Day with a social media post, saying: “Paraguay reaffirms its relationship of friendship and cooperation, based on shared values and principles: the self-determination of peoples, human rights and democracy.”

The Belize embassy in Taiwan also posted a message on its Facebook celebrating the 37th anniversary of their diplomatic relations.

“Together, we look forward to a future of growth, opportunity, and lasting friendship,” the embassy wrote.

Last month, Taiwan’s Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung visited Belize. His ministry said the two sides had agreed to deepen ties.

Taiwan’s other allies in the Americas include Guatemala and Haiti. It also has formal diplomatic ties with three Caribbean islands.

The United States does not have ⁠formal diplomatic ties with Taiwan, but Washington is bound by law to provide the island with the means to ‌defend itself.

Earlier this month, the US [delivered](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2/us-delivers-f-16v-fighter-jets-to-taiwan-as-island-eyes-threat-from-china) two fighter jets to Taiwan as the island seeks to build its defence capabilities to deter a feared attack from [China](https://www.aljazeera.com/video/101-east/2026/8/15/is-china-seeking-to-copy-irans-strait-of-hormuz-blockade-around-taiwan).

content:
【大紀元2026年10月11日訊】（英文大紀元記者Petr Svab撰文／張紫珺編譯）中美人工智能（artificial intelligence，簡稱AI）正在展開激烈的競賽。專家表示，由於對人工智能的掌控可能決定世界經濟和軍事的領導權，這場競賽的走向對中美兩國的未來都至關重要。

為了評估中美人工智能競爭的現狀，《大紀元時報》採訪了國防和網絡安全領域的10位專家。大多數專家一致認為，美國在前沿人工智能模型、計算能力（簡稱「算力」/compute）規模以及微芯片質量等方面都保持領先地位。

然而，中國已經證明能夠以遠低於西方頂級競爭對手的成本和計算量，高效地開發出AI模型，效果足以匹敵美國模型。這種高效性部分得益於「蒸餾」（distillation）技術，使用該技術，中國的AI模型能夠模仿美國模型的輸出結果。此外，中國龐大的製造業能力也令其在快速部署和疊代AI產品方面具有優勢。

人工智能是中共黨魁習近平與美國總統唐納德·川普（特朗普）今年9月華盛頓會談的核心議題之一。華盛頓尋求與中國開展雙邊合作，以防止最強大的人工智能模型被恐怖分子和犯罪集團利用。然而，據《大紀元時報》此前援引內部消息人士的判斷稱，北京不太可能做出實質性承諾，因為中共懷疑美國提出這一安全舉措的實質目的，是要評估中國的技術能力和漏洞。

現在，北京將人工智能視為與美國抗衡甚至超越美國的戰略工具。專家警告說，這種轉變將從根本上改變全球秩序。

多年來，習近平一直將人工智能發展視為國家優先事項而投入大量的國家資源，強制要求在各個經濟領域實施人工智能，並開始建設必要的基礎設施，包括數據中心和發電廠等。

專家表示，中共也在加速部署人工智能武器和其它軍事能力。而在幕後，它正在將人工智能用作黑客攻擊和信息戰行動的祕密網絡武器。

一些專家認為，中國日益明顯的計劃經濟特徵是一種優勢，因為自上而下的官方指令可以立即掃清監管障礙；而相比之下，美國的監管障礙現象卻相當嚴重。

不過一些專家指出，中共的國有經濟模式也存在弊端，因為它會限制創新，而且常常導致資源浪費。

[![Image 1: 2026年9月15日，在北京舉行的第十四屆中國國際國防電子展覽會上，人們正在觀看為軍警用途製造的機器狗。(Adek Berry/AFP via Getty Images)](https://www.theepochtimes.com/_next/image?url=https://img.theepochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/06/id6100179-GettyImages-2294913984-ed.jpg&w=3840&q=75)](https://www.theepochtimes.com/_next/image?url=https://img.theepochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/06/id6100179-GettyImages-2294913984-ed.jpg&w=3840&q=75)

2026年9月15日，在北京舉行的第十四屆中國國際國防電子展覽會上，人們正在觀看為軍警用途製造的機器狗。(Adek Berry/AFP via Getty Images)

華盛頓方面非常清楚人工智能領先地位對經濟和安全的影響，美國財政部長斯科特·貝森特（Scott Bessent）在最近接受布萊巴特新聞網（Breitbart，總部位於加州洛杉磯）採訪時也強調了這一點。「如果中國在這方面勝出，那麼『後天』將不復存在。」他說道。

（譯註：「後天」的說法來自於2004年上映的美國科幻災難片《後天》（The Day After Tomorrow，香港、新加坡譯《明日之後》）。該片由羅蘭·艾默瑞奇執導，描述全球寒冷化後造成新的冰河時期給人類帶來的災難。）

大多數專家都認為，情況或許沒有世界末日那麼嚴重，但他們也絕對不會輕視。

「如果我們都能認同，目前世界上最先進的能力是人工智能的能力，並且這種能力可以用來實現經濟和政治目標，那麼我們就必須充分利用這種能力。」科技軟件公司Splunk（總部位於加州舊金山）和數據分析公司Databricks（總部位於加州舊金山）的前安全研究負責人、人工智能網絡安全平台Crogl（總部位於新墨西哥州）的聯合創辦人蒙齊·梅爾扎（Monzy Merza）說道。

在國家安全領域，這種緊迫性可能更為突出。

「人工智能是近未來幾十年乃至未來幾十年內最重要的武器系統。」總部位於弗吉尼亞州的人工智能情報和風險分析公司Babel Street的美國政府領域高級副總裁麥克丹尼爾·威克（McDaniel Wicker）表示。

這位前美國空軍情報官員告訴《大紀元時報》：「我們現在正處於一個將人工智能融入國家安全的時期，這與原子能時代極為相似——就像二戰之後擁有了原子彈一樣。」

「如果一方遠遠領先於另一方，那麼國家實力上的失衡就會顯而易見；如果美國遠遠落後於中國，那麼中國就會利用其優勢，更快地做出更多決策，更快地取得更多進展。」

[![Image 2: 圖為美國財政部長斯科特·貝森特，攝於2026年9月20日。(Kena Betancur/AFP via Getty Images)](https://www.theepochtimes.com/_next/image?url=https://img.theepochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/06/id6100180-GettyImages-2295683511-ed.jpg&w=3840&q=75)](https://www.theepochtimes.com/_next/image?url=https://img.theepochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/06/id6100180-GettyImages-2295683511-ed.jpg&w=3840&q=75)

圖為美國財政部長斯科特·貝森特，攝於2026年9月20日。(Kena Betancur/AFP via Getty Images)

## 美中兩國究竟誰贏？

「就誰是這場競賽的贏家而言，我認為我們顯然是贏家。」總部位於華盛頓特區的智庫美國優先政策研究所（America First Policy Institute，簡稱AFPI）人工智能和新興技術高級顧問喬爾·泰耶（Joel Thayer）說道。

「從任何可以想像的指標來看，美國都占據了明顯的優勢。」他向《大紀元時報》表示。

然而，其他專家並不認為局勢已經如此明朗。

「如果可以這麼說的話，美國的AI生態系統更加強大。」人工智能治理和網絡安全諮詢公司Digital 520的首席執行官兼首席顧問諾亞·肯尼（Noah Kenney）說道。

「美國擁有先進的芯片設計技術。我們擁有更完善的雲基礎設施和數據中心，還有大多數重要的尖端機型。」

他補充說，中國也有一些自己的優勢。

「中國在供應鏈零部件方面遠遠領先於我們。」他告訴《大紀元時報》。

「實際上，我們在美國研發了很多先進的硬件，但如果沒有中國提供的供應鏈，就沒有辦法大規模生產。」

中國的製造業能力對於人工智能設備的快速推廣應用尤為有利。中國已經在無人機市場占據主導地位，同時也在自動化和機器人領域投入巨資。

[![Image 3: 2026年3月20日，北京人形機器人創新中心，一名工程師正在測試人形機器人。中國正投入數百億美元發展人形機器人產業。（Kevin Frayer/Getty Images）](https://www.theepochtimes.com/_next/image?url=https://img.theepochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/06/id6100173-GettyImages-2267517613-ed.jpg&w=3840&q=75)](https://www.theepochtimes.com/_next/image?url=https://img.theepochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/06/id6100173-GettyImages-2267517613-ed.jpg&w=3840&q=75)

2026年3月20日，北京人形機器人創新中心，一名工程師正在測試人形機器人。中國正投入數百億美元發展人形機器人產業。（Kevin Frayer/Getty Images）

「即使擁有地球上最先進的技術，但是如果沒有能力推廣應用，那麼這些技術的用途將會受到極大的限制。」總部位於華盛頓特區的智庫史汀生中心（Stimson Center）的人工智能和合規專家大衛·阿克曼（David Ackerman）說道。

他表示，在錯綜複雜的監管環境之下，川普政府為將關鍵製造業遷回國內所做的努力遲遲未能見效。

「至少在公開層面上，人們對美國提升製造業能力和加強關鍵基礎設施給予了極大的關注。然而，遺憾的是，和這些項目資金相關的政策和程序實際上並沒有發生太大變化。」他向《大紀元時報》解釋道。

「你不可能讓一艘戰艦90度轉彎。……無論在人工智能領域還是在能源領域，我們還沒有看到保持競爭力所需的加速發展。」

阿克曼表示，SpaceX創辦人埃隆·馬斯克（Elon Musk）提議在太空建造數據中心，可能僅僅是因為他對政府監管的繁文縟節的感到沮喪。

「像埃隆·馬斯克這樣的人更希望監管制度能夠作出調整，從而更有利於加快發展的速度。」

## 強力反彈

「計算能力的增長不可能無限持續；它與能源密不可分。因此，挑戰在於各國如何提高能源效率。」台灣人工智能實驗室（Taiwan AI Labs）創始人杜奕瑾（Ethan Tu）表示。

「我們可能會遇到因為遇到能源瓶頸而導致發展停滯的情況。」他向《大紀元時報》解釋道。「雖然業界此前已經將芯片視為主要制約因素，促使存儲器和芯片的產量大幅增長，但是能源上的限制很可能成為下一個主要障礙。」

據總部位於特拉華州的商業能源採購平台BOX Energy Solutions的能源戰略主管斯科特·埃貝林（Scott Ebeling）稱，美國科技巨頭試圖快速建設用於人工智能的巨型數據中心，目前已經遇到了能源瓶頸。

他在大紀元視頻（Epoch TV）節目「市場內幕」（Market Insider）中透露，一個「超大規模」（hyperscaler）數據中心可能消耗一吉瓦的電力，這個電量足以供大約100萬戶家庭使用。儘管能源基礎設施的建設正在加速，但是電網仍然無法以科技公司計劃的速度來應對新的數據中心的需求。

「我不認為事情會像這些預測所說的發生得那麼快。」他說道。他以變壓器為例加以解釋。變壓器可以將高壓輸電電壓降至消費者可以使用的較低電壓。

「2020年的時候，變壓器通常14週就能恢復運行。現在，卻要兩年時間了。」他說道。

與此同時，中國已經投入大量資源發展國內電力生產——涵蓋煤炭、水力、風能和太陽能發電——為其工業和科技領域提供了充足而且低成本的電力供應。

據埃貝林稱，中國大型數據中心支付的電費大約只有美國同類數據中心的一半。

他指出，北京自上而下的指揮體系是中國電網快速擴張的關鍵因素。

「如果中國政府想修建一條輸電線路，而某個社區剛好位於輸電線路上，他們會直接將那片社區夷為平地。」他說道。

## 中國能贏嗎？

專家們一致認為，中國不太可能在人工智能競賽中取得絕對勝利。

「他們的計算能力不足以真正與我們的前沿模型競爭。」泰耶說道。

相反，中國專注於開放權重模型，這類模型的數值參數向公眾發布，用戶可以下載並進行調整。

「這之所以重要，主要是因為開放權重模型需要的基礎設施要少得多，因此可以快速部署投入實際應用。」他說道。

多位專家指出，在各項性能基準測試中，中國模型的表現已接近美國模型。

「中國已經基本消除了模型之間的基準差距，而且他們在開發超高效模型方面尤其強大。」肯尼說道。

但是對於這些測試結果，似乎存在一些重大的保留意見。

9月8日，美國聯邦調查局（FBI）、美國國家安全局（National Security Agency，簡稱NSA）和美國網絡安全與基礎設施安全局（Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency，簡稱CISA）聯合發布公告稱，六家中國人工智能公司至少從2024年底開始，就對美國前沿模型進行了「大規模的、具有侵略性的、惡意的、有針對性的蒸餾活動」。

蒸餾（distillation）是指對一個人工智能模型進行大量查詢，然後利用其輸出結果訓練一個新的人工智能模型。這樣，新模型就能夠以更少的訓練和計算量，模仿出原模型的回答。

目前尚不清楚這種方法在多大程度上促進了中國人工智能模型的發展。一些專家認為，這些中國模型表現卓越，主要是藉助來蒸餾技術而；另一些專家則認為，這種效率和中國更廣泛的創新能力有關。

「對於人工智能基準測試，我們必須謹慎判斷。」杜奕瑾說道。「因為這些性能是在固定的測試框架內取得的。」

他指出，中國的人工智能模型似乎是經過專門訓練，以超越基準測試。

「雖然中國模型在已知標準答案的任務上表現非常出色，但它們在預期測試（有時被稱為『體驗式』或『真實世界感覺』測試）中往往表現不佳。」他說道。

「這主要是因為這些模型過分強調考試式的表現，而當應用於實際行業用例中各種不同的真實場景時，可能會導致結果不盡如人意。」

以這種方式開發的模型會存在固有的局限性。

「根本問題在於，中國很大程度上是效仿美國的系統進行開發；因此，雖然中國模型的表現可以接近美國模型，但很難真正超越它們。」杜奕瑾說道。

對此泰耶舉了一個例子作類比。

「可以把我們想像成一艘快艇，而他們就像跟在我們後面玩滑水一樣。他們的速度基本上取決於我們的速度，如果我們減速，他們也會減速。」他說道。

中國早就已經意識到這個問題，正在試圖快速提升計算能力，減少對蒸餾技術的依賴。但泰耶認為，這樣做會背離中國的核心戰略。

「如果他們通過創新擺脫困境，那情況就完全不同了。但我認為，中國人工智能建模的根本目的，是確保他們的投入不會像美國那麼多。」他說道。

「他們想用人類所能達到的最低成本來實現建模的目標……但我實在看不出，這怎麼能算得上是一種的制勝策略。」

即使中國沒有最好的模型，也可能通過更低的價格來搶占市場份額。一些專家表示，這似乎是它的策略。

前美國國家安全局（NSA）黑客、現任網絡安全諮詢公司應用網絡安全研究所（Institute for Applied Network Security）教師傑克·威廉姆斯（Jake Williams）指出，中國開發的小規模開源模型可以免費下載，因此很難實現商業化。

但商業化可能並非中共的最終目的。相反，中共似乎試圖將儘可能多的用戶鎖定在其生態系統之中。

杜奕瑾表示，中國的「目標是讓這些模型得到廣泛應用，從而最終令它們成為標準」。

梅爾扎表示，作為回應，元宇宙（Meta）和谷歌（Google）等美國公司也發布了免費的開放權重模型。

「對他們來說，這是一場足跡之戰。」他向《大紀元時報》描述道。

然而，在建立市場主導地位方面，中國面臨著一個主要的障礙：信任。

「人工智能是一個關鍵的信息平台——類似於5G基礎設施——因此，是否使用它以及它是否值得信賴，這是至關重要的問題。」杜奕瑾說道。

「雖然中國目前的模式很容易複製，而且通常允許初期免費試用，但是建立真正的信任仍然是一個巨大的挑戰。」

梅爾扎也表達了同樣的看法。

他說，他的歐洲客戶對美國的AI模型「多少有點不信任」，但他補充說，「我沒有聽說有人說他要轉而使用中國的模型，因為對中國模型的不信任程度甚至更高。」

他說，這不僅僅是將敏感信息交給人工智能平台的問題。

「這固然是一個需要考慮的方面，但是（主要的擔憂）在於：這個模型會不會欺騙我，或者給我不完整或者錯誤的答案，或者消耗過多資源而無法切中要點？因為它是一個外國開發的模型，而削弱美國的能力符合那個外國實體的利益。」梅爾扎說道。

此外，由於美國目前處於領先地位，因此它擁有設定議程的能力。

「從治理、安全和隱私方面來看，現在美國在很大程度上掌控著當前的局勢——什麼是可以接受的，什麼是不可以接受的——他們可以認定：中國開發的人工智能缺乏防護措施，或者缺乏適當的安全保障。」肯尼說道。

## 如果中國贏了呢？

大多數專家認為，中國的人工智能能力在短期內不太可能超越美國。但有一種可能性可能會使判斷變得複雜：中國可能擁有超出其公開承認範圍的祕密人工智能能力。

「他們可能在隱瞞這一切。」泰耶說道。「中國的運作完全不透明，所以很難看清他們的底細，了解他們在做什麼。」

所有專家都在一定程度上預見到中國在人工智能領域的取得領先會對美國產生怎樣的影響。這將帶來經濟和國家安全方面的後果，而且這些後果大部分是相互交織。

「人工智能已經滲透到製造業、物流業、金融業、醫療保健業、軟件業、機器人業和科學研究等各個方面。」杜奕瑾說道。「因此，人工智能的應用越廣泛、能力越強大，就能在這些不同領域建立更大的領先優勢。」

他指出了「數字殖民主義」（digital colonialism）的預測。

「如果較弱的國家無法建立自己值得信賴的平台，而必須依靠較強國家的平台才能生存，那麼平台所有者必然會獲得巨大的權力。」杜奕瑾說道。

「這一點在中美兩國爭奪人工智能霸權的競爭中尤為明顯，雙方都在爭奪制定議程和主導該領域的權力。」

## 網絡戰

人工智能帶來的直接安全威脅主要分為兩類：網絡戰（cyber warfare）和軍事應用（military application）。

「即使在今天，人工智能在國家安全領域已經發揮著巨大的作用，如果中國能夠超越美國，那麼無論在區域層面和全球範圍內，你會看到他們越來越多地利用這個優勢。」威克爾說道。

中共政權長期以來一直是網絡安全威脅，運營著一支由國家支持的龐大黑客網絡。其行動遠遠超出了常規的情報收集範疇。
