title: 國慶大會總統府前登場 賴總統：打造「山巔之城」
summary: 【大紀元2026年10月12日訊】（大紀元記者倪爾森／安平雅台灣台北報導）中華民國中樞暨各界慶祝115年國慶大會於10月10日上午在總統府前廣場盛大展開，史瓦帝尼王國國王恩史瓦帝三世與王妃與各國使節出席觀禮。 今年全球有近4,200名僑胞專程返國出席國慶活動，其中2,000名僑胞親臨府前觀禮。「2026海外華文媒體人士訪問團」深入現場，深刻感受台灣在科技實力、民主制度與社會韌性上的蓬勃發展。 ## **序幕暖場****巨幅國旗震撼進場** 大會首先由娜麓灣樂舞劇團及屏東原鄉部
content:
【大紀元2026年10月12日訊】（大紀元記者倪爾森／安平雅台灣台北報導）中華民國中樞暨各界慶祝115年國慶大會於10月10日上午在總統府前廣場盛大展開，史瓦帝尼王國國王恩史瓦帝三世與王妃與各國使節出席觀禮。

今年全球有近4,200名僑胞專程返國出席國慶活動，其中2,000名僑胞親臨府前觀禮。「2026海外華文媒體人士訪問團」深入現場，深刻感受台灣在科技實力、民主制度與社會韌性上的蓬勃發展。

## **序幕暖場****巨幅國旗震撼進場**

大會首先由娜麓灣樂舞劇團及屏東原鄉部落青年會《Kinaqadavang 生日快樂》帶來充滿文化生命力的樂舞演出，接著國防部聯合樂隊暨三軍儀隊以《鼓號齊鳴慶雙十 攜手齊心衛家邦》操演展現精實陣容，曉明女中與莊敬高職的《T-CORE臺灣之心》、《星圖璀璨 光耀雙十》與《八音行前路 臺灣創新途》接續帶來精彩表演。

[![Image 1](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868182-b699e1a0bf4440b4ac48feb7-600x337.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868182-b699e1a0bf4440b4ac48feb7.jpg)

10月10日雙十國慶大會，陸軍航空特戰指揮部CH-47直升機吊掛巨幅國旗凌空飛過府前。（倪爾森／大紀元）

金門縣合唱團與金門兒童合唱團領唱國歌之際，陸軍航空特戰指揮部CH-47直升機吊掛巨幅國旗凌空飛過府前，將全場歡慶氣氛推向高潮。

## **賴總統：以務實治理****築起「山巔之城」**

今年國慶大會主題「TAIWAN．TOGETHER AS ONE」，賴總統以「臺灣 山巔之城，地上的鹽，世上的光」為題發表演說。

賴總統表示，山巔之城是建造在護國群山之上的民主治理成果，「不能只有耀眼的天際線，更要有穩固的地基」，而臺灣的地基就是人民的生活。

他說，今年上半年經濟成長率達14.15%，全年有望突破11%，創39年新高。人均GDP預估達45,332美元，臺股也衝上4萬9千點。

在瑞士洛桑管理學院（IMD）的世界競爭力排名中，臺灣升至全球第四，創歷來最佳成績。

民生政策方面，賴總統宣布規劃自明年起推動0至18歲成長津貼，每名孩子每月5,000元，並提到長照3.0、青安3.0與百萬租屋家庭支持計畫。

國防與外交方面，他強調將持續推動國防改革與全社會防衛韌性，並以「Taiwan Can Help」與國際夥伴分享能力、承擔責任。

賴總統最後呼籲國人團結，為臺灣下一個30年打下更堅實的基礎。

[![Image 2](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868181-5de864c9297b192978eaa9ce-600x338.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868181-5de864c9297b192978eaa9ce.jpg)

10月10日雙十國慶大會，看台上的貴賓與僑胞揮舞國旗歡慶國家生日。（倪爾森／大紀元）

## **大會主席韓國瑜致詞：許下安全、有錢與民主三願望**

國慶籌備委員會主任委員、立法院長韓國瑜致詞時特別歡迎遠道而來的僑胞，並提出三個國慶願望：「臺灣安全」、「人民有錢」與「民主萬歲」。

韓院長呼籲各黨派化解國家認同上的分歧，也提醒政府不能只讓高科技業獲益，應兼顧傳統產業與基層民眾。

談到民主時，他提到立法與行政兩院的歧見，並表示不能讓國際社會對臺灣民主產生質疑，甚至誤認臺灣是「假民主、真獨裁」，期盼朝野以溝通與妥協尋求共識。

[![Image 3](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868180-5574b844ba6370dee4209157-600x338.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868180-5574b844ba6370dee4209157.jpg)

10月10日雙十國慶大會，客家《八音行前路 臺灣創新途》表演。（倪爾森／大紀元）

## **僑胞代表熊強生致詞：見證時代躍升****以民主自信連結世界**

代表全球僑胞致詞的大洋洲僑領、甫卸任世界臺灣商會聯合總會第32屆總會長的熊強生，以自身從核工專業轉戰IT產業、赴澳洲創業的深刻歷程，向世界傳遞海內外同胞的驕傲與自信。

[![Image 4](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868179-8e7cf8197c5d1a2bbe0f49f8-600x425.png)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868179-8e7cf8197c5d1a2bbe0f49f8.png)

115年國慶僑胞致詞代表熊強生（右）與僑務委員會代理委員長李姸慧合影（左）。（僑委會檔案圖片）

身為長期投身科技產業的僑胞，熊強生指出，在AI與半導體浪潮推升下，台灣競爭力名列瑞士IMD全球第4，經濟成長勢頭強勁。

他感性談到，「臺灣精神」不只是故鄉眷戀，更是血液中「一枝草，一點露」的堅韌與「一卡皮箱走天下」的移民勇氣。他強調，僑胞是台灣連結世界的重要橋樑，回顧去年花蓮馬太鞍溪遭遇天災，全球臺商在第一時間全力馳援災區；今年3月在雪梨召開的世總會議上，全球臺商亦共同發表聲明，全力支持台灣加入CPTPP。

熊強生進一步提到，近年全球上百個海外急難救助協會積極配合政府推動「全社會防衛韌性」，在當地舉辦防災講座與急救訓練，逐步架構起海外預警與應變網絡，成為國家在海外的重要韌性夥伴。

他堅定呼籲，民主賦予大家表達不同意見的權利，但在國家主權與民主自由面前，海內外國人唯有團結一致，才能讓台灣走得更長、更遠。

## **主題表演 從災害救援到雷虎衝場**

典禮後半段的主題表演共12項，包括《榮耀在憲》、空中分列式、《突破極限 國際揚威》、《榮耀英雄》，以及模擬災害應變救援與直升機吊掛。

日本台灣友好議員聯盟與台日交流聯誼會也組隊參加祝賀遊行。

[![Image 5](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868178-334626dc681a2fbe3ca7130a-600x338.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868178-334626dc681a2fbe3ca7130a.jpg)

10月10日雙十國慶大會，海巡署《韌性國安 巡守海防》車隊展示。（倪爾森／大紀元）

節目另有《韌性科技 航太先鋒》、《韌性國安 巡守海防》、《韌性防災 守護生命》與《忠誠勇毅 士在必行》，之後是梯隊遊行，最後由空軍雷虎小組衝場壓軸。

## **僑委會代理委員長李妍慧：僑胞是國力的延伸**

僑務委員會代理委員長李妍慧歡迎全球各地的僑胞回來台灣，參加115年的國慶慶活動！

她對記者表示：「台灣這幾年經濟持續成長，民主成熟發展，各項進步指標持續上升，一步步往世界領先國家邁進。 而僑胞是台灣國力的延伸，也是讓世界看見台灣的重要力量。歡迎各位僑胞回家，你們是台灣之光！ 感謝你們支持台灣！一起為台灣加油！」

## **僑界觀禮心得：看見韌性的臺灣**

[![Image 6](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868177-4c9e5371cf14be888e3f9ddb-600x337.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868177-4c9e5371cf14be888e3f9ddb.jpg)

10月10日雙十國慶大會，昆士蘭僑務委員陳秋燕接受採訪。（倪爾森／大紀元）

澳洲昆士蘭僑務委員陳秋燕表示，昆士蘭僑界組成20多人的慶賀團返國，親身看到「韌性的臺灣」與民主的永續，也看到經濟進步，股市接近5萬點。

她同時參加海外臺僑政策說明會，並引述賴總統談話，說明政府推動的兒少成長津貼，其中部分款項將為孩子預存，滿18歲可領出，可視為國家送給青年的「第一桶金」。

陳委員說：「身為臺灣人感到非常榮耀。」

[![Image 7](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868176-b4094a313bfc05f744a8ad61-450x488.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868176-b4094a313bfc05f744a8ad61.jpg)

10月10日雙十國慶大會，行政院政務顧問陳文龍接受採訪。（陳文龍顧問提供）

行政院政務顧問陳文龍首先祝福國家繁榮昌盛、人民平安幸福。

他接著說：「看到慶典的表演隊伍，隊員們面帶微笑邁力的演出和觀禮熱情民眾拍手互動，一起為台灣生，好溫暖、好歡樂。看到這一幕著實讓我感動。然而在國慶大會韓國瑜主席致詞時，「假民主、真獨裁」失態的言詞，在典禮上做政治批叛鬥爭，把國家慶典當成個人的政治秀場。他應該知道大會現場有祝賀的使節團，有駐台的大使代表，慶典活動全球直播。－個大會的主人這種言論實在很難看，讓我錯愕、失望、不滿。這是我參加今年國慶大會的感慨。」

[![Image 8](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868175-9b1e00f4b03a1e32bd8b98cd-600x461.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868175-9b1e00f4b03a1e32bd8b98cd.jpg)

昆士蘭回台參加雙十國慶的部分僑胞合影。（琳達／大紀元）

## **海內外心繫台灣****民主共識凝聚力量**

透過此次國慶大會的親身採訪，「2026海外華文媒體人士訪問團」深刻感受到台灣在面對國際地緣變局時，所展現出的強大經濟實力、堅定防衛決心與深厚多元的民間活力。

儘管島內政壇對於治理理念與政治運作仍有交鋒與不同觀點，但全球僑界心繫故土的情誼始終如一，這份對民主、自由與家園的共同認同，依然是台灣走向世界最無可取代的底氣。

[![Image 9](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868190-Picture1-600x338.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14868190-Picture1.jpg)

「2026海外華文媒體人士訪問團」團員合影。（媒體訪問團提供）

title: 中欧就混动汽车贸易达成谅解，避免经贸摩擦升级
source: 美国已不是世界老大 - 纽约时报中文网
summary: 欧盟与中国在北京举行的高级别[会谈](https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20261008/china-europe-trade-issues/)于周五结束，双方出人意料地达成一项协议，有望避免一场迫在眉睫的贸易战。 这项协议最引人注目的内容涉及中国出口的混动汽车。双方均表示，已就这一问题达成谅解。混动汽车一直是中欧贸易关系中最具争议的问题之一。 欧盟委员会贸易和经济安全委员马罗什·谢夫乔维奇表示，根据双方达成的谅解，中国可能在未来四年内将出口欧盟
content:
欧盟与中国在北京举行的高级别[会谈](https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20261008/china-europe-trade-issues/)于周五结束，双方出人意料地达成一项协议，有望避免一场迫在眉睫的贸易战。

这项协议最引人注目的内容涉及中国出口的混动汽车。双方均表示，已就这一问题达成谅解。混动汽车一直是中欧贸易关系中最具争议的问题之一。

欧盟委员会贸易和经济安全委员马罗什·谢夫乔维奇表示，根据双方达成的谅解，中国可能在未来四年内将出口欧盟的混动汽车数量削减一半。双方均未提及对这类汽车征收关税的问题，中国一直坚决反对加征关税。

中国商务部在另一份声明中说，双方“以符合世贸组织规则的方式就混动汽车贸易达成谅解”。遵守世贸组织规则意味着欧洲很难迅速加征关税。此外，即使征收关税，也难以确定还会有多少汽车继续从中国运来，但谢夫乔维奇表示，这项谅解将实现具体的进口汽车数量削减目标。

谢夫乔维奇所描述的妥协方案似乎既满足了欧盟立即限制中国汽车进口数量的要求，也回应了中国希望通过某种安排缓解中国车企在欧洲市场激烈竞争的需求。这种竞争往往十分惨烈，也是造成中国汽车制造商巨额亏损的原因之一。

这项关于混动汽车的协议似乎与双方2013年达成的太阳能电池板协议极为相似。当时，中国同意减少每年向欧洲出口的太阳能电池板数量，欧洲则同意放弃此前对这些产品加征关税的计划。这使中国太阳能电池板制造商得以大幅提高在欧洲市场的售价，凭借受到限制的供应量获得丰厚利润，扭转了此前的亏损局面。

中国制造商随后将这些利润投入更多研发及新工厂的建设，如今几乎生产了全球所有的太阳能电池板。

中国出口欧洲的插电式混合动力汽车迅速扩大了在当地的市场份额，也是大众汽车最近计划在本十年结束前[再裁员5万人](https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20260904/volkswagen-job-cuts/)、使其裁员总人数达到10万人的原因之一。

两年前，欧盟在通常对进口汽车征收的10%关税基础上又对中国电动汽车征收7.8%至35.3%的关税。但欧盟当时没有对插电式混合动力汽车加征额外关税。

比亚迪电动车，2023年摄于慕尼黑。Felix Schmitt for The New York Times

短短三年间，中国插电式混合动力汽车出口从每月不足1万辆飙升至每月近20万辆，其中许多销往欧洲。

中国一直强烈反对欧盟为限制中国电动汽车进口数量而对其加征的额外关税。北京方面主张应该取消这些关税，改为对汽车出口数量设定限制。

这样一来，中国电动汽车制造商就能够提高售价，改善盈利能力。这也正是目前逐渐成形的混动汽车安排所采用的思路。

周五，当被问及目前的混动汽车协议是否与类似当年的太阳能电池板协议时，谢夫乔维奇说情况不同，而且欧洲需要立即采取行动应对混动汽车问题。他说：“公众舆论和领导人都确实期待我们迅速采取行动。”

中国认为，单方面加征关税违反世界贸易组织的贸易规则，而北京和欧盟都仍然致力于维护这些规则。相比之下，特朗普政府一再采取违背世贸组织规则的单边行动。特朗普总统的贸易顾问声称，中国实行的是政府主导的经济体制，并不遵循世贸组织赖以创立的自由市场原则。

为促使欧盟与北京达成妥协，中国商务部提出了几项优惠措施。谢夫乔维奇表示，中国已同意降低汽车零部件、橄榄油和鞋类等欧洲商品的进口关税，这些商品的年贸易额接近40亿欧元。

他说，这将使欧洲出口商每年向中国出口商品时节省约1.25亿欧元的关税。

中国与欧盟发表的联合声明则没有如此具体，只是表示，“双方将继续探讨在世贸组织规则框架下，降低部分商品关税的可能性。”

一些问题仍未解决，尤其是欧盟是否会放弃要求电动汽车和风力涡轮机等技术产品的关键部件必须在欧洲制造的计划，以及欧盟是否仍将对风力涡轮机征收反补贴关税。谢夫乔维奇说，双方计划于明年初举行更多会谈。

谢夫乔维奇定于周六返回布鲁塞尔，并将在下周欧洲各国领导人举行会议之前，向有关官员通报此次会谈的情况。

欧洲领导人下周会议的首要议题是如何应对该地区经济竞争力不断减弱的问题，而对华贸易是其中的核心议题。欧洲领导人一直警告说，随着来自中国的制成品[进口激增](https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20261008/china-europe-trade-manufacturing/)，欧洲的工业基础正面临被掏空的危险。

时间站在中国一边。每过去一个月，中国就能获得超过300亿美元的贸易顺差，并进一步削弱中国制造商的欧洲竞争对手。

中国商务部在声明中说，中国将继续批准对欧洲出口[稀土](https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20260923/china-rare-earth-summit/)和稀土磁体。自2025年4月以来，中国一直限制这两类产品的出口，并威胁如果欧洲对中国出口采取行动，将实施进一步限制。

中国商务部还表示，欧盟已同意协助解决围绕其出口管制措施的争端。

在前总统拜登以及现任总统特朗普的压力下，欧洲企业一直避免向中国出售最先进的半导体制造设备，因为这些设备生产的芯片可能被用于军事目的。北京官员认为，欧洲若想较快缩小对华贸易逆差，一个办法就是不顾美国反对，向中国出售最先进的设备。

欧洲还一直在筹备立法，要求电动汽车或风力涡轮机等产品的重要零部件必须在欧洲制造。中国过去曾对汽车和风力涡轮机实施类似要求，但在欧洲和其他贸易伙伴多年抱怨后取消了这些规定。北京如今主张，欧洲不应出台这样的规定，因为这将迫使中国企业在欧洲投资建厂，而无法继续从生产成本通常更低的中国本土工厂向欧洲出口。

中国商务部的声明称，中欧双方“同意探讨投资合作，促进彼此经济发展，并讨论开展面向未来的合作”。

title: Global risks cloud remittance outlook
summary: **REMITTANCES —**a key pillar of the Philippine economy — will likely post slower growth as global uncertainties weigh on overseas employment and income prospects, a Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) official said. “Remittances are still ex
content:
**REMITTANCES —**a key pillar of the Philippine economy — will likely post slower growth as global uncertainties weigh on overseas employment and income prospects, a Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) official said.

“Remittances are still expected to grow in the next two to three years, albeit at a slower pace amid global uncertainties,” BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Abenoja told The Manila Times.

“The main risks to remittance growth are weaker labor demand in host economies and geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Middle East,” he added.

*   [No collection of taxes in BIR’s ‘Oplan Kandado’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/business/top-business/no-collection-of-taxes-in-birs-oplan-kandado/2441215)

The outlook carries significant implications for the Philippines, where remittances are equivalent to around eight percent of gross domestic product (GDP), helping sustain household spending and providing a steady source of foreign financing.

Data from the BSP’s third-quarter 2026 Consumer Expectations Survey showed that food and other household expenses were the most common uses of remittances, with 98 percent of remittance-receiving households reporting that they used the money for these needs.

Education and healthcare were also among the main uses.

Abenoja said the importance of these inflows extended beyond immediate consumption.

“Remittances not only help households meet their day-to-day needs but also contribute to investments in human capital and long-term financial well-being,” he said.

*   ![Image 1: Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254608.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/legarda-may-rejoin-senate-majority-pangilinan/2443223)

Among the principal risks to remittance growth are reduced demand in host countries and geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Middle East.

“Slower economic growth in host countries, tighter immigration policies, and workforce localization initiatives may reduce hiring opportunities for overseas Filipinos and limit wage growth,” Abenoja said.

“These developments could also raise the need for evacuation, repatriation, and reintegration support for affected workers,” he added.

Remittance growth has slowed since the war in the Middle East broke out in March. While July saw a rebound, the rate remains below the 3.0 percent and above seen prior to the conflict.

*   ![Image 2: Are Marcos’ minions in Congress plotting to amend the Constitution?](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1255043.png?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Are Marcos’ minions in Congress plotting to amend the Constitution?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/opinion/columns/are-marcos-minions-in-congress-plotting-to-amend-the-constitution/2443331)

Based on latest BSP data, overall remittances grew by 2.0 percent to $3.6 billion in July, with cash remittances in particular up by 1.9 percent to $3.37 billion.

Year to date, personal remittances expanded 2.3 percent to $22..73 billion, with cash remittances also 2.3 percent higher at $20.39 billion.

The central bank expects remittances to grow by 2.7 percent and reach $36.6 billion this year.

Abenoja said the Middle East was of particular concern “given its importance as a destination for overseas Filipinos.”

*   ![Image 3: Quo haec patria tendit?](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1255079.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Quo haec patria tendit?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/opinion/columns/quo-haec-patria-tendit/2443321)

“While remittances have historically shown resilience and a countercyclical nature, the current contraction in deployment highlights vulnerability to geopolitical shocks, which could weigh on remittance flows,” he added.

Beyond geopolitical tensions and slower growth in host economies, Abenoja said technological changes could also reshape overseas employment over the medium term.

“Over the medium term, advances in artificial intelligence and automation could also change the nature of work,” he said, “especially in occupations involving routine tasks while increasing demand for higher-level technical skills.”

This presents a longer-term challenge for Filipino workers and the remittance-dependent households they support.

“Overall growth is likely to be modest, hinging on diversification of migrant corridors and adaptation to shifting global labor needs,” Abenoja said.

As labor markets evolve, the BSP official said the types of skills sought by overseas employers could change, affecting employment opportunities and the potential for wage growth.

“The goal is for remittances to contribute not only to current consumption, but also to long-term economic security,” Abenoja said.

title: OceanaGold upgrades monitoring system
summary: KASIBU, Nueva Vizcaya — As the southwest monsoon (habagat) brings heavy rains to this gold-deposit-rich upland town, the listed firm OceanaGold (Philippines) Inc. (OGP) has upgraded its monitoring system for the tailings storage facility (T
content:
KASIBU, Nueva Vizcaya — As the southwest monsoon (habagat) brings heavy rains to this gold-deposit-rich upland town, the listed firm OceanaGold (Philippines) Inc. (OGP) has upgraded its monitoring system for the tailings storage facility (TSF) at its Didipio Mine, a structure often at the center of community concerns over mining risks.

The company said it partnered with GHD, a global engineering advisory group, to strengthen oversight of the facility’s structural performance, operational safety and long-term integrity during the rainy season.

The upgrade, completed in January 2026, integrates data from geotechnical instruments installed across the facility and from satellite monitoring into a single dashboard that can be accessed remotely, allowing continuous visibility of the dam’s condition.

*   [More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

At the core of the system are the vibrating wire piezometers that track water pressure and levels within the tailings dam, and the Global Navigation Satellite System or GNSS sensors that detect ground movement and deformation.

By consolidating these sources, the company said it can more quickly assess changes in performance indicators and respond accordingly.

The system has been accumulating monitoring data through August and issues automated alerts, including email notifications, when readings hit predefined thresholds.

These alerts feed into the mine’s existing early warning and response protocols. The automated collection also streamlines monthly monitoring and reporting to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources.

The timing is tied to seasonal risk. Rainfall in Didipio typically intensifies in August and peaks in November, when tailings facilities face increased water load and stability challenges.

*   ![Image 1: Quo haec patria tendit?](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1255079.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Quo haec patria tendit?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/opinion/columns/quo-haec-patria-tendit/2443321)

“Historically, rainfall at Didipio begins to intensify in August and peaks in November,” said lawyer Joan Adaci-Cattiling, OGP president and general manager for external affairs and social performance.

“Amid the current habagat season, the upgraded monitoring system gives us greater visibility of the TSF even during periods of heavy rainfall, supporting our early warning and response protocols and helping our teams make informed decisions.”

For residents living downstream and near the mine, the ability to monitor in near real-time during a heavy downpour is presented as a measure to reduce anxiety over possible dam failure, seepage or overflow, risks that have historically fueled opposition to large-scale mining in the province.

GHD said the technology links field data with engineering design.

*   ![Image 2: Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254608.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/legarda-may-rejoin-senate-majority-pangilinan/2443223)

“The innovative monitoring technology at the Didipio Mine gives us consistent, data-led insights. Linking target data with engineering design, OGP engineers can now access real-time information remotely and act with confidence in a challenging and evolving environment,” said Jonathan Dickson, global business leader of GHD’s Dams and Geotech Management Solutions.

OGP said that automation is intended to support, not replace, professional judgment.

“Automation does not replace the expertise and judgment of our engineers. It gives us a more accurate source of information to make decisions earlier and with greater confidence,” Adaci-Cattiling said.

“Responsible mining requires us to continuously improve how we monitor and manage risk. Through this initiative, we are strengthening our TSF monitoring capabilities and reinforcing our commitment to safe and responsible operations.”

*   ![Image 3: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

LEANDER C. DOMINGO

Barangay officials said the upgrade helps address local apprehension.

“We are happy that OGP continues to innovate and ensure the safety of the community,” said Nestor Gayamo, Barangay Didipio councilor.

“Knowing that the company is using advanced monitoring technology, especially during the rainy season, gives Didipio residents added assurance that potential risks are being closely monitored and managed.”

The Didipio TSF uses a downstream construction method, where successive embankment raises are built on competent rock rather than on deposited tailings, a method considered more stable than upstream construction.

The company said its design criteria are aligned with the Australian National Committee on Large Dams.

**SUBIC, ZAMBALES**— Fishers from Zambales and Bataan who rely on the West Philippine Sea (WPS) for their livelihood have expressed concern following allegations that Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband Manases Carpio allegedly received millions of pesos from China-linked parties for the vice president’s silence on China’s harassment and violence against Filipino fishers.

At a press conference in Subic, Zambales on Sunday morning, the civil society coalition Atin Ito said the allegations against the vice president is deeply alarming and must be answered clearly, especially as Filipino fishers continue to face intimidation, dangerous encounters, and restrictions in their traditional fishing grounds.

Present at the press conference are leaders from the New Masinloc Fishermen Association; Subic Commercial Fishers Association; San Miguel Pundaquit Fisherfolk Association; Samahan ng Cabangaan-3 Fishermen’s Unity; and Agri-Aqua Association.

*   [Cebu hospital defends one-watcher rule amid viral post](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/cebu-hospital-defends-one-watcher-rule-amid-viral-post/2443354)

“Madam VP Sara, is it because your silence was paid for by millions that you remain quiet amid the violence and cruelty we suffer in the West Philippine Sea at the hands of China?” said Leonardo Cuaresma, president of the New Masinloc Fishermen Association.

“While we are harassed, intimidated, robbed of our last fish, and driven away by Chinese ships in our own sea, the vice president and her husband allegedly received millions from China. Is this not treachery? Should this not be explained to the people?”

The coalition questioned whether the allegation could explain the vice president’s apparent silence on China’s aggression in Philippine waters. The group also said that the issue strikes at the heart of national sovereignty and the welfare of ordinary Filipinos.

“Every boat driven away, every fisherman intimidated, and every day we cannot fish means lost livelihood and hungry families. While we suffer under China’s coercion, we have the right to know where our leaders stand,” Cuaresma said.

Advertisement

Cuaresma, also a co-convenor of Atin Ito, called on Duterte and her husband to explain the nature, source, and purpose of the reported China-linked multimillion peso transaction and to address the issue publicly.

*   ![Image 25: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

The coalition also challenged Duterte to openly condemn China’s harassment in the WPS and ensure that the protection of Filipino fishers and national sovereignty is never subordinated to private interests.

“For us, the impeachment trial of the vice president is not only about unexplained and ill-gotten wealth. It is about our livelihood, safety, and the country’s sovereignty. We face danger at sea, and we deserve leaders who will fight for us, not multimillionaire traitors,” Cuaresma said.

“The West Philippine Sea is ours. China’s millions must not prevail over the right of Filipino fishermen to fish freely and safely in their own sea.”

title: US sanctions: A ‘test of resilience’ for ICC
summary: DONALD Trump’s US administration has announced sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court that threaten to cripple its operations and spark fresh transatlantic tension. AFP breaks down the likely impact of the sanctions, possibl
content:
DONALD Trump’s US administration has announced sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court that threaten to cripple its operations and spark fresh transatlantic tension.

AFP breaks down the likely impact of the sanctions, possible responses, and the reasons behind Washington’s unprecedented move, which the court said was an “assault on the rule of law.”

**What is the ICC, and what does it do?**

*   [UST activist suspensions: Testing the boundaries of academic freedom and student rights](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/opinion/columns/ust-activist-suspensions-testing-the-boundaries-of-academic-freedom-and-student-rights/2443319)

Based in the Dutch city of The Hague, the ICC tries individuals suspected of the world’s worst offenses — war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide.

Established in 2002 by the Rome Statute, it currently has 125 members. Major powers such as the United States, Russia, China, India, and Israel are not members of the court.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

It is governed by a strict policy of “complementarity,” meaning it can only take on cases a suspect’s home country is unwilling or unable to try itself.

Since its establishment, the court has convicted 15 people, with four acquitted. Critics say the court has focused too heavily on war crimes committed in Africa and failed to convict major political leaders.

However, its most high-profile current case concerns ex-Philippines president Rodrigo Duterte, the first former Asian head of state to stand in the ICC dock.

*   ![Image 1: Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254827.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/marcos-names-lino-cayetano-new-pco-chief/2443262)

The court, housed in a shiny glass building on the outskirts of The Hague, employs around 900 staff from 100 nationalities.

It is often confused with the International Court of Justice, also based in The Hague, which settles disputes between countries.

**What impact will sanctions have?**

The Trump administration has already issued several rounds of sanctions against top ICC officials, but these latest announced actions go further, targeting the entire court.

*   ![Image 2: Panama begins earthquake recovery](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254850.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Panama begins earthquake recovery](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/world/americas-emea/panama-begins-earthquake-recovery/2443275)

ICC officials are concerned about access to banking, credit card facilities, insurance, and especially technology, given a heavy reliance on US systems.

“We have been extremely dependent on US technology solutions, Microsoft or systems related to Microsoft,” Acting Chief Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang told AFP in a recent interview.

“We are trying to find alternative means, maybe not as effective as the US technology, but at least to be able to maintain our independence, to be able to continue to work,” said Niang.

The prosecutor, himself the target of sanctions, said they crippled daily life — he was unable to book transport, hotels, or conduct banking operations.

*   ![Image 3: Cassandra Templora carries Filipino pride into her pursuit of medicine](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254088.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cassandra Templora carries Filipino pride into her pursuit of medicine](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/the-sunday-times/filipino-champions/cassandra-templora-carries-filipino-pride-into-her-pursuit-of-medicine/2443067)

But expanding them to the entire institution raises questions about the ICC’s ability to pay staff, conduct investigations abroad, protect witnesses, and even operate its detention facilities.

“This is a test of our resilience,” admitted Niang.

**What can the Dutch/Europeans do?**

As the host city, the Dutch have a special responsibility to the ICC under the terms of a “Headquarters Agreement” signed in 2008.

This obliges the Netherlands to protect ICC facilities and staff, provide “any means of communication,” and ensure “freedom of financial assets from restrictions.”

In an unusually fiery speech last month at the United Nations General Assembly, Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten vowed to defend the ICC “in my country, in my city.”

“How can you possibly be opposed to prosecuting the very worst crimes? I believe there can be only one response: ‘hands off the ICC,’” said Jetten to warm applause.

Reacting to the announcement from Washington, Jetten said the Dutch would do “whatever we need” to ensure the ICC could continue to function.

One possibility would be for the European Commission to deploy a legal instrument known as the “blocking mechanism.”

This prohibits European firms from obeying the US sanctions “actively or by deliberate omission,” giving the EU a potential means of cushioning some of the impact.

The EU blocking mechanism is seen as the “nuclear option,” said Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen, adding that the Netherlands had nevertheless asked Brussels to prepare it.

Jetten said a six-month pause before sanctions took effect should be used to pursue dialogue with Washington — “this will give us plenty of time.”

**Why is the US doing this?**

The US is furious the court issued an arrest warrant for close ally, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, over alleged crimes in Gaza.

It is also concerned an ICC investigation into Afghanistan could result in accusations against US personnel.

Trump has upped his rhetoric against what he has called a “rogue institution” and “evil group of people,” and the US has vowed to dismantle the court “brick-by-brick.”

But even under less pugnacious presidents, Washington has never been a fan of the ICC and never considered joining.

The US has a law dubbed the “Hague Invasion Act,” allowing it to take “all means necessary and appropriate” to defend US personnel or allies detained by the ICC. AFP

title: PH urges global action on climate forecasts
summary: THE Philippines urged countries to translate climate forecasts into early action and preparedness ahead of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), warning that intensifying El Niño conditions could compound risks to water
content:
THE Philippines urged countries to translate climate forecasts into early action and preparedness ahead of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), warning that intensifying El Niño conditions could compound risks to water, food, energy, health and local economies.

Climate Change Commission (CCC) Vice Chairman and Executive Director Robert E.A. Borje made the call during a Pre-COP31 plenary discussion on priorities for the conference, citing a World Meteorological Organization forecast that El Niño would intensify and would persist until February 2027.

“The forecast gives us a clear warning, but also a window to prepare and respond,” Borje said. “We must build right at first sight so every investment reduces risk rather than locks it in.”

*   [Marcos on alleged China money to VP Sara: A threat to the highest level](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/marcos-on-alleged-china-money-to-vp-sara-a-threat-to-the-highest-level/2443294)

The official said climate forecasts should guide government decisions before their effects escalate, in line with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s push for predictive governance.

For the Philippines, this means incorporating climate risk assessments into policies and investments involving agriculture, water security, public infrastructure and community livelihoods, he said.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Borje urged countries to use COP31 to support the preparation and implementation of their Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and National Adaptation Plans (NAPs), which guide their climate mitigation and adaptation efforts.

He cited the Philippines’ NDC Implementation Plan, National Adaptation Plan and National Climate Risk Management Framework as existing mechanisms for integrating climate considerations into national economic decisions.

The Philippine official called for increased and more accessible climate financing, saying current funding falls far short of developing countries’ needs.

*   ![Image 1: Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254608.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/legarda-may-rejoin-senate-majority-pangilinan/2443223)

The United Nations Environment Program estimates that developing countries will require $310 billion to $365 billion annually for adaptation by 2035.

However, international public adaptation finance for developing countries totaled only $26 billion in 2023, less than one-tenth of the estimated annual requirement.

While water and wastewater systems receive the largest sectoral share of tracked adaptation finance, Borje said the overall amount remains insufficient.

“A large share of an inadequate pool remains inadequate,” the CCC official said.

*   ![Image 2: Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254827.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/marcos-names-lino-cayetano-new-pco-chief/2443262)

He also raised concerns over limited and poorly tracked financing for oceans, which are vital to small island developing states and archipelagic countries such as the Philippines.

Borje called for climate finance that is adequate, predictable, new, additional, scaled up and readily accessible to developing countries.

He said funding flows should be transparently measured, provided on fair terms and directed to national and local institutions responsible for implementing climate programs.

Public and concessional financing remain essential, Borje said, adding that private funding should complement rather than replace governments’ responsibilities.

*   ![Image 3: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

He also called for faster technology transfer and capacity-building to help developing countries respond to climate risks.

Borje said the conference’s Action Agenda could help advance the goal of making COP31 an “implementation COP” by supporting practical partnerships in energy, water, oceans and resilience, while linking multi-hazard early warning systems to early action.

He said the success of the conference would ultimately depend on whether its negotiations produced agreements that reach vulnerable communities, protect lives and sustain development.

COP31 will be held in November at the Antalya Expo Center in Türkiye.

title: India court frees ‘cockroach’ party leaders
summary: **NEW DELHI**— The founder of India’s youth-led online “cockroach” movement and two other leaders were released on Sunday, their lawyer said, a day after they were detained to thwart a major protest against the election commissioner. The gr
content:
**NEW DELHI**— The founder of India’s youth-led online “cockroach” movement and two other leaders were released on Sunday, their lawyer said, a day after they were detained to thwart a major protest against the election commissioner.

The group said thousands of protesters were detained before Saturday’s planned demonstration in New Delhi, the culmination of weeks of opposition mobilization following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter roll revision.

Abhijeet Dipke and two other Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders were detained before they could disembark from their flight after arriving in the capital from Mumbai.

*   [Panama begins earthquake recovery](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/world/americas-emea/panama-begins-earthquake-recovery/2443275)

Ratna Singh, the CJP’s head lawyer, said in a social media post that Dipke and the others had been released by an executive magistrate’s court.

She said they had been released on the condition that they made “no breach of peace for one year.”

Dipke, wearing a white shirt, was driven away in a black vehicle soon after walking out of the court, Agence France-Presse (AFP) reporters saw.

Authorities mounted a sweeping security operation across the capital on Saturday, detaining thousands to prevent protesters from gathering at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar protest site, the CJP and Indian media reports said.

The protest was organized to demand the resignation of the head of the Election Commission of India (ECI) over the nationwide voter-roll revision.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)

Media reports said the revision resulted in more than 133 million names being removed from electoral lists.

Election authorities say the exercise was aimed at eliminating duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries.

Critics say the process has disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims, potentially benefiting Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.

The ECI has rejected allegations of wrongdoing.

*   ![Image 2: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)

In Geneva, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights called for the immediate and unconditional release of all those “arbi­trarily detained” in New Delhi.

Both the CJP and opposition leader Rahul Gandhi have vowed to press ahead with protests despite the crackdown.

Gandhi said his Congress party “... and the youth of the country will once again take to the streets in large numbers” on Monday.

title: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor
summary: MAGALANG, Pampanga — More complaints had been filed before the Office of the Ombudsman against Magalang Mayor Malu Lacson and four others. Employees of Kingsmen Manpower Agency accused Lacson, her husband Odilon Lacson, Norman Lacson, Pablo
content:
MAGALANG, Pampanga — More complaints had been filed before the Office of the Ombudsman against Magalang Mayor Malu Lacson and four others.

Employees of Kingsmen Manpower Agency accused Lacson, her husband Odilon Lacson, Norman Lacson, Pablo Elmer Mercado and Jose Tiburcio Canlas of falsifying public and private documents, using of falsified documents, perjury, grave misconduct, dishonesty and gross neglect of duty. Their formal complaint was filed on Sept. 29, 2026.

The complaintants — Arcadio Templa, Jerome Layog, Junel Pimentel and Rainy Mones — said the respondents identified in the complaint are the owners of the employment agency.

*   [10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

They also alleged that Lacson submitted a Deed of Sale of Shares of Stock in a separate case before the Pampanga Prosecutor’s Office. They said the document was presented as proof that Lacson had divested her interest in Kingsmen Manpower Agency.

However, the complainants said the documents were ­allegedly falsified.

They further alleged that the deed was notarized by lawyer Almario Marimla on May 25, 2022, but that no record of the notarization could be found at the Angeles City Regional Trial Court, based on a certification issued by the court’s Office of the Clerk of Court.

The complainants also questioned the authenticity of the signature attributed to Marimla on the deed. title: Duterte’s lawyers to present evidence
summary: VICE President Sara Duterte’s defense team is preparing to present its witnesses and evidence before the Senate impeachment court after the House prosecution panel concluded its presentation of witnesses. The defense has indicated it will p
content:
VICE President Sara Duterte’s defense team is preparing to present its witnesses and evidence before the Senate impeachment court after the House prosecution panel concluded its presentation of witnesses.

The defense has indicated it will present a financial expert and other witnesses to challenge the prosecution’s findings, including its estimate of P817.87 million in allegedly undeclared assets and unexplained wealth involving Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio.

On Friday, financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera testified that GenCorp Industries Inc., in which Duterte declared owning shares in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN), underdeclared more than P1 billion in income over four years.

*   [Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/dutertes-tax-records-need-audit-bir-exec/2442826)

Cabrera said GenCorp, which operates five Jollibee franchises, had P1.049 billion in undeclared income, representing an average annual underdeclaration of 87 percent.

Cabrera compared GenCorp’s records with those of Cale88 Foods Corp. and Metro Chow.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

He said GenCorp reported only about 10 percent to 13 percent of its income annually, raising questions about the reliability of its financial statements.

Cabrera attributed about P212 million of the undeclared income to Duterte, based on his conservative estimate that she had a 20-percent share in the company.

He also cited a discrepancy between Duterte’s SALN and GenCorp’s corporate records filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

*   ![Image 1: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

Although Duterte declared herself a GenCorp stockholder in her SALN, her name did not appear in the company’s General Information Sheet (GIS), he said.

Cabrera said other shareholders might be holding shares on Duterte’s behalf, increasing her potential ownership interest at between 20 percent and 45 percent.

He questioned whether Duterte’s absence from GenCorp’s SEC ownership records was connected to the company’s government contracts with Davao City.

Records presented before the impeachment court showed that GenCorp secured P35.88 million in government contracts from July 2022 to June 2026, including P34.22 million from Davao City under Mayor Sebastian Duterte, the vice president’s brother.

*   ![Image 2: Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254827.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/marcos-names-lino-cayetano-new-pco-chief/2443262)

“If VP Sara’s name were listed on GenCorp’s GIS, GenCorp would not be allowed to secure a contract from the city of Davao. That is prohibited. It is a conflict of interest,” Cabrera testified.

Cabrera also questioned GenCorp’s declared capital of P1.25 million, saying its five Jollibee franchises required a combined investment of at least P175 million.

His findings on GenCorp were separate from his broader estimate of P817.87 million in allegedly undeclared assets and unexplained wealth involving Duterte and Carpio from 2022 to 2025.

Cabrera said Duterte’s SALNs for four consecutive years were untruthful because substantial assets belonging to the couple had not been disclosed.

*   ![Image 3: Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254608.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/legarda-may-rejoin-senate-majority-pangilinan/2443223)

The defense is expected to challenge his findings when it presents its evidence.

In a related development, Sen. Francis Pangilinan said the prosecution’s withdrawal of the bribery charge against Duterte could shorten the trial, particularly if the defense reduces its initial list of 30 witnesses.

In an interview with DWIZ radio, Pangilinan said a smaller witness list could mean fewer hearing days, depending on how the defense presents its case.

The prosecution withdrew Article III, which accused Duterte of bribing Department of Education (DepEd) officials to influence procurement decisions during her tenure as education secretary.

Prosecutors said the move would allow them to focus on the remaining charges.

Remaining in the impeachment complaint are Article I, involving allegations of misuse of confidential funds; Article II, concerning alleged unexplained wealth and inaccurate SALN declarations; and Article IV, involving alleged grave threats against senior government officials.

Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano said many Filipinos were more concerned about everyday corruption and the rising cost of living than Duterte’s impeachment trial.

In a Facebook livestream on Saturday, Cayetano cited high electricity and fuel prices, rising food costs and lost income, particularly among communities affected by flooding, as more immediate concerns for ordinary Filipinos.

“Actually, impeachment is for you politicians. For us ordinary people, it’s really the day-to-day corruption,” Cayetano quoted a person he had spoken with as saying.

“And it’s really how to exist,” he added, recounting the conversation.

Cayetano said flooding had disrupted livelihoods and prevented some people from going to work, while higher fuel and electricity costs further strained household budgets.

He also cited rising tuition, daily expenses and operating costs affecting schools, families and food businesses.

Cayetano also discussed personal accountability, faith and the choices people make when confronted with difficult situations.

In another radio interview Sunday, prosecutor and Bukidnon Rep. Jonathan Keith Flores said the decision to drop the bribery charge was not a concession but a strategic move anchored on evidence already presented before the impeachment court.

Flores said the prosecution no longer considered it necessary to present evidence on the bribery allegations after what he described as a solid presentation under the other articles.

“If you look back — take a look at the three articles — the prosecution’s presentation was actually quite solid. So, in our view, it is no longer necessary to proceed with presenting the article on bribery,” said in English and Filipino.

Flores said the move was also intended to keep the proceedings on schedule, with the trial set to take a one-month break.

He said that even if a bribery case has been dropped, criminal charges can still be filed against the vice president before the Office of the Ombudsman or the Department of Justice.

title: Quo haec patria tendit?

content:
“WHERE is the country going” is the meaning of the above Latin sentence, Quo haec patria tendit. That seems to be the question of every Filipino citizen watching the gravely disconcerting political development unfolding in the country.

It looks like the brains behind the ouster of Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte and her disqualification from the 2028 presidential elections are on track in their devious plan of convicting her in the impeachment trial.

The political bullet train carrying the judgment of conviction, if one is to believe the spokesman of the impeachment court, is arriving at its designated place on Dec. 16 of this year.

*   [Are Marcos’ minions in Congress plotting to amend the Constitution?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/opinion/columns/are-marcos-minions-in-congress-plotting-to-amend-the-constitution/2443331)

All the forced circumstances that will bring to fruition such devilish design have transpired, to wit: the arrest, detention and rendition of her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, to the International Criminal Court (ICC) at The Hague; the overwhelming vote by the members of the House of Representatives to impeach VP Sara; the filing of nonbailable charges of plunder against identified allies of VP Sara and their incarceration; the service of an ICC warrant on Sen. Ronald “ Bato” de la Rosa that forced the embattled lawmaker to go into hiding to evade an unlawful arrest; the shake-up at the Senate that resulted in the ouster of Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano from the Senate leadership following the somersaulting of two senators who are facing capital offenses in connection with the flood-control project corruption, forcing them to abandon their colleagues in the majority resulting in the Cayetano bloc’s loss of control of the upper chamber; the threatened filing of criminal charges against a female senator and her lawmaker-son and the issuance of a warrant of arrest against the latter; and the filing of graft and corruption criminal complaints against sibling senators Camille and Mark Villar and their parents, former senator Manuel “Manny” Villar and former senator Cynthia Villar, as well as another member of the Villar family, that forced Senator Mark Villar to leave the minority and vote with the majority to unlawfully reduce the constitutional threshold of conviction in the Senate impeachment vote.

The scuttlebutt is that there are three more senators who are to join the majority to secure their liberty. If that probability happens, and the highest court of the land does not intervene to derail the unconstitutional amendment of reducing the required number of senators for conviction, then such circumstances will seal the political coffin of the impeached official.

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The social media is abuzz with the bashing of Sen. Mark Villar for not only abandoning the minority but also voting to reduce the voting threshold for conviction. It is, however, easy to render rash judgment on him, to unmask him as a traitor to the cause of justice and truth, and for betraying his colleagues. But we must remember that a person under coercive and threatening circumstances where his or her liberty or life or both are at stake, especially when the members of his/her family are also at perilous risk, succumbing to a repulsive act against his will is inevitable.

Most of the members of both the majority and the minority are hostage to the power holders owing to their alleged involvement in some anomalies related to the release and use of the national budget. They have to toe the line, obey as ordered. Should they defy the command, the guillotine will swiftly fall on them. That will explain why, like dominoes, one by one of them is falling to the ground.

Rather than crucify them, the powers-that-be should be exposed and prosecuted to the fullest when the time of reckoning comes and they face the unforgiving wrath of the people and the law of retribution.

*   ![Image 1: Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254827.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/marcos-names-lino-cayetano-new-pco-chief/2443262)

For now, they appear to control the three branches of government, weaponizing the law against those whom they perceive to be roadblocks to their unquestionable lust for power and ill-gotten wealth.

They rule their fiefdom with absolute authority and impunity. They wallow in luxury, ransacking the natural resources and wealth of the nation as the people suffer in silence. Those who resist are subjected to black propaganda and dishonored, or worse, those who challenge their authority are thrown in jail.

The people are in despair even as they are disgusted and angry. They are waiting for the constitutionally designated protectors to fulfill their task, but they seem to be not forthcoming, waiting for a trigger that is either still in the making or has not taken shape. The last bulwark of democracy on Padre Faura appears to be vacillating or in a state of suspended animation.

The country is on the precipice. The seething outrage and desolation are percolating and near boiling point. There must be an end to this political insanity, but how and when?

*   ![Image 2: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

Que sera, sera; what will be, will be.

title: HEADLINES: Duterte’s lawyers to present evidence | October 12, 2026
summary: Good day. Here are the stories of The Manila Times for Monday, October 12, 2026. Today’s episode is brought to you by Wilcon Depot, The Philippines’ leading home improvement and construction supplies retailer — your Trusted Building Partner
content:
Good day. Here are the stories of The Manila Times for Monday, October 12, 2026.

Today’s episode is brought to you by Wilcon Depot, The Philippines’ leading home improvement and construction supplies retailer — your Trusted Building Partner.

**BANNER: Duterte’s lawyers to present evidence**

VICE President Sara Duterte’s defense team is preparing to present its witnesses and evidence before the Senate impeachment court after the House prosecution panel concluded its presentation of witnesses. The defense has indicated it will present a financial expert and other witnesses to challenge the prosecution’s findings, including its estimate of P817.87 million in allegedly undeclared assets and unexplained wealth involving Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio. On Friday, financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera testified that GenCorp Industries Inc., in which Duterte declared owning shares in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN), underdeclared more than P1 billion in income over four years. Cabrera said GenCorp, which operates five Jollibee franchises, had P1.049 billion in undeclared income, representing an average annual underdeclaration of 87 percent.

**‘Lacson threatened contractors with plunder’**

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

SENATE Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano has accused Sen. Panfilo Lacson of threatening to sue contractors for plunder to pressure them into signing affidavits concerning alleged irregularities in projects in the Laguna Lakeshore area in Taguig City. In a Facebook livestream on Saturday, Cayetano said four of the contractors implicated in the controversy refused to sign the affidavits, and two agreed to do so. He said Lacson warned the four holdouts they could face plunder charges if they refused to sign. He also alleged that Lacson, his staff and lawyers associated with them had prepared affidavits and were pressuring contractors to sign them. He did not identify the contractors or present copies of the affidavits during the livestream.

**Legarda may rejoin Senate majority – Pangilinan**

SEN. Francis Pangilinan has not ruled out Sen. Loren Legarda’s return to the Senate majority bloc, saying she was originally part of a group of five senators that included several members of the chamber’s current majority. Pangilinan said Legarda belonged to a group composed of Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente Sotto III, Sen. Panfilo Lacson, Sen. Risa Hontiveros and Sen. Lito Lapid. Legarda joined the minority bloc led by Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano amid changes in Senate leadership. Her return to the majority came under discussion after Sen. Mark Villar joined the bloc on Oct. 8, replacing Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri in the powerful Commission on Appointments and taking over the Senate Committee on Public Works.

**2 Filipinos among hundreds injured in Riyadh attack**

TWO Filipinos were among those wounded in the missile attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia, the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) said Sunday. The attack, blamed on Houthi rebels, killed 12 people and injured 309 others. It was the deadliest strike on Saudi soil in more than a decade. Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac confirmed the two Filipino casualties but gave no further details, including their identities, the extent of their injuries and their current condition.

**BUSINESS: Global risks cloud remittance outlook**

REMITTANCES — a key pillar of the Philippine economy — will likely post slower growth as global uncertainties weigh on overseas employment and income prospects, a Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) official said. BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Abenoja told The Manila Times that remittances are still expected to grow in the next two to three years, albeit at a slower pace amid global uncertainties. He added that the main risks to remittance growth are weaker labor demand in host economies and geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Middle East. The outlook carries significant implications for the Philippines, where remittances are equivalent to around eight percent of gross domestic product (GDP), helping sustain household spending and providing a steady source of foreign financing. Data from the BSP’s third-quarter 2026 Consumer Expectations Survey showed that food and other household expenses were the most common uses of remittances, with 98 percent of remittance-receiving households reporting that they used the money for these needs.

[**SPORTS: Eala on track for Alexandrova, Fernandez rematch**](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/sports/eala-on-track-for-alexandrova-fernandez-rematch/2443256)

FILIPINO sensation Alex Eala is on track for a rematch against Russian Ekaterina Alexandrova or a rubber match against Canadian Leylah Fernandez at the WTA 1000 Wuhan Open in China. World No. 18 Eala needs to get past a qualifier in her opening match likely on Monday before facing either No. 28 Alexandrova or No. 26 Fernandez who is of Filipino descent. Alexandrova and Fernandez were pitted against each other as the draw revealed on Saturday. Tournament No. 13 seed Eala battled Alexandrova at the Abu Dhabi Open quarterfinals where she fell to the latter, 3-6, 3-6, last February.

Rigoberto Tiglao and Fr. Ranhilio Callangan Aquino are today’s front page columnists. Tiglao’s column is about the alleged plot to amend the Constitution by allies of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in the lower house. Fr. Aquino’s column, meanwhile, talks about confidentiality in the impeachment court.

Today’s editorial is about the conflict between Houthi rebels and Saudi Arabia.

title: Senate to probe rice smuggling – Pangilinan
summary: SEN. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan has called for the same level of public scrutiny and accountability for agricultural smuggling as for the flood control corruption scandal, saying both involve abuses that harm ordinary Filipinos. His call fol
content:
SEN. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan has called for the same level of public scrutiny and accountability for agricultural smuggling as for the flood control corruption scandal, saying both involve abuses that harm ordinary Filipinos. His call followed the interception of two vessels carrying nearly 20,000 metric tons of rice allegedly smuggled from Vietnam, with the shipments estimated to be worth about P700 million.

“Rice smugglers profit from farmers’ losses. Corrupt contractors profit while communities are submerged in floods,” Pangilinan said in an interview with DWIZ radio.

He said agricultural smuggling threatens food security, undermines local farmers and livestock raisers, and can leave consumers bearing the consequences.

*   [DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

“Rice smugglers and the government officials protecting them are like corrupt contractors involved in the flood control scam and the public officials enabling them. Both trade away the welfare of the people,” said Pangilinan, who chairs the Senate Committee on Agriculture, Food and Agrarian Reform.

He warned that officials from the Bureau of Customs (BOC), local government units, the Department of Agriculture (DA), the Department of Public Works and Highways, and other agencies should also be held accountable if found to have allowed or facilitated the illegal activities.

**“Even accomplices and enablers must be held accountable,” he said.**

Pangilinan requested that his committee investigate the rice smuggling cases, expecting the probe to begin before the end of October, possibly alongside the DA’s budget hearings scheduled for Oct. 20 and 21.

Authorities intercepted vessels MV Lucky Star and MV Tay Son 2 in separate operations in September in Limay, Bataan, and Davao, respectively. Pangilinan cited shipments of about 7,500 metric tons and roughly 12,000 metric tons of rice.

*   ![Image 1: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

He said the shipments had incomplete documentation and that he had asked the DA and BOC to reconcile discrepancies in their reported cargo volumes.

Pangilinan added that the Senate panel inquiry would examine the shipments’ consignees, the vessels’ captains, and any possible involvement of government personnel. He also said the Department of Justice should participate because it would handle the filing of criminal complaints.

Pangilinan stressed the importance of securing official documents and sufficient evidence to avoid court dismissal of the cases. He recalled that previous smuggling investigations had problems when cases were filed with incomplete records or photocopies instead of original official documents.

**“We will expose all of it and closely monitor the case,” he said, adding that government agencies had committed to cooperating with the investigation.**

*   ![Image 2: Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254827.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/marcos-names-lino-cayetano-new-pco-chief/2443262)

Pangilinan said the investigation would also test the enforcement of the law against agricultural economic sabotage, which he said provides authorities with stronger legal tools to prosecute large-scale agricultural smuggling.

He cited previous Senate investigations into smuggling, including a 2024 case involving imported pork worth about P100 million that was allegedly unfit for human consumption. Pangilinan said the Senate would revisit earlier cases and follow up on individuals who had failed to appear at hearings despite being subpoenaed.

The senator also raised concerns about the low number of cases filed in past smuggling investigations, saying seizures would have little deterrent effect if those responsible were not prosecuted.

“Especially with Super El Niño expected to further burden the agriculture and fisheries sectors, and with other threats to our food security, no one should be untouchable,” he said.

*   ![Image 3: Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254608.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/legarda-may-rejoin-senate-majority-pangilinan/2443223)

Pangilinan said the Senate would also examine how the seized rice would be accounted for and disposed of, noting that discrepancies between initial announcements and records submitted during case filing had been a concern in previous cases.

**He said the government must show that agricultural smuggling demands meaningful accountability, not just mere seizure of shipments.**

He added that the looming Super El Niño makes protecting local food production more urgent, as farmers and fisherfolk face additional risks from adverse weather.

title: Polish leader says school attacks were fueled by online glorification of violence
summary: **WARSAW, Poland —**The attacks at Polish schools over the past week were “spontaneous acts” driven by the online “glorification of violence,” Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Sunday. Three attacks at schools in the Mazovian province in c
content:
**WARSAW, Poland —**The attacks at Polish schools over the past week were “spontaneous acts” driven by the online “glorification of violence,” Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Sunday.

Three attacks at schools in the Mazovian province in central Poland took place within four days this week, leaving one dead and many wounded, including children.

By Sunday morning, police had detained 117 people across Poland for carrying knives or other dangerous weapons, or for threatening to attack schools or fellow students. Some 64,000 schools were checked.

*   [12 killed and over 300 hurt in latest attack on Riyadh airport, Saudi authorities say](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/world/americas-emea/12-killed-and-over-300-hurt-in-latest-attack-on-riyadh-airport-saudi-authorities-say/2443213)

“We are not dealing with any group organized on a big scale,” Tusk said on Sunday morning, during a crisis meeting with government and security services. “These are very often spontaneous actions inspired by online activity.”

“In the past years and months, we have noted — globally and in Poland — a rise in the fascination with violence.”

 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Tusk said the acts could be associated with “nihilistic violence,” a term used by authorities to describe acts of violence driven by a nihilistic worldview and misanthropy rather than specific political goals.

In the case of Poland, he said “some of the people detained are active in the ultraright environment." He said authorities have observed intensified online searches of Nazi content as well as of “mass killers who have become idols online.”

Tusk said Poland was facing a “civilizational phenomenon” where kids playing video games, even banal ones, or those interested in crime stories, were getting exposed to more and more violence.

*   ![Image 1: Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254608.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/legarda-may-rejoin-senate-majority-pangilinan/2443223)

“This is essentially a copycat scenario, something of a long trail of attackers going back to at least 2019, if not decades earlier,” Kacper Rekawek, senior researcher at the International Center for Counterterrorism in The Hague, told the AP. He was referring to Brenton Tarrant, the white supremacist who shot and killed 51 Muslims at two mosques in Christchurch, New Zealand, in 2019.

[![Image 2: A police officer and a volunteer firefighter look down the street near a cordoned-off area following an attack on the Vocational School Complex No. 4 in Ostroleka, Poland, Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026. AP PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254801.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254801.jpg)
A police officer and a volunteer firefighter look down the street near a cordoned-off area following an attack on the Vocational School Complex No. 4 in Ostroleka, Poland, Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026. AP PHOTO

Rekawek said that one of the suspects in the latest Polish attacks used the same imagery and esthetics as Tarrant, which means the Polish incidents should be “placed within the confines of essentially terrorist behavior.”

*   ![Image 3: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

Tusk said police checks at schools across Poland would continue into next week in case kids exposed to the stories of the past attacks might “get stupid and unsafe thoughts” to imitate them.

He said Poland had lots of work to do as a society, with parents and teachers having an especially important role to play in communicating with kids about their experiences online and explaining that “fascination and membership in these online practices can lead to very negative consequences.”

On Wednesday, a 19-year-old student at a vocational school in the Mazovian province attacked fellow students, teachers and passersby with a sharp object, wounding nine people. He was arrested nearby. The following day, a 15-year-old killed a school custodian and wounded two other people in a knife attack at his former school in the same province. On Saturday, a 21-year old woman wounded three at a post-secondary school in Warsaw.

Rumors that the attacks were coordinated and that there would be more on “bloody Friday” were shared in parents’ online groups and by mainstream media. It led to 59 schools preemptively suspending classes on Friday across Poland, the majority in Mazovian province.

*   ![Image 4: Lacson threatening contractors with plunder charges — Cayetano](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254606.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson threatening contractors with plunder charges — Cayetano](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/lacson-threatening-contractors-with-plunder-charges-cayetano/2443221)

Those detained on Friday by the police include a 14-year-old boy from Warsaw who was found in possession of a knife with a concealed blade and 11 firecrackers, and a 16-year old who came to school with a butterfly knife in his backpack, police said.

title: Lacson threatening contractors with plunder charges — Cayetano
summary: **MANILA, Philippines —**Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano has accused Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson of threatening contractors with plunder charges to pressure them into signing affidavits concerning alleged irregularities in project
content:
**MANILA, Philippines —**Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano has accused Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson of threatening contractors with plunder charges to pressure them into signing affidavits concerning alleged irregularities in projects along the Laguna Lakeshore area in Taguig City.

In a Facebook livestream on Saturday, Cayetano claimed that six contractors were involved in the controversy. Four refused to sign the affidavits and two agreed to do so.

He alleged that Lacson warned the four holdouts they could face plunder charges if they did not sign.

*   [DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

“Sen. Lacson once said, ‘There are six of you contractors. Four of you refused to sign, while two signed. If the four of you do not sign, you will be charged with plunder,’” Cayetano said.

“Who wouldn’t be afraid of plunder charges now, especially given the people Sen. Lacson has been pointing to?” he added.

 delivered to your inbox

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Cayetano said several people had approached him, claiming they felt caught in the middle of the pressure.

He alleged that Lacson, his staff and lawyers associated with them had prepared affidavits and were pressuring some contractors to sign the documents.

He did not identify the contractors.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

“If there is nothing wrong, why would you sign? They are being threatened, and there are consequences,” Cayetano said.

“Not everyone has the courage, stamina, patience or guts to stand up for what is right, especially when going up against very high-ranking officials in this highly charged atmosphere. But having said that, how can our country change?” he added.

The senator linked the dispute to the broader investigations into alleged irregularities in government infrastructure and flood control projects.

Cayetano cited Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon, who earlier said that there were no ghost projects in the Laguna Lakeshore area of Taguig.

*   ![Image 2: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254518.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

He also questioned the activities of the Laguna Lake Development Authority and the Public Reclamation Authority in areas along the lake in Rizal and Laguna, contrasting them with projects in Taguig.

Cayetano urged government personnel involved in the controversy to focus on evidence and their responsibilities rather than take sides.

“This is not about following Senator Lacson or Senator Alan. No. Do what is right,” he said.

Lacson has yet to respond to Cayetano’s latest allegations.

*   ![Image 3: Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254608.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/legarda-may-rejoin-senate-majority-pangilinan/2443223)

In an earlier statement, Lacson said anomalies he found in flood control projects last year prompted him to dig deeper, eventually leading him to deliver two privilege speeches on alleged corruption involving projects in Bulacan and Oriental Mindoro.

As chairman of the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee at the time, Lacson said hearings uncovered additional evidence that eventually led to cases against several individuals.

He said he would continue to answer Cayetano’s allegations with documents and other evidence.

“I’m just responding. Whenever he speaks, I respond with the receipts," he said.

title: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’
summary: THE House prosecution on Friday questioned Vice President Sara Duterte’s public image of simple living as its final witness presented financial findings that included P11.35 million in checks allegedly paid to her dentist and estimated P817
content:
THE House prosecution on Friday questioned Vice President Sara Duterte’s public image of simple living as its final witness presented financial findings that included P11.35 million in checks allegedly paid to her dentist and estimated P817.87 million in allegedly undeclared assets and income.

Financial forensic expert Alexander Cabrera, a certified public accountant and lawyer, estimated that Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, had P817.87 million in allegedly undeclared assets and income from 2022 to 2025.

Among the transactions highlighted in Cabrera’s report were check payments totaling P11.35 million to Lourdes Lebosada, identified during the hearing as Duterte’s dentist.

*   [DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

He also flagged P299,142 in Nike purchases at SM Davao Annex in a single day.

The prosecution said Cabrera tied together bank records, statements of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALNs), corporate filings and audited financial statements to support its allegations under Article II of the impeachment complaint, which covers unexplained wealth, inaccurate financial declarations and prohibited business interests.
