【大紀元2026年10月13日訊】（大紀元記者梁耀採訪報導）中共駐多倫多總領事館前，一名華裔男子襲擊、恐嚇法輪功學員，並發出死亡威脅，近日台北駐加拿大經濟文化代表處代表曾厚仁撰文抨擊這種外國脅迫行為。

9月22日，在多倫多中領館前，一名身穿帶有五星血旗圖案夾克的男子突然衝向法輪功學員的展板，砸毀展示物品，並推搡、責罵法輪功學員，其中包括年長女性。現場錄影顯示，該男子告訴法輪功學員他們的抗議是非法的，並將中領館前公共區域稱為「中國領土」，同時指責他們同時指責他們「分裂國家」。

曾厚仁代表在文中稱，該衝突引發了一個遠超單一抗議事件的問題：在加拿大的土地上，究竟應該由誰的規則來管轄政治表達？「分裂國家」是北京常用於針對其認為威脅國家統一人士的言辭。

他表示，該男子的身分及其所屬機構尚未得到公開確認，也沒有證實其為領事官員或受官方指使的證據。但無需做此類假設，也能理解為什麼這一事件應引起加拿大學者的關注。在多倫多的街道上，一個威權政府的政治話語被用來恐嚇行使加拿大法律所保護自由的人們。其傳遞的信息很簡單：即使在這裡，某些觀點也不應該被表達。

## 跨國鎮壓進入日常生活

曾代表說，這就是跨國鎮壓進入人們日常生活的方式。「它可能涉及公共集會上的監視、網絡威脅、對海外親屬施加壓力，或是讓人無法確定在加拿大行使自由是否會在其它地方引發後果。」

曾厚仁在文中稱，台灣的處境，為中共跨境施加政治壓力提供了更廣泛的例證。台灣一直面臨著來自北京的虛假信息、經濟壓力、網絡攻擊和政治恐嚇；而前往中國的台灣公民則必須應對界定寬泛的國家安全罪名，這些罪名可能導致他們面臨詢問、拘留或限制人身自由。

中共於2026年3月12日通過《民族團結進步促進法》，並於同年7月1日施行，曾代表認為，該法使這些擔憂更為明確。中共利用該法推進了其國家定義的「中華民族共同身分」觀念，將法律責任延伸到境外行為。

曾代表認為，對於與新疆、西藏和香港有聯繫的海外社群來說，其暗示令人不安：在加拿大合法的政治表達，可能在其它地方帶來後果。

加拿大前副總理方慧蘭（Chrystia Freeland）於2026年8月4日在台北「凱達格蘭論壇：2026印太安全對話」發表演講時，批評《民族團結進步促進法》的域外管轄條款，稱其「特別險惡」，並呼籲民主國家公開、一致反對。

## 中共海外政治脅迫打擊加拿大自由

曾厚仁撰文強調，無論北京是企圖在加拿大強加「一中」政策，還是在加拿大土地上恐嚇海外社群，其潛在的問題都是一樣的：企圖將其政治和法律議程延伸至中國本土之外。加拿大是一個主權國家。在其它地方實施的政治限制，不應決定加拿大的政策或在其國界內行使的自由。

「遺憾的是，一項外國法律根本不需要在加拿大取得任何一次有罪判決，就能在這裡產生影響。如果它能說服人們放低聲音、遠離示威活動或不敢表達合法的觀點，那麼脅迫就已經穿透了國界。」

他說：「生活在多倫多、渥太華或溫哥華的人，在加拿大法律下享有批評外國政府、參加示威或主張某種政治訴求的充分自由。但如果行使這種自由會導致對出國旅行的恐懼、對親屬的牽連或其它形式的報復，那麼這種自由的意義就會大打折扣。」

曾厚仁分析稱，多倫多人行道上的這場衝突不僅關乎一次抗議。無論涉事個人的身分或動機如何，它都提出了一個更大的問題：一個威權國家所施加的政治限制，是否會跟隨人們進入一個民主國家。

他說：「原則應當是明確的。任何外國政治教條或法律主張，都不應決定加拿大合法表達的邊界。在這裡，規範和平表達的法律是加拿大的法律，這些法律所保護的自由也必須是加拿大的自由，無論其它地方有誰對行使這些自由表示異議。」

## 中共加強海外滲透的深層解析：中共形勢艱難

近年來，多國政府、情報機構、學者與人權組織一致指出：中共正加強海外滲透、影響力操作與跨國脅迫（transnational repression），涵蓋政治、社群、學術、媒體、商業與僑界，並以法律、外交、情報與科技手段擴大其域外施壓能力。

2026年10月4日，美國華裔房地產經紀人張婉瑩在洛杉磯國際機場被美國聯邦探員逮捕。她涉嫌監視台灣總統賴清德之子賴廷與並收集情報，被控在未申報的情況下充當中國政府的代理人。

曾厚仁表示，最近這幾年中共的動作很多，可能他們感覺到目前其國內形勢對其不利，在許多領域表現不佳，經濟狀況持續惡化，內部的政治局勢也顯露出高度不穩定。他分析表示，中共如今可能正陷入極為艱難的形勢。

責任編輯：田青

title: Experts urge parents to prepare kids for possible livestreamed execution
summary: This is not an article about politics, capital punishment or whether the Fort Hood shooter deserves to be executed in public for his crimes. Instead, it's focused on the unprecedented parental challenge of handling the near-certain prospect
content:
This is not an article about politics, capital punishment or whether the Fort Hood shooter deserves to be executed in public for his crimes.

Instead, it's focused on the unprecedented parental challenge of handling the near-certain prospect that children will hear of or see footage of the Dec. 3 U.S. execution by firing squad of Nidal Malik Hasan if the Trump administration follows through with plans to livestream the event.

The danger stretches beyond the broadcast itself, because history shows graphic video from the event could be clipped, copied and pushed into children’s social feeds even if the original stream is restricted.

*   [Selma Blair taken into custody in New York after an alleged assault on a Delta flight](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/world/selma-blair-taken-into-custody-in-new-york-after-an-alleged-assault-on-a-delta-flight/2444092)

Experts suggest that grownups who care about children start by setting aside matters of politics and public policy — like the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections and the debate over capital punishment. Focus instead on how witnessing someone's death by firing squad might land with young viewers — and how best to reassure and protect them.

Here are some guidelines that might help.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

**Keep empathy for kids in mind — and facts at hand**

Mis- and disinformation reach children, too. It's important for parents to have credibility with them, especially because their real, unspoken question might be: Are we safe? Have in hand some basic facts about the case and state them gently.

“It will be easier to have a position, share your family’s values, and discuss things with a potentially overwhelmed child once you’ve taken the time to gather accurate, up-to-date info and assess your child’s needs,” according to Common Sense Media, which advises parents on entertainment and technology.

*   ![Image 1: Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/lacson-asks-padilla-to-clarify-disregard-for-law-comment-on-duterte-trial/2444142)

Trump approved Hasan's execution by firing squad Dec. 3 at Fort Hood. A few days later, the Pentagon announced the event would be livestreamed.

“People need to understand that there’s serious consequences for these types of things,” Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told Real America's Voice, a conservative outlet.

Hasan, an Army psychiatrist, was convicted of killing 13 people there in 2009 when he walked into a medical building where soldiers were getting checkups and opened fire with a laser-sighted handgun. He said it was an effort to stop them from going to Afghanistan and killing his fellow Muslims. He made almost no effort to defend himself at trial. The U.S. military has not carried out the death penalty since 1961.

The last widely recognized public execution took place on Aug. 14, 1936. Kentucky, the last state to permit them, outlawed the practice in 1938.

*   ![Image 2: ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1257681.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/icc-prosecutor-removes-253-items-from-evidence-list-in-duterte-case/2444598)

**Stay updated on the plans**

Also, experts suggest, parents should stay updated on how a livestreamed execution would unfold. Many questions remained unanswered, such as whether the moment of death and its aftermath will be shown, whether any age restrictions will apply, and whether there will be a broadcast delay or a threshold for stopping the feed.

Be informed about the technology involved. While the government often uses YouTube to carry its livestreams, including those embedded within government websites, YouTube prohibits content that is “violent or gory” and “intended to shock or disgust viewers,” and doesn’t allow livestreams that show someone holding, handling or transporting a firearm.

YouTube does make exceptions in select cases for content it deems to be in an educational, documentary, scientific or artistic context or that it determines to be in the public’s interest. In such cases, the content may be age-restricted. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment regarding how its policies relate to the execution.

*   ![Image 3: 'Time for Alex to really regroup. A very disappointing loss' — Noli Eala](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256804.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
['Time for Alex to really regroup. A very disappointing loss' — Noli Eala](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/sports/time-for-alex-to-really-regroup-a-very-disappointing-loss-noli-eala/2444175)

But the danger to kids spills beyond the live broadcast to unexpected exposure on social media in the form of memes, for example.

It’s unclear whether the Trump administration is considering children in its decision-making. Emails over two days asking White House spokespeople for thoughts from the president and first lady Melania Trump on the prospect of children seeing the execution went unanswered. Trump said that he’ll soon make a decision on the plan to livestream the event.

**Assume kids will at least hear about the execution, if not see it**

From the old-fashioned grapevine to social media, grisly news has a way of reaching school-aged children, experts agree. Consider their need for calm and age-appropriate guidance, they suggest.

“With young kids, parents should keep it short and focus on reassurance over explaining the events,” said Jill Murphy, chief content officer at Common Sense Media. “Reassure them that they are safe. With teens, ask honestly what they have heard first, then ask whether they need to watch it.”

Remember you are your child's parent, not their friend — and don't overexplain, advises Dr. David Rosenberg, chair of psychiatry and behavioral neurosciences at Wayne State University School of Medicine in Michigan. Answer the questions children ask, and don't be afraid to assert parental authority by, for example, restricting or banning a child's access to the footage.

“It's okay to say, 'I don't have all the answers. But here's what we know, you're safe, you're secure, this is what we believe,'” Rosenberg said.

“Where parents get into trouble is when they talk too much, and they usually do that because they're anxious and insecure," he added. "What makes a child feel safest, or an adolescent, is can I count on my parents to be calm in challenging situations and give me the information I need?”

Choosing to watch the footage, one physician said, doesn’t necessarily indicate a child is psychologically ready to do so.

Timothy Lesaca, a Pittsburgh-area psychiatrist, cited a series of studies showing that repeatedly watching footage of events like the Boston Marathon bombings, at least part of an ISIS beheading video and the Oklahoma City bombing can be linked to post-traumatic stress, if not PTSD, in adults and children. He argues that making Hasan’s execution public is a medical and public health issue.

“Ongoing anxiety, trouble sleeping or problems with daily life should be taken seriously," Lesaca wrote in KevinMD.com, an online publication by physicians.

**Watch how this event interacts with existing conditions**

The people most at risk of negative long-term effects are those who already have clinical depression or anxiety, or who have already been exposed to other traumatic situations, Rosenberg said. That’s because repeat exposure to trauma can cause cumulative damage.

The part of the brain that handles executive decision-making, emotional regulation, impulsivity and empathy doesn’t finish developing until around age 24, and so parents should consider having proactive conversations even with their older children who may be away at college or living on their own, Rosenberg said.

“We have to at least offer help in these circumstances to be the leaders, to be the decision-makers, to at least help them make informed decisions."

title: El Niño Watch: the impacts around the world this week
summary: BANGKOK, Thailand — Food security concerns, wildfires and power warnings are among the impacts around the world this week from an exceptionally strong El Niño weather cycle. Here is a look at how this year's phenomenon, in which a warmer se
content:
BANGKOK, Thailand — Food security concerns, wildfires and power warnings are among the impacts around the world this week from an exceptionally strong El Niño weather cycle.

Here is a look at how this year's phenomenon, in which a warmer sea surface shifts global weather patterns, has been affecting people globally:

- Indonesia and Amazon fires, orangutans rescued - El Niño is associated with strong drought in Indonesia, where tracts of forest and plantations have been burning in biodiverse Borneo and the South Sumatra region for months.

*   [France, Eq. Guinea in standoff over luxury Paris mansion](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/world/americas-emea/france-eq-guinea-in-standoff-over-luxury-paris-mansion/2444867)

The fires have caused a regional haze crisis, with Malaysia last week closing schools in several regions and Singapore announcing subsidies for people seeking medical treatment for haze-linked illness.

**Malaysia has called for a meeting of regional body ASEAN to discuss the haze, and offered firefighting assistance.**

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Experts say years of deforestation and peatland drainage in Indonesia have made it more vulnerable to fires during dry periods.

The fires have sickened tens of thousands of people, while conservationists have rescued dozens of orangutans trapped by smoke and flames, including Novita, a female found clinging to a treetop with burns on her hands and feet.

"She had to leave her habitat, and we had to rescue her, primarily because of the flames," said Andi Muhammad Khadafi, head of the Central Kalimantan Natural Resources Conservation Agency.

*   ![Image 1: 'Time for Alex to really regroup. A very disappointing loss' — Noli Eala](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256804.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
['Time for Alex to really regroup. A very disappointing loss' — Noli Eala](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/sports/time-for-alex-to-really-regroup-a-very-disappointing-loss-noli-eala/2444175)

Haze from fires also blanketed Manaus, the largest city in the Brazilian Amazon, where public schools were shut on Friday.

Amazonas state recorded nearly four times more fire hotspots this September than the year before. On Wednesday alone, over 749 fires were burning.

**- Myanmar power outages, Philippines prepares -** Myanmar warned citizens to expect power outages as the electricity grid is strained by an unseasonal heatwave authorities blamed on El Nino.

"Due to the effects of severe El Niño conditions, temperatures across the country have risen significantly, resulting in increased electricity consumption," the energy ministry said.

*   ![Image 2: Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/lacson-asks-padilla-to-clarify-disregard-for-law-comment-on-duterte-trial/2444142)

Weather officials also warned the country to expect "abnormal" rainfall, drought, extreme heat and drinking water shortages.

In the Philippines, Energy Secretary Sharon Garin said the government was preparing for higher demand and the possibility of hydropower declines due to hotter and drier weather.

"The appeal is for the public to be aware of this so that we can all start having the mindset of energy savings," she said.

**- IMF 'very concerned' on food -** International Monetary Fund chief Kristalina Georgieva told AFP she is "very concerned" about El Niño's global impacts, particularly on food security.

*   ![Image 3: ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1257681.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/icc-prosecutor-removes-253-items-from-evidence-list-in-duterte-case/2444598)

The IMF is "getting ready" to offer support to countries that may struggle to absorb the impact, she added.

The United Nations Development Program also warned Sunday that the combined impacts of higher borrowing costs, surging energy prices and the powerful El Niño created "a perfect storm that could throw tens if not hundreds of millions of people back into poverty".

In southern Madagascar, aid workers told AFP they are already battling the effects of a famine and conditions are expected to worsen as El Niño's full impact on Africa takes hold from this month.

**- What scientists say -** El Niño will continue intensifying until a December peak, the UN's World Meteorological Organization said Thursday.

"It is likely to bring above-average temperatures to much of the globe and shift rainfall patterns, increasing the risk of drought and floods in different regions," the body said in its monthly update.

Sea-surface temperatures in a key monitoring region in the Pacific reached an "all-time high" last month, the European Union's Copernicus Climate Change Service said, while Japan's weather agency on Friday declared this El Niño was of "the strongest intensity on record".

Not all forecasters use the same scale to interpret El Niño, and the comparison is complicated by the background effects of climate change.

**- By the numbers -** 29.70C: the all-time high sea-surface temperature recorded in part of the Pacific by Copernicus

1: number of hurricanes this Atlantic season, which has been exceptionally light due to El Nino, unlike the busy Pacific season

71: death toll in Thailand floods since mid-September

46: orangutans rescued from Indonesia fires by authorities and conservation group YIARI between August and October 9

**- 'Super El Ni**ñ**o' explained -** El Niño is associated with higher global temperatures, and a stronger cycle intensifies the extreme weather patterns it brings to different regions, like drought or heavy rain.

This year's cycle has been called a "super El Niño" but the term many scientists use is "very strong".

The World Meteorological Organization last month said it expected this cycle to meet that definition before it peaks in December.

The benchmark for the definition is the sea-surface temperature anomaly in part of the Pacific Ocean, which is now at record levels.

Climate change complicates the picture because the oceans are now warmer, but scientists can strip out that background effect to determine the absolute rise.

title: HK sponsor workloads ease, but SFC warns on IPO funding tricks
summary: 香港证券及期货事务监察委员会报告称，经过监管审查，1 月至 9 月期间，过度扩张的保荐公司和签约委托人数量下降了 78%。它警告看门人对不透明的IPO融资计划和人为夸大的需求保持警惕 [![图1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 13 Oct 2026 at 20:53 HKT · 2 min read Hong Kong's securities regulator said on Tuesday that workloads and ca
content:
香港
香港证券及期货事务监察委员会报告称，经过监管审查，1 月至 9 月期间，过度扩张的保荐公司和签约委托人数量下降了 78%。它警告看门人对不透明的IPO融资计划和人为夸大的需求保持警惕

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

13 Oct 2026 at 20:53 HKT · 2 min read

香港证券监管机构周二表示，今年香港首次公开募股保荐人的工作量和能力限制有所缓解，但警告看门人要警惕不透明的融资计划和人为夸大的需求。

在一份监管​​通知中，证监会报告了自一月份启动监管审查以来整个保荐行业的可衡量的运营进展，并指出已采取建设性措施来解决资源瓶颈。证监会表示，1 月至 9 月期间，捉襟见肘的签约委托人和资源紧张的保荐公司数量均下降了 78%。
赞助商工作在整个市场的分布也变得更加广泛，五个最活跃的赞助商处理的活跃管道申请的份额从 1 月份的 77% 下降到 9 月份的 65%。监管机构通过加快新签约委托人的审批来支持该行业的努力，八个月内签约委托人数量同比激增 65%。

However, the watchdog stressed that deficiencies persisted and quality control remains under tight scrutiny.证监会在 1 月至 9 月期间暂停了 65 份上市申请的审核程序，并向 11 家保荐人发出正式书面质询，理由是其业务实质存在问题和尽职审查不足。

证监会还对某些首次公开招股中的可疑安排表示严重关注，据称上市申请人向指定投资者或关连方提供未披露的认购资金或保证回报。监管机构表示，此类做法扭曲了市场需求，损害了公平价格发现，并使公众面临上市后交易的操纵性。

包括保荐人、总体协调人和资本市场中介机构在内的把关人被指示留意危险信号，例如上市前后不久的大量预付款、贷款或资金流动，使首次公开募股投资者受益，以及隐藏最终投资者身份的结构。
证监会行政总裁梁凤仪在声明中表示，“自一月份以来市场取得的进展值得欢迎，保荐人能力和管理监督的改善将为严格把关和优质上市奠定基础。” “与此同时，中介机构必须对与可疑安排相关的警告信号保持警惕，并对任何不合逻辑的事情提出质疑。证监会会毫不犹豫地对少数不良行为者采取行动。”

Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission reported a 78 per cent drop in overstretched sponsor firms and signing principals between January and September, following regulatory scrutiny. It warned gatekeepers to remain vigilant against opaque IPO financing schemes and artificially inflated demand

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

13 Oct 2026 at 20:53 HKT · 2 min read

Hong Kong's securities regulator said on Tuesday that workloads and capacity constraints among the city's initial public offering sponsors have eased this year, but warned gatekeepers to guard against opaque financing schemes and artificially inflated demand.

In a regulatory circular, the Securities and Futures Commission reported measurable operational progress across the sponsor industry following regulatory scrutiny initiated in January, noting that constructive steps had been taken to resolve resource bottlenecks. The number of overstretched signing principals and resource-strained sponsor firms both dropped by 78 per cent between January and September, the SFC said.

Sponsor work also became more broadly distributed across the market, with the share of active pipeline applications handled by the five most active sponsors falling to 65 per cent in September from 77 per cent in January. The regulator supported the industry's efforts by expediting approvals for new signing principals, which surged 65 per cent year-on-year over the eight months.

However, the watchdog stressed that deficiencies persisted and quality control remains under tight scrutiny. The SFC suspended the vetting process for 65 listing applications between January and September and issued formal written inquiries to 11 sponsors over questionable business substance and deficient due diligence.

The SFC also flagged serious concerns over dubious arrangements in certain IPOs, where listing applicants allegedly provided undisclosed subscription funds or guaranteed returns to designated investors or connected parties. Such practices distort market demand, impair fair price discovery, and expose the public to manipulative post-listing trading, the regulator said.

Gatekeepers, including sponsors, overall coordinators, and capital market intermediaries, were instructed to watch for red flags, such as substantial prepayments, loans, or fund flows shortly before or after listing that benefit IPO investors, as well as structures that conceal ultimate investor identities.

"The market progress made since January is welcome, improved sponsor capacity and management oversight would strengthen the foundation for rigorous gatekeeping and quality listings," SFC chief executive Julia Leung Fund-yee said in the statement. "At the same time, intermediaries must remain alert to the warning signs associated with questionable arrangements, and challenge anything that does not add up. The SFC will not hesitate to act against the few bad actors."

title: Remulla tags Subic as ‘smuggling capital’
summary: THE Port of Subic has come under fresh scrutiny after being branded the country’s “smuggling capital” by Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla, as the Bureau of Customs (BOC) uncovered P29.17 million worth of cigarettes concealed in a shipment de
content:
THE Port of Subic has come under fresh scrutiny after being branded the country’s “smuggling capital” by Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla, as the Bureau of Customs (BOC) uncovered P29.17 million worth of cigarettes concealed in a shipment declared as scrap metal.

The latest bust involved 320 boxes of Astro and Redwood cigarettes discovered during spot checks on two 20-foot containers shipped from Zamboanga at the Subport of North Harbor, with assistance from the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency’s K9 unit.

One container yielded the cigarettes, which did not match the shipment’s declaration, while the other contained boxes of white cigarette filters bearing Chinese markings, the BOC said.

*   [10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

The seized cigarettes have an estimated import value of P9.6 million and a market value of P29.17 million.

The BOC did not disclose the consignee or importer or clarify whether the cigarette filters were also seized.

The discovery adds to a series of major smuggling-related enforcement actions involving Subic, including the destruction in August of three 40-foot containers containing about 3,000 cases of cigarettes worth P129.065 million.

The cigarettes were part of a 10-container batch of abandoned goods valued at P413 million, with the disposal of the remaining shipments still underway at the time of the report.

He also pointed to the seizure of several containers of smuggled cigarettes in Cebu aboard a vessel owned by Gothong Lines.

The Ombudsman also criticized the BOC over what he described as repeated failures to provide complete documentation needed to investigate and prosecute smuggling cases.

“Lagi sa customs ayaw nila kumpletuhin ang documentation para ma-dismiss ang kaso,” Remulla said, alleging that requested documents often failed to reach investigators, undermining efforts to file cases and hold suspects accountable.

In response, BOC Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno reaffirmed the bureau’s commitment to improving interagency coordination, saying timely access to records and information is essential to effective enforcement and successful prosecution.

Nepomuceno said the BOC would continue cooperating with the Office of the Ombudsman, DOJ, and other partner agencies, adding that the bureau supports lawful requests for information and is strengthening its systems to improve data sharing.

“Smuggling is a challenge that requires a united government response,” Nepomuceno said, vowing continued cooperation and transparency to protect government revenues and prevent illicit goods from entering the market.

title: Cebu hospital defends one-watcher rule amid viral post
summary: CEBU CITY — The Vicente Sotto Memorial Medical Center (VSMMC) defended its one-watcher-per-patient policy following online criticism over viral photos showing relatives of hospitalized patients sleeping by the roadside outside the hospital.
content:
CEBU CITY — The Vicente Sotto Memorial Medical Center (VSMMC) defended its one-watcher-per-patient policy following online criticism over viral photos showing relatives of hospitalized patients sleeping by the roadside outside the hospital.

In a statement, the Department of Health-run hospital acknowledged the difficulties faced by families who travel from different parts of Cebu and neighboring provinces to seek medical care for their loved ones, particularly those without a place to stay while patients remain confined.

The VSMMC said it must balance the needs of patients and their families with safety, security, infection prevention and control, and the orderly delivery of healthcare services.

*   [COA flags Mandaue’s P55M Christmas expenditure](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/regions/coa-flags-mandaues-p55m-christmas-expenditure/2443100)

Under Hospital Order 2024-123, only one screened and authorized watcher may stay at a patient’s bedside. The hospital said the policy helps prevent overcrowding in patient care areas and allows healthcare workers to provide safe, efficient and uninterrupted medical services amid increasing patient numbers and referrals.

It also said that the restriction does not intend to separate patients from their families but to manage limited hospital space and resources while ensuring the safety of everyone inside the facility.

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The hospital also recognized the difficulties faced by companions who have no immediate place to stay while their loved ones receive treatment inside the hospital.

VSMMC said it previously worked with local government partners to provide temporary accommodation for eligible patient watchers and companions. Under the arrangement, buses transported them to designated temporary housing facilities and brought them back to the hospital during appropriate visiting and caregiving periods.

However, the hospital discontinued the initiative after some watchers and companions stopped using the accommodation and scheduled transportation services, resulting in lower participation.

*   ![Image 1: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

VSMMC said it remains open to coordinating with government and community partners to explore sustainable options for families who genuinely need temporary shelter while their loved ones undergo treatment.

As part of its long-term response, the hospital is constructing a new building with a ground-floor area intended for watchers and companions of patients in the Emergency Room.

“While this facility is a significant step toward addressing the needs of patient watchers and companions, VSMMC recognizes that the available space may not, by itself, be sufficient to accommodate the needs of all patients and their families,” the hospital said.

The medical center did not specify the building’s expected completion date or the capacity of the planned companion area.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

VSMMC also clarified that not everyone staying around its premises is accompanying a hospitalized patient. Some may be experiencing homelessness or lack stable housing and may have sought temporary refuge in the area for reasons unrelated to a patient’s confinement.

The hospital said concerns involving these individuals require coordination with social welfare offices, local government units and other concerned agencies.

While acknowledging that loitering and vagrancy may fall beyond its direct scope and control, VSMMC said it remains willing to work with authorities and local governments to explore appropriate measures.

The hospital also urged the public to verify information about its policies, services and operations through official communication channels before sharing posts online.

*   ![Image 3: Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254827.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/marcos-names-lino-cayetano-new-pco-chief/2443262)

It appealed for sensitivity when documenting or posting situations involving patients, their families, watchers and healthcare workers, emphasizing the importance of protecting their privacy, dignity and welfare.

VSMMC said it welcomes legitimate public concerns and constructive dialogue but urged people not to turn the experiences of patients and their families into social media content unrelated to patient welfare or public information.

The hospital reiterated its commitment to providing quality healthcare while maintaining a safe, orderly and dignified environment for patients, family members, authorized watchers and healthcare workers.

title: UST activist suspensions: Testing the boundaries of academic freedom and student rights
summary: THE University of Santo Tomas suspended four student activists after they faced disciplinary complaints following a confrontation with military personnel at a Philippine Air Force (PAF) exhibit on campus on April 21, 2026. In addition to th
content:
THE University of Santo Tomas suspended four student activists after they faced disciplinary complaints following a confrontation with military personnel at a Philippine Air Force (PAF) exhibit on campus on April 21, 2026. In addition to the suspension, the university will withhold certificates of good moral character from the four students, effectively ousting one of them from a student council officer position.

The case stemmed from the confrontation at the PAF exhibit, held as part of UST’s 415th anniversary celebrations. The student activists heckled Air Force personnel about military equipment and operations, as well as alleged human rights abuses, two days after an armed encounter in Toboso, Negros Occidental, that left 19 people dead.

The UST Central Student Council criticized the university’s decision, saying the suspensions amounted to the “weaponization of the student handbook” and would prevent students from exercising dissent. The student council wrote an open letter to Pope Leo XIV, asking the pontiff to intervene against the alleged suppression of UST.

*   [Quo haec patria tendit?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/opinion/columns/quo-haec-patria-tendit/2443321)

**UST’s academic freedom and students’ right to free speech**

In determining whether the UST suspension move was proper or violated students’ rights requires the application of two constitutional guarantees: students’ right to freedom of speech and expression, and the academic freedom of institutions of higher learning. In other words, was the sanction within UST’s valid exercise of academic freedom? Or did it violate students’ rights to freedom of speech and expression?

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

While schools and universities are unique environments devoted to learning and discipline, they are not places where constitutional freedoms are completely left at the gate. Educational institutions like the University of Santo Tomas must balance their authority to maintain school peace and order with their duty to respect and protect students’ fundamental liberties while on campus.

**Jurisprudence on students’ free speech**

The landmark US case Tinker v. Des Moines firmly established that students and teachers do not shed their constitutional rights to freedom of speech and expression upon entering the schoolhouse gate. Tinker introduced the now-classic standard that school authorities may regulate student expression only when it materially and substantially interferes with school activities or contradicts reasonable disciplinary policies. Note, however, that in Tinker, the students are participating in a public educational institution, not a private university like UST.

*   ![Image 1: Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254827.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/marcos-names-lino-cayetano-new-pco-chief/2443262)

Building on this principle, key Philippine Supreme Court decisions — Malabanan v. Ramento, Villar v. Technological Institute of the Philippines, and Non v. Dames — adapt and apply it in the Philippine context. These cases recognize that student assemblies, rallies and protests, even when critical of school policies, are generally protected forms of expression so long as they do not create a clear and present danger to the educational process. At the same time, they affirm that schools may regulate the time, place and manner of such activities and impose penalties, provided they are lawful, proportionate, and respect due process.

In the UST incident, did the students obtain prior permission from the university administration before they held protests against guests from the Armed Forces of the Philippines? Was the venue of such protest valid based on applicable university rules?

On the other hand, did UST observe administrative due process in the disciplinary case involving the students before imposing the suspensions and accessory penalties? Are these sanctions proportionate to the gravity of the offense committed, consistently imposed, and imposed in good faith?

A central theme running through these issues is the tension between the university’s academic freedom and students’ rights. Institutions of higher learning, such as UST, have the prerogative to set academic standards and to enforce discipline. This pertains specifically to the freedom of the university to determine “who shall be admitted to study.” However, this prerogative cannot be used as a pretext to silence dissent or discriminate against students for exercising their constitutional freedoms.

*   ![Image 2: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

On the other hand, the university’s obligation to respect students’ right to education, along with their rights to free speech and peaceful assembly, also implies students’ obligation to follow the institution’s established rules. They cannot simply hold lightning rallies without the proper permit or outside designated areas on campus. Students should also observe proper conduct even when protesting, as these policies still apply. They cannot disrespect persons in authority, such as the PAF personnel.

After all, educational institutions such as the University of Santo Tomas have a constitutional mandate to instill personal discipline and inculcate patriotism and nationalism, among other values. The university’s authority to promulgate its own rules governing student discipline aligns not only with the constitutional guarantee of academic freedom but also with its duty to shape the character of the youth.

Ultimately, while upholding students’ rights to freedom of speech and expression as vital, universities like the University of Santo Tomas must also exercise academic freedom to maintain discipline and order in the academic environment. The institution’s authority to set standards and enforce guidelines is essential to fostering a conducive atmosphere for learning and growth. Upholding academic integrity and ensuring respectful dialogue help prepare students for responsible citizenship. By navigating this delicate balance, UST can cultivate an environment where respectful discourse thrives while maintaining the discipline and order necessary in an academic setting.

title: Trump, Zelenskyy clash over diesel deal as Russian strikes kill 21
summary: **WASHINGTON— ‎**US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy traded barbs Saturday after Washington moved to ease sanctions on Russian diesel and Moscow's continued strikes on Ukraine killed at least 21 people, includ
content:
**WASHINGTON— ‎**US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy traded barbs Saturday after Washington moved to ease sanctions on Russian diesel and Moscow's continued strikes on Ukraine killed at least 21 people, including four children.

Trump, whose party faces dim prospects in next month's midterm elections partly over soaring US fuel prices, announced Friday that he had called Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin and agreed to allow Moscow to release large amounts of diesel onto global markets.

Ukraine and its European allies expressed dismay at the move, with Zelenskyy telling reporters Friday it was a "weak decision."

*   [Taiwan ups defense spending to ‘deter war’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/world/asia-oceania/taiwan-ups-defense-spending-to-deter-war/2443116)

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas meanwhile said on Saturday that lifting sanctions on Russian diesel would only help fuel the Kremlin's war on Ukraine.

"This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won't," she wrote online.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Asked about the criticism on Saturday, Trump told reporters that Zelenskyy had disobeyed his orders not to strike Russian refineries. Trump said the strikes risk worsening global fuel shortages caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran.

"He better damn well stop," Trump said of the strikes, before adding that Ukraine should "get a new president."

"I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal, because he could have made many deals that, for some reason, he never does," Trump said.

*   ![Image 1: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254518.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

**Deadly Ukraine bombardment**

Moscow has intensified its deadly bombardment of Ukraine in recent months, sending civilian casualties soaring, while US-led efforts to broker an end to the more than four-and-a-half-year conflict remain deadlocked.

Early Saturday, a Russian glide bomb attack on the southeastern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia killed 20 people, including three children, according to Ukraine's state rescue service.

"Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia," Zelenskyy said in a post on X.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

An AFP correspondent at the scene saw rescuers pulling people from the rubble.

"We saw people under the rubble -- a woman, her husband and a child," one rescuer, Daniil Pishkin, told AFP.

He added that he saw two people rescued from the wreckage but "unfortunately there was a little girl who died".

A resident of one of the buildings that was hit, who identified herself as Iryna, 69, said she just had time to seek refuge in the bathroom after receiving an air raid warning.

*   ![Image 3: DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254558.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

Her two neighbors were killed, she said.

"They were 75 years old. They were simply thrown out there, onto the street. They didn't make it to the hospital," she told AFP.

A Russian drone attack on Ukraine's central Dnipropetrovsk region killed an 11-year-old boy, the region's governor said.

Russian strikes meanwhile triggered large-scale power outages in the capital Kyiv, Ukraine's DTEK energy provider said, as the city's mayor reported a strike on a restaurant.

AFP reporters heard booms over Kyiv earlier in the day.

The Russian defense ministry said it had hit a "data center" used by Ukraine's military.

**Trump's talk with Putin**

The announcement on Friday of the diesel deal came as US, Ukrainian and European officials were meeting in Miami, in a renewed diplomatic push to end the war.

Ukraine's delegation was headed home on Saturday, an aide to Zelenskyy said.

Trump, who has repeatedly touted his credentials as a peacemaker, has long sought to broker a deal since taking office last January.

US envoy Steve Witkoff posted to X after the meeting that the "constructive discussions" tackled "potential avenues to de-escalate and conclude the war with Russia ahead of winter and advance efforts toward a durable and lasting peace".

Witkoff said the meeting included "the E3, the European Commission, Ukraine and NATO".

The Kremlin said Saturday that Trump had conveyed his ideas about how to de-escalate the war to Putin during a phone call on Friday.

Putin received the proposals "with understanding", the Kremlin said, without elaborating on what the proposals were or the Russian president's response.

Russia, which launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, now occupies roughly one-fifth of Ukrainian territory.

title: New logic of modern data center
summary: BUSINESS growth in Asia-Pacific is entering a new phase. The sustained increase in data, process automation, and the advancement of artificial intelligence are redefining the way enterprises compete and operate. In this scenario, computing
content:
BUSINESS growth in Asia-Pacific is entering a new phase. The sustained increase in data, process automation, and the advancement of artificial intelligence are redefining the way enterprises compete and operate.

In this scenario, computing has ceased to be a technical support function and has become a strategic factor, directly linked to productivity and growth capacity.

The growing adoption of artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, and automation is increasing the demands placed on enterprise technology infrastructure. As models and workloads become more complex, organizations require platforms that can scale efficiently while maintaining performance and optimizing energy consumption. In this context, modern computing architectures are evolving toward models that enable greater processing capacity to be consolidated within a smaller physical infrastructure footprint. The typical result is a more efficient operation, with reduced space, power, and management requirements. In fact, comparing a solution powered by 5th Gen AMD EPYC processors to a legacy solution to deliver the same workload showed that the EPYC solution could reduce the number of servers required by up to 86 percent, lower energy consumption by as much as 69 percent, and decrease total cost of ownership (TCO) by up to 41 percent over a three-year period.

*   [Accentuate professional development better at Accenture](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/business/accentuate-professional-development-better-at-accenture/2442156)

[![Image 1: TRANSFORMATIONAL SHIFT Growing adoption of artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, and automation is increasing the demands placed on enterprise technology infrastructure. AI-GENERATED GRAPHICS](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254162.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254162.jpg)
TRANSFORMATIONAL SHIFT Growing adoption of artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, and automation is increasing the demands placed on enterprise technology infrastructure. AI-GENERATED GRAPHICS

This shift is driving a transformation in data center architecture. The model based on physical expansion — more servers, more space, more consumption — is being replaced by schemes that prioritize efficiency, compute density and load consolidation. In practice, this means doing more with less: running more applications on fewer servers, reducing costs and operational complexity.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The approach can have a direct impact on total cost of ownership (TCO). By optimizing the use of existing infrastructure, companies can reduce energy consumption, reduce space requirements and simplify technology management. This approach is especially relevant in markets such as the Philippines, where operational efficiency has become a key factor in sustaining competitiveness.

At the same time, energy efficiency has become a priority. Electricity consumption represents one of the main costs in data centers, so improving performance per unit of energy not only has a financial impact but also affects the sustainability commitments that more and more companies are assuming.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Another central element is scalability. Organizations require infrastructure capable of adapting to variations in demand, especially in environments where artificial intelligence demands real-time processing. Frictionless scaling allows you to accelerate service deployment and respond more quickly to market needs.

In the Philippines’ case, this change in focus offers potential benefits: greater processing capacity without the need for physical expansion, reduced operating costs and an infrastructure prepared to sustain future growth. In an environment where digital transformation is progressing unevenly, the adoption of more efficient models can make a significant difference in terms of competitiveness.

In this sense, recent technological evolution points toward more compact, efficient platforms designed for modern workloads. The focus is no longer on the volume of infrastructure but on its capacity for performance and optimization.

The breaking point is clear: the future of the data center is not necessarily about growing in size but about improving efficiency. Consolidating loads and optimizing resources has become a strategic decision to help reduce costs and sustain growth in the digital economy.

*   ![Image 3: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

As a final reflection, the opportunity for companies in the Philippines is not only to adopt new technologies but to do so with a strategic approach. Organizations that understand that computing is the core of their growth, and not just a support function, will be better positioned to capture the value of artificial intelligence. Today, efficiency is not optional; it is the basis on which tomorrow’s competitiveness is built.

title: When persuasion begins to erode trust
summary: AT A RECENT marketing community event, I shared with a peer why I have become more selective about where I spend my time online. Facebook and LinkedIn increasingly feel like crowded marketplaces of expertise, with professionals competing fo
content:
AT A RECENT marketing community event, I shared with a peer why I have become more selective about where I spend my time online. Facebook and LinkedIn increasingly feel like crowded marketplaces of expertise, with professionals competing for attention through articles, commentary, advice and carefully produced content. Artificial intelligence (AI) has made it easier to participate in this competition. Still, I have begun questioning whether producing more content in already crowded feeds is necessarily the best way to build meaningful connections.

During our conversation, my peer raised another concern: the amount of manipulative content circulating on social media. Even the way some posts are scripted can make readers feel that their emotions or decisions are being deliberately influenced. The observation stayed with me because it pointed to a problem beyond content saturation. When people become suspicious of what they encounter online, even useful information may struggle to earn their confidence.

Marketing has always involved persuasion. Businesses communicate value, appeal to customer needs and encourage people to act. Storytelling is part of this process because decisions are influenced not only by facts but also by experiences, aspirations and emotions. The concern is not that businesses want to influence decisions. It is whether they do so in ways that respect the audience’s ability to make informed choices.

*   [When security creates friction, employees find workarounds](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/business/sunday-business-it/when-security-creates-friction-employees-find-workarounds/2443042)

**When polished content raises questions**

While preparing a digital storytelling session for tourism stakeholders in two provinces lately, I explored how a destination could be communicated through information, promotion and storytelling. Information helps travelers understand what is available. Promotion gives them reasons to consider a destination. Storytelling helps them imagine what an experience might mean to them.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

AI can now help transform a narrative into realistic images, videos and social media materials. This creates opportunities for smaller businesses that previously lacked the resources for professional content production. However, it also introduces questions about authenticity. An imagined visitor experience can look convincing even when no such visit occurred.

Fictional illustrations have legitimate uses in marketing and education, provided audiences are not misled about their nature. Problems arise when invented experiences resemble actual customer testimonials or when edited visuals create expectations that the business cannot fulfill.

There is also a less obvious consequence. As people become more familiar with AI-generated content, they may question genuine photographs and stories simply because they appear unusually polished. Businesses therefore face a communication challenge that cannot be solved by improving production quality alone.

*   ![Image 1: Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253968.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/senate-impeachment-court-to-rule-on-dropped-bribery-charge-next-week/2442987)

**Difference between persuasion, manipulation**

Manipulation does not require AI. Misleading claims, selective information, manufactured urgency and exaggerated emotional appeals existed long before generative tools became widely available. AI can make producing and adapting such messages faster, but the responsibility remains with those deciding what to communicate.

A story can be emotional without being manipulative. A customer sharing a meaningful experience may help others appreciate a product or service. But when a business invents that experience, omits important limitations or creates pressure that prevents thoughtful evaluation, it risks crossing a different line.

This distinction matters because successful communication does not end when someone clicks, inquires or makes a purchase. The customer eventually encounters the actual product, service or experience. If reality falls short of the impression created, the attention gained through marketing may come at the expense of confidence in the business.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

**Why relationships matter again**

My growing preference for Viber communities and participation in professional associations reflects a different approach to communication. I still value Facebook and LinkedIn, but I increasingly prefer spaces where conversations can continue beyond a single post and where people have opportunities to get to know one another through shared activities and discussions.

These environments are not automatically more trustworthy. Misleading content and self-promotion can appear anywhere. What makes them useful to me is the additional context that relationships provide. When people have interacted with someone, asked questions and observed how that person responds, they have more information on which to form their judgments.

This also changes how I think about visibility. Reaching a large audience is useful, but it is not the only measure of meaningful communication. A smaller group of people who read, question, respond and remember may contribute more to a lasting professional relationship than a much larger audience that encounters a post briefly before moving on.

*   ![Image 3: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

For businesses, the implication is not to abandon social media or stop using AI. Both remain valuable for communication, discovery and customer engagement. The opportunity is to connect digital visibility with experiences and relationships that support the claims being made.

As creating persuasive content becomes easier, the challenge may increasingly shift from attracting attention to sustaining confidence. Businesses will still need compelling messages, but those messages must be supported by accurate information, credible behavior and experiences that justify customer expectations.

Perhaps the more useful question is no longer how to become more convincing online, but how to give people genuine reasons to believe us.

title: No first-round bye for Eala at Wuhan

content:
DUE to a smaller draw, projected No.13 seed Alexandra “Alex” Eala won’t receive a first-round bye at the WTA 1000 Wuhan Open in China.

[![Image 1: Alexandra ‘Alex’ Eala POC PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254216.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254216.jpg)

The Filipino tennis ace will compete in the tournament — her first Tour event after a bronze medal finish at the 20th Asian Games in Japan — slated from Oct. 12 to 18.

Unlike most 1000 events where 96 players make up the field and the top 32 players receive first-round byes, Wuhan is limited to a 56-player draw.

In this case, only the top eight get to skip the first round and start their campaign in the second.

The same rule applies to the only two other 1000 events with a 56-player draw in Doha and Dubai.

**JERUSALEM —** The axe-wielding co-pilot who attacked the captain of a FlyDubai flight to Tel Aviv last month intended to seize control of the airplane and fly it into the passenger terminal at Israel’s main international airport, authorities in the United Arab Emirates said Friday.

The suspect, an Omani national, did so “with the intention of causing the greatest possible number of human casualties,” the UAE’s top prosecutor said in a statement carried by the state news agency WAM. Most of the 174 passengers on the flight were from Israel.

The statement said the co-pilot “drew inspiration” from the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks in the United States and used two previous flights from Dubai to Tel Aviv to “familiarize himself with the flight route and the airport.”

*   [Japan protests Russia’s extradition requests for ICC president Tomoko Akane and 8 other court staff](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/world/americas-emea/japan-protests-russias-extradition-requests-for-icc-president-tomoko-akane-and-8-other-court-staff/2442504)

It said none of FlyDubai's security or professional checks had indicated that the pilot, who was identitifed by The Associated Press as 29-year-old Hamam al-Hammami, harbored extremist views or plans to carry out an attack.

Hammami “admitted that he had acted alone, without the involvement of others,” the statement said, adding that he “provided a detailed confession outlining his motives and the stages of planning and execution” in the presence of his lawyer. It also suggested he was radicalized at a mosque in Australia while attending the Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology in 2017.

The crisis unfolded suddenly in the skies above Jordan and Saudi Arabia, when Hammami attacked the captain, Smit Machchhar, with a crash axe in the cockpit. Bloodied and beaten, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, alerting passengers and crew to the assault.

title: Haze prompts school closures in Malaysia
summary: **KUALA LUMPUR** — Malaysia closed schools in Kuala Lumpur and other parts of the country on Friday as haze from fires in neighboring Indonesia again plunged local air quality to among the world’s worst. Toxic smoke from peatland and forest
content:
**KUALA LUMPUR** — Malaysia closed schools in Kuala Lumpur and other parts of the country on Friday as haze from fires in neighboring Indonesia again plunged local air quality to among the world’s worst.

Toxic smoke from peatland and forest fires has shrouded cities in the region for more than a month, sending respiratory complaints skyrocketing.

The school closures came as Malaysia’s leader discussed the choking smoke with his Indonesian counterpart and called for an urgent regional meeting.

*   [Trump: No new Iran attack before midterms](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/world/americas-emea/trump-no-new-iran-attack-before-midterms/2442642)

Air quality in Kuala Lumpur has been firmly in “unhealthy levels” this week, with a Swiss-based air quality monitor ranking the Malaysian capital among the world’s most polluted cities on most days.

Malaysia’s Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said she has instructed whole school closures in four states and two federal territories, as well as one partial closure in central Pahang state.

Malaysia’s king, Sultan Ibrahim, weighed in on the matter on Thursday, saying schools should be closed as air quality readings reached 150 or higher on the Air Pollutant Index (API).

Under Malaysian guidelines, API readings above 100 are classified as unhealthy, above 200 as very unhealthy and above 300 as hazardous. Reading beyond 500 constitute the threshold for declaring a local emergency.

Kuala Lumpur on Friday showed a reading of around 170 API.

The city was the second-most polluted globally behind neighboring Singapore on Friday morning, Swiss-based air monitor IQAir said.

“And he also agreed to take the necessary steps,” the premier added, without going into specific details.

He said Malaysia has been taking measures to combat the haze, including increasing attempts to trigger rain via cloud seeding.

Experts said the flames were being fanned by a turbo-charged El Niño weather phenomenon, causing the worst pollution conditions in years.

Anwar said he had asked Malaysia’s Foreign Minister Mohamad Hasan to contact the 11-nation Association of Southeast Asian Nations’ secretariat for an urgent meeting between environmental ministers to discuss the matter.

“So these are all the steps we are taking, but we are monitoring and will try the measures that we ought to take next,” Anwar said.

Singapore’s air quality levels also dipped into the “very unhealthy” range, with a reading of 205 on the Air Quality Index (AQI), according to the IQAir website.

The AQI converts measurements of pollutants into a single figure indicating air quality and potential health risks.

Readings above 150 are classified as unhealthy, while levels above 300 are considered hazardous.

title: Xinjiang’s “Blue Miracle”
summary: 2025 年 8 月 21 日，新疆维吾尔自治区吐鲁番市的冷水鱼养殖基地。_图片来源：Gou Lifeng/新华社 [Getty]图片](https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/this-photo-taken-on-aug-21-2025-shows-a-cold-water-fish-news-photo/2287190051?phrase=fish%20farm%20xinjian&adppopup=true)_中国的新疆地区，位于该国西北边陲，是一片无情的极端。新疆西南边境矗立着世界第二高峰乔戈里峰，海拔 28,251 英尺。 K2 所在的喀喇昆仑山脉只是毗邻的四大山脉之一
content:
2025 年 8 月 21 日，新疆维吾尔自治区吐鲁番市的冷水鱼养殖基地。_图片来源：Gou Lifeng/新华社 [Getty]图片](https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/this-photo-taken-on-aug-21-2025-shows-a-cold-water-fish-news-photo/2287190051?phrase=fish%20farm%20xinjian&adppopup=true)_

中国的新疆地区位于该国西北边陲，是一片严酷的极端之地。新疆西南边境矗立着世界第二高峰乔戈里峰，海拔 28,251 英尺。

乔戈里峰所在的喀喇昆仑山脉只是毗邻、穿过或环绕新疆的四大山脉之一。昆仑河沿该省东南边境流淌；阿尔泰山位于新疆北部，天山横跨其中心。这些山脉虽然景色令人叹为观止，但同时也导致新疆大部分地区缺乏水分。新疆 60 万平方英里的土地上每年降雨量只有不到 6 英寸。

中国新疆塔克拉玛干沙漠一座石油小镇的鸟瞰图。 _图片来源：郑通过 [Adobe Stock](https://stock.adobe.com/images/aerial-view-of-a-small-oil-town-in-the-heart-of-the-taklamakan-desert-in-xin Jiang-china/1844330384?prev\_url=detail)_

新疆大片地区被中国最大的沙漠塔克拉玛干沙漠占据。塔克拉玛干不断变化的沙丘最高可达 600 英尺，比埃及吉萨大金字塔还要高。
总的来说，新疆适合人类居住的面积还不到10%。那些勉强维持生计的人大多是游牧民，他们和家人在天山和昆仑山顶冰川提供的少量绿洲周围找到了避难所。历史上，新疆的土著居民包括突厥维吾尔族、汉族、哈萨克族、蒙古族和塔吉克族。

中国中央当局长期以来一直满足于将新疆视为抵御西方外部威胁的偏远而崎岖的战略缓冲地带。然而，1949年革命后不久，国家开始将新疆想象为不仅仅是一个荒凉的前哨基地，而是一块值得驯服和剥削的宝贵领土，它的人民被说服或征召加入中国进入现代世界的行列，并最终加入中国争夺全球经济霸权的运动。

新疆塔里木油田探井。 _来源：国资委_

从 20 世纪 50 年代开始，中国政府地质学家在新疆的三个地形盆地——塔里木盆地、准噶尔盆地和吐哈盆地——发现了石油和天然气，并开展了一些有史以来最深的钻探项目。新疆成为西气东输管道的西部支柱，这是一项于 2004 年竣工的重大工程，将天然气输送到上海等城市超过 2,400 英里。
与此同时，国家对新疆最长的塔里木河进行了改造，以期将该省坚硬干燥的土壤变成耕地。塔里木河支流上修建了水库；分水闸测量并分配流量，衬砌的运河将水输送到新平整的农田。塔里木河曾经是一条不起眼的水道，在干旱的土地上容易发生季节性洪水，但突然间变成了一个高度监管和可靠的供水系统。对塔里木河的控制利用将有助于推动新疆一系列农作物的种植，包括积极推动棉花的种植和收获。

[视频13](https://www.thewirechina.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Troops-Xin Jiang.mp4)

【原文 English Original】
A cold-water fish breeding base in Turpan, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, August 21, 2025. _Credit: Gou Lifeng/Xinhua via [Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/this-photo-taken-on-aug-21-2025-shows-a-cold-water-fish-news-photo/2287190051?phrase=fish%20farm%20xinjiang&adppopup=true)_

China’s Xinjiang region, located on the country’s far northwest frontier, is a land of unforgiving extremes. At Xinjiang’s southwest border stands K2, the second-highest mountain in the world at 28,251 feet.

The Karakoram Range, where K2 is situated, is just one of four major ranges abutting, slicing through, or ringing Xinjiang. The Kunlun runs along the province’s southeastern border; the Altai is found in Xinjiang’s northern reaches, and the Tian Shan spans its center. Together, the mountains, while breathtaking to look at, work to keep much of Xinjiang starved of moisture. Barely six inches of rain fall every year across Xinjiang’s 600,000 square miles.

An aerial view of a small oil town in the Taklamakan Desert in Xinjiang, China. _Credit: Zheng via [Adobe Stock](https://stock.adobe.com/images/aerial-view-of-a-small-oil-town-in-the-heart-of-the-taklamakan-desert-in-xinjiang-china/1844330384?prev\_url=detail)_

A huge swath of Xinjiang is taken up by China’s largest desert, the Taklamakan. The Taklamakan’s ever-shifting dunes can top 600 feet, taller than the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt.

In total, less than 10 percent of Xinjiang has ever been fit for human habitation. Those who have eked out an existence have mostly been nomadic herdsmen, with refuge for them and their families found around a modest number of oases fed by mountaintop glaciers in the Tian Shan and Kunlun. Historically, Xinjiang’s native populations have included Turkic Uyghurs, Han Chinese, Kazakhs, Mongols, and Tajiks.

Central Chinese authorities were long content to regard Xinjiang as a remote and rugged strategic buffer against an outside threat from the west. Shortly after the 1949 revolution, though, the state began to imagine Xinjiang as more than a wild outpost, and rather as a valuable territorial holding to be tamed and exploited, its people persuaded or conscripted to join China’s emergence into the modern world, and, in time, its campaign for global economic supremacy.

Exploratory wells, Tarim oilfield, Xinjiang. _Credit: SASAC_

Beginning in the 1950s, Chinese government geologists discovered oil and gas in three of Xinjiang’s topographical basins — the Tarim, Junggar, and Tuha — and mounted some of the deepest drilling programs ever seen. Xinjiang became the western anchor of what was called the West-East Gas Pipeline, a monumental project completed in 2004 that sends natural gas over 2,400 miles to cities such as Shanghai.

At the same time, the state reengineered the Tarim River, Xinjiang’s longest, in a bid to turn the province’s hard and dry soil into farmable land. Reservoirs were built on the Tarim’s tributaries; diversion gates measured and allocated flow, and lined canals carried water to what would become newly leveled farmland. The Tarim, once an unremarkable waterway prone to seasonal flooding in an otherwise parched landscape, was suddenly a highly regulated and reliable supply system. The controlled use of the Tarim would help jumpstart the growing of a range of crops in Xinjiang, including an aggressive push to plant and harvest cotton.

[Video 13](https://www.thewirechina.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Troops-Xinjiang.mp4)

Troops from the People’s Liberation Army entered Xinjiang in 1949. Demobilized troops became part of the XPCC, Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, established under a directive to “cultivate and guard border areas” in 1954. _Credit: VideoChinaTV, Channel 4_

Amid the discovery of natural resource riches and the marvels of technology, there was always the daunting human project of somehow creating a workforce for the state’s ambitions in Xinjiang. The Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps would handle that feat of reinvention. The XPCC is a corporate unit of the Chinese army, made up of former soldiers turned economic developers. They were sent to Xinjiang as the government agents meant to convert herdsmen into farmers. Land was seized, training programs were implemented and enforced, state-backed companies were launched, the reluctant were threatened with detention, and many were shipped out of Xinjiang to work in China’s larger eastern cities.

The company’s record of coercive tactics in Xinjiang has earned it a notorious international reputation. Over the past decade, the XPCC has seized more than half a million acres in Xinjiang to use for growing cotton, as well as for a variety of other industries, from fruit farming to solar fields. The company has also helped the government relocate more than 10 percent of Xinjiang’s population — over 2.5 million people between 2014 and 2019 — through labor transfers. If brutal, the XPCC’s work in Xinjiang has been effective. Today, Xinjiang produces roughly 20 percent of the world’s cotton supply and is a major source of export crops such as tomatoes, lavender, and wine grapes.

Left: Workers load cotton onto a truck in Alar, Xinjiang. Right: Farmers put harvested tomatoes on a sunning ground for air-drying in Yanqi Hui Autonomous County, Xinjiang. _Credit: IC Photo via Depositphotos_

Of all the successes in Xinjiang over the last 75 years none may be as remarkable as the latest: The Chinese are growing fish in Xinjiang, a place often referred to as the most landlocked spot on the planet.

> China’s desert fish farming project is actually as much a consequence of self-preservation as creative ingenuity… Aquaculture, a 2024 report by the Center for Strategic and International Studies explained, is central to Beijing’s efforts “to bolster food security.” As a result, China has been perhaps the most aggressive practitioner of fish farming.

It turns out that in China’s earliest efforts to pull oil out of Xinjiang, its government drilling teams were regularly turning up evidence of underground aquifers, including underneath the Taklamakan. Researchers knew that the Taklamakan had once been entirely underwater, connected to one of Earth’s oceans. The desert’s sand and soil were littered with ancient coral fragments, microscopic plankton, bivalves, and gastropods. The Taklamakan’s salty soil, in fact, helped explain why some of the world’s best-preserved mummies had been unearthed there.

[Video 14](https://www.thewirechina.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Sand-Dunes.mp4)

Qiemo County Shishixian Aquatic Products built a roughly eight-acre fish farm on the southeastern edge of the Taklamakan Desert in March 2024. Today, the farm raises golden pomfret, grouper, and mullet in two outdoor ponds and an indoor greenhouse with 68 tanks. _Credit: Xinhua_

The aquifers found beneath Xinjiang’s arid vastness would eventually be mapped, and tests would be done on the discovered water — to see both how pressurized and just how salty the water was. Initially, the tests suggested the waters under the Taklamakan and elsewhere across Xinjiang were too salty to be used for farming, too bitter to be consumed by humans. Chinese scientists eventually realized that the underground waters in Xinjiang could be adjusted to mimic seawater.

As a result, over 1,000 fish farms now dot Xinjiang, producing about 200,000 tons of seafood annually. Atlantic salmon, lobster, bass, carp, crab, shrimp — all of them and more raised in Xinjiang. Chinese media calls it the “Blue Miracle,” a maritime economy in a frontier home to what is known as the Eurasian Pole of Inaccessibility. [The Outlaw Ocean Project](https://theoutlawocean.com/), a news organization in Washington, DC, mapped these farms as part of a sweeping [investigation](https://foodforfeed.theoutlawocean.com/) showing how much seafood is reaching the U.S., including government facilities, in violation of the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA).

In recent years, China has pushed fish farming into its arid and high-altitude far west, particularly in Xinjiang and across the Tibetan Plateau. [This map](https://chinafishfarms.theoutlawocean.com/) highlights more than 1,000 of these farms and provides access to a national database of over 63,000 sites. _Credit: [The Outlaw Ocean Project](https://chinafishfarms.theoutlawocean.com/)_

“Raising fish in the desert?” China’s state broadcaster CCTV wrote in a 2025 article. “It sounds impossible, but in Xinjiang, it’s becoming a reality.”

###### **FARMERS OF FISH**

Aquaculture is a global phenomenon. More than half of all seafood the world consumes now comes from aquaculture rather than wild catch. India alone produces some 11 million metric tons of farmed fish products every year. The raising of clams, oysters, scallops, and mussels — distinctive aquaculture marvels because they require no feed and very little freshwater — has driven much of the explosive growth. In a 2019 report, the Nature Conservancy argued that by 2050, sustainably managed fish farms should become humanity’s primary source of seafood.

A floating fish farm in Xiapu, Fujian, China._Credit: [Yujie](https://stock.adobe.com/images/aerial-view-of-the-sea-fish-farm-cages-and-fishing-village-in-xiapu-fujian-province-china/727202819?prev\_url=detail)_

Most ambitious fish farming falls into a small handful of models. In Asia, the dominant system is the freshwater pond: excavated basins stocked with hatchery-raised juveniles, fed daily, and aerated mechanically to prevent oxygen crashes. Along coasts, floating net pens hold fish in open water, relying on currents to disperse waste. Some fish farms operate fully enclosed recirculating systems, filtering and reusing water inside warehouses.

The $313 billion industry has generated varied and extraordinary benefits. In India, it is a major source of employment, particularly for women. In Bangladesh, the expansion of fish farming has helped drive down prices, making seafood more affordable for poorer households. The industry, even accounting for transporting the farmed fish around the world, is a far smaller source of carbon emissions than beef or pork.

Recent efforts to push the nature and reach of the business have wound up pushing the boundaries of the imagination and technology. The Norwegians have built enormous, semi-submersible structures in the open ocean, capable of holding volumes of water great enough to house 1.5 million salmon. The Chinese have built “aquaculture ships,” huge vessels sent to sea with 15 breeding cabins capable of holding 90,000 cubic meters of water.

[Video 15](https://www.thewirechina.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Fish-Farms-in-Desert.mp4)

On the southern rim of the Taklamakan Desert in Xinjiang, two companies, Hotan Yujianjianglai and Qiemo Shishixian, began farming fish around 2024. Roughly 250 fish farms in and around the Taklamakan produce $100 million in desert seafood — including species like cod and grouper — every year. _Credit: Hotan Yujianjianglai Aquaculture, Xinhua News_

In Scotland, underwater robots are used to combat the threat of sea lice, a parasite that feeds on salmon. The robots identify the lice and fire laser pulses to eradicate them. The inventions have not been exclusive to major commercial farm fishing. Modest fish farms in Indonesia have been using smartphone apps to manage timed, more cost-effective feeding schedules at their ponds.

And then there is the engineering of the fish themselves. In the U.S., the seafood company AquAdvantage has won approval to raise cloned salmon. Fish farming, therefore, isn’t only about cages, pumps, and sensors anymore. It’s also about re-writing biology — treating growth rates and production timelines as variables that can be redesigned, not just managed.

But as with many feats of human ingenuity and profit-making, aquaculture is freighted with a multitude of downsides. Crowding millions of fish together produces
