By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The complainants alleged that the respondents watched the house burn from beside a white vehicle nearby. Emil said he later found gasoline containers on the property.

The allegations have yet to be established in court.

The couple said Aquino had been claiming about 260 square meters of the property since 2023 while Lucas attended barangay meetings as his attorney-in-fact.

*   ![Image 1: 44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258812.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/44-expect-sara-dutertes-conviction-in-impeachment-trial-survey/2445251)

A June 9, 2025 letter signed by Lucas as UPACC chairperson asked the barangay captain to investigate and remove the fence and a hut on the disputed property.

The complaint also cited an alleged statement by Aquino days before the fire: "Si Ma'am Pyra na lang ang bahala sa inyo" (Ma'am Pyra will take care of you).

It further referenced a neighbor's account that Aquino allegedly said the group had agreed only to scare the family. The neighbor was not identified as a firsthand witness to the fire.

The BFP, meanwhile, classified the fire as intentional, citing clean burn patterns, substantial material loss in the middle of the structure and the absence of an accidental heat source.

*   ![Image 2: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

Fire responders arrived at 5:37 p.m., when the blaze had already been extinguished. The BFP estimated the damage at P200,000 and said evidence had been submitted for forensic analysis.

In a letter to The Manila Times, Lucas denied committing or intending to commit destructive arson, saying her involvement in the dispute was limited to asking barangay officials to address the fence and nipa hut on land belonging to Aquino.

Lucas said she had written to barangay officials in Bueno, Capas, Tarlac, requesting an investigation into the structures, which she described as illegally built on Aquino’s property. She said she had asked officials to resolve the matter through lawful and peaceful means.

“We did not commit any illegal acts,” Lucas said.

*   ![Image 3: Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/lacson-asks-padilla-to-clarify-disregard-for-law-comment-on-duterte-trial/2444142)

She maintained that her presence in the area did not establish criminal liability and rejected the allegations against her.

“My mere presence in the area cannot be considered a crime,” she said, adding that she believed the accusations were politically motivated and intended to harass her and malign her reputation.

Lucas also alleged that, months before the complaint was filed, she had received information that the Cadiangs would be used to bring a fabricated case against her.

She offered a counter-account of the fire, saying passersby had seen Emil inside the nipa hut while it was burning. She described the structure as having been illegally built on Aquino’s property.

summary: 美国总统特朗普表示，台湾已同意购买阿拉斯加管道项目 30% 的液化天然气，商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克补充说，台湾承诺投资 44 亿美元。台湾政府尚未证实该交易，细节仍不清楚。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 14 日香港时间 11:46 · 2 分钟阅读美国总统唐纳德特朗普周二表示，台湾已同意购买 30%
content:
商务
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，台湾已同意购买阿拉斯加管道项目 30% 的液化天然气，商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克补充说，台湾承诺投资 44 亿美元。台湾政府尚未证实该交易，细节仍不清楚。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 14 日 11:46 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周二表示，台湾已同意购买阿拉斯加拟议管道项目中 30% 的液化天然气 (LNG)，但交易条款尚未立即明确。特朗普是在共和党全国委员会在该州组织的一次集会上发表上述言论的。

出席集会的商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克表示，台湾已承诺投资 44 亿美元用于该管道的开发。负责监督能源政策的台湾经济部没有立即发表评论。

当被问及特朗普的言论时，台湾行政长官赵正台告诉记者，政府的工作是“稳定整个能源供应并增强其弹性，就像世界各地的政府一样”。
在此之前，台湾官员在二月份表示，他们将增加对美国天然气的采购，使其占台湾今年进口供应量的三分之一左右，并减少从其他国家的采购。台湾国有能源公司中油集团去年与阿拉斯加天然气开发公司签署协议，购买液化天然气并投资该管道项目。阿拉斯加州州长去年表示，台湾签署了一份意向书，每年从该项目购买 600 万吨液化天然气。

台湾总统赖清德当时表示，这项投资将确保台湾的能源安全。特朗普的言论没有明确表明最终协议是否已经签署。

去年，台湾总统府秘书长潘文安参观了阿拉斯加拟议的液化天然气项目现场，特朗普政府一直在向亚洲盟友推销该项目，作为供应选择。如果建成，阿拉斯加液化天然气项目每年将出口多达 2000 万吨过冷天然气。到目前为止，它已与亚洲买家和法国主要能源公司TotalEnergies签订了每年1300万吨的协议。它还需要另外 300 万吨的协议，并且必须将其转化为具有约束力的协议以确保融资。
该项目将使美国制造的液化天然气直接进入包括台湾在内的亚洲市场，而无需经过巴拿马运河或绕过非洲之角，从而减少运输时间和成本。台湾已承诺大幅增加从美国的采购，包括能源，以减少激怒华盛顿的巨大贸易顺差。特朗普上个月表示，韩国已同意投资这条价值 540 亿美元的管道，但首尔表示尚未敲定。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编

负责 CLB.org.hk 报道和编辑标准的主编。

【原文 English Original】
Business
US President Donald Trump said Taiwan has agreed to buy 30 per cent of liquefied natural gas from an Alaska pipeline project, with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick adding that Taiwan committed to invest $4.4 billion. Taiwan's government did not confirm the deal, and details remain unclear.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

14 Oct 2026 at 11:46 HKT · 2 min read

US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that Taiwan has agreed to buy 30 per cent of the liquefied natural gas (LNG) from a proposed pipeline project in Alaska, but the terms of the deal were not immediately clear. Trump made the remarks at a rally in the state organised by the Republican National Committee.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who also appeared at the rally, said Taiwan has committed to investing US$4.4 billion in the development of the pipeline. Taiwan's economy ministry, which oversees energy policy, had no immediate comment.

Asked about Trump's comments, Taiwan Premier Cho Jung-tai told reporters that the government's job is to "stabilise the entire energy supply and build its resilience, like governments everywhere."

The remarks come after Taiwan officials said in February they would ramp up purchases of US natural gas to constitute about a third of the island's imported supply this year, and reduce purchases from other countries. Taiwan state energy firm CPC Corp signed an agreement with Alaska Gasline Development Corp last year to buy LNG and invest in the pipeline project. Alaska's governor said last year that Taiwan signed a letter of intent to buy 6 million metric tons of LNG per annum from the project.

Taiwan President Lai Ching-te said at the time that the investment would ensure the island's energy security. Trump's comments did not make it clear whether a final deal had been signed.

Last year, Taiwan Presidential Office Secretary-General Pan Men-an visited the site of the proposed LNG project in Alaska, which the Trump administration has been promoting to Asian allies as a supply option. If built, the Alaska LNG project will export up to 20 million tons of the superchilled gas a year. So far it has lined up agreements covering 13 million tons a year from buyers in Asia and French major TotalEnergies. It needs agreements for another 3 million tons and must turn them into binding deals to secure financing.

The project would open direct access for US-made LNG to Asian markets, including Taiwan, without having to go through the Panama Canal or around the Horn of Africa, reducing transit time and costs. Taiwan has pledged to massively ramp up its purchases from the United States, including energy, to reduce a yawning trade surplus that has angered Washington. Trump said last month that South Korea had agreed to invest in the US$54 billion pipeline, but Seoul said it was not yet set in stone.

title: The ‘captain of the ship’ doctrine
summary: _**Dear PAO,**_ _**I am a victim of “plastic surgery gone wrong.” After the surgery, my face became permanently asymmetrical and swollen. When I confronted the head plastic surgeon, he argued that his assistant made a mistake in administeri
content:
_**Dear PAO,**_

_**I am a victim of “plastic surgery gone wrong.” After the surgery, my face became permanently asymmetrical and swollen. When I confronted the head plastic surgeon, he argued that his assistant made a mistake in administering the proper dosage of the medicine required during the surgery. However, since I directly transacted and conferred with this head surgeon before, during, and after the surgery, I want to implead him in the lawsuit. Can I file a lawsuit against him?**_

_**Paula**_

*   [Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/legal-advice/who-should-pay-capital-gains-tax/2443313)

Dear Paula,

Yes, a lawsuit against the head plastic surgeon may be meritorious, notwithstanding the fact that it was his assistant who was directly negligent during the surgery.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

In Dr. Milagros L. Cantre v. Sps. Go and Go, GR 160889, April 27, 2007, penned by Associate Justice Leonardo Quisumbing, the Supreme Court explained that the head surgeon or the surgeon in charge of an operation is liable for the negligence of his/her assistants, saying:

“In cases involving medical negligence, the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur allows the mere existence of an injury to justify a presumption of negligence on the part of the person who controls the instrument causing the injury, provided that the following requisites concur:

“1. The accident is of a kind which ordinarily does not occur in the absence of someone’s negligence;

*   ![Image 1: Duterte keeps 56% trust rating, Marcos remains at 36% – SWS survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258343.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte keeps 56% trust rating, Marcos remains at 36% – SWS survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/national/duterte-keeps-56-trust-rating-marcos-remains-at-36-sws-survey/2444939)

“2. It is caused by an instrumentality within the exclusive control of the defendant or defendants; and

“3. The possibility of contributing conduct which would make the plaintiff responsible is eliminated.

“As to the first requirement, the gaping wound on Nora’s arm is certainly not an ordinary occurrence in the act of delivering a baby, far removed as the arm is from the organs involved in the process of giving birth. Such injury could not have happened unless negligence had set in somewhere.

“Second, whether the injury was caused by the droplight or by the blood pressure cuff is of no moment. Both instruments are deemed within the exclusive control of the physician in charge under the ‘captain of the ship’ doctrine. This doctrine holds the surgeon in charge of an operation liable for the negligence of his assistants during the time when those assistants are under the surgeon’s control. In this particular case, it can be logically inferred that petitioner, the senior consultant in charge during the delivery of Nora’s baby, exercised control over the assistants assigned to both the use of the droplight and the taking of Nora’s blood pressure. Hence, the use of the droplight and the blood pressure cuff is also within petitioner’s exclusive control.”

*   ![Image 2: ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1257681.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/icc-prosecutor-removes-253-items-from-evidence-list-in-duterte-case/2444598)

Thus, as the head surgeon, your doctor may be held liable not only for his own negligence, but also for the negligence of his assistants during the surgery or when such assistants were under his professional control. As the proverbial “captain of the ship,” the head surgeon may be impleaded and held directly liable for the medical malpractice or negligence committed by the assistants he is supervising.

We hope that we were able to answer your queries. This advice was solely based on the facts you have narrated and our appreciation of the same. Our opinion may vary when other facts are changed or elaborated.

Thank you for your continued trust and support.

_Editor’s note: Dear PAO is a daily column of the Public Attorney’s Office. Questions for Chief Acosta may be sent to dearpao@manilatimes.net_

title: Homeware line designed for dormers, young couples, small families
summary: College students in dorms and young couples starting out often need a few items to make their spaces more comfortable. These often include basics like flatware, plates, beddings and maybe a lamp or two. While there are department stores and
content:
College students in dorms and young couples starting out often need a few items to make their spaces more comfortable. These often include basics like flatware, plates, beddings and maybe a lamp or two.

While there are department stores and home store chains that offer pretty much the same kind of mix, one of the newer entrants is the Metro Retail Stores Group. Last month, it launched its own brand of home basics, Metro Living in its four Metro Department Stores located in Alabang, Market Market, Ayala Center Cebu, and Super Metro Colon.

Arranged on open shelves and in compact displays, the merchandise is basic and designed to work together.

*   [Comedian Russell Brand appears in UK court for start of rape trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/entertainment-lifestyle/comedian-russell-brand-appears-in-uk-court-for-start-of-rape-trial/2443698)

“For Metro Living, we’ve shifted our entire retail philosophy from selling individual products to delivering fully integrated lifestyle solutions. Previously, customers had to navigate different aisles to assemble a look,” Joel Orense, Metro Retail President and COO told The Manila Times in an email interview.

“Through our dedicated shop-in-shop concept, we bring fully curated, pre-styled living spaces directly to the retail floor. It eliminates decision fatigue, offers immediate aesthetic inspiration, and maximizes customer convenience. We are elevating the overall shopping experience, and based on initial performance, we plan to scale this format to additional key stores next year,” he added.

Placing these household staples in a dedicated location inside their stores was only logical as it takes out the guesswork for shoppers.

Orense said that historically, people bought items for their homes from different stores. While this can actually be a fun exercise on a weekend or during sale season, it can also be a chore for people who might prefer to do something else with their time.

“By engineering a cross-category, cohesive product matrix, Metro Living bridges that gap — transforming single-item transactions into complete room solutions,” he said.

title: The plight of our farmers and our food insecurity
summary: FILIPINOS consume 17 million to 18 million metric tons of rice annually. On the supply side, Filipino rice farmers produce only 12 million to 13 million metric tons of rice from a mere 6 percent of land area of the entire country devoted to
content:
FILIPINOS consume 17 million to 18 million metric tons of rice annually. On the supply side, Filipino rice farmers produce only 12 million to 13 million metric tons of rice from a mere 6 percent of land area of the entire country devoted to rice farming. We are one of the top rice-consuming countries in the world. This small percentage of land area for rice farming is under pressure to be reduced further to a smaller percentage as urbanization sprawls into the rural areas. The demand for land for renewable energy, particularly solar power plants, aggravates the shrinking of these rice fields.

Basic economics will tell us that this kind of shortage in supply and high demand in rice should translate to higher income for our rice farmers. However, our rice farmers continue to be the poorest among our citizens. Farming has become so discredited among the next generation that even farmers themselves would not encourage their children to be farmers. At present, the average age of a Filipino farmer is 56 years old. On the other hand, the median age of Filipinos is 27 years old. This puts the difference between the average age of Filipino farmer to the median of the population at 30 years old. The Philippines has one of the youngest populations in the world, albeit there are signs of aging. But it also has one of the oldest farmers’ populations. Policy makers are concerned about food security as less Filipinos engage in farming, particularly the back-breaking rice farming. The growing scarcity of farmers in the rural areas is felt not only with the increasing labor cost, but with the extreme difficulty of finding warm bodies to help till the land and retaining them. Data shows that our food security is going towards import dependency. This is not security at all as we depend on other countries to feed our population.

*   [Paper is not proof](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/opinion/columns/paper-is-not-proof/2443919)

[![Image 1: No Image](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256392.jpeg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256392.jpeg)

Who would like to be a farmer in the Philippines if over generations, farmers remained and continue to wallow in the miseries of penury and hard labor? Add to this the losses incurred in the damaging effects of climate change such as El Niño and La Niña, the vicious and merciless wrath of pestilence such as the African swine fever and avian flu that take away the other sources of farmers in tending livestock and animals. No wonder our farmers are being pushed to the edge of despair, a lot of whom has already fallen into.

Since I engaged in rice-farming and livestock farming myself, I experienced these losses firsthand. Fortunately, I have a stable source of income from my professional employment. This allows me to absorb the losses as they happen. But for most poor farmers, an occurrence of one of these disasters will mean terrible hunger and radical disruption of their family’s lives such that children will have to stop going to school and sick members of family will be left without medical care and tragically left to the mercies of benefactors without which a family will lose such precious life of a loved one.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

When I started rice farming in 2023, the cost of rice production was P15 per kilogram. When harvest time came, rice traders offered to buy it at a mere P9 per kg. As I had no storage facility nor drying and milling machines, I was thinking of selling at a loss so I could dispose of the palay grains to avoid the God-given bountiful harvest rotting unnecessarily. Thus, it was such welcome news to hear Sen. Kiko Pangilinan advocating fiercely for the implementation of the Sagip Saka Act, which he so painstakingly worked on to be passed into law in 2019. Upon returning to the Senate floor, he put to task the government agencies, specifically the Department of Agriculture (DA), on the law’s implementation. His efforts in compelling government agencies to buy locally produced rice raised the buying price of palay to between P20 to 23 per kg.

One major reason also for the ridiculous pricing of rice is the lack of storage, grain drying equipment and milling facilities for farmers. With these facilities inaccessible, the traders force the farmers to sell to them even at a loss whenever harvest time comes. This explains why palay was priced at an extremely low price of P9 per kg while milled rice is priced at a high price of P55 per kg. It would truly help the farmers if they could mill their harvest on their own and sell the milled rice directly to the market.

*   ![Image 2: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

Our leaders in the Department of Agriculture can devote a substantial chunk of the budget to providing these agricultural equipment, storage and drying facilities to the farmers instead of allocating budget for more farm-to-market roads which since my childhood have been getting copious budget allocations. Yet most of these farm-to-market roads earned the moniker of being roads coming from the farm and not leading to the market but to the politician’s private resort, or the project funds going into the politicians’ pockets. This is just one of the many reforms that must be done, including better enforcement of laws against the illegal smuggling of rice into the country. Until then, our farmers remain poor and our country remains to be food-insecure.

content:
（收件人：ADDS 第 5-6 段中首尔外交部的回应）
作者：金贤洙

首尔 10 月 12 日（韩联社）——韩国军方表示，朝鲜周一向东海发射了多枚弹道导弹，这显然是针对韩国最近成功试射的高超音速导弹的武力展示。

参谋长联席会议（JCS）表示，上午 9 点 20 分左右检测到从平壤地区发射的导弹，至少其中一枚导弹飞行了 900 多公里。

联合参谋长联席会议发言人张道永在新闻发布会上表示：“初步分析表明，（周一的发射）被视为对我们高超音速滑翔飞行器（HGV）成功发射的抗议，也是朝鲜在增强防御能力的五年计划下所取得的成就的展示，也是朝鲜有意展示其导弹能力的举动。”

当被问及发射的导弹是高超音速导弹还是中程导弹时，张拒绝发表评论，称军方需要进一步分析发射的规格。

朝鲜官方通讯社朝鲜中央通讯社于 2026 年 10 月 4 日刊登的这张照片显示，朝鲜前一天在其领导人金正恩的监督下发射了一枚中程战略导弹。 （仅限在韩国使用。不得重新分发）（韩联社）
韩国外交部也谴责此次发射是违反联合国安理会决议的“严重行为”，并表示这无助于朝鲜半岛当前局势的管理。

一位不愿透露姓名的国防部官员表示：“韩国、美国和日本建立了一个渠道，以便在朝鲜发射弹道导弹时迅速分享信息和局势评估。”

继 9 月 21 日非军事区 (DMZ) 韩国一侧发生地雷爆炸事件后，韩国于周四进行了首次 HGV 试射，此举显然是为了向朝鲜展示武力。

早些时候与联合国司令部的联合调查确定，爆炸是由朝鲜故意埋设的杀伤人员地雷引起的。平壤否认承担任何责任，指责首尔捏造其调查结果。

高超音速导弹通常很难用现有的导弹防御系统拦截。它的飞行速度至少为 5 马赫（音速的五倍），并且设计用于在不可预测的飞行路径上进行机动并在低空飞行。

朝鲜最近一次导弹发射是在10月3日从元山地区向东海发射一枚弹道导弹之后进行的。

朝鲜官方媒体第二天报道称，平壤发射了一枚中程战略导弹，作为训练操作“高超音速战略武器系统”的导弹部队的一部分。
朝鲜最后一次从平壤地区发射弹道导弹是在8月20日。

青瓦台于 2026 年 10 月 9 日提供的这张照片显示，在 9 月 21 日非军事区韩国一侧发生地雷爆炸后，韩国在总统李在明的监督下首次试射高超音速滑翔飞行器，明显是在向朝鲜展示武力。（照片不出售）（韩联社）

sookim@yna.co.kr

(ATTN: ADDS response from Seoul's foreign ministry in paras 5-6)
By Kim Hyun-soo

SEOUL, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- North Korea launched multiple ballistic missiles toward the East Sea on Monday, South Korea's military said, in an apparent show of force against the South's recent successful test-fire of a hypersonic missile.

The Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) said it detected the launch at about 9:20 a.m. from the Pyongyang area and that at least one of the missiles flew more than 900 kilometers.

"Initial analysis suggests (Monday's launch) was seen as a protest against the successful launch of our hypersonic glide vehicle (HGV) and a display of the North's achievements under its five-year plan to bolster defense capabilities and a deliberate show of its missile capabilities," JCS spokesperson Jang Do-young told a press briefing.

When asked if the missiles launched were hypersonic or intermediate-range missiles, Jang declined to comment, saying the military needs to further analyze the specifications of the launch.

This photo, carried by North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency on Oct. 4, 2026, shows the North firing an intermediate-range strategic missile the previous day, overseen by its leader Kim Jong-un. (For Use Only in the Republic of Korea. No Redistribution) (Yonhap)

South Korea's foreign ministry also condemned the launches as "a grave act" that violates U.N. Security Council resolutions and said it is not helpful in the management of the current situation on the Korean Peninsula.

"South Korea, the United States and Japan operate a channel to promptly share information and assessments of the situation in the event of North Korean ballistic missile launches," a ministry official who asked not to be named said.

South Korea conducted its first test launch of a HGV on Thursday in an apparent show of force against North Korea following the Sept. 21 mine blast on the South's side of the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ).

A joint investigation with the U.N. Command earlier determined that the explosions were caused by antipersonnel land mines planted deliberately by North Korea. Pyongyang has denied any responsibility, accusing Seoul of fabricating its findings.

A hypersonic missile is usually hard to intercept with existing missile defense shields. It travels at a speed of at least Mach 5 -- five times the speed of sound -- and is designed to be maneuverable on unpredictable flight paths and fly at low altitudes.

The North's latest missile launch came after it fired one ballistic missile from the Wonsan area toward the East Sea on Oct. 3.

North Korean state media reported the following day that Pyongyang launched an intermediate-range strategic missile as part of efforts to train missile troops operating the "hypersonic strategic weapon system."

The North last fired ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area on Aug. 20.

South Korea conducts its first test launch of a hypersonic glide vehicle overseen by President Lee Jae Myung in an apparent show of force against North Korea following the Sept. 21 mine blast on the South's side of the Demilitarized Zone, in this photo provided by Cheong Wa Dae on Oct, 9, 2026. title: Saudi-Houthi conflict in a ‘no peace, no war’ stalemate
summary: THE full-scale fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi rebels in Yemen has for the moment taken the focus away from the bigger war between the United States and Iran. Last week, a Houthi missile attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid Internati
content:
THE full-scale fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi rebels in Yemen has for the moment taken the focus away from the bigger war between the United States and Iran.

Last week, a Houthi missile attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport killed 12 people and injured 309. It was the deadliest attack in any Gulf Arab country since the US-Iran war ignited in February, and its impact could reshape the geopolitical landscape of the Middle East.

*   [US-China war now](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/us-china-war-now/2442742)

For more than a decade, the Saudis and the Houthis have been locked in a conflict that is driven by domestic instability, sectarian and tribal differences, and regional rivalries.

The Houthis began as a movement backing a minority Shiite sect in northern Yemen. In 2014, the group joined anti-government forces in a coup and took over the capital city, Sana’a.

Get the latest news

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Saudi Arabia, the region’s leading Sunni potentate, was uncomfortable with having a Shiite-dominated state for a neighbor, especially one that is closely aligned with Iran.

In 2015, Riyadh spearheaded a coalition of Arab states to dislodge the Houthis from Sana’a and restore power to the pro-Saudi regime. Iran stood by the Houthis, supplying its proxy with weapons, including attack drones.

Fighting raged throughout Yemen until April 2022, when the United Nations mediated a two-month truce between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis. The truce was extended twice before expiring seven months later.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Since then, a “no war, no peace” stalemate has settled in Yemen, with Oman activating back-channel negotiations to keep the two sides talking.

The stalemate crumbled in 2023, when the rebels began targeting commercial shipping passing through the Red Sea, claiming the attacks were launched “in solidarity” with other Iranian proxies Hamas and Hezbollah, which have come under heavy attack from Israel.

The last vestiges of the truce dissolved after the US-Iran conflict escalated into a full-blown war, and the Houthis intensified missile and drone barrages against Saudi targets. Riyadh has countered by launching air strikes on Houthi military bases and arms depots around Sana’a.

It used to be that the US was quick to respond militarily to any attack on Saudi Arabia, considered to be its most trusted ally in the Middle East. Today, President Donald Trump doesn’t seem too eager to respond to personal appeals from Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for US military intervention. The reluctance could stem from a promise the Houthi leadership made in 2025 that it would not attack US commercial and military vessels in the Red Sea.

*   ![Image 2: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

Another reason may be that Trump doesn’t want the US to be still at war with Iran when the midterm elections are held on Nov. 3, a situation that could prove fatal for Republican candidates.

Then again, Riyadh might have realized it was time to phase down its long dependence on American military might to shield it from its enemies.

That shield failed to stop Iranian and Houthi missiles from raining down on the kingdom.

Saudi Arabia, in fact, still wields enough influence to persuade Gulf states to enter into collective negotiations with Iran.

*   ![Image 3: Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254827.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/marcos-names-lino-cayetano-new-pco-chief/2443262)

Omar and Qatar maintain back-channel lines with Tehran, and Riyadh could tap those lines to expand the scope of negotiations.

In 2023, a China-brokered rapprochement pact managed to restore ties between Riyadh and Tehran. The agreement, while hailed as a breakthrough, didn’t last long, as Saudi Arabia found out that Iran continued to secretly provide the Houthis with weapons.

Interestingly, Iran itself has volunteered to bring Saudi Arabia and the Houthis to the negotiating table. Iran, however, insists that Saudi Arabia must first lift its air and naval blockades of Yemen. Saudi Arabia says it will do so only if the Houthis give up control of the Red Sea coast and stop attacking Saudi airports.

Political observers say an alternative security realignment might work. Riyadh has integrated Turkey and Pakistan into the Makkah Defense Pact, a collective regional strategy modeled after NATO’s Article 5.

Under the pact, an armed attack against any one of the three states would be regarded as an attack against all of them.

The agreement is a radical shift from Middle Eastern politics. Perhaps that is what the region needs now.

Christian Jade Bullod, Nelson Camboli, Chris Jefferies Dilan and Jeric Taripe are the founders of M.R. Yogheart, a yogurt drink brand that is proving that profit and philanthropy can coexist in a single bottle.

Operating under the tagline “Your Yogurt with a Heart,” the team is part of a rising wave of Gen Z “student-preneurs” turning academic requirements into viable market competitors.

*   ![Image 9: DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254558.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The timing of M.R. Yogheart’s entry into the market aligns with a significant shift in Philippine consumer behavior.

Post-pandemic, the local beverage industry has seen a move away from high-sugar soft drinks toward functional beverages.

Yogurt — once a niche health food — has entered the mainstream as a “guilt-free” indulgence.

In the Philippines, the demand for probiotics and gut-friendly snacks has grown at a compound annual growth rate of nearly 7 percent over the last three years.

*   ![Image 10: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

By pivoting from traditional yogurt ice cream to a portable drink format, the BSU team is tapping into the “on-the-go” lifestyle of the city’s massive student population.

The success of M.R. Yogheart highlights the strength of the Accountancy, Business and Management (ABM) strand, and specialized entrepreneurship programs in the Philippine educational system.

Under the K-12 curriculum and Commission on Higher Education-mandated entrepreneurship degrees, students are no longer just studying balance sheets; they are required to launch “business simulations” that face actual market pressures.

*   ![Image 11: Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254608.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/legarda-may-rejoin-senate-majority-pangilinan/2443223)

However, the transition from classroom theory to the pavement of Bonifacio Street was not without its hurdles.

“One challenge was internal — questioning if we had the capability to make this successful,” said Jeric Taripe. “There was doubt and fear. You worry about whether the target market will actually accept the product.”

What sets M.R. Yogheart apart from commercial, mass-produced alternatives is its commitment to the Cordilleran “terroir.”

The group bypasses imported milk solids in favor of fresh milk sourced directly from the dairy farm at the Baguio Animal Breeding and Research Center.

“One goal of M.R. Yogheart is to support local production,” Taripe explained. “We realized, why should we not support our own? We found out we have a local dairy farm right here, so we took the leap.”

By sourcing locally, the students reduce their carbon footprint and ensure a higher nutrient profile for their drinks, while providing a steady revenue stream for government-backed breeding centers.

**Branding**

The “heart” in their branding refers to their social mission. A portion of the proceeds from every bottle sold at their stall near the University Belt is donated to various charitable organizations.

For Taripe, the venture is a message to his fellow youth.

“Take the risk. We have to step out of our comfort zones. It is OK to struggle and be uncomfortable, as long as we remain wise in the decisions we take.”

Currently located along Bonifacio Street, M.R. Yogheart stands as a model for how the next generation of Filipinos is reimagining the “probiotiko” culture — one local bottle at a time.

The group is also among the participants of the 2026 Young Farmers Challenge Start-up Competition in the region, an initiative that highlights promising agri-based enterprises of young entrepreneurs.

**How the ABM strand redefined K-12 promise**

When the Philippines transitioned to the K-12 curriculum in 2012, the shift was met with a mixture of skepticism and logistical hurdles.

However, a decade later, the Accountancy, Business and Management (ABM) strand has emerged as the curriculum’s most tangible “silver lining.”

By bridging the gap between classroom theory and the cutthroat reality of the marketplace, ABM has transformed senior high school from a mere academic requirement into an incubator for the next generation of Filipino “technopreneurs” and corporate leaders.

The brilliance of the ABM strand lies in its departure from traditional, lecture-heavy education. The curriculum is built on the foundation of “Business Simulation,” where students are not just taught about supply chains — they are required to build them.

Student-led ventures like M.R. Yogheart are the direct result of this shift.

These students are introduced to specialized subjects such as Applied Economics, Business Ethics and Fundamentals of Accountancy, which provide the “hard skills” necessary to navigate the business landscape.

One of the primary criticisms of the old 10-year system was the “job-skills mismatch,” where graduates lacked the practical knowledge required by the industry.

The ABM strand addresses this through mandatory work immersion.

By placing students in actual accounting firms, retail offices and local government units, the curriculum ensures that 18-year-olds are already familiar with the software, professional ethics and administrative workflows that were previously only taught at the college level.

For the Philippine economy, which is 99 percent comprised of micro, small and medium enterprises, this influx of business-literate youth is a vital injection of energy.

ABM graduates enter the workforce or higher education already knowing how to read a balance sheet, conduct market research and — crucially — calculate the risks of a startup.

Beyond the technical skills, the ABM strand’s greatest contribution is the cultivation of an entrepreneurial mindset.

In a culture where the traditional goal was often to become an employee, the ABM curriculum encourages students to become employers.

It empowers youth to see social problems as business opportunities. Whether it is sourcing milk from local dairy farms to support farmers or creating digital investment portals for the diaspora, ABM students are taught that profit is most sustainable when it serves a community purpose.

While the K-12 transition faced significant growing pains, the ABM strand has proven to be a resounding success in vocational and professional preparation.

It has democratized business education, providing students from all walks of life with the tools to innovate.

As these young graduates transition into the professional world, they carry with them more than just a diploma; they carry the wit, wisdom and bravery to reshape the Philippine economy from the ground up.

title: The Cuban lesson
summary: IN October 1962, the world came very close to nuclear war. American surveillance flights discovered Soviet missiles in Cuba, an island about 90 miles (144 kilometers) from the coast of Florida. For 13 tense days, then-president John F. Kenn
content:
IN October 1962, the world came very close to nuclear war. American surveillance flights discovered Soviet missiles in Cuba, an island about 90 miles (144 kilometers) from the coast of Florida. For 13 tense days, then-president John F. Kennedy and his advisers weighed military options while Soviet ships continued sailing toward the island. The crisis only ended when both sides stepped back from the edge.

More than 60 years later, the same basic dangers of brinkmanship, miscalculation, and coercive pressure appear in the South China Sea. The Philippine experience with Chinese actions in the disputed body of water and the presence of American forces under the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) offer a test of those lessons.

The Cuban Missile Crisis began when the Soviet Union (now Russia) secretly placed medium- and intermediate-range missiles in Cuba. Shortly thereafter, American spy planes confirmed the sites. Kennedy formed an executive committee that debated whether to use airstrikes or diplomacy. He chose a naval quarantine that blocked further Soviet deliveries while still allowing time for negotiation. Soviet submarines and American destroyers nearly clashed. A U2 spy plane was shot down over Banes, Cuba, killing the pilot, Major Rudolf Anderson Jr. On the most dangerous day, known as Black Saturday, both sides faced intense pressure to escalate. In the end, then-Soviet premier Nikita Khrushchev agreed to remove the missiles, and Kennedy pledged not to invade Cuba. The American president later ordered the withdrawal of Jupiter missiles from Turkey. The crisis showed that even nuclear-armed rivals can avoid a catastrophe when they combine firm pressure with private diplomacy and mutual concessions.

*   [Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

Today the Philippines faces a different but related challenge. Under the EDCA, the US holds rotational access to nine Philippine military sites. Four of the sites added in 2023 are in Northern Luzon, near the Luzon Strait and Taiwan, facing the South China Sea. China views these arrangements as a strategic threat and has responded with sustained pressure in the contested waters. On several occasions, the China Coast Guard (CCG) and Chinese maritime militia have blocked Philippine resupply missions to the grounded ship that serves as Manila’s outpost. At Scarborough Shoal, the CCG used water cannons to restrict Philippine access. These actions function much like the American naval quarantine in 1962. Both represent the use of maritime power to limit an opponent’s movement and resupply without venturing into open warfare. Both aim to change the facts on the waters while testing the other side’s resolve.

The parallel carries serious risks. Geographic proximity reduces decision time, and alliance commitments raise the stakes. Red lines are ignored, and any collision during a resupply mission can trigger a firefight between coast guard or naval units. Such an exchange might then draw in the US under the 1951 Mutual Defense Treaty. What begins as a maritime dispute could expand into a wider confrontation. The structure of geographic proximity and alliance commitments recreates the dangerous situation of 1962.

The Cuban experience offers valuable guidance for Manila. Public firmness should be matched by private channels that allow both sides to explore solutions without strong public rhetoric. Security concerns must be pushed, but there should be room for the other side to climb down. The American quarantine succeeded because it was paired with active diplomacy and willingness to reciprocate. The same combination of resolve and flexibility remains essential today.

If the current dispute is not carefully managed, the outcome could resemble the conflict in the Middle East. Low-level pressure could harden into sustained fighting and may draw in larger powers. The costs can go far beyond what any side intended. The Cuban Missile Crisis demonstrated that even the most dangerous confrontations can still be defused when leaders choose restraint and communication. The war in the Middle East shows what follows when those choices are not made in time.

The anniversary of the Cuban crisis, therefore, carries a direct message to the Philippines. Proximity and coercive maritime actions do not have to produce catastrophe. The leaders of 1962 ultimately preferred negotiation to escalation. That preference remains available in the disputed areas of the South China Sea.

The enduring legacy of the Cuban Missile Crisis is that even the most perilous standoffs can be defused when leaders choose the hard work of diplomacy over the catastrophic gamble of war.

Rafael P. Tuvera is a lawyer who taught law and political science. He analyzes geopolitics and diplomatic strategy with an emphasis on productive approaches with legal and historical context.

【大紀元2026年10月11日訊】（大紀元記者陸希休斯頓報導）小說家兼詩人梁莉姿（Gigi Leung）10月8日（週四）應邀在聖湯瑪斯大學舉行文學講座，以小說集《日常運動》（Everyday Movement）為主題，探討2019年香港反送中運動期間，社會動盪如何影響個人生活，以及集體信念與個人價值之間的張力。

[![Image 11](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867549-01-600x450.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867549-01.jpg)

梁莉姿（Gigi Leung）以小說集《日常運動》（Everyday Movement）為主題Book Talk座談。（陸希／大紀元）

梁莉姿現居台北，此次展開美國六大城市巡迴演講，休斯頓為第二站。講座由聖湯瑪斯大學教授葉耀元主持，台灣書院副主任林忠憲、該校國際研究與當代語言學系教授翁定暐，以及多位文學愛好者到場參與。

[![Image 12](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867551-03-600x450.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867551-03.jpg)

活動以圓桌式面對面和讀者對話。（陸希／大紀元）

《日常運動》2022年於台灣出版，以2019年7月至11月的香港反送中運動為背景，透過大學室友、教師及店主等普通人的故事，描寫恐懼、罪疚、愛與猶豫等情感，呈現政治危機如何滲入日常生活。英文版由珍妮佛．貝利（Jennifer Bailey）翻譯，於2026年2月由企鵝蘭登書屋旗下Riverhead Books出版。

梁莉姿表示，她不希望將人物塑造成英雄或特定政治立場的代表，而是呈現人性的矛盾，以及集體的「我們」與個人的「我」之間的拉扯。她認為，文學不只記錄事件，也能保存人們在歷史變動中的情感與記憶，讓讀者看見新聞事件背後更複雜的生命經驗。

[![Image 13](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867552-04-600x450.jpeg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867552-04.jpeg)

多位文學愛好者仔細聆聽作者的寫作分享。（陸希／大紀元）

在問答環節，葉耀元提問，作者為何以2019年香港區議會選舉作為全書結尾。梁莉姿指出，這並不代表香港歷史就此結束，而是藉此反思反送中運動的集體力量進入選舉政治後，究竟屬於整個群體，還是轉化為個人的政治資本。

談及香港未來，她引用蘇軾詩句「不識廬山真面目，只緣身在此山中」，表示離開香港、重新回望故土，有助於理解香港特殊的歷史背景與身分認同。她認為，香港未來不一定需要所有人共同追求單一的宏大目標，更重要的是持續探索香港身分的意義與獨特的生活方式。

[![Image 14](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867553-05-600x450.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867553-05.jpg)

葉耀元教授（左）主持座談，邀請與會者提問。（陸希／大紀元）

對於反送中運動對香港社會的長期影響，梁莉姿表示，2020年香港國安法實施後，公開表達與抗議的環境有所改變，使後續觀察與比較更加困難，相關影響仍有待持續研究。

梁莉姿並透露，《日常運動》是規劃中「香港三部曲」的第一部，後續作品《樹的憂鬱》將探討香港國安法與新冠疫情後的香港社會及離散經驗。

[![Image 15](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867554-06-600x422.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867554-06.jpg)

《日常運動》著作中文版，2022年於台灣出版。（陸希／大紀元）

講座透過小說創作與讀者交流，帶領與會者思考反送中運動中的集體力量、個人選擇與身分認同，並重新審視公共危機過後，日常生活與人們內心留下的痕跡。

title: Now is not a good time, Russian plague
summary: AS if we did not have enough to cause us individual and collective stress and worry, news has emerged in the past several days about an apparent outbreak of a dangerous infection in Russia’s vast Siberia region. The memory of the Covid-19 p
content:
AS if we did not have enough to cause us individual and collective stress and worry, news has emerged in the past several days about an apparent outbreak of a dangerous infection in Russia’s vast Siberia region. The memory of the Covid-19 pandemic is still fresh for most of the world, and so the heightened concern about anything that might result in another such calamity is understandable. And in fact, that greater awareness of pandemic risk was likely one of the good results of Covid-19, although it also presents a risk of panic and overreaction.

At this point, panic and overreaction may be the most immediate potential problem because of the other challenges we are facing: deteriorating geopolitical stability, an economy that is steadily weakening while basic living costs steadily increase, persistent energy shortages in large parts of the country, political turmoil within our own government and the worsening effects of an El Niño of unprecedented strength. There is never a time when facing the threat of a dangerous pandemic is welcome, but this news coming now may indeed feel like too much to bear for many people.

This can be relieved significantly by ensuring that accurate information is being shared with the public. Unfortunately, that is proving difficult because the Russian government, despite the entreaties of the World Health Organization (WHO) and Russia’s legal obligations as a WHO member to be transparent about a potential epidemic or pandemic threat, has been secretive about exactly what is happening.

*   [The banana chip witch hunt: China, CALE88 and the weaponization of national security against Sara Duterte](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/the-banana-chip-witch-hunt-china-cale88-and-the-weaponization-of-national-security-against-sara-duterte/2442743)

What is known so far is that Russian authorities reported that a 28-year-old lab worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East, which is located in the city of Irkutsk, contracted a rapid, unknown pneumonia infection and died on Oct. 2. As a precaution, the Russians said, approximately 200 people who had come into contact with her (according to its website, the research institute has a staff of 95) were quarantined, although the government has informed the WHO that the same sort of infection has not been found in others, and that about 120 of the quarantined contacts had been released. On Oct. 6, it was reported that a second person had died, although this is uncertain due to the Russian government’s reluctance to discuss the situation publicly.

The inference that has been drawn from what little information has been disclosed is that the lab worker died as a result of an accidental release of the plague bacteria — yersinia pestis — the same infection that caused the Black Death in Europe in the 14th century. The reason the research institute (referred to by its transliterated Russian acronym “Chumin”) is in Irkutsk in the first place, having been established there in 1934, is that Siberia is one of several “plague reservoirs” around the world. These are areas where the plague pathogen is endemic among wildlife, and from where the infection can occasionally jump to humans; other hot spots are in Central and West Africa, the southwest United States, parts of India, and parts of Brazil and Peru in South America.

The plague bacteria can cause two types of infections in humans. The bubonic plague is an infection of the lymphatic system, and is the less deadly of the two, although it is still an extremely dangerous illness, with a human mortality rate of between 30 and 60 percent. It is not contagious between people, however, as that form of the infection is caused by bites from infected fleas. The more serious pneumonic plague can be passed between people, and can develop from an untreated bubonic plague infection; it is an infection of the lungs, and has a mortality rate of nearly 100 percent if not treated promptly — within a day or two — with massive doses of antibiotics. It is believed that this is what befell the deceased lab worker, although it must be emphasized that the only evidence for that so far is the large number of people who were reported quarantined after she became ill.

Looking at the situation rationally, there is a strong probability that this is not the beginning of another deadly pandemic, but the lack of information so far does not rule that out with certainty. There is nothing at all to be gained by Russia or anyone else by allowing the question to go unanswered, and fear and speculation to run rampant, particularly not now when the entire world seems to be on edge. We urge the Russian government to fully cooperate with the WHO, and for the WHO in turn to promptly disclose any and all information to the public.

title: Nigeria: Military Plane Crash - Traditional Ruler Cries Out As Decaying Bodies 'Pollute' Community's Source...

content:
_"This same river where the plane crashed into is what supplies our drinking water. We have a water treatment machine at Aboto about seven kilometres away from here. The water doesn't come every day, and when it comes, it is this same water that flows there, pumped to be treated for our drinking. So, it means whatever happens, pollution is already in the river, either as a result of decayed bodies or as oil that dropped into the river."_

A humanitarian crisis may hit Igbokoda, the headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, following the pollution of the source of water for the community by decaying bodies of the victims of the**[Nigeria Air Force](https://x.com/NigAirForce "https://x.com/NigAirForce")** (NAF) plane that crashed there last week.

The traditional ruler of the community, Afolabi Odidiomo, told PREMIUM TIMES on Tuesday that the body of water has been polluted, leaving the people with contaminated water both for drinking and other domestic uses.

He also said the crash destroyed economic trees and fish, which are the community's source of livelihood.

The NAF plane crashed into the swamp in the area on Monday, 5 October, killing the 25 people on board.

Efforts by divers and rescue teams to retrieve the wreckage of the plane and the bodies of the victims have been largely unsuccessful because of the terrain.

The search and rescue efforts deployed by a combined team of NAF, the Nigerian Navy, the police, the Igbokoda community and the state government about a week ago have only succeeded in retrieving pieces of human body parts as well as the broken parts of the airplane.

Officials confirmed that the main body of the airplane is yet to be located, as it is suspected to be deeply submerged in the underlay of the swamp where the crash occurred.

**Water pollution concern**

However, concerns have shifted from the initial shock following the crash to fresh fears of water pollution.

The body of water where the crash occurred is the same source of water for the Igbokoda community.

Rescuers have indicated that working on the site at the moment is hazardous as the area stinks badly of decayed human flesh littering the water.

The traditional ruler of Igbokoda, Mr Odidiomo, who spoke to PREMIUM TIMES at his palace on Tuesday, said the water has been polluted, leaving the people with contaminated water both for drinking and other domestic uses.

"The concern of everybody in this community today is that our government spent time, energy, money, and effort looking for people that had been chopped into pieces by the crash. The pieces that are floating everywhere in our rivers. The pieces that have decayed left so much stench that is unbelievable.

"Going close to the river is so scary now for children who usually go to swim when they return from school, because they see human flesh everywhere as they swim. Fish are also dying everywhere.

"So, the river that used to be friendly with children has become scary, as we wonder why the government cares so much for the dead rather than the living.

"This same river where the plane crashed into is what supplies our drinking water. We have a water treatment machine at Aboto about seven kilometres away from here. The water doesn't come every day, and when it comes, it is this same water that flows there, pumped to be treated for our drinking.

"So, it means whatever happens, pollution is already in the river, either as a result of decayed bodies or as oil that dropped into the river, and any other pollution that went into the water thereof."

The traditional ruler called for immediate clean-up of the water in order to prevent a worse disaster in the form of an epidemic due to the polluted water.

He said the lack of a plan to protect the people from the inherent pollution was unfair to the people, as the government could have cordoned off the area so that the polluted water could be kept back from flowing into the main river.

Mr Odidiomo said that besides the pollution, the crash also destroyed economic trees and fish, which are the community's source of livelihood.

"We are asking the government for cleanup. We are asking the government for remediation, a kind of restoration of the environment. The restoration now does not mean that we want the trees planted back, but we want the government to still do something in memory of those that died just as we have in Lagos and Ogun states," he said.

He also said efforts should be made, in addition to cleaning up the water, to also provide an alternative source of clean drinking water.

Also speaking on the pollution, Benjamin Omoyele, a resident of Igbokoda and a 100 Level student of Civil Engineering at the Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA), said the water pollution arising from the crash is a genuine concern that the people expect the government to look into urgently.

According to him, the body parts still left in the water are creating health concerns and contamination in the water, which might affect residents who depend largely on it.

However, Odunsola Dada, popularly called General at Igbokoda, said he believed that since the water is deep and keeps flowing down into the ocean, it would clean itself with time.

Mr Dada said the water would clean itself with time and that he did not see any present danger to the community.

"We are all humans, and what happened is a tragedy. We will all also die at our time. The water is deep and flowing steadily. It is not a well or a pool. It is a flowing river. In a short while everything will flow into the sea and people will be able to use it as before," he said.

Meanwhile, excavations are ongoing at the site with more machinery being deployed to assist in the removal of the remaining parts of the aircraft.

The search for the black box is the new focus of the operation as directed by the Chief of Air Staff, Sunday Aneke, during his visit to the site last week.

【看中国2026年10月14日讯】因涉嫌为中国政府从事间谍活动而被美国联邦调查局（FBI）逮捕的加州华人房地产经纪人[张婉莹](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E5%BC%A0%E5%A9%89%E8%8E%B9)（Wanying Zhang），近日又被曝出拥有规模庞大的房地产资产。她与丈夫名下疑似拥有7套住宅，总价值约1,100万美元，远超她此前向司法部门申报的资产数量，其财富来源也因此受到关注。 [看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。](https://www.secretchina.com/)

据《纽约邮报》报道，现年34岁的张婉莹，又名希瑟（Heather），被指与中国方面的人员合作，监视中华民国总统的儿子。她于10月4日在洛杉矶机场准备登上飞往上海的航班时被FBI逮捕，随后被控充当未登记的外国政府[代理人](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E4%BB%A3%E7%90%86%E4%BA%BA)。 [看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。](https://www.secretchina.com/)

检方指出，张婉莹被捕后，在接受审前服务部门调查时，没有如实申报自己拥有的房产和资产。她只申报了一处房产，但《纽约邮报》调查发现，她与丈夫似乎共同拥有七套住宅，估计总价值高达1,100万美元。

对此，张婉莹的律师克雷格・哈博（Craig Harbaugh）解释称，这是一场误会。不过，美国助理检察官阿曼达・埃尔博根（Amanda Elbogen）在洛杉矶法庭上指出，张婉莹本身就是房地产经纪人，理应清楚自己拥有多少房产。

[![Image 13](https://img6.secretchina.com/pic/2025/7-29/p3676411a560438137.jpg)](https://www.naturenergy.us/)

[![Image 14](https://img6.secretchina.com/pic/2024/11-2/p3556881a508884777.jpg)](https://naturexcels.com/language/zh/)

[![Image 15](https://img6.secretchina.com/bigpic/2024/11-4/p3557701a911506510.jpg)](https://naturexcels.com/language/zh/)

[![Image 16](https://img6.secretchina.com/pic/2025/7-29/p3676411a560438137.jpg)](https://www.naturenergy.us/)

上周，洛杉矶一名法官认定张婉莹存在潜逃风险，下令将她交由美国法警局拘押，不准保释。

**10年卖出125套房产 夫妻名下资产庞大**

《纽约邮报》调查发现，张婉莹与家人居住在加州橙县尔湾市（Irvine），生活相当富裕，经常搭乘飞机前往世界各地。

她与丈夫丁埃德里克（Edric Ding）都是南加州小型房地产经纪公司JC Pacific Capital的经纪人。

根据房地产网站Zillow的资料，张婉莹于2016年9月取得房地产经纪人执照。过去十年，她至少经手出售125套住宅，成交价格从51万美元到880万美元不等。

报道指出，张婉莹夫妇不仅替客户买卖房产，还积累了规模庞大的个人房地产资产。他们通过出售自己名下的住宅，获得了接近1,600万美元的销售收入。

不过，这些数字引起了同行的怀疑。

一名在JC Pacific Capital与张婉莹共事、要求匿名的房地产经纪人告诉《纽约邮报》，得知张婉莹拥有如此多房产后，感到十分震惊。

这名经纪人认为，单靠房地产交易佣金，很难积累如此庞大的财富，并怀疑张婉莹是否还有其他收入来源，甚至猜测她可能真的在为[中国](https://www.secretchina.com/)工作。

与此同时，检方还指控，张婉莹可以动用一个秘密的中国加密货币账户，涉及金额约19万美元，而且仍在从该账户获得收益。

检方还指出，张婉莹的兄弟与中国政府存在联系。

不过，报道并未证实张婉莹名下房产的资金来自中国政府，也没有证明这些房地产交易与她所面临的间谍指控存在直接关联。

**房产交易牵出另一名华商 FBI搜查其住所**

《纽约邮报》进一步调查张婉莹经手的房地产交易后发现，其中多套住宅位于加州亚凯迪亚市（Arcadia）。

今年5月，该市58岁的前市长王艾琳（Eileen Wang）曾承认，自己非法充当中国共产党的代理人。

报道指出，张婉莹经手的一笔房产交易，还涉及出生于中国的加州商人苗发台（Fatai Miao）。

现年54岁的苗发台从事建筑业，去年曾出售位于亚凯迪亚市的一栋六卧室豪宅，成交价约400万美元。

《纽约邮报》称，苗发台被认为就是联邦法院文件中提到的“1号人物”（Individual 1）。

根据法院文件，2025年9月，张婉莹涉嫌在西雅图监视[台湾](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E5%8F%B0%E6%B9%BE)总统的儿子时，这名男子曾与她同行。

据称，监控摄像头拍下的照片显示，张婉莹与一名男子坐在汽车内，对台湾总统儿子的住宅及其近亲进行拍照。

不过，苗发台目前并未受到任何违法行为指控。

据哥伦比亚广播公司新闻（CBS News）报道，苗发台是FBI调查张婉莹案件时关注的一名相关人物。

苗发台的亲属表示，过去两周，他一直待在中国，照顾正在当地接受治疗的妻子。

张婉莹在洛杉矶机场被捕后不久，FBI探员于周日持搜查令进入苗发台位于尔湾的住宅，当时屋内无人。

苗发台的儿子苗佳琪（Jiaqi Miao，音译）向CBS新闻表示，事发当天中午，他与姐姐接到一通自称来自FBI的电话，对方表示持有搜查令。

苗佳琪起初以为遇到诈骗电话，但查看家中监控后，发现多名持枪执法人员站在屋外。

他试图通过手机远程开门，但执法人员已经使用破门工具进入住宅。

苗佳琪还透露，父亲与张婉莹认识超过十年，两人一直是朋友，张婉莹甚至曾暂时住在父亲位于亚凯迪亚市的房产内。

不过，他否认父亲是中国间谍，认为父亲没有能力策划此类行动，而且经常听从他人的意见。

苗佳琪还强调，父亲是家中唯一主动选择加入美国国籍的人，因此他认为父亲没有理由替中国政府工作。

《纽约邮报》还发现，在张婉莹经手的另一笔房地产交易中，一名刚从大学毕业的中国留学生，以超过350万美元的价格购买了一栋六卧室住宅。

JC Pacific Capital此前曾发表声明，确认已知悉张婉莹涉及联邦刑事指控。公司表示，理解这些指控的严重性及公众的关注，将全力配合联邦当局调查，并依法提供所需信息和协助。

目前，张婉莹所涉及的外国代理人案件仍在司法程序中，相关指控尚未经过审判认定。

PHILIPPINE Feng Shui Queen Marites Allen unveiled her exclusive Year of the Fire Sheep 2027 forecast at her annual media press conference at Spaces, Penthouse, World Plaza Tower, Bonifacio Global City (BGC), on Oct. 12, 2026.

The briefing covered prosperity, careers, relationships and the 12 animal signs, alongside Destara – Destiny Is in Your Stars – her pioneering artificial intelligence (AI) lifestyle and destiny-guidance platform.

“Briefly, 2026 was about movement; 2027 is about making that movement meaningful,” Allen said.

**2027: A year to build, nurture and grow**

YEAR OF THE SHEEP In Chinese calendar, the Year of the Sheep begins on Feb. 6, 2027 and this year the element is Fire, which encourages inspiration and visibility. IMAGE FROM MARITES ALLEN

The lunar Year of the Fire Sheep begins Feb. 6, 2027.

For Four Pillars calculations, the astrological year turns at the traditional Beginning of Spring, around Feb. 4.

In Allen’s interpretation, Yin Fire encourages inspiration and visibility, while Sheep Earth favors responsibility and lasting results.

The absence of visible metal in her annual destiny chart places added emphasis on structure, clear agreements and accountability.

Her global outlook highlights preparation for developments in AI, business transformation, infrastructure and financial resilience.

Under Allen’s annual Flying Star chart, the Southeast holds the No. 8 Wealth Star; the Northwest, No. 1 Victory Star; the Southwest, No. 6 Mentor Star; and the South, No. 4 Romance and Scholastic Star. The No. 9 Future Prosperity Star occupies the Center. Greater care is advised in the North, West, Northeast and East.

**The 12 animal signs: Marites Allen’s exclusive outlook**

*   ![Image 3: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

**Winners – Prosperity and Progress:**Boar (allies and new beginnings), Horse (connections and learning), Dog (victory, with diplomacy needed), Dragon (wealth and recognition) and Snake (strategy and partnerships).

**Stable – Growth and Opportunities:** Monkey (mentors and guidance), Sheep (leadership and personal growth) and Rabbit (supportive relationships, balanced by caution over finances and trust under the No. 7 Star).

**Challengers – Navigate with Care:** Tiger (thoughtful communication), Rooster (wellness and balance), Rat (savings and clarity) and Ox (diplomacy and due diligence).

Allen emphasizes that these are general annual tendencies: “Individual destiny charts matter more than the animal sign alone.”

A full chart requires exact birth details and verified calendar and time calculations.

**On politics and accountability**

Asked about current political issues, Allen declined to speculate on individual outcomes and emphasized fairness and due process.

“Everyone deserves due process and the right to be heard. Feng Shui may guide us in understanding the times, but it cannot decide legal matters. When an issue reaches that stage, it is no longer in the stars; it is in the hands of the law,” she told _The Manila Times_ for this exclusive otherwise off-the-record question.

**Destara: The Marites Allen IP Brain**

Destara grew from a practical challenge: intense demand for Allen’s time, particularly around Chinese New Year.

[![Image 4: DESTINY-GUIDANCE PLATFORM DESTARA – Destiny Is in Your Stars – is Allen’s pioneering artificial intelligence lifestyle and destiny-guidance platform, on Google Play for Android users; iPhone users may scan its official QR code or visit destara.app in a browser to download. iMAGE FROM MARITES ALLEN](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258840.png)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258840.png)
DESTINY-GUIDANCE PLATFORM DESTARA – Destiny Is in Your Stars – is Allen’s pioneering artificial intelligence lifestyle and destiny-guidance platform, on Google Play for Android users; iPhone users may scan its official QR code or visit destara.app in a browser to download. iMAGE FROM MARITES ALLEN

Technology professionals in her family, including those working in data science and software architecture for international clients, helped inspire a platform that could make her knowledge more accessible.

For Allen, a Computer Science graduate who later earned an MBA from the Ateneo Graduate School of Business, the venture brings together her original training and professional practice.

The proprietary Marites Allen IP Brain is being developed around her Feng Shui methods and precise chart-calculation rules.

General-purpose AI models can explain concepts, but should not be relied upon alone to produce verified, personalized Four Pillars charts.

Destara continues to be refined and is intended to complement, not replace, professional consultations.

“Use AI responsibly. It should strengthen your judgment, not replace it. If you refuse to learn how to use it, you may be overtaken by someone who does,” she said.

Allen also views the platform as a legacy project, created to preserve and extend her life’s work for future generations.

**Publications, access and media contact**

Allen also presented the Marites Allen 2027 Horoscope Guides, Feng Shui Almanac 2027 and Feng Shui Planner 2027.

The Marites Allen × INA Fine Jewellery collection is available by private inquiry only.

Destara is available on Google Play for Android users. iPhone users may scan its official QR code or visit destara.app in a browser; the dedicated App Store version is coming soon.

The 2027 books are available at frigga.com.ph and through Frigga Charmed Life on Shopee and Lazada.

The beauty of Feng Shui, Allen says, lies in preparation and knowing when to let go, “And peace is priceless,” she asserts.

Her guiding principle remains: “Feng Shui is a forecast, not a prediction.”

**Coming up**

Follow Marites Allen on her official social media channels for her 2027 Chinese New Year forecast and media appearances.

content:
香港
香港将于2027年5月首次主办由香港大学医学院主办的世界健康峰会区域会议。该活动以“健康跨界”为主题，预计将吸引约2,000名参与者前往香港会议展览中心。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 14 日 04:09 香港时间 · 阅读时间 1 分钟

香港大学李嘉诚医学院（HKUMed）正式接手在中国香港举办2027年世界健康峰会（WHS）区域会议的接力棒。交接于 2026 年 10 月 11 日在柏林举行的 WHS 开幕之夜举行，2026 年主办国内罗毕接替了这一角色。

该会议定于 2027 年 5 月 7 日至 9 日在香港会议展览中心举行，这将标志着香港首次主办全球健康对话的领先国际平台。此次活动以“健康跨越国界”为主题，预计将迎来约2,000人参加。

即将上任的2027年世界健康峰会国际主席兼港大医学院院长刘泽声教授表示：“从内罗毕接过接力棒是一种荣幸，港大医学院已准备好帮助塑造全球卫生合作的新篇章。我们将利用香港作为超级联络人的角色，将领导者和变革者聚集在一起。”
港大医学院于2024年加入WHS学术联盟，成为香港首间加入国际学术网络的院校。它被选为 2027 年区域会议的主办国，突显了它与全球卫生界日益密切的接触。

世界卫生峰会主席阿克塞尔·R·普里斯教授表示，区域会议将区域优先事项和专业知识提升到全球卫生对话中，2027 年会议将为合作应对卫生挑战提供一个中心平台。

会议将举行 40 多场会议，涵盖五个主题：健康公平；数字时代的健康；伙伴关系作为健康之路；科学与创新；以及卫生政策的多部门性。恰逢香港特别行政区成立30周年及香港大学医学院成立140周年。

Hong Kong
Hong Kong will host the World Health Summit Regional Meeting for the first time in May 2027, organised by HKUMed. The event, themed 'Health Across Borders', is expected to draw about 2,000 participants to the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

14 Oct 2026 at 04:09 HKT · 1 min read

The University of Hong Kong's LKS Faculty of Medicine (HKUMed) has officially received the baton to host the World Health Summit (WHS) Regional Meeting 2027 in Hong Kong, China. The handover took place at the WHS Opening Night in Berlin on October 11, 2026, with Nairobi, the 2026 host, passing on the role.

The meeting, scheduled for May 7 to 9, 2027, at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, will mark the first time Hong Kong hosts the leading international platform for global health dialogue. Under the theme "Health Across Borders", the event is expected to welcome about 2,000 participants.

Professor Lau Chak-sing, incoming International President of the World Health Summit 2027 and Dean of Medicine at HKU, said: "Receiving the baton from Nairobi is such a privilege, and HKUMed is ready to help shape the next chapter of global health collaboration. We will harness our city's role as a super connector to bring together leaders and changemakers."

HKUMed joined the WHS Academic Alliance in 2024, becoming the first institution from Hong Kong to join the international academic network. Its selection to host the 2027 Regional Meeting underscored its growing engagement with the global health community.

Professor Axel R. Pries, President of the World Health Summit, said the regional meetings elevate regional priorities and expertise to the global health dialogue, and that the 2027 meeting will provide a central platform for collaboration on health challenges.

The meeting will feature more than 40 sessions across five thematic tracks: Equity in Health; Health in the Digital Era; Partnerships as Pathways in Health; Science and Innovation; and the Multi-sectorality of Health Policy. It will coincide with the 30th anniversary of the Hong Kong SAR and HKUMed's 140th anniversary.

title: PH qualifies for AFC U17 Women’s Asian Cup

content:
THE Philippine Under-17 Women’s National Football Team (Filipinas U17) qualified for the AFC U17 Women’s Asian Cup for the third consecutive time, sweeping Group H of the 2027 qualifying tournament with a 3-0 win over Bangladesh on Sunday at Do’stlik Stadium Training Pitch 1 in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.

The Philippines had earlier beaten host Uzbekistan, 4-0, on Oct. 5.

“Qualifying once is an achievement. Qualifying three times in a row tells us the work behind this program is sustainable. Each batch of the Filipinas U17 has built on the one before it, and we are proud of every player, staff member and supporter who made this possible,” said PFF President John Anthony Gutierrez.

*   [Eala slump continues with Wuhan exit](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/sports/eala-slump-continues-with-wuhan-exit/2445012)

Bangladesh held the Philippines scoreless for 72 minutes. Noelle Granger had a shot in front saved by goalkeeper Meghla Rani Roy in the fifth minute and Aryanna Capsa’s shot from the left was saved in the sixth. Ariana Enderes’ lob from the top was saved in the 16th, and Granger’s running shot from the right was saved in the 24th.

Bangladesh created chances of its own before halftime. Defender Mousumi Akter headed a left corner slightly wide in the 44th minute, and striker Alpi Akter’s lob from outside the box hit the crossbar in first-half stoppage time.

The result extends a run of Asian Cup qualifications by the Filipinas U17, and players from earlier batches are now part of the senior Filipinas squad. Alexa Pino, Jael Guy and Ariana Markey of Batch ’24, and Aiselyn Sia, Tea Pidding and Leah Bradley of Batch ’26, are now regular members of the national team. The senior Filipinas are seeking a second straight FIFA Women’s World Cup appearance next year.

“Sustainable excellence means a young player can see a path from the U17 team to the senior national team. Alexa, Jael, Ariana, Aiselyn, Tea and Leah are examples of that path, and they are helping the Filipinas as the senior team pursues a second straight World Cup. We want every new batch to follow them, and we are seeing great potential in the current U17 Filipinas,” Gutierrez said.

Team manager Selu Lozano said the qualification is an achievement the whole team shares.

**“Credit goes to our players, coaches, staff and everyone who has supported this journey,” he said.**

title: Why the US-China trade truce matters
summary: **NEW YORK —**Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit to Washington in September produced no major new agreement. But it did result in an extension of the trade truce that Xi and US President Donald Trump struck in Busan, South Korea, la
content:
**NEW YORK —**Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit to Washington in September produced no major new agreement. But it did result in an extension of the trade truce that Xi and US President Donald Trump struck in Busan, South Korea, last October. Instead of expiring on Nov. 10, the truce will expire on Jan. 10, 2027. Though modest, this achievement has given an unstable world economy a reprieve.

The core agreement is simple enough: China will refrain from enforcing the export controls on rare earths and related materials that it unveiled last October, and the United States will refrain from raising tariffs further, holding the overall duty on Chinese goods near the 47 percent level reached in Busan (down from 57 percent beforehand). Both sides have grumbled about compliance, but neither wants the truce to lapse before the presidents meet again, first in Shenzhen in November, then the following month in Miami.

China clearly has a great deal of leverage in dealing with Trump. It accounts for roughly 60–70 percent of global rare-earth mining and 85–90 percent of rare-earth processing (the step that turns mixed ores into the oxides used in many critical technologies). And when it comes to the heavy rare-earth elements, China’s grip is even tighter. Processing of dysprosium and terbium, essential ingredients in electric-vehicle magnets, wind turbines, and missile-guidance systems, is carried out almost exclusively in China.

*   [Quo haec patria tendit?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/opinion/columns/quo-haec-patria-tendit/2443321)

On a detailed element-by-element accounting, the US and its allies have meaningful non-Chinese extraction capacity for only seven or eight of the 17 rare earths, but essentially no processing capacity. That could change in the next two years, with the processing figure growing to five elements. The Australian miner Lynas and the US-based MP Materials already ship commercial volumes of lighter elements like neodymium and praseodymium, and within ten years, non-Chinese extraction could cover nearly all light elements and most heavy ones.

But even then, the processing figure may reach only nine elements, with dysprosium and terbium remaining overwhelmingly under Chinese control. While future innovations in processing, or in designing rare earths out of manufactured goods altogether, could alter the picture, such scenarios are harder to predict.

It is also useful to question the belief that “de-risking” from China would leave the US and Europe unambiguously better off. Recent geopolitical developments suggest otherwise. Now that the US no longer wants to be bound by international rules that it considers inconvenient, rare-earth leverage is one of the few remaining restraints on US protectionism and economic warfare.

Since the Trump administration seems oblivious to the cost of tariffs on US households, there is no guarantee that the next round of tariffs would stop at a level Americans can comfortably bear. In fact, by threatening to reduce, but not eliminate, the rare-earth supply, China may be saving Trump from himself, at least in the short term.

The European Union faces a similar situation. It has been more cautious than the US about raising tariffs on Chinese goods, partly because European industry is heavily reliant on Chinese inputs. Although the EU’s own Critical Raw Materials Act targets 40 percent domestic processing by 2030, its auditors reported in February that actual capacity remains near 25 percent. Tellingly, although Japan has spent over a decade and roughly $1.2 billion diversifying away from China since a 2010 rare-earths dispute, its heavy rare-earth imports collapsed by 70–80 percent in early 2026.

*   ![Image 1: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

Export controls were not invented by the Chinese. The US Commerce Department’s Entity List has grown roughly ninefold over the past decade, to nearly 1,200 entries, while China’s own retaliatory lists have grown only through the occasional addition of a few dozen entities at a time. On this measure, the US and the EU currently maintain considerably longer control lists than China does.

Although export controls are nominally aimed at military applications, the national-security rationale is not always as clean as advertised, and the civilian collateral damage often rivals the intended effect. In the case of the US and Chinese export controls, one unintended consequence has been a reduction in US exports and Chinese imports. This is probably because export controls cut off Chinese customers from US suppliers, who mostly failed to find replacement buyers and instead suffered a loss of revenue, profitability, and employment. Whereas Oxford Economics estimates that export controls cost China a cumulative 0.8 percent of GDP in 2024–26, a 2023 input-output study concludes that the US has, in relative terms, lost more, with Japanese, South Korean, and European firms capturing the resulting market share.

In a world where the rules-based trading system is not functioning, a fragile status quo stabilized by mutual leverage is probably better than unilateral acts of dominance or chaos. If the zero-sum wrangling ultimately inspires a return to multilateral negotiation, so much the better.

Shang-Jin Wei, a former chief economist at the Asian Development Bank, is professor of Finance and Economics at Columbia Business School and Columbia University’s School of International and Public Affairs.
