content:
**第十篇：基督住在我们里面**

主题：认识基督如何住在信徒里面，经历基督作生命、作人位，并在日常生活中活基督。

**壹、基督徒最大的奥秘，就是基督住在我们里面**

歌罗西书一章二十六至二十七节：「就是历世历代以来所隐藏的奥秘，但如今向祂的圣徒显明了；神愿意叫他们知道，这奥秘的荣耀在外邦人中是何等的丰富，就是基督在你们里面成了荣耀的盼望。」

哥林多后书十三章五节：「你们要试验自己是否在信仰中；你们要验证自己。岂不知你们自己里面有耶稣基督么？除非你们是经不起试验的。」

这两处经文启示一个极其宝贵的真理：基督不仅是为我们死而复活的救主，更是今天住在我们里面的生命。许多初信者知道主耶稣为我们的罪死在十字架上，也知道祂已经复活、升天。但是，他们可能还不清楚，今天这位复活的基督，竟然住在每一个真实相信祂的人里面。这就是神历世历代所隐藏、如今向圣徒显明的奥秘。

歌罗西书一章二十七节说：「基督在你们里面成了荣耀的盼望。」神不仅要赦免我们的罪，更要把基督分赐到我们里面，使祂成为我们的生命、供应和荣耀的盼望。

**生活中的例子**

一个人拥有一本介绍丰富食物的书，虽然知道许多营养知识，却仍然需要实际吃进食物，才能得到生命的供应。照样，我们不仅需要知道基督的丰富，更需要实际接受并享受基督。

属灵应用：

每天早晨，我们可以向主宣告：「哦，主耶稣！谢谢你不仅是我的救主，更是住在我里面的生命！」

**贰、基督如何住在我们里面？——借着复活成为赐生命的灵**

哥林多前书十五章四十五节下半：「末后的亚当成了赐生命的灵。」

约翰福音十四章十六至十八节：「我要求父，祂必赐给你们另一位保惠师，叫祂永远与你们同在，就是实际的灵，乃世人不能接受的，因为不见祂，也不认识祂；你们却认识祂，因祂与你们同住，且要在你们里面。我不撇下你们为孤儿，我正往你们这里来。」

罗马书八章九至十节：保罗告诉信徒，神的灵住在他们里面；有基督的灵，就属于基督，并且基督是在他们里面。

这几处经文告诉我们，基督今天能够住在信徒里面，是与祂的死而复活，以及圣灵的内住密切相关的。主耶稣在地上时，是神成为肉体，住在人中间。祂经过十字架的死，又从死人中复活。哥林多前书十五章四十五节告诉我们，末后的亚当，就是基督，成了赐生命的灵。

按照李常受弟兄关于经过过程并终极完成之三一神的职事，复活的基督作为赐生命的灵，将祂自己分赐到相信的人里面。这并不是说父、子、灵之间没有区别，乃是强调复活的基督借着那灵，能够真实地住在我们里面，成为我们的生命。

**生活中的例子**

空气虽然看不见，却能够进入人的身体，维持人的呼吸。照样，我们虽然不能用肉眼看见住在里面的基督，却可以借着信心、祷告和操练灵，实际接触并经历祂。当然，基督不是物质的空气；这个例子只是帮助我们认识，看不见不等于不存在。

属灵应用：

我们不需要到遥远的地方寻找主。当我们转向祂、呼求祂时，就能够在灵里接触这位住在我们里面的基督。

**叁、基督住在我们里面的地方，是我们重生的灵**

提摩太后书四章二十二节：「愿主与你的灵同在。愿恩典与你们同在。」

罗马书八章十六节：「那灵自己同我们的灵见证我们是神的儿女。」

哥林多前书六章十七节：「但与主联合的，便是与主成为一灵。」

这三处经文给我们看见，基督住在我们里面，与我们人的灵有特别密切的关系。按照圣经，人有灵、魂、体三部分。（帖前五23）身体是我们接触物质世界的器官。魂包括心思、情感和意志，使我们能够思想、爱好和选择。灵是神所创造、使我们能够接触并接受神的器官。

当我们相信主耶稣时，圣灵使我们的灵得着重生。如今，主与我们的灵同在。基督不仅在天上作我们的救主，也在我们重生的灵里作我们的生命。

**生活中的例子**

一个人遇到困难时，天然的反应可能是立刻担心、着急或发脾气。但是他里面有主。当他停下来，简单呼求：「哦，主耶稣！」他就开始从忙乱的心思转向灵里的主。这就是操练灵、接触主的开始。

**属灵应用**

初信者可以每天操练三件事：呼求主名、向主祷告、将心思转向灵。不必追求特别的感觉，只要凭信接触主。

**肆、基督住在我们里面，是要作我们的生命**

歌罗西书三章四节：「基督是我们的生命，祂显现的时候，你们也要与祂一同显现在荣耀里。」

约翰福音十四章十九节：「还有不多的时候，世人不再看见我，你们却看见我，因为我活着，你们也要活着。」

约翰福音十章十节下半：「我来了，是要叫羊得生命，并且得的更丰盛。」

这些经文告诉我们，基督住在我们里面，首先是要作我们的生命。什么叫作基督作生命？就是我们不再仅仅靠自己的天然能力，努力过一个外面良善的生活，乃是学习凭里面基督的生命生活。

例如：我们天然的生命可能缺少忍耐，但基督是我们的忍耐。我们天然的生命可能没有足够的爱，但基督是我们的爱。我们天然的生命可能常常忧虑，但基督能够成为我们的平安。

这不是说我们不需要作任何选择，而是我们需要学习转向主，与祂合作，让祂的生命在我们里面运行。

**生活中的例子**

一位姊妹在家里照顾孩子，整天忙碌，非常疲倦。当孩子不听话时，她很容易发脾气。但是她想起基督住在她里面。于是，她简单祷告：「主耶稣，我没有忍耐，但你是我的忍耐。求你在我里面活着。」这样的祷告，就是学习经历基督作生命。

属灵应用：

遇到自己不能胜过的软弱时，不要只靠意志努力，更要转向基督，接受祂生命的供应。

**伍、基督不仅作我们的生命，更要作我们的人位**

加拉太书二章二十节：「我已经与基督同钉十字架；现在活着的，不再是我，乃是基督在我里面活着；并且我如今在肉身里所活的生命，是我在神儿子的信里，与祂联结所活的，祂是爱我，为我舍了自己。」

以弗所书三章十七节上半：「使基督借着信，安家在你们心里……」

这里我们需要认识一个更深的真理。基督住在我们里面，不仅要作我们的生命，还要作我们的人位。生命是使我们能够活着的。人位则涉及我们的思想、爱好、选择、决定和生活方向。基督作生命，是祂成为我们生活的供应；基督作人位，是我们让祂在我们里面作主，支配我们的思想、爱好和决定。

**生活中的例子**

一个人买了一栋房子，却只允许新主人使用客厅，不允许他进入卧室、厨房或书房。虽然新主人已经进了房子，却还没有完全安家。照样，基督已经住在我们重生的灵里，但我们可能仍然不愿意让祂管理我们的心思、情感和意志。

我们可能愿意在主日聚会时爱主，却不愿意在家庭生活、金钱使用或个人选择上让主作主。因此，以弗所书三章十七节说，基督要借着信安家在我们心里。这说明基督不仅要住在我们里面，更要在我们心的各部分逐渐得着地位。

**属灵应用**

每天作决定以前，可以先问主：「主耶稣，你喜欢我这样作吗？主啊，我愿意让你作我的人位。」

**陆、如何经历「不再是我，乃是基督在我里面活着」？**

腓立比书一章二十一节上半：「因为在我，活着就是基督……」

哥林多后书四章十至十一节：保罗告诉我们，他常常在身体上带着耶稣的治死，使耶稣的生命也显明在他的身体上。

这说明活基督不是单单学习模仿耶稣外面的行为，乃是借着十字架的工作，使基督复活的生命从我们里面活出来。

我们可以从三个方面操练。

第一，学习否认自己。

当我们天然的意见、脾气和喜好与主的引导相冲突时，愿意放下自己。

第二，学习转向灵。

借着呼求主名、简短祷告，将心思从天然的反应转向里面的基督。

第三，学习顺从里面生命的感觉。

当主光照我们需要道歉、饶恕别人或停止某种不合宜的行为时，愿意顺服。

**生活中的例子**

一位弟兄在工作中受到同事批评。他天然的反应是立刻反驳。但他里面感觉需要安静，先听清楚对方的意见。于是，他在心里呼求：「哦，主耶稣！求你作我的人位。」他没有立即发脾气，而是温和地回应。这不只是外面的修养，更可以是他在具体环境中学习经历基督的结果。

属灵应用：

每天至少在一件事情上操练：不立即凭自己反应，而是先转向主，让祂在我们里面活着。

**柒、基督住在我们里面，是为着生命长大与身体建造**

以弗所书三章十六至十九节：保罗祷告，求父照着祂荣耀的丰富，借着祂的灵，用大能使信徒得以加强到里面的人里，使基督借着信安家在他们心里，并使他们被充满，成为神一切的丰满。

以弗所书四章十五至十六节：这两节经文告诉我们，我们需要在爱里持守真实，在一切事上长到元首基督里面，并借着各部分的功用，使基督的身体在爱里把自己建造起来。神将基督分赐到我们里面，不只是为了改善我们个人的生活，更是为了完成祂永远的经纶。

基督住在我们里面，要逐渐扩展到我们全人。祂要更新我们的心思，变化我们的性情，使我们在生命里长大。当众圣徒都这样经历基督，基督的身体就得着实际的建造。

**生活中的例子**

在召会生活中，一位弟兄可能习惯坚持自己的意见。但当他学习让基督作人位时，就开始愿意听取其他圣徒的交通，学习配搭，并顾到身体的感觉。这样的生命变化，不仅使他个人蒙恩，也使基督的身体得着建造。

属灵应用：

我们不仅要在个人生活中经历基督，也要在家聚会、小排聚会和主日聚会中，学习让基督作我们的生命和人位。

**捌、基督在我们里面，是荣耀的盼望，最终完成新耶路撒冷**

歌罗西书一章二十七节：「……就是基督在你们里面成了荣耀的盼望。」

罗马书八章二十九节：「因为神所预知的人，祂也预定他们模成神儿子的形像，使祂儿子在许多弟兄中作长子。」

神为什么要使基督住在我们里面？不仅是为了叫我们今天有平安、有喜乐、有供应，更是为了使我们在生命里长大，最终被模成基督的形像。

基督今天住在我们里面，是生命。祂天天在我们里面运行，使我们得着更新与变化。将来，祂还要使我们身体得赎，进入荣耀。最终，所有蒙救赎、得重生、被变化并得荣耀的圣徒，要成为新耶路撒冷，作神永远团体的彰显。

按照神永远经纶的启示，神成为人，为要使人在生命和性情上成为神，却无分于神的神格。而这一切，都是借着基督不断将祂自己分赐到我们里面而实现的。

基督住在我们里面，是神经纶的中心经历；基督安家在我们心里，是生命变化的过程；基督从我们里面活出来，是神人生活的实际；新耶路撒冷，是这生命分赐与建造的终极完成。

**玖、结束的话——基督徒生活的秘诀，就是让基督在我们里面活着**

亲爱的弟兄姊妹，今天我们认识了一个极其宝贵的真理：基督住在我们里面！祂不是一位遥远的神，也不是一位只存在于历史中的救主。祂是经过死而复活、今天借着那灵住在我们里面的基督。祂住在我们重生的灵里，作我们的生命。祂还要借着信安家在我们心里，成为我们的人位。

因此，正常的基督徒生活，不是单单靠自己的努力做好人，乃是天天转向里面的基督，享受祂、经历祂，并让祂从我们里面活出来。

当我们发脾气时，让基督作我们的忍耐。当我们缺少爱时，让基督作我们的爱。当我们忧虑时，让基督作我们的平安。当我们需要作决定时，让基督作我们的人位。当我们参加召会聚会时，让基督成为我们彼此交通、配搭和建造的实际。

我们越让基督在里面活着，就越能活出基督；越活出基督，就越能在生命里长大，并与众圣徒一同建造基督的身体。最终，这身体要完成于新耶路撒冷，成为神与人永远团体的彰显。愿我们每天都能宣告：「现在活着的，不再是我，乃是基督在我里面活着！」阿们！

**拾、简短应用祷告**

「哦，主耶稣！谢谢你住在我的灵里，作我的生命。主啊，求你借着信安家在我心里，管理我的思想、爱好和选择。使我天天转向你、享受你、经历你，不再凭自己而活，乃让你从我里面活出来。阿们！」

title: (EDITORIAL from Korea JoongAng Daily on Oct. 9)
summary: 统一部长官淡化朝鲜的地雷挑衅事件 军事调查人员称此次爆炸是一次蓄意挑衅，而统一部长官郑东泳则将其描述为一次意外。国防部得出的结论是，朝鲜军队故意在军事分界线以南埋设地雷，造成三名韩国士兵重伤，这是明显的挑衅行为，违反了《停战协定》。该结论是在参谋长联席会议（JCS）和联合国司令部（UNC）进行调查后得出的。在昨天的议会审计中，
content:
统一部长淡化朝鲜的地雷挑衅行为
军事调查人员称这次爆炸是一次蓄意挑衅，而统一部长官郑东泳则将其描述为一次意外。

国防部得出的结论是，朝鲜军队故意在军事分界线以南埋设地雷，造成三名韩国士兵重伤，这是明显的挑衅行为，违反了《停战协定》。

该结论是在参谋长联席会议（JCS）和联合国司令部（UNC）进行调查后得出的。在昨天的议会审计中，参谋长联席会议主席宣称：“我从未将其视为挑衅。”

然而统一部长官郑东泳周三告诉立法者，该事件尚不能归类为蓄意的地雷袭击。相反，他将其描述为根本上是一次地雷爆炸事故。

统一部长官拒绝接受军方的调查结果，说明了李在明政府对朝政策的混乱。

朝鲜根据其宣布的边境防御政策，一直在 MDL 沿线安装围栏和雷区。

军事当局认为，朝鲜可能已经在分界线以南埋设了数百枚地雷。朝鲜围栏疑似跨越 MDL 的区域也已被确定。韩国和北卡罗来纳大学当局正在准备现场调查。
地雷爆炸发生之际，朝鲜显然正在努力将边界逐渐向南推进。将故意埋设地雷描述为一次事故，实际上为平壤的挑衅提供了借口。

郑在审计期间表示，允许联合国军司令部和朝鲜在没有韩国参与的情况下重新确认 MDL 可能有助于和平与稳定，这进一步引发了争议。 MDL 是防止朝韩两国发生军事冲突的重要边界。

平壤将朝韩关系定义为两个敌对国家之间的关系，并明显向南扩张，自愿削弱韩国在确定边界方面的作用是危险且不负责任的。

政府采用朝鲜语“朝鲜-韩国关系”来描述朝韩两国关系同样是不明智的。

军方的准备工作也需要密切关注。去年9月，参联会利用卫星图像将坡州陆军第25步兵师管辖的MDL以南地区确定为疑似布雷地点。

它向参谋长联席会议主席和国防部长报告了调查结果，并警告可能会发生进一步的入侵。当局必须确定谁在发出警告后做出了决定以及采取了哪些预防措施。
政府必须追究朝鲜的挑衅责任。同样重要的是，它必须彻底调查军事指挥官是否在一年前收到危险预警后仍未能做出适当反应。

国家安全要求政府机构之间做出一致的判断、明确的责任和协调一致的反应，特别是当士兵的生命受到威胁时。
（结尾）

【原文 English Original】
Unification minister downplays North Korean mine provocation
Military investigators called the blast a deliberate provocation, while Unification Minister Chung Dong-young instead described it as an accident.

The Ministry of Defense has concluded that North Korean troops deliberately planted land mines south of the military demarcation line (MDL), seriously injuring three Korean soldiers in a clear provocation that violated the Armistice Agreement.

The conclusion followed investigations by the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) and United Nations Command (UNC). At a parliamentary audit yesterday, the JCS chairman declared, "I have never once considered it anything other than a provocation."

Yet Unification Minister Chung Dong-young told lawmakers Wednesday that the incident could not yet be classified as a deliberate mine attack. He instead described it as fundamentally a land mine explosion accident.

That the unification minister refuses to accept the military's findings illustrates the confusion surrounding the Lee Jae Myung administration's North Korea policy.

North Korea has been installing fences and minefields along the MDL under its declared policy of fortifying its border.

Military authorities believe hundreds of North Korean mines may already have been planted south of the demarcation line. Areas have also been identified where North Korean fences are suspected of crossing the MDL. Korean and UNC authorities are preparing on-site investigations.

The mine explosion occurred amid North Korea's apparent efforts to push the boundary gradually southward. Describing deliberate mine placement as an accident effectively grants Pyongyang an excuse for its provocations.

Chung further stirred controversy by suggesting during the audit that allowing the UNC and North Korea to reconfirm the MDL without Korean participation could contribute to peace and stability. The MDL has served as a crucial boundary preventing military clashes between the two Koreas.

With Pyongyang defining inter-Korean relations as those between two hostile states and apparently encroaching southward, voluntarily diminishing Korea's role in determining the boundary is dangerous and irresponsible.

The government's adoption of the North Korean expression "Joseon-Hankook relations" to describe relations between the two Koreas is similarly ill-advised.

The military's preparedness also requires scrutiny. In September last year, the JCS identified an area south of the MDL under the jurisdiction of the Army's 25th Infantry Division in Paju as a suspected mine-laying site using satellite imagery.

It reported its findings to the JCS chairman and defense minister, warning of possible further incursions. Authorities must establish who made decisions following that warning and what preventive measures were taken.

The government must hold North Korea accountable for its provocation. Equally important, it must thoroughly investigate whether military commanders failed to respond appropriately despite receiving advance warnings of the danger a year earlier.

National security demands consistent judgments, clear accountability and coordinated responses across government agencies, particularly when soldiers' lives are at risk.
(END)

title: China’s crackdown on house churches: An interview with Su Ziming, wife of detained Chinese pastor Wang Lin
zh_title: 中国对家庭教会的镇压：采访被拘留的中国牧师王琳的妻子苏子明
source: 当局如何使用防火墙和其他互联网控制工具？- 国际特赦组织
summary: 2025年10月9日，王林牧师在锡安教会镇压中被警察带走。锡安教会是一个“家庭教会”——换句话说，它是中国主要的新教教会之一，独立于国家批准的宗教体系运作，因此没有正式注册。王林的案件突显了人们对中国独立基督教团体宗教自由的持续担忧。王被捕后的几个月里，他的妻子苏子明和年幼的儿子和女儿遭受了持续的监视和骚扰，并限制他们离开C
content:
2025年10月9日，王林牧师在锡安教会镇压中被警察带走。锡安教会是一个“家庭教会”——换句话说，它是中国主要的新教教会之一，独立于国家批准的宗教体系运作，因此没有正式注册。王林的案件突显了人们对中国独立基督教团体宗教自由的持续担忧。王被捕后的几个月里，他的妻子苏子明和年幼的儿子和女儿遭受了持续的监视和骚扰、限制出境以及长期与家人分离。如今，苏和她的孩子住在美国，而她的丈夫仍被拘留在中国。在这里，苏向国际特赦组织讲述了这次镇压如何改变了她家人的生活轨迹，并描述了中国“家庭教会”及其信仰团体所面临的更广泛的镇压。你丈夫是如何成为信仰领袖的？在成为牧师之前，王林是一名律师。 2006年，他成为基督徒后，离开法律界，进入神学院，并在美国学习了几年神学。 2017年底我们回到中国，王林成为北京锡安教会的信仰领袖。作为一名牧师，他最大的快乐来自于与他人在一起。 2018年，中国当局关闭了北京锡安教会。接下来发生了什么？
政府关闭后，许多成员被当局通过骚扰（包括强制驱逐）或对自己工作的担忧而赶出北京。曾经一起做礼拜的会众发现自己分散在全国各地。在 COVID-19 大流行期间，信徒通过 Zoom 服务和在线圣经学习保持联系。渐渐地，教会不再是一个位于北京的教会，而是一个跨越多个省份的网络。当局允许这样做吗？不！在这个网络发展的同时，监视和镇压也加强了。我想当局长期以来一直试图将家庭教会全面置于他们的监管之下。当家庭教会拒绝政府控制并希望自由行使信仰时，政府就会认为这是一个问题。他们并不害怕利用现行刑法中捏造的指控来解决这个问题。归根结底，无论他们使用什么罪名，他们的最终目的都是摧毁教会并使其消失。当局针对锡安教会采取了哪些策略？在针对锡安教会的案件中，当局指控教会领袖收受“欺诈性收益”，将信徒的什一税和奉献视为非法获得的资金。他们还将教会培训项目和神学院课程视为从事“非法商业活动”。我的丈夫王林因两项罪名被指控。
我认为针对锡安教会的指控反映了近年来更广泛的趋势。虽然一些教会领袖像许多人权捍卫者一样因国家安全指控而受到起诉，但当局越来越多地以“欺诈”和“非法经营”等罪名来针对机构和社区本身的正常行动和管理。这些指控针对哪些活动？在锡安案中，当局将信徒的自愿奉献定义为通过欺诈手段获得的金钱。他们认为这是从人那里获得的钱

【原文 English Original】
On 9 October 2025, Pastor Wang Lin was taken away by police during a crackdown on Zion Church. Zion Church is a “house church” – in other words, one of the primarily protestant churches in China that operate independently of the state-approved religious system and therefore lack official registration. Wang Lin’s case highlights ongoing concerns about religious freedom for independent Christian communities in China. In the months that followed Wang’s arrest, his wife Su Ziming and their young son and daughter endured constant surveillance and harassment, restrictions on their ability to leave China, and prolonged family separation. Today, Su and her children live in the United States, while her husband remains detained in China. Here, Su tells Amnesty International how the crackdown changed the course of her family’s life and describes the wider repression faced by China’s “house churches” and its faith-based communities . How did your husband end up a faith leader? Before becoming a pastor, Wang Lin worked as a lawyer. In 2006, after he became a Christian, he left the legal profession, enrolled in seminary, and spent several years in the US pursuing theological studies. We returned to China at the end of 2017 and Wang Lin became a faith leader at Beijing Zion Church. As a pastor, his greatest joy came from being with others. In 2018, the Chinese authorities shut down Beijing Zion Church. What happened next? After the shutdown, many members were driven out of Beijing by authorities through harassment, including coerced evictions, or concerns about their jobs. A congregation that had once worshipped together found itself scattered across the country. During the COVID-19 pandemic, believers stayed connected through Zoom services and online Bible studies. Gradually, the church became a network spanning multiple provinces rather than a single congregation based in Beijing. And did the authorities allow this? No! At the same time this network developed, surveillance and repression intensified. I think the authorities have tried for a long time to bring house churches fully under their supervision. When house churches refuse government control and wish to exercise their beliefs freely, the governments see this as a problem. And they’re not afraid to use trumped up charges under existing criminal law to solve that problem. At the end of the day, whatever charges they use, their ultimate goal is to crush the church and make it disappear. What are some of the tactics used by the authorities to target the Zion Church? In the case against Zion Church, authorities accused church leaders of receiving “fraudulent proceeds”, treating believers’ tithes and offerings as unlawfully obtained funds. They also characterized church training programmes and seminary courses were deemed as engaging in “illegal business activities.” My husband Wang Lin has been charged on both counts. I think the charges against Zion Church reflect a broader trend in recent years. While some church leaders, like many human rights defenders, are prosecuted on national security charges, authorities have increasingly used charges such as “fraud” and “illegal business operations” to target the normal actions and management of the institutions and communities themselves. What activities are being targeted with these allegations? In the Zion case, the authorities have defined believers’ voluntary offerings as money obtained through fraud. They see it as money that was obtained from people through deception. And as to the theology courses, this was a discipleship training programme within the church. It was never intended to make money. I don’t think this was about actually finding problems with our financial activities; it was aimed at faith communities themselves. What’s been the impact of these allegations? A lot of human rights activists, and very high-profile church leaders, face serious criminal charges like “inciting subversion of state power”. But a lot of damage can be done with these ordinary or more “minor” criminal prosecutions. Not least because it affects the ability of parishioners and believers to exercise their right to freedom of religion. These charges not only stigmatize normal religious activities but also obscure the broader issue of freedom of religion. By treating voluntary offerings as “fraudulent proceeds” and church training programmes as “illegal business activities”, the authorities are effectively criminalizing the peaceful exercise of religious freedom, making it easier to target church leaders and entire faith communities. What about the family members of those targeted – how has it affected you and your family? Even before my husband’s arrest, we were living under immense pressure. We had to move repeatedly, we’d get evicted for no reason, we couldn’t finalize a contract to buy our own home. Wherever we went, it seemed like someone was watching. The most painful thing was seeing our children unable to get an education. Su Ziming Obviously, this had an effect on our children, too. But the most painful thing was seeing our children were unable to get an education. One afternoon, a teacher packed up all of our children’s books and supplies and sent them home. My son asked: “Mom, why do we always have to take our things home?” Even he had begun to realise that this was not the first time our family had faced such disruption. How can I explain? It’s terrible that in China today, simply because of their father’s work, my children don’t have the right to go to school. And so, you decided to leave? Yes. When I tried to leave with our two children in November 2025, we were stopped after entering the airport in Shanghai. The airport security took me aside and escorted me to an interview room; they said I was under an exit ban. They refused to show me any legal documents to justify their actions until hours later – at around 4 in the morning, when I copied down the details of the restriction. Our children were there and saw everything: their mother confronting a room full of police officers. Following sustained international attention and pressure, the authorities eventually lifted the exit ban, allowing us to leave China. But I know this experience has taken an emotional toll on our children. Even here safe in the US, the trauma remains. They often ask: “What if you get arrested too?” It’s a question no mother ever wants to answer. Why have you and other family members decided to go public with this case and the challenges facing Christians, among many faith communities, in China? There have been other church cases that received little public attention over the years, and we have heard reports that people detained then were subjected to abuse and mistreatment. Another house church leader, Yang Rongli, was sentenced to 15 years in prison on fraud charges. But we think that if a case becomes internationally known, authorities often become more cautious in how they treat those in custody. This would be important for the family members of Zion Church, but also to other house churches and believers facing persecution because of their faith. You – international NGOs, governments, the media, the UN – your voices can be the strongest support. Would you like to share a message for your husband? Our children and I will stand with you. I will always believe in you. And no matter if you get sentenced, or for how long, our children and I will wait for you. Amnesty International continues to document the ways in which human rights defenders and others, including faith-based leaders, are targeted with punitive measures by the authorities – and the ways this extends to their family members, despite them not being accused of any crime themselves. Amnesty is concerned about the new Entry-Exit Regulations and the risk that they codify a persistent use of de facto travel and exit bans to constrain freedom of movement for activists and their families. Stand with Su and her family call on Chinese authorities to release Wang Lin and stop targeting faith leaders, their families and communities Sign our petition now The post China’s crackdown on house churches: An interview with Su Ziming, wife of detained Chinese pastor Wang Lin appeared first on Amnesty International .

title: Lawyer Sherily Cua makes memorable debut in Cagayan de Oro chess
summary: Cagayan de Oro City —‎The first time Woman Fide Master Sherily Cua set foot in the City of Gold for competitive chess, she made it personally memorable as the ‎three-time representative of the Philippines at the World Chess Olympiad emerged
content:
Cagayan de Oro City —‎The first time Woman Fide Master Sherily Cua set foot in the City of Gold for competitive chess, she made it personally memorable as the ‎three-time representative of the Philippines at the World Chess Olympiad emerged champion in the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) National Games 2026 Chess Tournament.

‎The Cagayan de Oro hosting of the prestigious IBF chessfest was held Oct. 9 at SM Uptown which saw the Central Luzon pawnpushers sharing the spotlight with Cua by lording it over in the team event.

‎"It's really fun to be here for the first time in Cagayan de Oro, playing on top of the pre-male dominated individual category. The many places for tourist spots, the good vibes, the food culture and peaceful environment to enjoy,"said Cua, a lawyer who wants to be an inspiration for the chess-playing youths that aspire to become legal professionals someday.

*   [WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

"Since chess involves strategic plans and thinking ahead in a smart way, it definitely gives an edge for a chess player to pursue law in college," she added.

‎‎The 39-year-old Cua, who represented‎ Southern Luzon Region, ruled the individual rapid category with a dominant 6.5 points performance in the 7-round Swiss System tournament.

‎Llanos settled for solo second place with 6 points, while defending champion Jason Maxino Bandal of Negros Oriental finished third after prevailing in the tie-break against Judylito Ulanday of Central Luzon.

‎Local bet Robert Manto of the Misamis Oriental Chapter put up a good fight for the home turf after a good start in the first four rounds with a win against Orlando Ba-alan of Palawan, Paulino Cangayo III of Bicolandia Region and Clifford Enoc of Central Visayas Chapter.

title: Kelly Clarkson and Brooklyn store clash on social media
summary: **NEW YORK —**It was something most people have likely done at one time or another: complain to others about feeling judged or dismissed during an interaction, maybe even take to social media to post about it. But just because we might all
content:
**NEW YORK —**It was something most people have likely done at one time or another: complain to others about feeling judged or dismissed during an interaction, maybe even take to social media to post about it.

But just because we might all have the same impulse, we all don’t have the same reach and impact. Exhibit A: a dispute between singer Kelly Clarkson and a small store in Brooklyn that's brought out angry fans and heated commentary.

The conflict from over the weekend, involving a high-priced mechanical bird, is raising more issues than just the quality of customer service. It's also a case study in power dynamics, and the differential that exists between someone with a high profile and those without.

*   [Marites Allen reveals fearless 2027 Fire Sheep forecast, pioneering ‘Destiny Is in Your Stars’ platform](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/entertainment-lifestyle/marites-allen-reveals-fearless-2027-fire-sheep-forecast-pioneering-destiny-is-in-your-stars-platform/2445260)

It started Saturday when Clarkson went to Art of Play, a store in Brooklyn that offers items like books, games and playing cards and also hosts magic shows. But the interaction turned negative, she said in a social media post, when she “was looked at as if I couldn’t afford it” and went on to say the store had “just lost a huge sale.” She named the store and gave it a thumbs down.

A back-and-forth ensued, with the store making its own posts saying initially that the item wasn't for sale and then adding that they had tried to find her an alternative. Clarkson said that wasn't true.

Since Clarkson's initial post, there's been a barrage of commentary online — and, the store owners say, in the real world. There have been hateful messages and reviews, and even someone showing up at the store, said Adam Rubin, one of the partners.

“I don’t understand why these people are willing to debase themselves on behalf of a celebrity they never met,” he said. Representatives for Clarkson did not respond to repeated attempts to get comment.

*   ![Image 1: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

[![Image 2: Kelly Clarkson. PHOTO BY RODIN ECKENROTH/GETTY IMAGES/ AFP](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259060.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259060.jpg)
Kelly Clarkson. PHOTO BY RODIN ECKENROTH/GETTY IMAGES/ AFP

**The power of celebrity is potent**

Celebrities have power in different ways. They can influence what people feel as well as impact what they think or believe, said Alfred Archer, assistant professor at Tilburg University in the Netherlands, who has done research around the ethics and politics of fame.

In a situation like Clarkson's, the influence is heavily weighted in the celebrity's favor as a result, he said. That doesn't mean celebrities should be censored or barred from speaking, but they should be cognizant of that reality in determining what they say and how they say it.

*   ![Image 3: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

“You can’t hold the celebrity responsible for everything that their followers do, of course,” Archer said, but those who have influence should remember that their words can resonate widely and “be careful about what they put on social media and what they communicate in public for that reason.”

That power can also have positive ripples — like when Ms. Rachel, the children's educator and YouTube star, asked people on social media for Black-owned businesses to support. She gave recognition to small businesses like a coffee shop in New Jersey, leading to a huge jump in sales and popularity.

“I think really the responsibility here is to use this power in a responsible way,” Archer said. “And of course, what that looks like in any individual case is going to be a decision for a particular celebrity to make. But they do have to think about it a bit more carefully than an ordinary member of the public does.”

*   ![Image 4: Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/lacson-asks-padilla-to-clarify-disregard-for-law-comment-on-duterte-trial/2444142)

[![Image 5: A general view shows Art of Play, Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, in the Brooklyn borough of New York. AP PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259027.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259027.jpg)
A general view shows Art of Play, Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, in the Brooklyn borough of New York. AP PHOTO

**Social media changed the equation**

While everyday people have always been fascinated by the famous, the explosion of social media and the glut of information — and the way we follow our family and friends right along with our favorite stars — means there's more of a likelihood that people can develop parasocial, or one-sided, unreciprocated relationships with celebrities. That can lead to the kind of harsh messages and bad reviews that the Brooklyn store says it has experienced.

That aspect of modern life is baffling to Franchesca Ramsey, a writer, podcaster, and content creator.

“I think social media itself has heightened people’s ability to feel a connection to a celebrity or a public person that they don’t know,” she said.

“Back in my day, you liked a musician, you put up a poster on the wall. You read the magazine articles about them. You maybe went to their concert. You watched their music videos. But beyond that, it didn’t feel like a two-way relationship. It felt like I’m the fan and this is the person that I really enjoy,” she said.

“Social media has... kind of created this false sense of reality where, I really think even the act of watching someone’s content on your phone and it looks like they’re talking directly to you," she said.

Asked what advice he would give another small-business owner facing this kind of situation, Rubin didn't have any. “This is not something that a small business owner has the capability to deal with,” he said. “This is something that happens on a level of fame and celebrity that I don’t have access to, (that) most normal people don’t have access to.”

Watching the crowd of reporters from his plumbing supply store next door to Art of Play, Daniel Graffeo couldn't believe the uproar was still going on several days after the initial encounter, but wasn't totally surprised. “Nowadays everybody's looking for something, you know, publicity,” he said.

He hoped it would never find him. “I would not want to be in that situation.”

title: 西澳为何视中国游客为祸害？
summary: 对广大珀斯华人来说，很难把马蹄莲和“有害杂草”联系起来。 洁白的花，修长的茎，往花瓶里插上几枝，不用怎么搭配就很好看。婚礼花束里也常有它，讲究的是纯洁、优雅，寄托对爱情的美好祝愿。 所以，第一次在西澳各处的树林中看见成片的马蹄莲，不少华人可能都会愣一下：国内花店里卖的花，这里怎么长得到处都是？ 有些人甚至还会有点替它可惜——这么漂亮，怎么没人要？ 殊不知，当地园林、环保人员看见这片花海，非但不觉得美好，反而只会发愁…… 这片“花海”，霸气外露 据澳大利亚广播公司ABC报道，野
content: 对广大珀斯华人来说，很难把马蹄莲和“有害杂草”联系起来。 洁白的花，修长的茎，往花瓶里插上几枝，不用怎么搭配就很好看。婚礼花束里也常有它，讲究的是纯洁、优雅，寄托对爱情的美好祝愿。 所以，第一次在西澳各处的树林中看见成片的马蹄莲，不少华人可能都会愣一下：国内花店里卖的花，这里怎么长得到处都是？ 有些人甚至还会有点替它可惜——这么漂亮，怎么没人要？ 殊不知，当地园林、环保人员看见这片花海，非但不觉得美好，反而只会发愁…… 这片“花海”，霸气外露 据澳大利亚广播公司ABC报道，野生马蹄莲正在西澳西南部森林持续蔓延，已有超过3000名私人土地业主求助，希望清除自家地上的这种植株。 其中就包括很多珀斯人南下游玩熟悉的地方：马河以南的Boranup Forest，以及Busselton附近的Ludlow Tuart Forest。 林子里，高大的树还在，下面开满白花。乍一看，很难觉得哪里出了问题。 但森林不能只剩下马蹄莲。 参与环境治理的工作人员Obelia Walker解释，森林中大量的生物多样性藏在林下植被里。马蹄莲成片扩张，会挤掉原有植物，也破坏野生动物的栖息地。 Obelia Walker 原本长着不同植物的地方，慢慢变成几乎只剩马蹄莲的地盘。花是越开越整齐了，森林却越来越单调。 而且，这位看着文静的花店常客，实在不太好请走。 它既能靠种子繁殖，也能靠地下根茎扩张。鸟类、水流、被丢弃的园艺垃圾和夹带根茎的泥土，都可能帮它搬家。 地面上的叶子夏天枯了，也不代表清除成功，地下根茎还可能在秋天重新发芽。 养花时盼着植物皮实一点，轮到除草，才知道“生命力旺盛”这几个字有多难办。 农场主Glen Taylor的烦恼就很具体。 他已经把自家土地上的马蹄莲清得差不多了，可附近公共林地仍有大片植株，边界处不断受到侵扰。 你这边认真除草，它那边继续生长。围栏能拦牛，拦不住鸟带来的种子。 这也是当地土地业主和志愿者催促州政府加大治理力度的原因：私人土地在清，公共土地上的问题也得跟上。 州政府则回应，过去九年已向西南部马蹄莲治理项目提供超过260万澳元拨款。目前重点是保护优先区域；然而，考虑到它分布广、再生和传播能力强，现阶段要在整个区域彻底根除，并不现实。 事情已经发展到这一步：当初请进花园的客人，如今只能尽量控制它别再扩大地盘。 不过，局部治理仍然有用。当地的Arum Lily Blitz项目强调，持续几年防治，可以逐步压低数量，后续工作量也会减少，只是很难靠一次清理就收工。 真是我们认识的马蹄莲吗？ 是的，西澳的野生Arum lily，学名是Zantedeschia aethiopica。中国科学院植物研究所的“植物智”资料中，这个学名对应的中文名称，就是马蹄莲。 它也不是从中国“跑来”的，原产地在非洲南部。当年被作为观赏植物引入澳洲，后来从花园逸生，在适宜的环境里扎了根。 所以，并不存在一种在中国温柔、到了西澳突然“变异”的马蹄莲。花还是那种花，只是长在花盆里和铺满自然保护地，后果差得太远。 喜欢归喜欢，在西澳还能养吗？ 先说结论：野外看到这种马蹄莲，别挖回家，也别分株送朋友。 西澳早在2006年9月就实施了全州性的Arum lily活株禁售，官方公告同时禁止植株和种子的移动。农业部门后来的资料也明确提示，发现有人出售或赠送活株，可以向主管部门报告。 不过，盆栽活株和花瓶里的切花要分开看。上述禁售公告明确保留了切花销售，并没有把插瓶用的马蹄莲鲜花一并禁掉。 如果家里已经长着马蹄莲，先确认具体种类，再向当地Council或生物安全机构咨询适用的管理和处置要求。别自行挖出来扔进附近林地，地下根茎碎片也可能继续生长。 至于想买彩色园艺品种的朋友，购买前应核实标签上的学名及西澳规定。颜色不是通行证：当年的禁令也包括这一物种的若干命名栽培品种，其中就有Green Goddess和Pink Mist。 还有一件事，跟它是不是入侵植物无关：马蹄莲有毒。 昆士兰毒物信息中心指出，它的各个部分都有毒，包括白色的佛焰苞和中间黄色的花序。 误食马蹄莲的任何部分，都有可能造成舌头、喉咙肿胀，以及腹痛、呕吐等症状。 汁液接触也可能引起皮肤刺激，对猫狗和牲畜同样有风险。 家里摆放鲜花时，要让孩子和宠物够不着，处理植株时戴手套，也别因为名字里有个“马蹄”，就联想到能吃的荸荠。 若发生误食，可拨打澳洲毒物信息热线13 11 26；出现呼吸困难等严重症状，应立即拨打000。宠物误食则应联系兽医。 说到底，喜欢马蹄莲，和理解西澳为什么要治理它，并不矛盾。 花瓶里插几枝，确实漂亮。森林里铺天盖地都是它，其他植物就没多少位置了。 下次看见林间一片白花，可以拍张照片。至于“这么多，挖两棵回家应该没关系”这一步，咱们还是省了把。 花瓶里插几枝，确实漂亮。森林里铺天盖地都是它，其他植物就没多少位置了。 下次看见林间一片白花，可以拍张照片。至于“这么多，挖两棵回家应该没关系”这一步，咱们还是省了把。

title: Taiwan shares rise as TSMC retreat limits gains - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 台积电撤退限制涨幅，台湾股市上涨 - 焦点台湾
summary: 中新社台北10月14日电 交易商表示，台湾股市周三收盘走高，但回吐了早前的部分涨幅，原因是投资者在台积电定于周四举行的投资者会议之前获利了结。台湾证券交易所基准指数在 48,382.64 点至 49,059.12 点之间波动，最终上涨 284.52 点，至 48,625.83 点，涨幅为 0.59%。营业额总计 9,286.2 亿元新台币（288.9 亿美元）。 “该指数周二暴跌（1.95％）后最初反弹，但在攀升至 49,000 点上方后面临强劲的技术阻力
content:
中新社台北10月14日电 交易商表示，台湾股市周三收盘走高，但回吐了早前的部分涨幅，原因是投资者在台积电定于周四举行的投资者会议之前获利了结。

台湾证券交易所基准指数在 48,382.64 点至 49,059.12 点之间波动，最终上涨 284.52 点，至 48,625.83 点，涨幅为 0.59%。营业额总计 9,286.2 亿元新台币（288.9 亿美元）。

Mega International Investment Services分析师Alex Huang表示：“该指数在周二暴跌（1.95%）后最初反弹，但在攀升至49,000点上方后面临强劲的技术阻力。”

黄说：“随着台积电面临更大的压力，获利回吐在临近尾盘时仍在继续。” “许多投资者宁愿等待，看看这家芯片制造商将在投资者会议上说些什么。”

作为AI应用芯片的主要供应商，占市场总产值约40%的台积电在触及新台币2,535.00元高点后，收盘持平于新台币2,490.00元。其从当日高点回落，使 Taix 指数下跌约 360 点。

“对人工智能基础设施大规模投资回报的怀疑越来越多，”黄说。 “由于人工智能相关半导体股票的估值已经很高，这种担忧阻碍了投资者的购买。”

博通首席执行官 Hock Tan 周一将流入人工智能领域的一些投资描述为“赌场赌博”，这加剧了人们的怀疑。
其他半导体股票也出现获利回吐。存储芯片供应商南亚科技股价下跌1.54%，至新台币480.50元；智能手机IC设计商联发科股价下跌1.10%，收于新台币4,475.00元。然而，IC封装和测试服务提供商日月光科技控股有限公司上涨0.95%，至新台币747.00元。

交易商表示，在半导体行业之外，买盘更为强劲。 iPhone组装商和人工智能服务器制造商鸿海精密工业股份有限公司上涨1.25％，至新台币243.00元，而电源管理解决方案提供商光宝科技股份有限公司上涨2.54％，至新台币283.00元。

黄说：“随着主要石化股从周二开始延续上涨势头，旧经济板块吸引了更多兴趣。”

继第三季财报好转后，台塑、台化纤双双上涨10%，创单日最大涨幅，分别收报新台币88.90元、85.50元，石化指数上涨6.64%。南亚塑胶股价上涨 9.40%，至新台币 349.00 元。

台泥集团董事会周二批准了其子公司 Cimpor International Holdings 的海外上市计划，股价上涨 2.66%，至新台币 27.05 元，水泥板块上涨 1.90%。亚洲水泥收涨 1.36%，报 37.30 新台币。

混合金融板块中，富邦金控上涨0.31%，至新台币160.50元；国泰金控下跌0.44%，至新台币114.00元。
黄说：“除了台积电的投资者会议外，投资者还应该密切关注当天晚些时候公布的美国通胀数据，这可能会影响市场。”

据台湾证券交易所称，周三外国机构投资者在主板净售股价值新台币200.4亿美元。

（弗朗西斯·黄）

结局/AW

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 14 (CNA) Shares in Taiwan closed higher Wednesday but gave up some earlier gains as investors took profits on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) ahead of the chipmaker's investor conference scheduled for Thursday, dealers said.

The Taiex, the Taiwan Stock Exchange's benchmark index, ended up 284.52 points, or 0.59 percent, at 48,625.83 after moving between 48,382.64 and 49,059.12. Turnover totaled NT$928.62 billion (US$28.89 billion).

"The index initially rebounded after a plunge (of 1.95 percent) Tuesday, but faced stiff technical resistance after climbing above 49,000 points," Mega International Investment Services analyst Alex Huang said.

"Profit-taking continued toward the end of the session as TSMC came under heavier pressure," Huang said. "Many investors preferred to wait and see what the chipmaker will say at its investor conference."

As a major supplier of chips used in AI applications, TSMC, which accounts for about 40 percent of the market's total value, closed unchanged at NT$2,490.00 after reaching a high of NT$2,535.00. Its retreat from the day's high shaved about 360 points off the Taiex.

"Doubts about the returns on massive investments in AI infrastructure are growing," Huang said. "With valuations of AI-related semiconductor stocks already high, such concerns have discouraged investors from buying."

Adding to the skepticism, Broadcom CEO Hock Tan described some investment flows into the AI sector as "casino gambling" on Monday.

Profit-taking was also seen in other semiconductor stocks. Shares in memory chip supplier Nanya Technology Corp. fell 1.54 percent to NT$480.50, while smartphone IC designer MediaTek Inc. lost 1.10 percent to close at NT$4,475.00. However, IC packaging and testing services provider ASE Technology Holding Co. rose 0.95 percent to NT$747.00.

Outside the semiconductor sector, buying was stronger, dealers said. iPhone assembler and AI server maker Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. gained 1.25 percent to NT$243.00, while power-management solutions provider Lite-On Technology Corp. rose 2.54 percent to NT$283.00.

"The old economy sector attracted more interest as major petrochemical stocks extended their momentum from Tuesday," Huang said.

Following improved third-quarter earnings reports, Formosa Plastics Corp. and Formosa Chemicals & Fibre Corp. both surged 10 percent, the maximum daily increase, to close at NT$88.90 and NT$85.50, respectively, as the petrochemical index rose 6.64 percent. Nan Ya Plastics Corp. jumped 9.40 percent to NT$349.00.

The cement sector gained 1.90 percent as TCC Group Holdings Co. rose 2.66 percent to NT$27.05 after its board approved a plan on Tuesday to list shares of its subsidiary, Cimpor International Holdings, abroad. Asia Cement Corp. ended up 1.36 percent at NT$37.30.

In the mixed financial sector, Fubon Financial Holding Co. rose 0.31 percent to NT$160.50, while Cathay Financial Holding Co. fell 0.44 percent to NT$114.00.

"In addition to TSMC's investor conference, investors should closely watch U.S. inflation data due later in the day, which could move the market," Huang said.

According to the Taiwan Stock Exchange, foreign institutional investors sold a net NT$20.04 billion worth of shares on the main board Wednesday.

(By Frances Huang)

Enditem/AW

title: Lee’s fighting heart shines in Pueblo de Oro triumph
summary: **MANILA, Philippines**– Tiffany Lee had waited two long years to win again, and when her chance finally came, she had to fight for every inch of it. The Manila-based Korean saw a seemingly comfortable four-shot lead unravel in a harrowing
content:
**MANILA, Philippines**– Tiffany Lee had waited two long years to win again, and when her chance finally came, she had to fight for every inch of it.

The Manila-based Korean saw a seemingly comfortable four-shot lead unravel in a harrowing front-nine struggle at the ICTSI Pueblo de Oro Championship on Wednesday.

But just when the title appeared to be slipping away, the 18-year-old summoned the resolve, composure and fighting heart that have come to define her young career, producing a clutch back-nine rally to turn back Yvon Bisera by two strokes on a closing 72 and end a frustrating wait for her second professional victory.

*   [Scorching 67 propels Zaragosa to share of lead at ICTSI Pueblo de Oro](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/sports/scorching-67-propels-zaragosa-to-share-of-lead-at-ictsi-pueblo-de-oro/2444288)

It was no runaway triumph. It was a test of character.

Lee stumbled early, surrendered her commanding advantage and found herself trailing in a gripping duel that went down to the final hole at Pueblo de Oro Golf and Country Club in Cagayan de Oro.

Get the latest news

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

With the pressure mounting and Bisera threatening to force a playoff, Lee refused to fold, rediscovered her touch at the crucial moment and delivered the decisive blows when the championship hung in the balance.

Back-to-back birdies from No. 14 brought Lee back to two-under overall and pulled her level with Bisera, wiping out the damage of a difficult opening stretch. She then birdied the par-5 No. 17 to regain the outright lead before calmly parring the last hole to close out a gritty even par card.

Her three-round total of four-under 212 secured the championship and the top prize of P162,500 – a richly deserved reward for a player who had endured two years of near-misses and frustration since bursting onto the Ladies Philippine Golf Tour scene with a one-stroke victory in her professional debut at Splendido Taal in 2024.

*   ![Image 1: Sara Duterte hits back at Kapunan over ‘bully’ remark](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258876.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Sara Duterte hits back at Kapunan over ‘bully’ remark](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/national/sara-duterte-hits-back-at-kapunan-over-bully-remark/2445268)

Bisera finished with a 70 for a 214, settling for runner-up honors once again despite having two victories to her credit. In a final round that demanded patience, precision and nerves of steel, she pushed Lee to the limit but could not find the finishing touch in the clutch.

For her, the path to victory was anything but smooth.

“It was a roller-coaster. There were a lot of downs and there were a lot of downs,” said Lee. “I think it was a combination of smart choices and confidence, which is very hard to have under pressure. But I tried my best.” Turning the tide required a moment of brilliance under pressure, which she found on the back nine. Pointing to a clutch birdie on No. 14 as the pivotal turning point.

“I was already one down at that point, so I really needed to make a birdie and create a chance,” she said.

*   ![Image 2: Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/lacson-asks-padilla-to-clarify-disregard-for-law-comment-on-duterte-trial/2444142)

Lee seized that opportunity – and followed it up with two more birdies that sealed her momentum.

Looking back at her journey, Lee was quick to credit her support system, especially her father, Youngin Lee, who serves a multi-faceted role in her career.

“He supports me, coaches me, and caddies for me. Unfortunately, he couldn’t caddie in the last two days due to a back injury,” shared Lee. “Most of the credit goes to my dad, my family, and to ICTSI for providing this circuit.”

Having endured a lengthy dry spell and a frustrating 2025 season where she struggled to contend, self-doubt had begun to creep in. When asked what this latest victory truly meant to her, she opened up about the mental hurdle: “It means a lot. It’s been hard not to win for a long time, and I wasn’t even getting close in 2025, which made me start doubting myself,” she admitted.

*   ![Image 3: Tagle to lead mass at St. Peter's Square while Pope Leo recovers from lung surgery](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258815.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Tagle to lead mass at St. Peter's Square while Pope Leo recovers from lung surgery](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/tagle-to-lead-mass-at-st-peters-square-while-pope-leo-recovers-from-lung-surgery/2445253)

Those doubts, however, have finally given way to renewed self-assurance and a refined mental approach.

“I just let go of the things I cannot control and focused on myself – which is hard because it’s a one-on-one, highly challenging competition,” she said.

“This win is a great reward for all the days I have silently and continuously fought for. So yeah, I’m really happy with this win.” The two-shot winning margin hardly told the full story of a final round that swung dramatically between control and crisis, with Lee's composure and determination ultimately proving decisive.

Armed with a four-shot cushion, she had room to manage the course and dictate the pace of the final round. But golf can be unforgiving, and a shaky front nine quickly transformed what looked like a comfortable march to victory into a battle for survival.

As Lee struggled to maintain her edge, Bisera steadily worked her way back into contention, turning the championship into a tense two-player showdown. Every dropped shot by Lee tightened the contest, while every opportunity for Bisera raised the prospect of another painful near-miss for the teenager who had waited so long to return to the winner's circle.

Lee, however, refused to let the frontside collapse define her day.

With the title slipping from her grasp, she regrouped and dug deep, finding the birdies she desperately needed to pull even at two-under overall. The consecutive gains changed the complexion of the contest, restoring her momentum and forcing Bisera to respond under mounting pressure.

Lee seized the initiative for good on the 17th, where another birdie pushed her back in front. Having fought her way out of trouble and reclaimed control, she faced one final task: keep her nerve on the final hole.

She did exactly that, settling for par and putting the pressure squarely on Bisera to produce something special to stay alive.

One stroke behind with only the closing hole remaining, Bisera went for broke off the tee but pulled her drive, leaving herself a difficult approach into the par-4 18th. She failed to find the green with her second shot, then chipped onto the putting surface but could not save par, taking two putts to finish with a bogey.

The closing mistake ended Bisera's bid to force a playoff and sealed Lee's hard-earned victory.

It was a two-player affair from the outset, and the two contenders delivered the kind of final-round drama that kept the championship in doubt until the final putt. Lee's front-nine troubles gave Bisera an opening, but the Korean’s late surge demonstrated that her long wait for another victory had strengthened rather than diminished her resolve.

The rest of the field could only watch as the duel unfolded.

Martina Miñoza fired a 71 to finish a distant third at 220, while Sarah Ababa carded a 71 for fourth at 222, and Harmie Constantino matched par 72 to take fifth at 223. Apple Fudolin and Velinda Castil shared sixth at 225 after 74 and 75, respectively.

Angela Mangana placed eighth at 226 after a 75, while Princess Superal and Gretchen Villacencio tied for ninth at 227, after 73 and 78, respectively.

Ace Superal shot a 76 to finish tied for 14th at 234 and captured the low amateur honors.

In the end, though, the day belonged to Lee.

Her victory was more than a return to the winner's circle. It was a reminder of the resilience required to survive the unforgiving swings of professional golf – the discipline to endure a collapse, the courage to fight back and the nerve to deliver when a championship is on the line.

Two years after her breakthrough debut victory with a one-shot escape over Mikha Fortuna, Lee finally had another trophy to show for her efforts.

And she earned it the hard way – not by protecting a lead, but by fighting to win it back. TMT

title: Tagle to lead mass at St. Peter's Square while Pope Leo recovers from lung surgery
summary: **(UPDATE) MANILA, Philippines** —Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle will preside over the Holy Mass at St. Peter's Square today,Wednesday. Tagle will lead the mass at 4 p.m. (Philippine time)"in place of Pope Leo XIV, who is recovering from surge
content:
**(UPDATE) MANILA, Philippines** —Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle will preside over the Holy Mass at St. Peter's Square today,Wednesday.

Tagle will lead the mass at 4 p.m. (Philippine time)"in place of Pope Leo XIV, who is recovering from surgery," a post on Tagle's Facebook page said.

The Pope, who had appointed Tagle dean of the College of Cardinals, underwent lung surgery and was diagnosed with lung cancer.

*   [Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/lacson-asks-padilla-to-clarify-disregard-for-law-comment-on-duterte-trial/2444142)

"Let us continue to pray for Pope Leo XIV's healing and full recovery," the post read.

Pope Leo XIV underwent surgery Tuesday that confirmed that he has lung cancer, and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung, the Vatican said.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Tests confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, the Vatican said in a medical bulletin after the surgery. It said the diagnosis had been suspected by preoperative tests and was confirmed during surgery.

The statement made no mention of treatment going forward, and the Vatican said doctors were not currently speaking of chemotherapy or other therapies pending the results of other tests. The Vatican press office noted the medical statement spoke of the “radical” removal of the lobe as an indication that doctors removed all suspect tissue in hopes of removing any lingering traces of the cancer.

Leo's lymph nodes also would have been removed and tested, to determine if the cancer had spread, and there was no word yet on those test results.

*   ![Image 1: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

“Adenocarcinoma is the most common (type of lung cancer), also with the most favorable prognosis,” said Dr. Stephen Liu, a lung cancer expert at Georgetown’s Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center. “While we know the diagnosis we now need to know the stage."

"We now need to know how big it is, how many spots in the lung are involved. Is it just one nodule, or more than one, and the lymph nodes, are they cancerous?” Liu said.

If the cancer has spread, more tests will be needed to determine what kind of therapy to pursue, he said. Options include chemotherapy, a combination of chemotherapy and immunotherapy or targeted therapy, which involves oral pills for specific cancers.

The Vatican says the surgery was successful

*   ![Image 2: Sara Duterte hits back at Kapunan over ‘bully’ remark](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258876.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Sara Duterte hits back at Kapunan over ‘bully’ remark](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/national/sara-duterte-hits-back-at-kapunan-over-bully-remark/2445268)

The 71-year-old was in the operating room for about three hours, the Vatican statement said. The surgery itself lasted approximately 90 minutes.

“The surgery was successful, and there were no complications,” the statement said, adding that the pope later returned to his room.

The right lung is divided into three sections or lobes while the left has two. After one lobe is removed, the remainder of the lung can gradually compensate, especially in otherwise healthy and physically active people.

Leo had walked into Rome’s Gemelli hospital through the main entrance earlier in the day and waved to dozens of well-wishers who had gathered to greet him. The Vatican said the surgery would be performed by a team led by Gemelli’s chief thoracic surgeon, Dr. Stefano Margaritora.

*   ![Image 3: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

The American pontiff has offered a rare level of transparency about the first publicly disclosed major health problem of his 17-month papacy. He revealed the discovery of the localized nodule during his Sunday noon prayer and announced that he would have it removed.

Oncologists said prior to the operation that even if the nodule turned out to be cancerous, Leo’s prognosis would be “excellent” since it would have been removed at an early stage.

The Vatican on Monday canceled all Leo’s audiences through Oct. 20.

While Gemelli has a specific papal apartment that past popes have used, complete with a private chapel on the 10th floor, Leo will actually be staying in a nearby room since the papal apartment is undergoing renovations, according to the Vatican press office.

Recovery could allow November travel to South America

There was no word on whether Leo would be able to keep his planned trip to South America next month.

Oncologists often advise patients not to fly for three weeks after surgery — which would give the pope just the interval needed to make his planned Nov. 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, depending on his recovery.

The current itinerary for the trip is ambitious and the longest of his papacy to date, calling for Leo to clock just over 31,000 kilometers (19,000 miles) on a dozen flights and two helicopter rides, and a significant altitude change in Peru.

"He has decided to undergo surgery soon in order to not change his plans for future overseas trips, so there is no need to worry, as it is not an emergency,” said Tokyo Cardinal Kikuchi Tsutomu, who saw Leo on Monday.

A lung nodule is a small abnormal area measuring less than 3 centimeters (1.2 inches) that sometimes appears on a CT scan of the chest or abdomen. Often, the scans are done to investigate trauma or a lung infection, unrelated to a lung cancer screening. A nodule can be benign or malignant, and oftentimes surgical removal is recommended both to establish whether it is cancer and to treat a malignancy while it is still localized.

The Pope was hospitalized for typhoid fever in 1985

This is believed to be the second hospitalization for Leo, who is known to be sporty and in good shape, with weekly tennis games and swimming.

As a young missionary priest, he came down with typhoid fever in 1985, soon after arriving in Chulucanas, Peru. The illness and hospitalization were a cathartic moment for him to decide to stay in the poverty and discomfort of Peru after living in relative comfort in Rome — a decision that ultimately paved the way to his papacy, according to an interview Leo gave to Elise Ann Allen in 2025 for “Pope Leo XIV: The Biography.”

According to the book, Leo said he prayed to God to let him die rather than suffer the “horrible” pain of the fever. “I was hooked up to an IV, and I said, ‘If this is your sense of humor, Lord, I think you could do a little better.’

“Obviously, I survived; I recovered, but it turned out to be a very significant moment for me, because it was like, ’Well, you’ve already dealt with the illness; you already see what the needs are here — the order, the Augustinians, the church are telling you, ‘We need you here; go for it.’ I never looked back.”

title: Four Hong Kong bus firms seek fare rises of 8.1% to 17.7%

summary: 香港 香港四家专营巴士运营商以燃油和工资成本上涨为由​​，申请加价8.1%至17.7%。政府表示将仔细审查申请，并可能减少或拒绝过度涨价。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 14 日 12:59 HKT · 2 分钟阅读四位特许经营香港巴士营办商已向政府提交加价申请，拟加价
content:
香港
香港四家专营巴士营运商以燃油和工资成本上涨为由，申请加价8.1%至17.7%。政府表示将仔细审查申请，并可能减少或拒绝过度涨价。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 14 日 12:59 香港时间 · 阅读 2 分钟

香港四家专营巴士营办商已向政府提交加价申请，建议加价介乎8.1%至17.7%。九巴申请加价16%，城巴申请加价17.7%，龙运申请加价8.1%，新大屿山巴士申请加价9.8%。政府目前正在考虑这些请求。

运输及物流局向立法会提交的文件显示，专营巴士在2024年及2025年平均每日载客量超过370万人次，较2023年约367万人次略有增加，但仍低于疫情前的水平。这些数字还反映了来自其他公共交通方式的竞争以及乘客出行习惯的结构性变化。
由于竞争、运营和工资成本上升以及燃料供应链中断导致油价持续高位，预计运营环境仍将充满挑战。运营商还需要进行长期的资本投资，例如引进新能源公交车及相关设施。

文件指出，今年中东爆发战争后，近几个月车用柴油标价大幅上涨，给主要使用柴油的运营商增加了额外负担，造成较大的财务压力和经营困难。根据四家运营商的数据，3月份燃油采购价格较1月份上涨约75％至134％，导致3月份燃油费用较1月份上涨约85％至132％。

截至今年6月，所有特许经营商的税后利润临时预测同比大幅下降。九巴的盈利下跌约55%，城巴下跌约52%，龙运下跌约31%，新大屿山巴士则下跌约129%。
该局表示，在评估运营商的财务表现时，会考虑维持其财务可持续性，同时也会考虑公众的支付能力以及对乘客的影响。政府会继续担当把关角色，仔细审核加价申请。在考虑专营巴士票价调整安排的各方面因素后，如认为个别营办商的建议加幅过高，就会减少加幅，甚至拒绝申请。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
Four franchised bus operators in Hong Kong have applied for fare increases ranging from 8.1% to 17.7%, citing rising fuel and wage costs. The government says it will review the applications carefully and may reduce or reject excessive rises.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

14 Oct 2026 at 12:59 HKT · 2 min read

Four franchised bus operators in Hong Kong have submitted fare increase applications to the government, with proposed rises ranging from 8.1 per cent to 17.7 per cent. Kowloon Motor Bus (KMB) has applied for a 16 per cent increase, Citybus for 17.7 per cent, Long Win for 8.1 per cent, and New Lantao Bus for 9.8 per cent. The government is currently considering the requests.

A document submitted by the Transport and Logistics Bureau to the Legislative Council shows that franchised buses recorded an average of more than 3.7 million passenger trips per day in 2024 and 2025, a slight increase from about 3.67 million in 2023, but still below pre-pandemic levels. The figures also reflect competition from other public transport modes and structural changes in passenger travel habits.

The operating environment is expected to remain challenging due to competition, rising operating and wage costs, and persistently high oil prices caused by disruptions to fuel supply chains. Operators also need to make long-term capital investments, such as introducing new energy buses and related facilities.

The document noted that, following the outbreak of war in the Middle East this year, the posted price of diesel for vehicles has surged in recent months, adding an extra burden on operators that mainly use diesel and causing significant financial pressure and operational difficulties. Based on data from the four operators, fuel purchase prices in March were about 75 per cent to 134 per cent higher than in January, leading to fuel expenses in March rising by about 85 per cent to 132 per cent compared with January.

As of June this year, provisional estimates of after-tax profits for all franchised operators had fallen sharply year on year. KMB's profit dropped by about 55 per cent, Citybus by about 52 per cent, Long Win by about 31 per cent, and New Lantao Bus by about 129 per cent.

The bureau said that, when assessing operators' financial performance, it would consider maintaining their financial sustainability while also taking into account the public's ability to pay and the impact on passengers. The government will continue to act as a gatekeeper and carefully review the fare increase applications. After considering all factors under the fare adjustment arrangement for franchised buses, if it believes an individual operator's proposed increase is too high, it will reduce the rise or even reject the application.

title: NASA rover sets interplanetary driving record on Mars
summary: NASA's Perseverance Mars rover has set a new record for the longest distance driven on another world, surpassing a mark held by the Opportunity rover for more than a decade. This was reported yesterday by Chelsea Gohd in Space.com. The six-
content:
NASA's Perseverance Mars rover has set a new record for the longest distance driven on another world, surpassing a mark held by the Opportunity rover for more than a decade. This was reported yesterday by Chelsea Gohd in Space.com.

The six-wheeled robotic explorer reached 28.10 miles (45.22 kilometers) on Oct. 11, exceeding Opportunity's record of 28.06 miles (45.16 kilometers). Opportunity took 14 years to cover that distance, while Perseverance reached the milestone in about five and a half years on Mars.

In a report published Oct. 13, Space.com journalist Chelsea Gohd said the achievement was far from the end of Perseverance's journey. NASA's mission team believes the rover could eventually travel a total of 100 kilometers, more than twice the distance it has covered so far.

Mark Maimone, a rover driver at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, told Space.com that Perseverance was originally designed to travel about 20 kilometers.

The rover has already exceeded that distance by more than twofold, and its systems remain in good condition, Maimone said.

The mission team hopes Perseverance will continue exploring Mars and collecting samples that could provide new information about the planet's geological history and its potential to have supported life.

Vivian Sun, deputy project scientist for the mission at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, told Space.com that most of the rover's original capabilities remain intact, particularly its scientific instruments.

Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater in February 2021. The crater, which measures about 46 kilometers across, is believed to have contained a lake billions of years ago. Its geological formations offer scientists an opportunity to investigate the environmental conditions that existed on ancient Mars.

The rover's capabilities build on decades of NASA experience with earlier Mars missions, including Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and Curiosity. Improvements to Perseverance's wheels, autonomous navigation system and onboard scientific equipment have helped it cover difficult terrain while conducting research.

Gohd reported that Sun credited the mission's success to the combined work of engineers, rover operators and scientists who coordinate driving decisions with the selection of research targets.

The team is preparing to continue south along the rim of Jezero Crater, where different rock formations could provide clues about the planet's earliest geological history.

Some of the rocks exposed along the crater rim may predate the impact that created Jezero. Scientists hope to examine these ancient materials to understand Mars during periods for which few comparable surface rocks remain accessible.

One planned destination is an area known as Rainbow Falls, where scientists suspect the presence of kaolinite, a clay mineral that forms through interactions between water and rock.

Studying such minerals could help researchers reconstruct the conditions under which water existed on Mars billions of years ago. The findings could also contribute to investigations into whether the planet once offered environments suitable for microbial life.

The search for potential signs of ancient life remains an important part of Perseverance's mission. The rover is examining geological formations and collecting rock samples for further study.

NASA designed Perseverance to investigate the habitability of ancient Mars, characterize its geology and collect samples that could eventually be returned to Earth for detailed laboratory analysis.

The rover's record-breaking mileage demonstrates the durability of the vehicle and the advances in autonomous navigation that allow it to operate across a distant planet. Its continued exploration of Jezero Crater could provide further evidence of how Mars evolved and whether its ancient environments were capable of supporting life.

# Kroger plans to eliminate 3K corporate roles

[![Image 19: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/3738_1716910034.jpg)![Image 20: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/3738_1716910034.jpg)](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/reuters "author image")

KROGER plans to cut roughly 3,000 corporate roles over the next three years, CEO Greg Foran told staff in a memo, seen by Reuters on Monday, as the grocer integrates AI into its workflow.

Kroger should reduce duplicative work and adapt with technology, Foran wrote in the memo, adding that the job cuts would help the company cut prices and invest in in-store employees.

Foran took over as Kroger’s CEO in February.

Companies have been rethinking corporate structures and cutting jobs as they increasingly turn to AI to streamline workflows and divert more resources toward the technology, fueling concerns over widespread disruption across sectors.

Last month, the company outlined the company’s AI strategy, including the use of models to manage workflows and leverage customer data to power tools such as its AI shopping assistant.

The grocery retailer had also lowered its annual identical sales target and said it is seeking to cut prices to better compete with rivals such as Walmart and Aldi as consumers grow more frugal under pressure from high gas prices.

Details on the job cuts, which would affect about 37 percent of its 8,200 corporate employees, would be shared in the coming months, Foran said in the memo.

WING.PH is strengthening its online entertainment offering by highlighting the role of gaming providers in delivering a diverse selection of digital games for eligible adult players in the Philippines.

For Wing.ph, the range of available titles and providers helps define the platform’s entertainment offering. Depending on the games currently available, categories may include online slots, classic table games and other interactive casino-style experiences.

DIVERSE PLAY Through its provider lineup, the platform aims to give users access to varied gaming experiences while emphasizing accessibility, clear information and responsible participation. PHOTO FROM WING.PH

Beyond game variety, technology and design influence how users interact with online entertainment. Clear menus, organized categories and accessible game information can help users navigate a platform more easily.

As online gaming continues to evolve, transparent information remains essential to building user confidence. Players benefit from understanding each game’s rules, conditions, payout information where available, and any applicable restrictions before playing.

title: Hong Kong railway builds station off-site to avoid night-time closures
summary: 香港地铁正在屯马线上采用模块化施工方式建造新的洪水桥站，将重达 10,000 吨的车站两半在 30 米外组装，然后滑行就位。该方法避免了在有限的“黄金两小时”夜间窗口期间破坏性的现场工作。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 14 日香港时间 00:04 · 2 分钟阅读 Hong香港铁路运营商正在采用创新的场外施工方法来建造新的铁路
content:
香港
港铁正在屯马线上采用模块化建造方式建造新的洪水桥站，将重达1万吨的车站半部在30米外组装起来，然后滑行就位。该方法避免了在有限的“黄金两小时”夜间窗口期间破坏性的现场工作。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 14 日 00:04 香港时间 · 阅读 2 分钟

一位资深工程师透露，香港铁路运营商正在采用创新的场外施工方法在屯马线建造新的洪水桥站，避免了直接在运营铁路上施工通常造成的干扰。

梁光浩在专栏中写道，该站的两部分长 210 米、宽 15 米、重 10,000 吨，主要由高强度钢制成。它们在距离最终位置约 30 米的地方进行组装，从而可以在正常工作时间内进行工作，而不是在受限制的夜间时段进行。

出于安全原因，带电铁路线上的传统施工只需要在所谓的“黄金两小时”（大约凌晨 2 点到 4 点之间）进行施工。传统方法还涉及混凝土浇筑、钢筋架设等繁杂的湿作业，会给附近设施带来安全隐患和不便。
梁说，模块化设计使得车站结构可以在场外制造并运输到现场，在那里组装好两半，然后滑入到位。他将这一过程描述为需要“全面的规划和完美的执行，以确保远远超出传统土木和建筑工程实践的卓越精度”。

工程师表示，滑移施工方法已广泛应用于世界各地的基建项目，香港专业人士也很快从中学习。他引用了之前粉岭公路高架桥的例子，该高架桥建在邻近空地上，并在临时转盘上旋转约90度就位，避免在拥挤地区进行长时间施工，以免中断铁路服务和供水。

梁振英表示，香港几十年前一直处于科技前沿，但后来慢慢落后于邻国。他对该市目前采用新的建设方法以保持竞争力和有效性表示满意。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编

负责 CLB.org.hk 报道和编辑标准的主编。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
MTR is building the new Hung Shui Kiu Station on the Tuen Ma Line using modular construction, assembling 10,000-tonne station halves 30 metres away before skidding them into place. The method avoids disruptive in-situ work during the limited 'Golden Two Hours' night window.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

14 Oct 2026 at 00:04 HKT · 2 min read

Hong Kong's railway operator is using an innovative off-site construction method to build the new Hung Shui Kiu Station on the Tuen Ma Line, avoiding the disruption normally caused by building directly on an operating railway, a veteran engineer has revealed.

Writing in his column, Edmund Leung Kwong-ho said the station's two halves, each predominantly of high tensile steel, measure 210 metres long and 15 metres wide and weigh 10,000 tonnes. They are being assembled about 30 metres away from their final position, allowing work to take place during normal working hours rather than in the restricted night-time window.

Conventional construction on a live railway line would require work to be done only during the so-called "Golden Two Hours", approximately between 2am and 4am, for safety reasons. Traditional methods also involve messy wet trades such as concrete pouring and the erection of reinforcement steel, which can pose safety risks and inconvenience to nearby facilities.

Leung said the modular design allows the station structure to be fabricated off-site and transported to the location, where the halves are assembled before being skidded into place. He described the process as requiring "comprehensive planning and flawless execution to ensure exceptional precision far beyond traditional civil and building work practices".

The engineer noted that skidding construction methods have been widely adopted in infrastructure projects around the world, and Hong Kong professionals have quickly learned from them. He cited a previous example of the Fanling Highway viaduct, which was built on an empty adjacent site and rotated about 90 degrees into position on a temporary turntable, avoiding prolonged construction in a congested area that could have interrupted railway services and water supplies.

Leung said Hong Kong had been at the forefront of technology decades ago but had slowly trailed behind its neighbours. He expressed satisfaction that the city is now adopting new construction methods to retain competitiveness and effectiveness.

[![Image 3: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

Editor in Chief

title: From parking lots to people places
summary: WALK through any of the Makati CBD’s neighborhoods, and one begins to notice the abundance of open lots serving as parking space. Empty, heat-soaked, lifeless. They sit in front of malls, beside offices, apartment buildings, and even next t
content:
WALK through any of the Makati CBD’s neighborhoods, and one begins to notice the abundance of open lots serving as parking space. Empty, heat-soaked, lifeless.

They sit in front of malls, beside offices, apartment buildings, and even next to schools and hospitals. Prime urban land — often in the most accessible locations — reduced to storage for idle vehicles. This is not just bad design; it is bad economics and irresponsible land use.

**The hidden cost of asphalt**

*   [The strongman finally meets a stronger institution](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/the-strongman-finally-meets-a-stronger-institution/2444846)

A surface parking lot is one of the least productive uses of land in a city. It generates little economic activity, no social interaction, and contributes directly to urban heat, flooding and environmental degradation. And yet, we continue to plan cities as if cars, and not people, are the primary users of space.

In Metro Manila, land values are among the highest in Southeast Asia. Why, then, do we dedicate some of our most valuable parcels to something that produces no life, no culture, and no community? The answer is simple: We do not plan for people.

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

A city is meant to be a place where people meet, linger and interact. Parking lots do the opposite. They hinder mobility, break up urban fabric, and create dead zones between buildings.

Worse, they silently dictate urban form. Buildings are pushed farther apart. Streets widen. Sidewalks shrink. Trees disappear. The city becomes barren, not by accident, but by design. Land area does not grow, yet we act as if it were replenishable.

**A systemic issue**

*   ![Image 1: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

When coming up with solutions, we must address the root of the problem. The deeper issue surrounding parking lots is not a lack of space, but a scarcity of mobility. In the field of urban transportation, there is a hierarchy of road users.

Pedestrians and cyclists sit at the top, for they are the most vulnerable. Automobiles and other motor vehicles sit below. Not only are they the biggest threat on the road, they also consume the most space. Parking is a problem because we prioritize the least efficient mode of transport.

This is most evident in many parts of the US. In a country where the majority travel by car, zoning laws have minimum parking requirements. Drive up to a Walmart, and you’ll easily see that the parking lot takes up as much space as the store itself. Stadiums are the ultimate example with the majority of land area allocated just for parking.

**Lessons from Boston**

*   ![Image 2: Academic freedom no alibi for enabling Sara Duterte](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256409.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Academic freedom no alibi for enabling Sara Duterte](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/opinion/columns/academic-freedom-no-alibi-for-enabling-sara-duterte/2443936)

I would like to reminisce on my time as a student at the Harvard GSD. One particular neighborhood in the Greater Boston Area that has become an exemplar in the management of parking space is the Fenway.

Because of the neighborhood’s integration with Fenway Park, the home of the Red Sox, it has no doubt become a hotbed for both foot traffic and vehicular traffic during game days in April to October of each year. In the early 2000s, the neighborhood surrounding the ballpark was composed almost entirely of parking lots.

Since the late 2000s and the early 2010s, up until the present day, the bulk of these parking lots have been turned into mixed-use and transit-oriented developments with retail, residential and office spaces.

Underground parking is still a component of these new projects. However, it was built to be mixed-use, accommodating vehicular traffic during game season in the Fenway and serving other purposes for the rest of the year.

*   ![Image 3: Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/lacson-asks-padilla-to-clarify-disregard-for-law-comment-on-duterte-trial/2444142)

By shaping a neighborhood to be people-centric, repurposing parking lots creates value instead of taking up space. Property values gradually increase, local businesses thrive, and the streets become safer. It’s a classic play from the urbanist’s handbook: Always aim for the highest and best use of land.

**Local examples in tactical urbanism**

While we can’t get rid of parking lots completely overnight, they can be repurposed for more productive uses. The Mayflower Parking in Greenfield used to be your ordinary parking lot, but when the Food Truck Fest reopened in 2022, the space has never been more productive.

The lot is filled with small businesses serving all sorts of food and beverages to a diverse community, consisting of condo residents, bikers, joggers and office workers. It’s conveniently located near the MRT Shaw Station, and creates night life since it’s open from late afternoon until close to midnight.

Makati also shows how streets flourish when they are closed off to cars and opened for people, as seen with the weekend markets in Legazpi and Salcedo, Makati Street Meet along Paseo de Roxas, and Car-Free Sundays at Ayala Avenue.

These should not be limited to one-day events; their essence should be part of the daily lives of people living and working in Makati. That is why the De la Rosa 2 Carpark is being redeveloped from a parking building into a mixed-use space. This is also known as adaptive reuse.

**The Philippine opportunity**

The Philippines has a rare advantage: We are still building much of our urban future. That means we still have the chance to correct the course.

Only 12 percent of households in Metro Manila own cars. Catering to motorists while neglecting pedestrians, cyclists and commuters is transport injustice. As I said in my UP term paper in 1973, development is not worthy of its name unless it is spread evenly like butter on a piece of bread.

If we continue to allow vast surface parking lots to exist in prime commercial districts, we are effectively subsidizing underdevelopment. Every open asphalt lot has an opportunity cost. That land could house residents and shorten their commute. It could host schools that provide education, or offices that generate employment. It could provide pocket parks that cool the area and improve public health.

We would like to live in smart, resilient and sustainable cities. However, in order for our cities to be future-ready, we must integrate modern planning concepts such as mixed-use zoning, transit-oriented development, proximity-based planning and vertical urbanism, to address the demand for urbanization.

When these concepts are acted upon by city planners, LGUs, property developers and property owners, our cities have a better chance of maximizing our underutilized parking lots and hardscaped open spaces. When land has a multitude of uses, all of the city’s denizens will thrive.
