content: 根据一位美国言论自由活动家的说法，工党工作人员对政府拟议的数字“注意义务”法律的运作情况“一无所知”。这位活动家表示，他在周二堪培拉举行的“狂野”议会大厦会议上感到震惊。 独立美国记者迈克尔·谢伦伯格（Michael Shellenberger）本周在堪培拉，当时工党正准备向议会引入该立法。他在周二下午分享了一段病毒式传播的视频，记录了与两名未具名的政府代表的会面。 “这太疯狂了，”他说，形容这次会议就像身处“苏联俄罗斯”。“首先，他们根本不知道该法案将允许政府运营攻击其政治对手的冒犯性虚假账号。” 谢伦伯格说，当他问为什么需要该法案时，他们告诉他这是为了防止播出诸如美国福特胡德基地恐怖分子尼达尔·哈桑（Nidal Hasan）即将进行的直播处决之类的东西。 “我说，‘你们具体担心什么？’他们回答说，‘我们担心模仿杀手，’”他说。 “我就像说，‘但按照这种逻辑，它将允许政府审查邦迪大屠杀。’他们犹豫不决，他们说，‘哦，但那样会是个新闻事件。’我就像说，‘但你的法案允许你审查新闻。’他们没有回应。 “归根结底，这赋予了政府 [权力] 审查暴力犯罪。任何他们认为可能导致他们所称的严重伤害的内容。该法案将允许政府审查诸如邦迪大屠杀之类的内容。” 一国党（One Nation）领导人保琳·汉森（Pauline Hanson）告诉 news.com.au，“该法案现在被描述为西方世界提出的最极端和最极权主义的审查法律。这就是你从伊朗的阿亚图拉、中国的习近平或俄罗斯的弗拉基米尔·普京那里所期望的那种法律。 一国党领导人保琳·汉森。图片：马丁·奥尔曼/新闻通讯社 “记住我的话，这些权力将被用来对付工党的政治对手，如一国党，以及敢于批评这个腐败政府的普通澳大利亚人。 “这些法律与自由和民主不相容。如果你不能自由地分享和接收信息，你就没有民主。 “最令人担忧的是，该法案允许工党政府运营虚假在线机器人账号来传播政府宣传。 “扼杀批评者和为政府制造同意是独裁政权的做法。它们在民主中没有位置。 “澳大利亚人有批评其政府的权利。他们有理由批评这个糟糕的工党政府。 “该法案绝不应见天日。” 通讯部长阿妮卡·威尔斯（Anika Wells）的发言人向 news.com.au 指出，她本周在议会就对该法案的批评发表了评论。 威尔斯女士将“袜偶”条款描述为研究人员进行“神秘购物式”测试所必需的，以确保有害内容在报告后被实际删除。 她说，Reset.Tech 和迪肯大学最近的一项研究使用袜偶账号在 Facebook、Instagram、TikTok、X、YouTube 和 Pinterest 上报告了 1204 条关于进食障碍的 pro-eating-disorder 内容，但平台只删除了其中一小部分。 “这些澳大利亚研究人员必须在意大利、波兰和德国进行研究，因为，目前，在澳大利亚，他们无法免受法律威胁，”她说。 工党称‘袜偶’是确保平台遵守法律所必需的。图片：达米安·肖/新闻通讯社 “这就是联合党想要阻止的那种透明度和问责制，当他们说袜偶是奥威尔式的间谍行动时。联合党要求解释为什么需要袜偶账号。原因如下——为了对这些公司造成对年轻澳大利亚人伤害的行为进行问责，不仅要听公司说什么，还要检查它们实际在做什么。” 在接受 news.com.au 采访时，谢伦伯格——他一直是他所称为“可怕”和“奥威尔式”法案的直言不讳的批评者——声称工党推动实施其数字“注意义务”法律是“一个认为它将‘永远掌权’的政府的‘非理性、绝望的举动’”。 谢伦伯格作为公共事务研究所（IPA）智库的访客访问澳大利亚，上个月引起广泛社交媒体关注，关注一个在暴露草案中“隐藏”的条款，该条款将赋予网络安全专员创建“袜偶”账号和推送 AI 生成内容的权力。 工党将该法案称为赋予澳大利亚社交媒体用户对其算法更多控制权并保护用户免受“有害”内容的方法，但反对党将其称为“政治审查的空白支票”。 “如果我必须猜测，我认为我们将能够击败它，”谢伦伯格在布里斯班的 CPAC 全国会议上告诉 news.com.au。 “我认为这是一场艰难的斗争。我认为袜偶这件事是许多人最后的稻草。我从未见过类似的事情。” 工党草案法案将袜偶身份定义为“个人在使用在线服务或从事与在线服务相关的任何活动时假扮的虚假或虚构身份”。 迈克尔·谢伦伯格在堪培拉。图片：马丁·奥尔曼/新闻通讯社 它规定网络安全专员“可为执行专员职能或行使本法项下专员权力的目的而假扮袜偶身份”。 它还将允许“经批准的研究人员”“为开展在线安全相关研究的目的而假扮袜偶身份”。 通讯部长的一名发言人上个月表示，“袜偶账号将允许网络安全专员和认证学者测试平台已实施的旨在保护澳大利亚人免受儿童性虐待、极端暴力和恐怖主义等伤害的系统。 但谢伦伯格认为，该立法为政府打开了大门，可以“发动欺骗性的信息战争，以制造对政府政策的表面支持，或反击其对手”。 “如果他们想要那样，如果只是为了执行 [规则]，那么他们会在立法中那样做，”他说。 “该立法 [比那] 更广泛。只要读读法案。不难读。它有一些法律术语，但它清楚地表明它将允许比那多得多。他们甚至说‘无限制’。” 谢伦伯格曾以多种身份在美国国会作证，包括关于所谓的“推特文件”，这是一系列独立网络记者对亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）在 2022 年收购该平台后向其提供的内部文件宝库提供的报告。 网络安全专员朱莉·英曼·格兰特接受媒体采访。图片：约翰·加斯 这位言论自由活动家还反对爱尔兰拟议的仇恨言论法律，这些法律在 2024 年被废除。 “我们英国所有的朋友都说 [爱尔兰法律] 会通过，没必要去 fight 它，因为他们已经输掉了他们在审查立法上的战役，他们称之为《在线安全法》，在 2023 年，”谢伦伯格说。 “在过去的几年里，我们对言论自由问题所获得的关注程度感到高兴。每个人都认为美国人特别热衷于言论自由，我同意这一点……但我总是对言论自由的支持储备感到高兴。” 法律的通过取决于绿党的支持，他们在周一要求包括对科技巨头的更严厉处罚，以及普通澳大利亚人起诉社交媒体平台的权利。 周末，工党同意削弱法律，通过删除有争议的个别部长关于何构成有害内容的决策权，并将其转移给整个议会。 “当你谈论打击在线虚假信息和仇恨言论……我认为你显然进入了审查政治言论、[审查] 新闻的领域，”谢伦伯格说。“它太广泛了。现在他们出来说他们必须回到议会来定义危害……但我假设它将足够宽，以至于能开一辆 Mack 卡车穿过。” 谢伦伯格建议这些法律是“阿尔巴尼斯政府的‘绝望之举’”。 人们在女王街商场用手机接收 Aus Alert。图片：亚当·海德 “推动这项立法的人一直在说，他们的对手，右翼民粹主义者，是法西斯主义者，也许像希特勒，”他说。 “所以他们要么不相信这一点，要么他们认为法西斯主义涉及审查——或者他们认为他们将永远掌权。这两者都不是理性的立场，所以这似乎是一个相当非理性、绝望的举动。” 他补充道，“人们可能会得出的令人不安的结论是，他们认为通过这项立法至少将阻止一国党或民粹主义者掌权，这是他们的真正目标。但他们错过了整个动态。” 谢伦伯格认为，“我们正处于一个像 20 世纪 30 年代或 60 年代那样的世界变革时期，伴随着重大的政治动荡和民粹主义的兴起。 “全球秩序显然正在转移，”他说。 “建制派政党实际上是在利用这一点，而不是试图调整，将所有这些西方国家的移民带入，实际上加强了他们的对手。移民增加了民粹主义的支持，建制派继续这样做……然后他们进行法律战和审查。我认为有一个很好的理由，不是每个例子，但在大多数例子中，它会适得其反。” 当公众认为像唐纳德·特朗普、玛丽娜·勒庞或保琳·汉森这样的人物正在“受到迫害和针对……选民会做出反应”。 工党称数字注意义务法律将保护澳大利亚人免受‘有害’内容。图片：奥利·斯卡夫/法新社 “我们习惯了认为人们按照自己的利益行事，当他们实际上采取自我毁灭的方式时，有点令人惊讶，但我认为这就是正在发生的事情，”他说。 “我们习惯了认为人们是利己主义的，但如果你从历史上看所有这些变革时期，建制派几乎总是参与其自身的自我毁灭。” 就在大卫·肖布里奇（David Shoebridge）作为绿党领导人首次就任周期间，他对草案立法提出了重大关切，拒绝承诺其党的支持，即使政府从法案中剥离了唯一的部长决策权。 根据 ABC，肖布里奇先生警告，立法中提出的最高 1 亿美元罚款对于赚取数十亿美元利润的科技公司来说是不充分的。 相反，他呼吁罚款与公司收入直接挂钩。 绿党还要求该法案赋予普通澳大利亚人直接起诉社交媒体公司的权利，如果他们在平台上受到伤害。 “你不能有这么多部长的自由裁量权。那必须去掉，”肖布里奇先生在周一告诉 ABC。 “如果我们要把数字注意义务放进去，它需要赋予普通澳大利亚人反击这些大型科技平台的权利。你不能有一个权利而没有补救措施。如果我们把它留给一个没有资源的官僚去做，澳大利亚人就会失去机会。” 工党对法案的让步是在联合党和绿党两方面的反弹之后，反对党领袖安格斯·泰勒（Angus Taylor）警告说，初稿是“政治审查的空白支票”。 “我绝对拒绝政治审查的空白支票，”泰勒先生在周一说。 安格斯·泰勒称这些法律是‘政治审查的空白支票’。图片：马丁·奥尔曼/新闻通讯社 “现在我明白阿妮卡·威尔斯想要这样做，因为她经常在议会和公众演讲中说过很多次。她想要那张空白支票。他们不明白。澳大利亚人不想在这个国家进行政治审查，他们也不应该想要它。 “我知道澳大利亚人想要处理对年轻澳大利亚人造成的伤害。我理解这一点，政府的政策在这方面失败了，他们需要修复，我们将与他们合作修复它。但我们不会做的是提供政治审查的空白支票。” 政府辩称，要求议会批准，而不是部长决策，可能会减少其在有害平台出现时快速行动的能力。 在更广泛的改革中，用户将有权选择“退出”算法式推送，平台将被要求保护儿童免受有害内容，包括色情和进食障碍，网络安全将能够发布所谓的 nudify 应用和儿童网络欺凌以及成人网络虐待计划的移除通知。 周六在 CPAC 上，汉森参议员发誓，一国党政府将完全废除网络安全专员，将朱莉·英曼·格兰特称为“凯伦”。 “言论自由是其他所有自由所依赖的自由——失去它，我们就失去一切，”她说。 “现在，堪培拉的一名非选举产生的官僚决定澳大利亚人可以在网上说什么。 “现在，工党爱她。但是是自由党雇佣了她。自由党给了她权力，自由党又给了她五年。所以当自由党在这个会议上站起来告诉你他们相信言论自由时，问他们一个问题。‘谁把凯伦放在负责的位置？’然后问问你自己是否相信他们的答案。 “因为只有一国党政府才能被信任来废除网络安全专员。” ——与佩吉·弗莱尔（Paige Fryer） ——与佩吉·弗莱尔（Paige Fryer）

# Meralco subdues Blackwater, pumps life in playoff bid

 By RICHARD DY

 October 13, 2026

 10

**MANILA, Philippines**— Meralco pulled off a much-needed victory following its 120-115 decision against Blackwater to bolster its PBA Season 50 Governors’ Cup playoff hopes on Tuesday at the Ninoy Aquino Stadium.

Import Jordon Varnado tallied 28 of his game-high 31 points in the last three periods as he helped the Bolts erect leads of as high as 20 points.

Blackwater managed to stage a comeback in the fourth period behind RK Ilagan, Kentrell Barkley and Sedrick Barefield.

*   ['Time for Alex to really regroup. A very disappointing loss' — Noli Eala](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/sports/time-for-alex-to-really-regroup-a-very-disappointing-loss-noli-eala/2444175)

But the Bossing fell short, allowing the Bolts to improve to 4-5, enough to seize fourth spot at Group B.

Blackwater dropped to 3-5, in a tie with Ginebra.

content:
INVESTOR demand for Mynt Inc.’s initial public offering (IPO) exceeded share allocations at several brokerages, with one firm reporting subscriptions more than four times its assigned quota, as investors bet on the growth prospects of GCash’s parent company ahead of its stock market debut.

AB Capital Securities Inc., which handles subscriptions through GCash’s GStocks PH platform, reported that its allocated shares were 165.11 percent oversubscribed as of Friday. Regina Capital Development Corp. head of sales Luis Limlingan, meanwhile, said his firm’s allocation was oversubscribed four times.

Domestic trading participants and retail investors were allocated 2.41 billion shares, equivalent to 30 percent of the base offering of about 8.03 billion shares, according to the offering details.

*   [Trade dept welcomes Mitsubishi-Ayala deal](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/business/corporate-news/trade-dept-welcomes-mitsubishi-ayala-deal/2443998)

COL Financial Inc.’s head of research April Tan attributed the strong investor interest partly to the participation of about 22 cornerstone investors along with the attractive offer price.

“And the price is also good, not expensive,” she added.

In a client memo issued Monday, COL Financial said Mynt retained significant growth potential through GCash, which had 41.5 million monthly active users, equivalent to 56 percent of the country’s adult population.

The brokerage noted that digital payment adoption in more developed markets typically reaches 70 percent to 80 percent of the adult population, suggesting room for GCash to expand its user base.

GCash also had 7.5 million active borrowers, representing about 18 percent of its monthly active users, indicating potential to expand its lending business, COL Financial said.

*   ![Image 1: Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256345.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/news/sandiganbayan-suspends-jinggoy-anew-over-floor-control-mess/2443890)

The platform could also grow through merchant acquisition and overseas remittance services for overseas Filipino workers.

SeA Focus Portfolio hedge fund manager Eric Jurado said the P6.60-per-share IPO price did not require Mynt to sustain its historical earnings growth rate to justify its valuation.

He said the offer price assumed annual growth of 15 percent from Mynt’s 2025 net income of P17.15 billion, or a 25.8 percent growth rate from 2026 to 2028, which he considered achievable based on the company’s historical performance.

“Given GCash’s market leadership, 41.5 million monthly active users, expanding financial ecosystem, and continued shift toward digital payments in the Philippines, I believe that is a realistic hurdle,” Jurado said.

*   ![Image 2: Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256531.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/unexplained-wealth-of-vp-could-hit-p15b/2443897)

He added that investors could benefit if Mynt’s earnings growth exceeded the rate implied by the offer price, potentially prompting the market to recognize greater earnings capacity.

COL Financial estimated that at P6.60 per share, Mynt would be trading at 21.7 times its projected 2026 earnings and 17.1 times its projected 2027 earnings, well below regional peer averages of 33.3 times and 24.2 times, respectively.

Mynt wrapped up its IPO on Monday and is scheduled to list on the Philippine Stock Exchange on Oct. 20 under the ticker symbol GCASH.

The base offering comprises 1.61 billion primary shares and 6.42 billion secondary shares for a total of about 8.03 billion shares, with an additional 1.2 billion secondary shares available through an over-allotment option.

*   ![Image 3: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

At P6.60 per share, the base offering could raise about P53 billion, with total proceeds reaching approximately P60.9 billion if the over-allotment option is fully exercised.

Mynt expects to receive P10.6 billion in gross proceeds from the primary share offering, of which it plans to allocate 60 percent to its credit technology business, 20 percent to product innovation, and the remaining 20 percent for general corporate purposes.

title: TSMC to get 6th straight record profit quarter
summary: TAIPEI — TSMC, the world’s largest manufacturer of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips, will likely report a sixth consecutive quarter of record earnings, driven by booming infrastructure spending in the tech sector. Analysts say de
content:
TAIPEI — TSMC, the world’s largest manufacturer of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips, will likely report a sixth consecutive quarter of record earnings, driven by booming infrastructure spending in the tech sector.

Analysts say demand for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.’s AI chipmaking capacity, as well as its advanced chip packaging technology, CoWoS, remains strong.

That has catapulted Asia’s most valuable company, a key supplier to Nvidia and Apple, to new heights. Its market capitalization is almost double that of South Korean rival Samsung Electronics at around $2.1 trillion.

*   [Mayabang talaga!](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/business/top-business/mayabang-talaga/2442100)

On Thursday, TSMC is expected to report a 65-percent surge in third-quarter net profit to ⁠NT$746.3 billion ($23.4 billion), according to an LSEG SmartEstimate compiled from 16 analysts. SmartEstimates place greater weight on forecasts from analysts who are more consistently accurate.

**An earnings call at which it will provide fourth-quarter and updated full-year guidance is scheduled for 0600 GMT.**

Any result above NT$706.56 billion would mark the company’s highest-ever quarterly net income, as well as its 11th consecutive quarter of profit growth.

Last Thursday, it posted a 50-percent year-on-year rise in third-quarter revenue, beating market forecasts and hitting a new record high.

In an Oct. 6 report, Morgan Stanley analyst Charlie Chan said he expected TSMC to raise its full-year revenue growth forecast to the low-to-mid 40-percent range from its current guidance of more than 40 percent, driven by strong demand for its 3-nanometer chips.

**Texas expansion prospects**

TSMC is investing $265 billion to ⁠build chip factories in the US state of Arizona, including an additional $100 billion that was unveiled in July.

In September, Reuters reported that TSMC was evaluating a potential investment in Texas. Tesla CEO Elon Musk also said last week that his companies would build and operate the Terafab AI chip complex, with TSMC potentially subleasing a part of it.

**Analysts expect TSMC to address questions about its potential expansion plans in Texas.**

*   ![Image 2: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

In his report, Chan ⁠said an expansion in Texas could become necessary given growing customer demand and limited space at TSMC’s Arizona site in five years’ time.

Phelix Lee, senior equity analyst at Morningstar, however, saw limited urgency for TSMC to expand into Texas, given that some of its planned fabs in ⁠Arizona have yet to be built.

“Texas is a good location for a 2030s or 2040s expansion grand plan, given its long history of semiconductor ecosystem and talent pool,” Lee said. “It may be a dangling carrot to preempt potential US trade and other policies.”

On ⁠its July earnings call, the company raised its capex forecast for this year to between $60 billion and $64 billion from a previous prediction at the high end of $52 billion to $56 billion.

title: PH warned of repeated Chinese deployments
summary: THE repeated deployment of a Chinese maritime militia vessel accompanied by dozens of small boats near Kota Island raises concerns over China's continuing efforts to assert its claims in the West Philippine Sea, national security expert and
content:
THE repeated deployment of a Chinese maritime militia vessel accompanied by dozens of small boats near Kota Island raises concerns over China's continuing efforts to assert its claims in the West Philippine Sea, national security expert and civil society leader Jose Antonio Goitia said.

The same Chinese Maritime Militia Vessel (CMMV) 9622 returned to the waters near the Philippine-held island on Oct. 9 with 22 sampans, just 11 days after it was reported in the area with 24 similar boats.

The latest incident involved an alleged attempt by the Chinese vessel to assert control over the area and order Filipino personnel to leave as Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) personnel, supported by the Philippine Marine Corps and Philippine Navy, moved to address the Chinese presence.

*   [Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/news/sandiganbayan-suspends-jinggoy-anew-over-floor-control-mess/2443890)

Goitia said Filipino defenders had the right to remain in Philippine waters and carry out their duties despite the Chinese vessel's reported demand.

“Our Coast Guard, Marines, and Navy have every right to perform their lawful duties in Philippine waters. No foreign vessel can simply order them to leave. They were there to protect our interests, and they had every reason to stay,” he said.

According to the National Task Force for the West Philippine Sea (NTF-WPS), one of the 22 sampans approached within about 250 meters of Kota Island's shoreline.

The Chinese mothership maneuvered around and encircled Philippine boats, claimed the area as Chinese territory and directed the Filipino team to leave.

The PCG and NTF-WPS said the coordinated Philippine response resulted in all the Chinese vessels leaving the island's territorial sea.

*   ![Image 1: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

The task force also accused the Chinese boats of engaging in unauthorized fishing and dumping waste at sea.

The return of CMMV 9622 so soon after its previous deployment highlights the recurring presence of Chinese maritime militia vessels and small boats near Philippine-held features in the disputed South China Sea.

Kota Island, also known as Loaita Island, is part of the Kalayaan Island Group in Palawan. Its territorial sea falls under Philippine sovereignty.

The NTF-WPS said the reported activities violated Philippine laws, including Republic Act 12064, or the Philippine Maritime Zones Act, and Republic Act 8550, or the Philippine Fisheries Code, as amended by Republic Act 10654.

*   ![Image 2: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

China claims most of the South China Sea, including areas disputed by the Philippines.

A 2016 arbitral ruling under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea rejected the legal basis of China's expansive historic-rights claim insofar as it exceeds the maritime rights allowed under the convention. Beijing rejected the ruling.

title: Aston Martin DBX GT puts luxury first
summary: ASTON Martin has expanded its DBX lineup with the new DBX GT, a more comfort-focused version of its high-performance SUV that places greater emphasis on refinement, craftsmanship, and daily usability while retaining the same 727PS twin-turb
content:
ASTON Martin has expanded its DBX lineup with the new DBX GT, a more comfort-focused version of its high-performance SUV that places greater emphasis on refinement, craftsmanship, and daily usability while retaining the same 727PS twin-turbo V8 used in the DBX S.

The DBX GT is aimed at buyers who want a quieter and more understated interpretation of the brand’s SUV. Aston Martin says the model combines improved ride comfort, lower cabin noise, and a more luxurious interior with the same performance capability expected from the DBX range.

*   [Geely Monjaro EM-i takes on Philippine roads](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/fast-times/geely-monjaro-em-i-takes-on-philippine-roads/2443717)

Despite its stronger focus on comfort, the DBX GT retains the performance hardware and chassis capability expected from Aston Martin’s high-performance SUV range.

“DBX GT is aimed at customers who prefer assured elegance over sporting aggression and demand a higher degree of luxury,” Aston Martin CEO Adrian Hallmark said.

“By refining the visual drama and elevating the interior with new elements of craftsmanship, the DBX GT delivers a true ultra-luxury experience; one which comes with no sacrifice in performance,” he added.

Exterior changes are intended to give the DBX GT a more restrained appearance than the sportier DBX S. The most noticeable update is a new double-vane grille, offered in bright or dark finishes, with the split metal vanes extending toward the outer vents and daytime running lights.

The SUV also receives a new two-piece metal side strake with polished and satin finishes inspired by traditional watchmaking. The lower front bumper, side sills, and rear diffuser are painted in body color as standard, while new quad exhaust finishers are arranged horizontally at the rear.

*   ![Image 7: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

A new 22-inch forged wheel with a Satin Titanium diamond-turned finish is standard, paired with all-season tires selected to improve ride comfort and reduce road noise. Buyers can also choose an optional 23-inch wheel and tire package.

Inside, Aston Martin has redesigned both the front and rear seats with additional cushioning, revised bolsters, and new comfort contours.

A 10-mm memory foam layer has been added to the seat cushions, while the rear cabin now features two individually sculpted seating positions designed to provide greater lateral support without sacrificing five-seat capacity.

The DBX GT also comes with a panoramic glass roof, semi-aniline leather, deep-pile floor mats, and GT-specific upholstery combinations. Aston Martin says each front seat uses 691 meters of thread, 3,297 perforation holes, and required more than four and a half hours of craftsmanship to complete.

*   ![Image 8: Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1255072.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/legal-advice/who-should-pay-capital-gains-tax/2443313)

The cabin also receives anodized metal switchgear and a new drive-mode controller, while additional sound-deadening materials, improved body sealing, and acoustic laminated rear side glass have been used to reduce outside noise. Aston Martin claims a 13-percent improvement in its Articulation Index measure, which evaluates how easily occupants can hold a conversation while the vehicle is moving.

Performance

remains unchanged

Despite the stronger focus on refinement, performance remains unchanged from the DBX S.

*   ![Image 9: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

The 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 produces 727 PS and 900 Newton-meters (Nm) of torque, using turbocharger technology shared with the Valhalla supercar. Aston Martin claims a 0-60 mph time of 3.1 seconds and a top speed of 193 mph, or about 311 kph.

Stopping power comes from carbon-ceramic brakes measuring 420 mm at the front and 390 mm at the rear. The DBX GT also uses the faster steering ratio from the DBX S, while retaining a 12-meter turning circle.

The suspension receives its own GT-specific calibration, including revised damper settings and new internal damper valves designed to better filter small, high-frequency road imperfections. Spring behavior also changes according to the selected drive mode to balance ride comfort with body control and steering response.

Aston Martin has also recalibrated the throttle and nine-speed wet-clutch automatic transmission for smoother and more progressive responses in everyday driving. A revised transmission mount and additional longitudinal dampers between the body and rear subframe are intended to improve structural refinement over rough roads and large suspension movements.

The exhaust system also receives a dedicated GT tune. In GT mode, the system is calibrated for quieter progress, while Sport and Sport+ modes restore a more aggressive exhaust note.

“The challenge with DBX GT was achieving meaningful improvements in comfort and refinement in everyday use cases, but keeping the same class-leading reserves of performance and handling we have achieved with the DBX S,” Aston Martin Chief Technology Officer Ian Hoban said.

The DBX GT joins the DBX range as its most comfort-oriented and understated variant while retaining the same headline performance figures as the DBX S.

First deliveries are scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.

title: With contract expiring, KBO club manager recounts fond memories at old home stadium
summary: By Yoo Jee-ho SEOUL, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- Ahead of his final game at Jamsil Baseball Stadium, a historic Seoul ballpark set to be demolished after this year, Lotte Giants manager Kim Tae-hyoung on Monday recounted some fond memories at the v
content:
By Yoo Jee-ho

SEOUL, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- Ahead of his final game at Jamsil Baseball Stadium, a historic Seoul ballpark set to be demolished after this year, Lotte Giants manager Kim Tae-hyoung on Monday recounted some fond memories at the venue over his playing and coaching career.

"My first game here came as a college player during the 1988 Olympics," Kim said, before facing the home team Doosan Bears in the two teams' regular-season finale. "Then I joined Doosan. I played for them and later managed the team for years. All told, I have probably spent 30 years of my baseball life here."

Kim spent his entire 12-year playing career with the Bears but did not leave much of a mark as mostly a backup catcher. As the Bears' manager, though, Kim had a wildly successful run, reaching the Korean Series every year from 2015 to 2021 and winning titles in 2015, 2016 and 2019.

"Those were some happy times," Kim said with a smile.

Asked if he felt sad that the stadium, which opened in 1982, will be replaced after this season, the 59-year-old cracked, "I am not really a sentimental type. Plus, I have my own future to worry about. I am not getting emotional about a stadium."

Lotte Giants manager Kim Tae-hyoung tips his cap toward the crowd after defeating the Hanwha Eagles 7-0 in a Korea Baseball Organization regular-season game at Daejeon Hanwha Life Ballpark in the central city of Daejeon on Sept. 22, 2026, in this file photo provided by the Giants. (PHOTO NOT FOR SALE) (Yonhap)

It provided a rare moment of levity in a season that has given Kim and the rest of the Giants little to celebrate.

Kim's three-year contract will expire after this year and the Giants are expected to go in a new direction after failing to make the postseason in all three years under Kim.

"If they wanted to keep me around beyond this year, they would have told me already," Kim said. "I guess we will find out in a couple of days."

This year, the Giants had gone 63-77-3 (wins-losses-ties) before Monday, eighth place in the 10-team Korea Baseball Organization.

"It is just disappointing overall. We did not make one postseason during my three years here. That is the frustrating part," Kim said, turning more serious. "I can sit here and talk about so many different things. But the bottom line is we just never won enough games.

"When I signed my three-year deal, I promised I would turn this team into a championship contender," Kim continued. "And I didn't get it done. I don't want to make excuses. Someone has to take the responsibility. If I had taken this group of players to the postseason, then it would have improved my own stock. But it is my responsibility as manager that I didn't get it done in my three years here."

jeeho@yna.co.kr

The campaign will first be rolled out in four countries and regions: Japan, Thailand, the Philippines and Taiwan — with the aim of introducing the brand and its enduring appeal to a wider audience.

title: Leaders and Their Movements - Discussing Themes of Progress in World History, Sun, Oct 18, 2026, 3:00 AM   | Meetup
summary: ## Details **Dawns** is a community for history enthusiasts interested in understanding the big picture of human history. The way it works is that there is a different theme each month: * January: **the natural world** (kinship or commodity
content:
## Details

**Dawns** is a community for history enthusiasts interested in understanding the big picture of human history.
 The way it works is that there is a different theme each month:

*   January: **the natural world** (kinship or commodity)
*   February: **industrial modernisation** (industrial revolutions 1-4)
*   March: **"the axial age"** (Moses, Buddha, Socrates, Laozi, Zoroaster)
*   April: **literary history** (oral to internet)
*   May: **energy** (from muscle to nuclear)
*   June: **different modes of living** (e.g. pastoralists, fishing)
*   July: **history of science** (Aristotle, Newton etc)
*   August: **politics and power** (tribes to superpowers)
*   September: **art history** (who and what is art for?)
*   October: **cradles of civilisation** (Egypt, Mesopotamia, Indus Valley, Yellow River, Olmecs and Chico Norte)
*   November: **economics and trade** (bartering to bitcoin?)
*   December: **progressive revelation** (Abraham, Moses, Jesus Christ, Muhammed, Baháʼu'lláh)

There are 5 recommended texts each month - you can read one or more of them if you'd like and this will form the basis of the live discussion.

This is considered an "intentional community" which exists to study human history in the spirit of common humanity.

So it's like a community which agrees that the world needs a new meta-narrative because the old ones are mutually exclusive and seen as not inclusive enough by broad segments of the population - which is driving culture wars and distracting massively from sustainable development.

We don't purport to dictate the meta-narrative of human history - however we intend to help people build their own meta-narratives or meta-frameworks for understanding how all people are part of the same story and share common heritage.

Please join us on telegram to build friendships and feel belonging [https://www.launchpass.com/brites/dawns](https://www.launchpass.com/brites/dawns).
 *******
**January: the natural world**

*   J. Donald Hughes, _An Environmental History of the World_
*   Juliet Clutton-Brock, _A Natural History of Domesticated Mammals_
*   Keith Thomas, _Man and the Natural World_
*   Donald Worster, _Nature's Economy_
*   Rachel Carson, _Silent Spring_

**February: Industrial revolutions**

*   Peter Laslett, _The World We Have Lost_
*   Robert Allen, _The British Industrial Revolution in Global Perspective_
*   E.P. Thompson, _The Making of the English Working Class_
*   Robert Gordon, _The Rise and Fall of American Growth_
*   Chris Miller, _Chip War_

**March: The axial age**

*   Karen Armstrong, _The Great Transformation_
*   Benjamin Schwartz, _The World of Thought in Ancient China_
*   Romila Thapar, _Early India: From the Origins to AD 1300_
*   Israel Finkelstein and Neil Asher Silberman, _The Bible Unearthed_
*   Robin Lane Fox, _The Classical World_

**April: Literary history**

*   Walter Ong, _Orality and Literacy_
*   Martin Puchner, _The Written World_
*   Erich Auerbach, _Mimesis_
*   Ian Watt, _The Rise of the Novel_
*   Pascale Casanova, _The World Republic of Letters_

**May: Energy**

*   Vaclav Smil, _Energy and Civilization: A History_
*   Alfred Crosby, _Children of the Sun_
*   Richard Rhodes, _Energy: A Human History_
*   Andreas Malm, _Fossil Capital_
*   Daniel Yergin, _The Prize_

**June: Different modes of living**

*   Bill Gammage, _The Biggest Estate on Earth_
*   Anatoly Khazanov, _Nomads and the Outside World_
*   Patrick Kirch, _On the Road of the Winds: An Archaeological History of the Pacific Islands_
*   James C. Scott, _The Art of Not Being Governed_
*   Chris Jennings, _Paradise Now: The Story of American Utopianism_

**July: The scientific worldview**

*   Steven Weinberg, _To Explain the World_
*   Jim Al-Khalili, _The House of Wisdom_
*   Thomas Kuhn, _The Copernican Revolution_
*   Bill Bryson, _A Short History of Nearly Everything_
*   Carlo Rovelli, _The First Scientist: Anaximander and His Legacy_

**August: Politics and power**

*   Christopher Boehm, _Hierarchy in the Forest_
*   Francis Fukuyama, _The Origins of Political Order_
*   David Stasavage, _The Decline and Rise of Democracy_
*   Benedict Anderson, _Imagined Communities_
*   Lynn Hunt, _Inventing Human Rights_

**September: Art history**

*   E.H. Gombrich, _The Story of Art_
*   David Lewis-Williams, _The Mind in the Cave_
*   Michael Baxandall, _Painting and Experience in Fifteenth-Century Italy_
*   Robert Hughes, _The Shock of the New_
*   Julian Stallabrass, _Contemporary Art: A Very Short Introduction_

**October: Cradles of civilisation**

*   Marc Van De Mieroop, _A History of the Ancient Near East ca. 3000-323 BC_
*   Toby Wilkinson, _The Rise and Fall of Ancient Egypt_
*   Li Feng, _Early China: A Social and Cultural History_
*   Gregory Possehl, _The Indus Civilization: A Contemporary Perspective_
*   Charles C. Mann, _1491_

**November: Economics and trade**

*   David Graeber, _Debt: The First 5,000 Years_
*   James C. Scott, _Against the Grain_
*   William Bernstein, _A Splendid Exchange_
*   Sven Beckert, _Empire of Cotton_
*   Jeffry Frieden, _Global Capitalism: Its Fall and Rise in the Twentieth Century_

**December: Progressive revelation**

*   Karen Armstrong, _A History of God_
*   Israel Finkelstein and Neil Asher Silberman, _The Bible Unearthed_
*   Geza Vermes, _The Religion of Jesus the Jew_
*   Fred Donner, _Muhammad and the Believers_
*   Moojan Momen, _The Bábí and Bahá'í Religions, 1844-1944_

title: Gordon nets first Barca goal as Liga leaders beat Getafe
summary: **BARCELONA,**Spain —Anthony Gordon scored his first goal for Barcelona as the Spanish champions extended their perfect start in La Liga with a 3-0 win over Getafe on Saturday. England international Gordon opened the scoring in the second m
content:
**BARCELONA,**Spain —Anthony Gordon scored his first goal for Barcelona as the Spanish champions extended their perfect start in La Liga with a 3-0 win over Getafe on Saturday.

England international Gordon opened the scoring in the second minute and Gabriel Jesus added another after half an hour for the league leaders, who have won every match they have played this season.

French defender Jules Kounde tucked home the third from Lamine Yamal's cross to cap Barca's solid win against Jose Bordalas's side at Camp Nou.

Barca were without their top scorer Raphinha, who sustained a hamstring problem during the international break with Brazil.

title: KBO's Eagles decide not to re-sign manager Kim Kyung-moon
summary: By Yoo Jee-ho SEOUL, Oct. 10 (Yonhap) -- The Hanwha Eagles announced Saturday they will not bring back manager Kim Kyung-moon after his three-year contract expires at the end of this season. Kim first took over the Eagles in June 2024. Last
content:
By Yoo Jee-ho

SEOUL, Oct. 10 (Yonhap) -- The Hanwha Eagles announced Saturday they will not bring back manager Kim Kyung-moon after his three-year contract expires at the end of this season.

Kim first took over the Eagles in June 2024. Last year, he guided the Eagles to their first Korean Series since 2006, but they lost to the LG Twins in five games.

This year, the Eagles had long clinched ninth place in the 10-team Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) prior to their final regular-season game Saturday, with a win-loss-tie record of 57-82-4.

The Eagles said they are looking to hire a new manager with Kim's contract expiring, and they also thanked the veteran skipper for his services.

Hanwha Eagles manager Kim Kyung-moon watches his team in action against the Kia Tigers during the clubs' Korea Baseball Organization regular-season game at Gwangju-Kia Champions Field in the southwestern city of Gwangju, in this Sept. 13, 2026, file photo provided by the Eagles. (PHOTO NOT FOR SALE) (Yonhap)

Kim himself announced he will not be back next year during his pregame media availability Saturday.

"This will be my last game here. I am really sorry to our fans that we have lost so many games," Kim told reporters at Daejeon Hanwha Life Ballpark in Daejeon, some 140 kilometers south of Seoul. "I feel bad that I am leaving without having made the team better. I would like to thank all the players, coaches and front office staff that have been with me on this journey."

At 67, Kim has been the oldest manager in the KBO this year. He has yet to win a Korean Series title in over 20 years as manager -- the 2025 runner-up finish being his fifth.

He is one of three managers in league history with over 1,000 regular-season wins. He came into Saturday's game with 1,078 wins, 957 losses and 39 ties.

In 2025, the Eagles nearly won the pennant and posted the second-best record in the regular season at 83-57-4. Their two American aces, Cody Ponce and Ryan Weiss, formed a deadly one-two punch atop the rotation, combining for 33 wins and 459 strikeouts in 359 1/3 innings. Ponce was voted the league MVP after winning the pitching Triple Crown as the league leader in wins, ERA and strikeouts. He and Weiss, with 252 strikeouts and 207 strikeouts, respectively, became the first pair of teammates to record at least 200 Ks in the same season.

However, both of them left for Major League Baseball this year, and their two replacements, Owen White and Wilkel Hernandez, never filled that void. After Hernandez was cut in July, his replacement, Bruce Zimmermann, also struggled mightily in the rotation before moving to the bullpen.

The Eagles' offense this year has been better than 2025, as they are tops in the KBO with 175 home runs and 813 runs scored. Their big free agent acquisition Kang Baek-ho has led the way with his career-high 34 dingers.

But they have the KBO's second-worst ERA at 5.27, compared with their league-best mark of 3.55 in 2025.

## Details

Are yoAre you ready to walk on the wild side? Embrace your inner Norse goddess as you learn about travel in Iceland.
 Are you ready to walk on the wild side?
 Embrace your inner Norse goddess as you learn all about how to **travel to Iceland**, land of hot springs, glaciers, and the hypnotic shimmer of the Aurora Borealis (northern lights) in dark skies.
 Iceland may be small - less than 400,000 inhabitants - but the terrain is mighty.
 There is nothing quite like this volcanic, rugged, remote island that will have you humming Led Zepplin's _[Immigrant Song](http://%5Bhttps//%5B%5Byoutu.be/TRjH\_gJbUqQ?si=3LgVhFpRzRh8UzG6%5D%5D%5D(%5Byoutu.be/TRjH\_gJbUqQ?si=3LgVhFpRzRh8UzG6%5D%5D)(%5Byoutu.be/TRjH\_gJbUqQ?si=3LgVhFpRzRh8UzG6%5D%5D(youtu.be/TRjH\_gJbUqQ?si=3LgVhFpRzRh8UzG6%5D))(%5B%5Bhttps://youtu.be/TRjH\_gJbUqQ?si=3LgVhFpRzRh8UzG6%5D%5D(https://youtu.be/TRjH\_gJbUqQ?si=3LgVhFpRzRh8UzG6%5D)(%5Bhttps://youtu.be/TRjH\_gJbUqQ?si=3LgVhFpRzRh8UzG6%5D(https://youtu.be/TRjH\_gJbUqQ?si=3LgVhFpRzRh8UzG6))) "[[[https://youtu.be/TRjH\_gJbUqQ?si=3LgVhFpRzRh8UzG6](https://youtu.be/TRjH\_gJbUqQ?si=3LgVhFpRzRh8UzG6)](https://youtu.be/TRjH\_gJbUqQ?si=3LgVhFpRzRh8UzG6)]([https://youtu.be/TRjH\_gJbUqQ?si=3LgVhFpRzRh8UzG6](https://youtu.be/TRjH\_gJbUqQ?si=3LgVhFpRzRh8UzG6))")_ (yeah, it's about Iceland.)
**What we will cover during this travel class:**

1.   Timing? Why we like to go in the early spring.
2.   Packing.
3.   Gear for Icelandic weather.
4.   Thingvellir National Park in the Golden Circle and the Caves of Hella.
5.   Hot spring spas (is the Blue Lagoon worth it?).
6.   Getting there and around.
7.   Iceland’s many waterfalls, including Gulfoss and Seljalandsfoss.
8.   Money matters.
9.   Tracking the Aurora Borealis.
10.   Where we go in **March 2027** (and why we think you should, too).
11.   Why we love all women trips and who comes on trips with us.
12.   And a Q&A sesh so you can ask us questions.

title: Digital portal aims to upgrade live-selling experience
summary: Jhaena Jewels is taking its six-year live-selling journey into the digital space with a new portal designed to connect live shopping, online transactions, order tracking and customer support in one platform. The new digital home allows cust
content:
Jhaena Jewels is taking its six-year live-selling journey into the digital space with a new portal designed to connect live shopping, online transactions, order tracking and customer support in one platform.

The new digital home allows customers to register for personal accounts where they can view their claims, orders, invoices, payments and delivery information in one place. Customers can also browse available jewelry through the online shop and continue to discover and claim pieces during live-selling sessions.

Founder and CEO Haena Sia-Foo said the portal is designed to complement, rather than replace, the live-selling experience that helped build the brand’s community.

“When we started Jhaena Jewels six years ago, live selling was one of the important parts of our journey. I love the connection with our clients and the community that we built together for the past six years,” Sia-Foo said during the launch.

The portal addresses some of the manual processes associated with live selling, including sending screenshots, messaging administrators to confirm item availability and following up on payments.

Jhaena Jewels OIC Arlene Natividad said the platform was developed as the company looked for ways to make transactions easier without losing the personal interaction customers have come to expect from the brand.

“As the community grew, we also started asking ourselves, how can we make the experience easier, clearer and more connected for our customers without taking away the live experience that they already love?” Natividad said.

Through the portal, customers can claim an available piece, proceed to checkout and receive an automatically generated invoice. They can also upload proof of payment directly to their account, while payment status and delivery information can be tracked through the system.

“Instead of looking for screenshots, going back through messages or asking where your transaction is, we are giving you a more organized way,” Natividad said.

The system also connects purchases made through live selling and the online shop, allowing customers to review their transactions and invoices in one purchase history.

“Less guessing, more transparency. We want our customers to feel more informed and more confident about their transactions,” Natividad said.

The platform is also designed for customers who miss live sessions. Available pieces featured during a broadcast can still be browsed through the portal after the live session, giving customers another way to see and purchase items.

[![Image 7: A selection of fine jewelry pieces featuring diamonds and colored gemstones ](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253059.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253059.jpg)
A selection of fine jewelry pieces featuring diamonds and colored gemstones

Sia-Foo emphasized that the familiar “mine” culture of live selling remains part of the experience, although it now takes on a digital form.

“On the website, ‘mine’ becomes a claim. You just have to tap the claim there for it to go to our portal or checkout,” Sia-Foo said.

Once a customer claims an item, the transaction moves through the cart, checkout, invoicing, payment and delivery stages within the system.

Sia-Foo said the company will continue using social media for live selling with broadcasts viewable on the website.

“Are we going to replace live selling? The answer, of course, is no. We’re actually upgrading it,” she said.

The portal forms part of the brand’s broader sixth-year theme, “Access is the New Luxury.” Sia-Foo said the company’s goal is to make access to jewelry, information, sourcing networks and opportunities more attainable for its customers and partners.

“Luxury is not just about owning something. Luxury is about access to quality, and to the better value of something that we know will create a memory for us forever,” she said.

Sia-Foo said the company spent years developing relationships with manufacturers, artisans, diamond cutters and polishers in jewelry markets around the world, including India, Hong Kong, Thailand, Japan and Italy.

The company is also looking to expand its ecosystem to include affiliates, live sellers, entrepreneurs, resellers and other business partners.

“We spent six years building a foundation. Now, we have the technology and infrastructure to open it to more people,” she said.

For Sia-Foo, the portal is the latest step in a journey that began with live selling and limited resources.

“I started with just one phone, one sticky note, a phone stand and my ball pen. But I had something much bigger than that. I had a dream,” she said.

“Real luxury today isn’t only about owning something beautiful. It’s having access to something that was once beyond our reach,” she finally added.

title: Guardians rally to stay alive in MLB playoffs
summary: **LOS ANGELES**— The Cleveland Guardians exploded for six runs in the sixth inning to beat the Chicago White Sox, 9-5, on Thursday (Friday in Manila) and force a deciding Game 5 in their Major League Baseball (MLB) playoff series. Jose Rami
content:
**LOS ANGELES**— The Cleveland Guardians exploded for six runs in the sixth inning to beat the Chicago White Sox, 9-5, on Thursday (Friday in Manila) and force a deciding Game 5 in their Major League Baseball (MLB) playoff series.

Jose Ramirez belted a two-run home run in fifth inning and delivered a run-scoring single in the Guardians’ big sixth to help Cleveland win a second straight game in Chicago after dropping the first two games of the best-of-five American League division series at home.

Having denied the White Sox’s bid to clinch a playoff series at home for the first time since 1906, the Guardians will host game five on Saturday.

*   [St. Benilde extends win streak to four](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/sports/st-benilde-extends-win-streak-to-four/2442657)

Ten teams have come back from an 0-2 deficit to win a best-of-five playoff series, the most recent the New York Yankees in 2017 — against Cleveland.

“It’s going to be a crazy energy,” said Ramirez, who followed pinch-hitter Patrick Bailey’s solo homer in the fifth by belting a 99.9 mph fastball from White Sox relief pitcher Jordan Hicks into the bullpen for a two-run home run that put the Guardians up, 3-2.

title: Inconvenience fee
summary: EVERY day, you are being robbed — and you probably don’t even notice it. When you buy load for your mobile phone, and you choose the GoEXTRA179 package to get data, calls and text for 15 days using the e-wallet GCash, you don’t pay just P17
content:
EVERY day, you are being robbed — and you probably don’t even notice it.

When you buy load for your mobile phone, and you choose the GoEXTRA179 package to get data, calls and text for 15 days using the e-wallet GCash, you don’t pay just P179 as the name of the product might suggest, but P181 with a P2 “convenience fee” tacked on.

Paying your power bill? Meralco Online charges a convenience fee of P6 if you pay by GCash, P7 if you use Maya and P15 if you pay with a credit or debit card.

*   [US-China war now](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/us-china-war-now/2442742)

If you go to the PLDT web portal to pay your phone and internet service bill, there’s a P15 charge when you use a credit or debit card, or a P7 fee if you use GCash.

Booking a flight? Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific charge a booking or payment processing fee ranging from P150 to P250 per passenger per sector for online card payments.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Even when buying movie tickets online, you’re paying P20 to P100 more per ticket or transaction.

The amounts may seem small, but add up to hefty sums when multiplied by millions of transactions every month.

Back when the internet was new and digital payments were novel, we accepted convenience fees as a tax for the luxury of skipping a long line. However, now that digital transactions make up the bulk of everyday commerce, the convenience fee is outdated at best. At worst, it gives companies an excuse to bilk their customers while providing little or no added value. After all, where is the convenience in paying for a service or commodity that can only be paid for online?

*   ![Image 1: Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252636.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/news/man-arrested-after-breaching-naia-security-to-reunite-with-ofw-wife/2442354)

These days, digital is no longer an alternative channel. Convenience fees were originally designed as a premium charge for an optional service. When a transaction channel becomes the standard or primary method of interaction, charging extra for it makes no sense.

Besides, who enjoys greater convenience from online transactions? Consumers or merchants?

Businesses can realize massive savings by processing payments digitally. This reduces cash-handling liabilities and theft risks, onsite staffing and real estate overhead, manual bookkeeping and reconciliation errors.

Digital adoption drives operational expenses down for the merchant. Passing payment processing costs onto the customer instead of absorbing them as standard overhead is like double-dipping — it’s greedy and inconsiderate.

*   ![Image 2: The banana chip witch hunt: China, CALE88 and the weaponization of national security against Sara Duterte](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253556.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[The banana chip witch hunt: China, CALE88 and the weaponization of national security against Sara Duterte](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/the-banana-chip-witch-hunt-china-cale88-and-the-weaponization-of-national-security-against-sara-duterte/2442743)

For private companies — especially utilities — charging the consumer for online transactions is completely unjustified. These companies actively reduce their operational footprint by pushing their customers online. Why do you think these companies are so eager to shift you to electronic billing? Because it costs them less.

These days, the processing fee should be treated as a basic cost of doing business, just like rent, electricity or point-of-sale hardware. Your neighborhood grocer doesn’t charge you a convenience fee to pay for his electronic cash register, so why should you be made to pay for your merchant’s computer network?

Some telcos try to justify the fee by saying the money goes to cybersecurity, server maintenance and fraud prevention measures to secure our online transactions and data. But what brick-and-mortar store charges you for the padlock on their gate or the security guard at the door?

On our side of the equation, customers are using their own devices, electricity and internet connections to complete online transactions. Without customers investing in their own gadgets and data, what use is a merchant’s digital payment platform? Customers are already paying for one end of the digital infrastructure necessary to make online transactions possible. Why should we pay more? Maybe it’s time these merchants pay us a convenience fee.

content:
## Details

**Dawns** is a community for history enthusiasts interested in understanding the big picture of human history.
 The way it works is that there is a different theme each month:

*   January: **the natural world** (kinship or commodity)
*   February: **industrial modernisation** (industrial revolutions 1-4)
*   March: **"the axial age"** (Moses, Buddha, Socrates, Laozi, Zoroaster)
*   April: **literary history** (oral to internet)
*   May: **energy** (from muscle to nuclear)
*   June: **different modes of living** (e.g. pastoralists, fishing)
*   July: **history of science** (Aristotle, Newton etc)
*   August: **politics and power** (tribes to superpowers)
*   September: **art history** (who and what is art for?)
*   October: **cradles of civilisation** (Egypt, Mesopotamia, Indus Valley, Yellow River, Olmecs and Chico Norte)
*   November: **economics and trade** (bartering to bitcoin?)
*   December: **progressive revelation** (Abraham, Moses, Jesus Christ, Muhammed, Baháʼu'lláh)

There are 5 recommended texts each month - you can read one or more of them if you'd like and this will form the basis of the live discussion.

This is considered an "intentional community" which exists to study human history in the spirit of common humanity.

So it's like a community which agrees that the world needs a new meta-narrative because the old ones are mutually exclusive and seen as not inclusive enough by broad segments of the population - which is driving culture wars and distracting massively from sustainable development.

We don't purport to dictate the meta-narrative of human history - however we intend to help people build their own meta-narratives or meta-frameworks for understanding how all people are part of the same story and share common heritage.

Please join us on telegram to build friendships and feel belonging [https://www.launchpass.com/brites/dawns](https://www.launchpass.com/brites/dawns).
 *******
**January: the natural world**

*   J. Donald Hughes, _An Environmental History of the World_
*   Juliet Clutton-Brock, _A Natural History of Domesticated Mammals_
*   Keith Thomas, _Man and the Natural World_
*   Donald Worster, _Nature's Economy_
*   Rachel Carson, _Silent Spring_

**February: Industrial revolutions**

*   Peter Laslett, _The World We Have Lost_
*   Robert Allen, _The British Industrial Revolution in Global Perspective_
*   E.P. Thompson, _The Making of the English Working Class_
*   Robert Gordon, _The Rise and Fall of American Growth_
*   Chris Miller, _Chip War_

**March: The axial age**

*   Karen Armstrong, _The Great Transformation_
*   Benjamin Schwartz, _The World of Thought in Ancient China_
*   Romila Thapar, _Early India: From the Origins to AD 1300_
*   Israel Finkelstein and Neil Asher Silberman, _The Bible Unearthed_
*   Robin Lane Fox, _The Classical World_

**April: Literary history**

*   Walter Ong, _Orality and Literacy_
*   Martin Puchner, _The Written World_
*   Erich Auerbach, _Mimesis_
*   Ian Watt, _The Rise of the Novel_
*   Pascale Casanova, _The World Republic of Letters_

**May: Energy**

*   Vaclav Smil, _Energy and Civilization: A History_
*   Alfred Crosby, _Children of the Sun_
*   Richard Rhodes, _Energy: A Human History_
*   Andreas Malm, _Fossil Capital_
*   Daniel Yergin, _The Prize_

**June: Different modes of living**

*   Bill Gammage, _The Biggest Estate on Earth_
*   Anatoly Khazanov, _Nomads and the Outside World_
*   Patrick Kirch, _On the Road of the Winds: An Archaeological History of the Pacific Islands_
*   James C. Scott, _The Art of Not Being Governed_
*   Chris Jennings, _Paradise Now: The Story of American Utopianism_

**July: The scientific worldview**

*   Steven Weinberg, _To Explain the World_
*   Jim Al-Khalili, _The House of Wisdom_
*   Thomas Kuhn, _The Copernican Revolution_
*   Bill Bryson, _A Short History of Nearly Everything_
*   Carlo Rovelli, _The First Scientist: Anaximander and His Legacy_

**August: Politics and power**

*   Christopher Boehm, _Hierarchy in the Forest_
*   Francis Fukuyama, _The Origins of Political Order_
*   David Stasavage, _The Decline and Rise of Democracy_
*   Benedict Anderson, _Imagined Communities_
*   Lynn Hunt, _Inventing Human Rights_

**September: Art history**

*   E.H. Gombrich, _The Story of Art_
*   David Lewis-Williams, _The Mind in the Cave_
*   Michael Baxandall, _Painting and Experience in Fifteenth-Century Italy_
*   Robert Hughes, _The Shock of the New_
*   Julian Stallabrass, _Contemporary Art: A Very Short Introduction_

**October: Cradles of civilisation**

*   Marc Van De Mieroop, _A History of the Ancient Near East ca. 3000-323 BC_
*   Toby Wilkinson, _The Rise and Fall of Ancient Egypt_
*   Li Feng, _Early China: A Social and Cultural History_
*   Gregory Possehl, _The Indus Civilization: A Contemporary Perspective_
*   Charles C. Mann, _1491_

**November: Economics and trade**

*   David Graeber, _Debt: The First 5,000 Years_
*   James C. Scott, _Against the Grain_
*   William Bernstein, _A Splendid Exchange_
*   Sven Beckert, _Empire of Cotton_
*   Jeffry Frieden, _Global Capitalism: Its Fall and Rise in the Twentieth Century_

**December: Progressive revelation**

*   Karen Armstrong, _A History of God_
*   Israel Finkelstein and Neil Asher Silberman, _The Bible Unearthed_
*   Geza Vermes, _The Religion of Jesus the Jew_
*   Fred Donner, _Muhammad and the Believers_
*   Moojan Momen, _The Bábí and Bahá'í Religions, 1844-1944_

content:
Hi, our Dharma friends!
 Welcome to the gateway to Buddhism 101 for all! Our Right View Lab meeting is a friendly get-together of like-minded people to learn about unbiased thinking in Buddhism.
 Our weekly “intro to Buddhism” meetup group is open to all! No experience in Buddhism is necessary. Each week we prepare a Dharma presentation for you all on that week’s Buddhism topic, followed by Q&A. We kick off each meeting with some introductions and short ice-breaking so that you get to know the other members of our sangha community! We have a good mix of regulars and newbies each meeting.
 The first 20 minutes I'd like to get to know who is joining our zoom session so **it's imperative you have your camera on**. After that, we will record our presentation and Q&A and upload to YouTube for access by our premium members. Thank you for your understanding.
 Our classes are free for the first 3 sessions. After 3 sessions, if you see the value in joining, please consider offering a contribution.
 Our classes & sangha are sustained completely by the dana gratitude contributions of people like you! _**Dana gratitude donations for our classes are gratefully accepted on Venmo @Bita-Enayati**_ If you don't have Venmo, please email me at **[bitadharma22@gmail.com](http://bitadharma22@gmail.com/)**
 so you can offer your contribution through PayPal or Zelle
 Suggested donation for the event is $5 - $20.
 Check out our YouTube channel at **[https://www.youtube.com/@EquanimityLab2025**](https://www.youtube.com/@EquanimityLab2025**)

If you have a schedule conflict, you can write to us at [bitadharma22@gmail.com](http://bitadharma22@gmail.com/) for one on one sessions by offering a contribution.
 ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 To better explain the philosophy behind Right View Lab (our weekly Monday events, focusing on unbiased thinking):
 Finding the “Right View” means trying to find an objective and impartial view of the world – and to remove the biases that we all have when viewing the world. We are unable to see anything except through the prism of thought and emotion. When it comes to examining ourselves in particular, it is impossible to take off the tinted glasses of partiality and self seeking. Egoism clouds our vision.
 Here’s a story to illustrate this. One day a princess in the legendary Dragon Palace under the sea held up a jewel and told all the fishes, “I will give a prize to anyone who can tell me what color this is.” Each of them named a different color: the black porgy said it was black, the bluefish said it was blue, and the white-fish said it was silver. Then they asked the princess, “Which one is right?” She replied, “The jewel has no color of its own. It is transparent, and simply reflects each of your colors.”
 In regards to how we view life, it's beneficial to remind ourselves that our minds are like an iceberg. There's some of it poking through above the water level, and there's a vast amount of it below which is unseen. Let me give an example of how a young couple moves into an apartment building. Each Saturday the wife would shout to her husband, "Look at our neighbors laundry hanging over there. It looks so dirty! They must be using the wrong detergent!" This went on each week for quite some time. Then one Saturday, the wife woke up and said, "Today they look beautiful and clean." Then the husband said, "I woke up early this morning and cleaned the window."
 If you're interested in learning Buddhism but have a schedule conflict, please write to me for a one on one session.

1.   Also please note that we might record this zoom session for later access by our premium members. There will be an announcement from the Zoom app when it starts.
2.   We would appreciate it if you use the same name as your Meetup account so that the host of the meeting will easily recognize the participants.
3.   Please make sure you RSVP 30 minutes prior to the start of the meeting.
4.   Our classes are free for the first 3 sessions or so. After 3 sessions, if you see value in joining, please consider offering a contribution.

Check out our YouTube channel at **[https://www.youtube.com/@EquanimityLab2025**](https://www.youtube.com/@EquanimityLab2025**)

**The Zoom meeting passcode is 426646.** We have about 10-20 people join us each week, including the regulars, so hope you don't get discouraged by seeing the few RSVPs here on this page. See you soon too!!!
 We are looking forward to meeting fellow truth-seekers such as yourself, interested in the path to the Right View!
 If you have a schedule conflict, feel free to email me at [bitadharma22@gmail.com](http://bitadharma22@gmail.com/) for one on one sessions by offering a contribution. Stay well now!

content:
A Lifeline for Healing and Hope

My name is Lori Engel. I’m 59, homebound in Oregon. I live completely alone with life-altering neurological injuries and disabilities that have reshaped every part of my world.

My Background

I grew up as a missionary child in Brazil, where faith, service, and compassion became the foundation of my life. As an adult, I carried that forward—serving six years as a missionary teacher in Taiwan, then eleven years as a chaplain, walking alongside people in illness, grief, crisis, and loss. Caring for others wasn’t just my work; it was my identity. The last two years of my career, I was the Director of Chaplain Services for a healthcare organization.

Prior to becoming a chaplain, I was an English teacher for almost two decades, teaching both in Taiwan and at universities in the U.S.

How Everything Changed

That path shifted profoundly starting in late 2006. Over time, I sustained multiple traumatic brain injuries and a toxic reaction to Cipro that damaged my nerves and muscles. I developed serious neurological conditions, including cerebellar damage, ataxia, polyneuropathy, spasticity, severe balance impairment, swallowing difficulties, and vision disturbances, to name a few. These affect my ability to walk, stand, use my arms consistently, regulate my nervous system, or handle even basic daily tasks.

Despite these initial injuries, I continued working as a chaplain until 2015, pushing through pain and limitations to serve others, through God's grace and the aid of nutraceuticals. Additional neurological injuries in 2015 made it impossible to continue, leaving me homebound ever since, unable to drive.

Here is a brief summary of all my injuries:

My injuries consist of multiple TBIs (traumatic brain injury) from falling backward onto the kitchen tile floor, hitting the back of my head; slamming my forehead into a concrete bunk bed; and falling and hitting the side of my head here in Oregon. I also experienced medical malpractice that damaged my cervical spine. I was erroneously prescribed fluroquinolones Avelox and Cipro for 30 days straight, which severely damaged my nerves and tendons. (The FDA has issued warnings about these drugs.) Then I got a bad infection. Later, I also experienced thermal burns to my spine and base of my head.

Then, I was exposed to and living in wildfires so severe that ashes were all around me here in Oregon in 2020, which exponentially exacerbated all my autonomic, nerve, and vascular damage, as well as breathing. Then in 2021 I had Covid, which causes neurological issues in even healthy people. For me, it created additional issues.

There has been a compounded, cumulative effect of all the layered injuries. Most people struggle to comprehend such a parade of horribles, but I do have records.

It has been more than I can ever put into words. I am just thankful to be alive. I am thankful for the many years I worked as a chaplain, until there were just too many injuries.

My Daily Reality

Simple things most people take for granted—opening a package, standing at the sink, stepping outside, or even too much visual input—can overload my fragile system, causing loss of balance, neurological shutdown, or crushing exhaustion. Some days I can’t get out of bed. Others, I push through just to care for myself and my faithful dog Teddie, only to crash afterward.

I haven’t seen my family in 13 years (they live on the East Coast), and for the last 10-plus years I can’t travel. I receive no family financial support. The isolation is profound, and Teddie—my constant companion, emotional anchor, and service companion in many ways—is one of the biggest reasons I keep going, in addition to God's miraculous care.

What I Am Fighting For

Yet every day, I fight to heal and hold onto as much independence as possible. As my health allows, I write devotional pieces that integrate faith, neuroscience, and psychology—sharing insights on resilience, hope, and spiritual growth on social media. It’s a small but meaningful way I continue to give back and encourage others, even from home.

My lifeline is an intensive, carefully managed regimen: specialized therapies, targeted nutrition, and essential supplements that stabilize my brain, muscles, emotions, and overall functioning. When I can stay consistent with these protocols, I feel more like myself—steadier, clearer, hopeful. When I can’t, everything declines quickly: neurologically, physically, and emotionally.

How Your Support Helps

My disability income is severely limited (SSDI), and it does not even cover rent. Ongoing costs far exceed what I can cover. Neurological medications/nutraceuticals alone are expensive and not covered by Medicare. I also need nutritious food tailored to my conditions, basic utilities, in-home support, and care for Teddie.

I’m not asking for luxuries—only the basics that allow me to continue healing, stay safe at home, avoid further decline, and keep writing when possible.

Your monthly - or one-time - support will directly help cover:

• Essential neurological and immunological supplements to stabilize my system and medical care not covered by Medicare.

• Food and daily living necessities

• Basic in-home support and utility expenses

• Veterinary care, food, and supplies for Teddie, my vital companion

• Unexpected critical needs that protect my independence and safety

A Message of Gratitude and Hope

Every gift—no matter the size—becomes part of this lifeline. It prevents eviction. It helps me get through the hardest days, hold onto hope for continued (even if gradual) improvement.

Sharing this campaign is also a huge gift. When you’re largely invisible due to homebound disability, profound isolation, and no nearby support network, awareness can make all the difference.

After a lifetime of caring for others, I now humbly need care myself. It’s been a difficult shift, but I’m grateful for every act of kindness.God has never failed me during these long, lonely years.

It's been a long, agonizing road, but I still believe healing is possible. I still hold fast to faith that God can bring restoration, step by step—and use even my writing to touch lives. I will never stop trying.

Thank you for seeing me, for caring, and for helping carry what I cannot carry alone. Your support—financial, prayerful, or simply shared—means more than words can express.

With deepest gratitude and hope,

Lori Engel

"Out of suffering come the strongest souls."

(With friends who brought Lori food in 2017)

In 2021, after wounds discovered under hair

2026

In 2009, as a chaplain.

title: Hong Kong proposes HK$10 billion injection for San Tin Technopole
zh_title: 香港拟注资100亿港元兴建新田科技城
summary: 政府 香港政府拟向新田科技城公司注资 100 亿港元，资金用于土地平整、科技用地开发和早期运营。该计划旨在通过公私合作伙伴关系吸引企业，并在五年内加快土地交付。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 14 日 11:33 HKT · 2 分钟阅读《香港报》政府拟向新港注资100亿港元
content:
政府
香港政府拟向新田科技城公司注资 100 亿港元，资金用于土地平整、科技用地开发和早期运营。该计划旨在通过公私合作伙伴关系吸引企业，并在五年内加快土地交付。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 14 日 11:33 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

香港政府拟从资本投资基金中向新田科技公司注资100亿港元，以加速新技术中心的发展。这笔资金包括约30亿港元用于利用市场资源加快土地开发、约60亿港元用于开发创科土地，以及约10亿港元用于公司早期运营开支。

创新科技及工业局在向立法会提交的文件中表示，新田科技城约210公顷的创科用地中，政府预计未来五年将交付约140公顷。为了吸引企业，新田科技公司最初可能需要投资建设工业设施。
该公司还可以通过招标或直接赠款的方式租赁部分科技城土地，允许企业、大学和研究机构建设和运营自己的设施。它还可以考虑通过持股或“土地换股权”安排与公司组建合资企业，共同开发和投资各个项目。

文件称，目标是采取更多公私合作模式开发科技城土地，逐步吸引民间资本，形成产业集群效应。

拟拨款30亿港元加速土地开发，将让公司根据发展规划、招商力度和资源情况，灵活选择合适地块直接参与土地开发，加快交付速度。

约60亿港元预留用于开发创科土地，包括设计及兴建工业设施以供出租，以期尽快吸引企业入驻。该公司还将为科技极的战略产业提供配套的基础设施和公用事业。

其余约10亿港元将用于支付早期运营成本，包括员工工资、业务发展和运营开支。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编
负责 CLB.org.hk 报道和编辑标准的主编。

【原文 English Original】
Government
The Hong Kong government proposes a HK$10 billion capital injection for the San Tin Technopole company, with funds for land formation, tech land development, and early operations. The plan aims to attract firms via public-private partnerships and expedite land delivery over five years.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

14 Oct 2026 at 11:33 HKT · 2 min read

The Hong Kong government has proposed a HK$10 billion capital injection for the San Tin Technopole company, drawn from the Capital Investment Fund, to accelerate development of the new technology hub. The funding includes about HK$3 billion to speed up land formation using market-based resources, about HK$6 billion for developing innovation and technology land, and about HK$1 billion for the company's early operating expenses.

In a paper submitted to the Legislative Council, the Innovation, Technology and Industry Bureau said that of the approximately 210 hectares of innovation and technology land in San Tin Technopole, the government expects about 140 hectares to be delivered in the next five years. To attract businesses, the San Tin Technopole company may initially need to invest in building industrial facilities itself.

The company may also lease parts of the technopole land through tenders or direct grants, allowing enterprises, universities and research institutions to construct and operate their own facilities. It could also consider forming joint ventures with companies through shareholding or 'land-for-equity' arrangements to jointly develop and invest in individual projects.

The goal is to adopt more public-private partnership models to develop the technopole land, gradually drawing in private capital and building up industrial clustering effects, the document said.

The proposed HK$3 billion allocation for accelerating land formation would allow the company to flexibly select suitable plots for direct participation in land development, based on its development plans, investment promotion efforts and resources, to speed up delivery.

The roughly HK$6 billion earmarked for developing innovation and technology land includes designing and building industrial facilities for lease, with the aim of attracting businesses as soon as possible. The company would also provide supporting infrastructure and public utilities for strategic industries in the technopole.

The remaining about HK$1 billion would cover early operating costs, including staff salaries, business development and operational expenses.

content: 作者臉書  2026-10-13 五十年前的十月六日，是中國當代歷史上重要一頁，由華國鋒、葉劍英、汪東興三人合作，一舉逮捕四人幫，那一天被視為老毛發動十年文革結束的日子，史稱「懷仁堂事變」。 逮捕四人幫，結束十年文革亂世，稍後權力盡歸鄧小平，老鄧發動經濟改革，自此中國走上四十年經濟發展的道路。懷仁堂事變對中共有起死回生的意義，對中國人民來說，也不失為一個歷史轉折的大關口。 關於這場事變，一般都認為是華國鋒與葉劍英、汪東興合作辦成，實際是否如此 ，值得認真想一想。華是老毛臨終指定的接班人，雖有權力合法性，但資歷淺，在中央毫無政治基礎，雖然表面中立，但與左右兩邊都不搭界。對四人幫實施殺手鐧，對他來說風險極大，搞得不好會腦袋搬家。 葉劍英雖是老革命，但與華國鋒並不是盟友，他當時擔任中共中央副主席，除了華國鋒為第一副主席外，還有另一位副主席是王洪文。也就是說，兩個副主席把一個副主席廢了，這種驚天動地的秘密勾當，除非華與葉極端互信，否則誰都不敢動這個念頭。 至於汪東興，當時他的身份是政治局委員，兼中央辦公廳主任和中央警衛局局長。他在懷仁堂事件中屬於執行的角色，如無華葉兩人合謀拍板，汪東興也沒有那個膽搞宮廷政變。 華國鋒在1976年4月才被老毛指定為中共中央第一副主席兼國務院總理，當年9月9日老毛就死了，10月6日華國鋒就逮捕了四人幫。也就是說，華國鋒真正掌權不到半年，其間基本上在辦老毛後事，政治上根本未站穩腳根，就辦了這件中共歷史上空前的大案，而且辦得如此有章法無風險，那是否證明他是一個有雄才大略的政治領袖？ 事後看起來又不像，他在逮捕四人幫後做了中共中央主席，他在任內只做了兩件事，一是提出「兩個凡是」（凡是毛主席作出的決策，我們都堅決維護，凡是毛主席的指示，我們都始終不渝地遵守」，兩個「凡是」互相重複，毫無神采，證明此人之政治見識很一般）；另一件事是與汪東興一起，竭力阻止鄧小平復出（葉劍英似乎未介入）。 華國鋒前後做了三四年「英明領袖」，後來禁不住黨內保守派圍攻，只能順從交出最高權力，退出歷史舞台。除了逮捕四人幫這件事之外，華國鋒給人的印象，就是一個平庸的黨官，一味追隨毛澤東，不敢越雷池一步，為何在逮捕四人幫這件事上，他又有如此驚天勇氣和魄力？ 華國鋒那麼忠於老毛，竟無視江青是偉大領袖毛主席遺孀？江青在被審時高呼「毛主席屍骨未寒」，這是言之成理的，偉大領袖剛死不到一個月，華國鋒就把他的老婆活捉了，如此翻臉也太快，也不符合華國鋒厚重少鋒芒的性情。 至於葉劍英，老毛對他評價相當高，說他救了黨救了紅軍，又說他「呂端大事不糊涂」，葉劍英正是老毛可以托咐大事最可靠的人。有老毛身邊看護回憶，毛晚年曾召來葉劍英，摒退左右，與葉關在房間裡密談一兩個鐘頭，這段時間裡兩人密商什麼，外人當然不知道。 九一三林彪叛逃後，老毛提拔王洪文為接班人，可惜王洪文不堪重任，花天酒地，玩弄權術，令老毛對他失去信任，再以華國鋒替換他。當年四人幫已成氣候，對華國鋒掌權當然極之忌恨，以老毛之梟雄性格，一定預知他身後中國局勢之凶險，他晚年對身邊的人一再感歎，說「恐怕要在風雨中交班了」。 老毛多次對江青說，我死後看你們怎麼辦？老毛老謀深算，一定深知他去世後中國有可能陷入左右兩派的爭權血戰中，四人幫絕不會接受權力旁落，一定把政治局勢搞得不可收拾，因此四人幫成為老毛身後一顆定時炸彈，老毛一定要預為之謀。 老毛當然也明白，處理四人幫是一件極之凶險的大案，不論誰都沒有那個膽量挑頭起事，除非他自己把最壞的形勢作充份估計，並將處理手段交代清楚，否則他死後中共就有嚴重執政危機。 為解中共倒懸之險，老毛唯有自己下決心，去解決引致社會亂動、中共政權瓦解的危機根源。當事態發展到不可收拾時，唯有放棄四人幫，再以保守派老人輔佐華國鋒，才能保中共政權之不失，這雖是迫不得已的一步棋，卻也是不得不準備的一步棋。 因此，可能的安排是，老毛預作最壞打算，分別對華國鋒、葉劍英和汪東興私下授意，當四人幫爭權搞事時，便以宮廷政變的非正常手段解決。對華國鋒來說，外事不決找葉劍英，內事不決找汪東興，而活捉四人幫，便是華葉汪共同配合的殊死一戰。 事實證明，老毛的預見相當英明，他死後四人幫果然搞事。江青在政治局開會大吵大鬧，要求控制老毛留下的機密檔案；王洪文向各省革委會發通知，要求向他報告工作；王洪文又指示向上海民兵發槍，準備與中央對抗。 如非老毛臨終交代，天給華國鋒膽，他都未必有膽量與能力去操作，反而，老毛將內外條件都替他安排好了，甚至可能連執行細節都設想周到，那時華國鋒要下決心就容易得多了。 內有汪東興帶領中央警衛局分頭執行現場逮捕，外有葉劍英串通老革命保駕護航，而當時黨內與社會上對四人幫早已恨之入骨，如此執行抓捕正是順天應時，能保黨內國內順利過渡，不會有大災難發生。 老毛竟然出賣自己的老婆，出賣親手扶植的親信，這是否說得通呢？當然說得通，老毛本就是這種無情無義的人，他對自己的親密戰友如劉少奇和林彪，都是手起刀落毫不含糊，更何況四人幫本就是他養起來對付老革命的走狗。江青受審時說：我是毛主席的一條狗，他叫我咬誰我就咬誰，政治鬥爭中用過即棄，本來對老毛就不是什麼稀罕事。 對老毛來說，是中共這個黨、中國這個江山重要，還是他老婆重要，這是不必問的。老毛沒有想到的是，在他死後，中共沒有垮台，但華國鋒不堪重任，鄧小平復出，私有經濟全面回潮，他最痛恨的資本主義復辟，間接經他的手實現了。 活捉四人幫這件事，如果由老毛主導，由華國鋒拍板，汪東興執行，葉劍英策應，那就是萬全之策，不得不承認，玩政治唯有老毛是絕世高手。中共黨內，唯有老毛有如此的強人手腕、歷史魄力，也有如此「與人奮鬥其樂無窮」的冷酷本色。 中共對此事諱莫如深，對華國鋒活捉四人幫的功績極力淡化，主要原因是，如果承認老毛主謀，親手毒害自己老婆和親信，那種毫無道義和人性的本質，將暴露在全世界人面前，對於中共引老毛為偉大領袖，那是強烈的自我諷刺，所以寧肯按下不表。 這件歷史懸案最終有沒有機會真相大白，那就要看中共會不會垮台了，中共垮台後檔案公開，那時就知道更多歷史細節，我們不妨將它視為一種假設，當作杯酒言歡時的談資好了。

title: 中国制裁伯利兹和巴拉圭的部长后，美国表示反对中国“胁迫”行动
summary: 华盛顿 — 在中国制裁台湾邦交国巴拉圭和伯利兹的两名部长级官员后，美国国务院告诉美国之音，美国反对中国的胁迫行动以及一切可能威胁和平与稳定的单边行动。 **美国反对中国的胁迫行动** 在华盛顿时间星期一(10月12日)傍晚给美国之音的电子邮件回复中，国务院的一位发言人说：“我们已多次重申，两岸分歧应以和平方式解决，不应诉诸胁迫。例行讲话绝不能成为采取攻击性或胁迫性行动的理由。” 声明还说：“美国关心台海地区的和平与稳定。我们反对任何威胁台海地区和平与稳定的单边行动。” 美国国
content:
华盛顿 —

在中国制裁台湾邦交国巴拉圭和伯利兹的两名部长级官员后，美国国务院告诉美国之音，美国反对中国的胁迫行动以及一切可能威胁和平与稳定的单边行动。

**美国反对中国的胁迫行动**

在华盛顿时间星期一(10月12日)傍晚给美国之音的电子邮件回复中，国务院的一位发言人说：“我们已多次重申，两岸分歧应以和平方式解决，不应诉诸胁迫。例行讲话绝不能成为采取攻击性或胁迫性行动的理由。”

声明还说：“美国关心台海地区的和平与稳定。我们反对任何威胁台海地区和平与稳定的单边行动。”

美国国务院所提的一次例行讲话应该指的是台湾总统赖清德10月10日在在台湾115年国庆典礼上的致辞。

赖清德在讲话中表示，台湾珍惜和平，但不会放弃自由；“和平不能只靠愿望，包容也不能成为侵略者得寸进尺的理由”。他还引用基督教《圣经》“山巅之城”的概念，强调台湾将成为“维护印太和平与稳定的关键力量”。他并向北京喊话：“武力不能凌驾规则”“台湾愿意交流，但不会接受矮化。

中国外交部当地时间星期一上午发表声明指责巴拉圭通信和技术部长比利亚特(Gustavo Villate)、伯利兹外交暨外贸部长弗朗西斯·丰塞卡(Francis Fonseca)为“反华政客”，顽固支持与台湾所谓的“邦交”关系，并对两人实施制裁措施，内容包括冻结两人在中国境内的财产、禁止境内组织及个人与其交易合作，以及不予签发签证、不准入境等。制裁同一天正式实施。

**伯利兹和巴拉圭：继续推进与台湾的关系**

针对中国的制裁，伯利兹外交部表示，丰塞卡只是履行其合法职责，中国制裁之举“毫无根据”。该部强调这些措施不会改变伯利兹的外交政策，伯利兹仍将全力维持与台湾的关系。

据路透社报道，比利亚特在得知被制裁的消息后，在当地媒体采访时表示，鉴于巴拉圭与台湾正在推进的合作项目，包括一项人工智能(AI)数据中心计划，中方采取这一行动是“意料之中的”。

“我们非常冷静。我们将继续推进所有现有项目，并会更加有力地推动这些工作。”比利亚特说。

分析人士此前告诉美国之音，这两位被北京制裁的友邦官员，可能是在国际场合发言的时候明显踩到中共在台湾议题立场的红线。

比利亚特10月10日在祝贺中华民国国庆日的X贴文中写的：“巴拉圭重申与台湾的友好合作关系，这段关系创建在双方共同的价值观与原则之上，包括人民自决权、人权及民主。”

而丰塞卡则是在联合国大会上发言说“台湾是一个国家”(Taiwan is a nation)。丰塞卡还曾两度访台，9月刚刚接待台湾外交部长林佳龙，两人签署外交人员训练与交流合作协定及联合公报。

伯利兹驻台大使馆在中国宣布制裁消息不久前，在脸书发布贴文纪念伯利兹与台湾建交37周年，“双方关系建立在相互尊重、彼此信任与密切合作的基础之上……我们期盼携手共创繁荣成长、更多机会，以及永恒不渝的友谊”。

**台湾：中国霸权引起世界共同的反感**

星期二，台湾行政院长卓荣泰批评中国“一再对外施展霸权心态与做法，已经引起全世界共同的反感”，并称中国无权干涉包含中华民国台湾在内、任何主权国家的内政外交。

台湾外交部在中国外交部制裁两位官员的消息出台后，随即谴责了中国的说法，指其内容荒谬至极，公然干涉他国主权及外交政策，违反国际法原则，赤裸展现中国妄图以政治恫吓与“跨境镇压”手段。台湾台外交部强调，中华民国台湾是主权独立国家，与中华人民共和国互不隶属，这是国际公认事实及台海客观现状，中国对于台湾的外交关系无权置喙。

title: 茶百道 IPO 涉嫌操纵市场被暂停上市

content: 界面新闻记者 |卢奕贝 牙韩翔 李烨 界面新闻编辑 |许悦 10月13日，界面新闻获悉，香港证监会指示香港联交所，自当天上午9时起暂停茶百道股份交易。证监会表示，高度关注茶百道的首次公开招股可能曾被人为操纵，意图就其股份需求营造非真实的表象。 “由于调查仍在进行中，证监会不会作进一步评论。”香港证监会对界面新闻表示。 这场调查涉及一个由孙然及八家相关公司组成的可疑集团。香港证监会称，该集团涉嫌参与茶百道及拨康视云首次公开招股的欺诈计划，已向六家经纪行发出限制通知，禁止处置或处理上述九个实体名下客户账户内的相关资产，限制金额上限约为43.79亿港元——这是香港证监会历来同类案件中最高的限制金额。 其中，八家相关公司分别注册于英属维尔京群岛、塞舌尔及萨摩亚。公告尚未披露它们各自在涉嫌计划中的具体角色，以及与茶百道之间的关系。 香港证监会怀疑，部分投资者买新股的钱，可能绕了一圈又回到自己或关联方手中。 根据公告，部分首次公开招股募集资金，可能依据上市公司与可疑集团之间未披露的协议，被转出用于所谓的金融产品投资，并暗中回流至主要获配新股的投资者或其关联方。 如果这套安排事先约好，投资者认购新股的理由就可能包括上市后能拿回部分资金。其他投资者不知道背后的约定，却可能把这些认购当成看好公司的信号，从而高估新股的真实需求。 上海新古律师事务所主任王怀涛向界面新闻表示，这类未披露的安排可能影响市场对新股需求及发行价格的判断，风险也可能延续至上市后的交易。 不过，公告尚未公开茶百道具体涉及哪笔协议、金融产品及资金流向，也没有认定茶百道公司或其管理层参与操纵。公司是否知情、是否参与，以及相关人员具体如何操作，仍有待进一步调查。 界面新闻向茶百道方面查询上述事宜，截至发稿暂未收到回应。 两年多前，茶百道曾是新茶饮品牌争相上市时最先跑出来的公司之一。 2024年初，蜜雪冰城、古茗、沪上阿姨等品牌接连向港交所递交上市申请。茶百道则于当年4月23日挂牌，成为继奈雪的茶之后第二家在港股上市的新茶饮公司，也是首家以加盟模式为主的新茶饮上市公司。 茶百道以每股17.5港元发行约1.48亿股新股，募集资金总额约25.86亿港元，成为当时港股年内规模最大的IPO。 但发行并未获得香港公众投资者的踊跃认购。面向公众发售的新股只获得约一半认购，并未售满；主要面向机构等投资者的国际发售，认购量则为原计划发售量的1.11倍。 由于公众认购不足，部分原本留给公众的股份被转至国际发售。调整后，约95%的新股通过国际发售分配，不包括额外超额分配的股份。 上市首日，茶百道便跌破发行价，最终收报12.8港元，较发行价下跌26.86%。 一位在国际律师事务所从事并购及资本市场业务的律师向界面新闻表示，判断的关键在于，认购资金是否通过其他协议被上市公司返还，相关金融产品投资是否真实并依法披露，以及投资者与公司之间是否存在未披露的关联。 换言之，香港证监会调查需要调查的，是茶百道IPO认购背后有没有市场不知道的条件。上市公司购买金融产品本身不等于违法，但如果投资早已与新股认购绑定，并将资金转回认购方，交易的性质就可能不同。 此次被点名的孙然，是嘉实国际投资有限公司的持牌代表。该公司是一家香港持牌金融机构，可从事证券交易、就证券提供意见及资产管理业务，也是收到资产限制通知的六家经纪行之一。 界面新闻试图联系嘉实国际投资有限公司，但未能接通。 孙然的任职关系并不等于相关活动属于嘉实国际投资的业务或授权范围，也不足以证明该公司管理的基金参与了茶百道IPO。证监会明确表示，收到限制通知的经纪行并非调查对象，相关通知不影响它们的运营或其他客户。 今年以来，香港证监会已多次针对涉嫌制造IPO需求假象的行为采取行动。 7月30日，香港证监会公布向富途证券发出限制通知，限制某涉嫌参与IPO欺诈计划的实体名下客户账户资产，金额上限约为1.25亿港元。该案中，富途同样并非调查对象。9月10日，香港证监会又因关注拨康视云IPO可能被人为操纵，指令其停牌。 王怀涛认为，对认购真实性的调查，关系到投资者能否信任新股发行中的需求和定价信号。查处虚假需求，也是在维护香港市场的融资信誉。 对茶百道而言，停牌已经发生，但公司最终需要承担什么责任，尚无定论。 此次停牌依据《证券及期货（在证券市场上市）规则》第8(1)条实施。该条款允许证监会在维护公平有序市场、保护投资者利益等情况下，指令联交所暂停股份交易。 上述资本市场律师表示，这属于调查期间的市场保护措施，并不等于公司已被认定违法。后续责任的判断，将取决于相关协议和资金经手相关方，以及公司和管理层是否知情或参与。 如果有关安排由个别人员在董事会或管理层不知情的情况下促成，主要参与者与上市公司的责任需要分别判断，公司也可能需要处理由此暴露的内部管理问题。 如果调查发现公司或相关人员知悉并参与，则可能进一步涉及招股文件是否真实、募集资金用途是否准确披露等问题。该律师表示，视最终查明的事实及适用法律，相关主体可能面临民事索赔、监管处分；涉及刑事违法的，还可能被追究刑事责任。 香港证监会对界面新闻称，就维护投资大众的利益或公众利益而言，发出该等通知书以保存有关资产是可取的做法。所涉各方日后可能会被饬令透过复还程序，向受影响的投资者作出赔偿。 而茶百道的个人股东眼下面临的直接影响，是无法通过联交所正常买卖茶百道股票，且复牌时间尚不明确。 上述资本市场律师表示，公司能否复牌，取决于监管疑虑是否得到妥善处理。公司可以向香港证监会作出申述，但不能自行决定恢复交易，调查结束也不意味着自动复牌。 至于其他港股茶饮餐饮企业，目前公告没有提供它们与上述涉嫌安排存在关联的信息。王怀涛对界面新闻称，此事可能促使投资者更加关注同类企业的IPO质量，也使拟上市企业及其保荐人、承销商更重视认购真实性的核查；而这种影响并不局限于茶饮或餐饮行业。 虽然停牌本身不直接影响茶百道的门店营业，但投资者对资金安全和公司治理的疑虑，可能抬高茶百道未来的融资成本，并影响其扩张所需的资金安排。

title: 法国冷冻食品区的“捷径”效应，能在中国重现吗？
